title: Per-slice encoding with max pooling, and a CNN backbone — the only untested difference of the right size
description:
EVERY KNOB IS EXHAUSTED AND THEY ARE ALL THE SAME SIZE. Measured on this architecture: schedule +0.0061, augmentation-applied +0.0110, TTA +0.0035, intensity augmentation +0.0019, weight floor +0.0019, better labels -0.0008, 32 slices -0.018. Apart from the three defects, nothing is worth more than 0.002.

THE REMAINING GAPS ARE AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE BIGGER: our per-member holdout 0.8269 against the .903 reference's reported OOF 0.8544, and 0.888 against the leader's 0.942. Nothing measured explains either.

THE .903 RECIPE DIFFERS STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY SETTINGS:
  backbone     single-channel ImageNet EfficientNet-B3   (ours: DINOv2-small ViT, 3-channel)
  study input  3 fluid-sensitive plane-diverse series    (ours: 6 plane x weighting slots)
  pooling      MAX over slice embeddings, then MEAN over series logits
               (ours: 3 consecutive slices stacked as CHANNELS, then per-diagnosis attention over slots)

THE POOLING DIFFERENCE IS THE ONE WITH A MECHANISM WE HAVE ALREADY FELT. Our channel stacking is what made 32 inference slices FAIL (-0.018): raising the slice count over a fixed band changes each group's physical thickness, so the model sees an input distribution it never trained on. Per-slice encoding has no such coupling — which is exactly why THEY can raise slices at inference and we cannot. The same coupling plausibly limits what a fixed 12-slice budget can see: a finding is either inside a sampled 3-slice group or invisible.

WHY IT IS NOW AFFORDABLE: `StudyModel` already takes its backbone as an injected `nn.Module` (structural, not a named protocol — written that way for exactly this), and timm 1.0.26 is in Kaggle's image, so an EfficientNet needs no wheel. What has to change is the bag layout and `_pool`.

SCOPE, and it is genuinely two experiments that should not be confused:
  1. AGGREGATION: keep DINOv2, encode each slice independently, max over slices. Isolates pooling.
  2. BACKBONE: keep the aggregation, swap the encoder. Isolates the encoder family.
Run 1 first — it is the one with a mechanism we have already observed, and it does not need a new model mount.

CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE FORGOTTEN: at ~0.002 per knob and an unmeasured noise floor, a single fold cannot resolve a small win here either. This is worth doing only because the hypothesised effect is 0.02-0.03, not 0.002 — if it lands in the noise, it is a refutation, not a tuning opportunity.
close_reason: REFUTED at the predicted size: per-slice max +0.0018 vs 0.0012 noise floor, for 3x encoder cost, on a matched pair (0.8099 vs 0.8081). The mechanism was also wrong - 32-slice inference costs the same -0.01 under BOTH poolings, so channel-stacking's thickness coupling was not why the wide read hurt. Backbone swap (experiment 2) not run: experiment 1 was the one with an observed mechanism and it did not survive.

title: We train on the second-worst public label table; a better one is free
description:
MEASURED ON THE 58 GOLD STUDIES (2026-08-11), mean per-finding AUC of each public reader against the expert annotations:

  pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels      0.8705   <- WHAT WE TRAIN ON
  stevenleehans llm_labels_v2        0.8905
  stevenleehans llm_labels_v4_blend  0.8982   <- +0.028, free, already public
  lixin73 report_labels_gpt56sol     0.8431

Per finding the gaps are much larger than the mean suggests: Synovitis 0.695 (pilkwang) against 0.805, Contusion 0.756 against 0.862, Lateral Meniscus 0.844 against 0.886. Those are three of our four weakest labels on the holdout, and each costs a full 1/12 of the competition metric.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE NUMBER: the .903 notebook states plainly that 'the image model is downstream of label quality'. We have been tuning the model (schedule, augmentation, TTA) against labels that are 0.028 worse than the best freely available ones, so every one of those measurements was made against a handicapped target.

FUSION IS REFUTED FOR OUR READERS, which is worth recording because the .903 system's headline mechanism is fusion:
  mean of all four        0.8938
  rank-mean of all four   0.8966
  rank-mean of top three  0.8952
  best single (steven_v4) 0.8982   <- still the winner
Averaging drags the best table toward the weaker ones, and v4_blend is ALREADY a blend, so there is little independent signal left to add. Their fusion presumably worked because their private Qwen reader was independent of pilkwang's; ours are not.

DO NOT hand-pick a per-finding winner. The oracle that does scores 0.9016, but it is chosen on the same 57 studies it is scored on, and at these counts a per-finding AUC carries roughly +/-0.09. That is the same trap the annotation check sets (identical members scoring 0.7356 to 0.9164 on it).

ACTION: retrain on steven_v4_blend and re-measure. Every recipe result so far (schedule +0.0061, augmentation +0.011) should be re-confirmed against the better labels, because a gain measured against noisier targets can shrink or grow when the targets improve.
notes:
SWAP NEEDS NO CODE (2026-08-11). `Targets.load` already handles the better table unchanged:

  report_labels_v2 (ours)   7 distinct target values, 12 __conf columns, mean weight 0.692
  llm_labels_v4_blend       186 distinct target values, NO __conf columns, mean weight 1.026

The absence of __conf is not a gap to fill. pilkwang's table carries a coarse score (five levels) plus a separate confidence; v4_blend carries a genuinely continuous score, so the uncertainty lives IN the target rather than beside it. BCE against 0.5 already pulls weakly in both directions, so adding a derived confidence would double-count the same doubt. It is also exactly what the .903 recipe does: 'BCE-with-logits on fused soft labels'.

CONSEQUENCE FOR AN OPEN ISSUE: with uniform weights, knee-9sy (the 0.25 weight floor) becomes moot under these labels — a floor only matters when some weights are zero, and none are. It stays open only for the old table.

QUEUED, so the GPU never idles between the five-fold run finishing and the ablations starting:
  A  fold 0, v4_blend labels, otherwise the recipe that scored 0.8202  -> isolates LABELS
  B  fold 0, v4_blend + intensity augmentation                        -> both changes together
  C  fold 0, old labels + intensity augmentation                      -> isolates AUGMENTATION

A, B and C against the 0.8202 baseline give both main effects and the interaction from three runs rather than four, because the baseline already exists.
METHODOLOGY BUG IN MY OWN ABLATION, caught mid-flight (2026-08-11).

`train.py` used ONE label table for both training and scoring, so the queued arms would have been measured with different rulers: the 0.8202 baseline was scored against pilkwang targets, while arm A (trained on v4_blend) would have been scored against v4_blend targets. A holdout AUC can rise simply because the labels agree with THEMSELVES more, and I would have read that as a better model.

FIX: `--eval-labels` separates the ruler from the training signal, defaulting to `--labels` so existing behaviour is unchanged.

RULER CHOSEN DELIBERATELY: pilkwang for every arm — the table the baseline used, and NOT the table the interesting arm trains on. A v4-trained model therefore earns no self-agreement credit; it is judged by the other reader. That makes the test conservative: it can understate v4's benefit but cannot manufacture one. If training on v4 improves a pilkwang-scored holdout, the labels are genuinely better rather than merely more self-consistent.

ARMS (fold 0, all scored on pilkwang):
  baseline  train pilkwang               0.8202  (already measured)
  A         train v4_blend               -> LABELS, conservative
  C         train pilkwang + intensity   -> AUGMENTATION, clean
  B         train v4_blend + intensity   -> both

45 minutes of GPU were killed to fix this rather than spending them on numbers that could not be compared.
ARM A RESULT — BETTER LABELS ARE NEUTRAL HERE (2026-08-11), which does not support the thesis I filed this issue on.

  baseline  train pilkwang, eval pilkwang   0.8202
  A         train v4_blend, eval pilkwang   0.8194   (-0.0008, i.e. flat)

The label tables differ by +0.028 in agreement with the 58 gold studies, and that difference did NOT translate into a better model on this measurement.

WHAT THE RESULT DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH, since the ruler is not neutral:
- The ruler is pilkwang, so the BASELINE enjoys a self-agreement advantage that arm A does not. 'Flat on a ruler tilted toward the baseline' is therefore weak evidence that v4 is at least as good, and is NOT evidence that it is worse.
- Equally, it is not the win the label-quality measurement suggested. BCE against soft targets is fairly robust to label noise, and both tables are derived from the SAME reports by different readers — so the readers' disagreement may be concentrated on studies whose reports are genuinely ambiguous, where neither label is reliable and the image cannot settle it either.

THE TEST THAT WOULD SETTLE IT is a cross-fitted evaluation on the 58 gold studies: each gold study scored only by the fold-model that held it out, for both label choices. Fold 0's holdout contains roughly a dozen gold studies, far too few alone, so this needs all five folds per arm — about 2.5 hours of GPU. That is the honest price of an unbiased ruler, and it is worth paying only if the augmentation arm does not turn out to be the larger lever.

DO NOT quietly switch the training labels on the strength of a label-quality number. The measurement that matters is the model's, and it says nothing so far.
CORRECTION (2026-08-11): closed as 'null' on a single-fold matched pair, but seed variance on the same fold is +/-0.012 while these effects are +/-0.002. The correct verdict is NOT DETECTABLE at n=1, not null. Neither is worth re-running bigger — resolving 0.002 against 0.012 needs ~36 paired runs — but the record should not claim more than it measured. See knee-uxg.
close_reason: Null on the model's own measurement (-0.0013 mean) despite +0.028 label quality against gold. Do not switch training labels on a label-quality number alone.

title: Augmentation was written, tested, and never called by the training loop
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11. `Trainer.augment` exists, is unit-tested, and `fit_epoch` NEVER CALLED IT. Every run to this point — all five folds and BOTH leaderboard submissions — trained with zero augmentation.

EVIDENCE IT MATTERED: the 40-epoch OneCycle curve peaks near epoch 16 and then declines monotonically (0.8143 -> 0.8043 by ep36). That is textbook overfitting, and it explains how they train 60 epochs where we degrade after 16.

WHY BOTH GATES MISSED IT, which is the part worth keeping:
- vulture (dead code) saw the method as USED, because its unit test references it.
- the mirror gate saw it as TESTED, because it has a `test_augment`.
A method can therefore be fully covered and completely disconnected. The gates check that a method exists, is referenced and is tested; none of them checks that the CALLER calls it.

FIX: `fit_epoch` now routes every batch through `augment_bag`, which converts uint8 -> float, warps, and converts back so `StudyModel.forward` (and therefore the fingerprint) is untouched. Slots are warped independently: they are separate acquisitions of one knee, not one volume, so a shared jitter would imply a registration that does not exist.

NEW TEST that would have caught it: `test_fit_epoch_augments` wraps `augment_bag` and asserts the training loop actually calls it. The general lesson: test the CALLER, not only the callee.
notes:
FIXED AND MEASURED (2026-08-11). Fold 0, every run matched on seed and data, only the recipe differing:

  constant LR, no aug, 16 ep   0.8092   <- the recipe BOTH leaderboard submissions used
  OneCycle,    no aug, 16 ep   0.8153   (+0.0061 from the schedule)
  OneCycle,    no aug, 40 ep   0.8181   best, but the tail DECLINES to 0.8043 by ep36
  OneCycle,    aug,    30 ep   0.8201   best, and the tail is FLAT (0.8172-0.8181 through ep29)

+0.0109 over the submitted recipe, and the overfitting is GONE rather than merely checkpointed around: the unaugmented 40-epoch run fell 0.014 from its peak, the augmented 30-epoch run falls 0.003.

That closes about half the 0.0236 per-member gap to their 0.8398, from two changes that were already written in our own code and simply not connected.

SIDE EFFECT WORTH KEEPING: epoch time fell 40s -> 30s from the memmap indexing fix (images[b, :, s:s+G] in one op rather than images[b][:, :, s:s+G], which materialised all twelve slices to use three). So the corrected recipe at 30 epochs costs about the same wall-clock as the old one at 16.
close_reason: fit_epoch now routes pixels through augment_bag; measured +0.0110 on fold 0, and a test asserts the CALLER not just the callee

title: Medial beats lateral on both pairs — is our laterality recovery wrong, or is it the labels?
description:
Per-label holdout AUC, our fold 0:

    Lateral Meniscus 0.742  vs  Medial Meniscus 0.785   (-0.043)
    Lateral OA       0.774  vs  Medial OA       0.840   (-0.066)
    MCL              0.747  vs  ACL             0.821

BOTH medial/lateral pairs favour medial, and the side-defined targets are exactly the ones a broken laterality normalisation would damage. That is a hypothesis, not a finding — medial pathology is also commoner and more often named in reports, which would produce the same asymmetry through label quality alone.

IT IS CHEAP TO SETTLE, and the audit found why: the diagnostic needs only HEADERS, not pixels. `Acquisition` already carries `laterality_tag` and `centre_x`, so resolving how each study's side was decided is ~24k header reads (~15 s with 20 workers). No cache rebuild.

MEASUREMENT: split the holdout three ways — side from the TAG, side from GEOMETRY, side UNRESOLVED — and compare the medial-minus-lateral AUC gap in each.
  - gap flat across all three  -> it is the labels; laterality is fine; this lead is dead.
  - gap worse on the geometry-resolved half -> our recovery is wrong, and it is worth more than any ensemble.
  - gap worse on the unresolved half -> those studies are being fed unmirrored and should be handled, not ignored.

The cache does NOT currently persist which rule decided each study, which is itself worth fixing once this is answered.
notes:
REFUTED (2026-08-11) — and cleanly, which is why it was worth running first.

PROVENANCE over 4407 studies (headers only, ~90s): tag 2203 (50.0%), geometry 2132 (48.4%), unresolved 72 (1.6%). On the 2135 studies where BOTH are available they agree on 98.6% (their notebook claimed ~97% for the same rule, so this validates the recovery on our corpus).

MEDIAL-MINUS-LATERAL AUC GAP, holdout of fold 0, split by how the side was decided:
  all (909)              meniscus +0.042   OA +0.060
  side from TAG (454)             +0.046      +0.036
  side from GEOMETRY (436)        +0.041      +0.085
  left knees, untouched (431)     +0.071      +0.074
  right knees, MIRRORED (459)     +0.015      +0.035

TWO REASONS THE HYPOTHESIS DIES:
1. Geometry-resolved studies show the SAME asymmetry as tag-resolved ones, so the recovery rule is not introducing it.
2. Decisively, the asymmetry is SMALLER on the knees we actually mirror (+0.015/+0.035) than on the ones we leave alone (+0.071/+0.074). A broken mirror would do the opposite.

So laterality is exonerated and the medial>lateral asymmetry is most likely prevalence/label driven: medial pathology is commoner and more often named in a report, so its derived labels are both denser and cleaner.

HONEST LIMIT: at ~450 studies per group these gaps carry roughly +/-0.02-0.03, so the tag-vs-geometry comparison is solid (it is the same number twice) while the left-vs-right split is suggestive rather than proven.

A METHOD BUG THIS FOUND, in the diagnostic itself: the first run computed the geometric side from only the UNTAGGED series of each study, which made 'both available' mean 'studies whose series disagree about having a tag' - a biased subsample of 74 that read as 86.5% agreement. Recomputing geometry from every series gave 2135 studies at 98.6%. The lesson generalises: when comparing two estimators, both must see the same input.
close_reason: Refuted: the asymmetry is identical across tag- and geometry-resolved studies and SMALLER on the mirrored knees. Laterality is exonerated; the cause is most likely label prevalence.

title: Overlap TTA at inference — implemented, free, and we submitted without it
description:
`Ensemble.predict_member` already takes `overlap: bool = False`, and both kernels call it without the argument. So both submissions averaged over 4 DISJOINT windows while their own inference path used 10 OVERLAPPING ones.

Costs one keyword argument and 2.5x a 0.3 s per-study step — against a 542 s fixed kernel cost, that is nothing. No retraining, no new decode: the cache already holds the slices.

Caveat worth measuring rather than assuming: the out-of-fold ablation found DISJOINT windows matched their stored predictions better (0.025) than overlapping (0.042). That was a statement about reproducing their OOF, not about which scores better. Run both against the same holdout locally before spending a submission.
notes:
MEASURED ON OUR OWN HOLDOUT (2026-08-11, fold 0, member_fold0):
  middle window only (1)   0.8092
  disjoint windows (4)     0.8180
  overlapping windows (10) 0.8205

So overlap is worth +0.0025 over disjoint and +0.0113 over a single window - free, no retraining, and the cache already holds the slices. Both submitted kernels used the DEFAULT overlap=False, so both left this on the table.

This also resolves the caveat: the out-of-fold ablation preferred DISJOINT because that reproduced THEIR stored predictions, which is a statement about matching their pipeline, not about which scores better. On our own holdout, overlapping wins. The two results do not conflict - they answer different questions.
close_reason: Measured (+0.0025) and enabled in both kernels: overlap=OVERLAP_TTA.

title: OneCycleLR: the plateau at epoch 12 is a missing schedule, not a missing epoch
description:
MEASURED: our five folds peak at epochs 13/13/10/12/11 and gain +0.0002/+0.0106/-0.0003/+0.0035/+0.0024 over their final five epochs. Training is saturated at ~12 epochs, so "they ran 60 epochs and we ran 16" does NOT explain the per-member gap (ours 0.8162, theirs 0.8398). Running longer at a constant learning rate would buy nothing.

AUDIT FOUND WHY: they wrap AdamW in

    torch.optim.lr_scheduler.OneCycleLR(opt, max_lr=[LR_BACKBONE, LR_HEAD], total_steps=EPOCHS * (len(tr) // BATCH), pct_start=0.15)

We have no schedule at all — constant 1e-3 head / 8e-6 backbone. A constant LR that plateaus at epoch 12 while a one-cycle run keeps improving to 60 is exactly the shape you would expect, and it is the single most likely cause of the per-member gap.

PROVES IT: retrain fold 0 with OneCycle, same seed, same everything else. If the holdout peak moves past 0.8092 AND the peak epoch moves late, the schedule was the cause. If it plateaus at 12 again, the cause is elsewhere and this is closed.
notes:
CONFIRMED, then partly superseded (2026-08-11). Fold 0, matched — same seed, same data, only the schedule differing:

  constant LR,  16 epochs   0.8092  (peak ep13)
  OneCycleLR,   16 epochs   0.8153  (peak ep12)   +0.0061
  OneCycleLR,   40 epochs   0.8181  best, but the curve PEAKS near ep16 (0.8143) and then declines
                                     monotonically: 0.8118 / 0.8101 / 0.8071 / 0.8061 / 0.8043

So the schedule is a real +0.0061, and MORE EPOCHS IS NOT THE LEVER: past ~16-20 the model overfits. Their 60 epochs is not something to copy directly.

WHY THEY CAN TRAIN 60 EPOCHS AND WE CANNOT — see knee-<AUG>: our `augment` was never called. Every run to this point, including both submissions, trained with ZERO augmentation. The declining tail of the 40-epoch curve is what unregularised training looks like.

OFF-BY-ONE PAID FOR: total_steps used `len(training) // batch`, but our batcher KEEPS the final partial batch while theirs drops it. OneCycleLR raised on the last step of the whole run — after every epoch had been logged, before the checkpoint was written. Fixed with a ceiling rather than by discarding data.
close_reason: Confirmed +0.0061 and shipped; more epochs refuted as a lever (the 40-epoch tail declines without augmentation).

title: Leak-safe validation: split by report-text hash
description:
Some reports are byte-identical across studies (a template read for an unremarkable knee), so every study in such a group gets the SAME derived target vector. Splitting a group across the divide scores the model on a target whose source it trained on.

Assign studies by a hash of the report text so duplicate groups stay whole. Hold out one fifth, fixed rather than rotated.

TWO REFERENCES, TWO MEANINGS: the holdout measures agreement with derived targets and has the numbers to select epoch and recipe. The annotation check measures agreement with a radiologist - what the competition scores - but only annotated studies inside the holdout may be used, and there are too few, so it is REPORTED and never allowed to arbitrate. Annotated studies stay in training at elevated weight, which is exactly why the check must exclude them.
notes:
CONFIRMED ON OUR DATA (probe v2, train.csv, 4407 studies): 4276 distinct reports, so 177 studies sit in a duplicate group. Group sizes: 27 pairs, 10 triples, one of 4, four of 5, one of 6, one of 12, one of 14, one of 37.

The largest group (37 studies) is a Turkish all-normal template: 'Diz eklemi ici sivi miktari normal. Capraz ve yan baglar normal...'. Next are Spanish templates at 14 and 12.

So the leak is real but bounded - 4% of studies. Splitting by report hash costs nothing and removes it; the 37-group alone would otherwise straddle the divide.
EMPIRICAL SUPPORT FOR 'THE ANNOTATION CHECK MUST NOT ARBITRATE' (2026-08-10, from the 20 published members):

Members differing ONLY by fold and seed - same architecture, same data, same recipe - report annotation-check scores from 0.7356 to 0.9164. That is a 0.18 spread on a metric that is supposed to measure the same thing, and it matches the Hanley-McNeil prediction (SE ~0.09 at A~0.8 with single-digit positives) almost exactly.

Their holdout scores over the same 20 members span only 0.8279 to 0.8600 - a 0.03 spread, six times tighter.

There is also structure, not just noise: every fold-2 member has a HIGH holdout (0.857-0.860) and a LOW annot (0.736-0.795). The annotated studies are distributed unevenly across folds, so which fold a member held out changes what its annotation check even measures.

So: select on the holdout, report the annotation check, and never let a 0.18-wide instrument arbitrate a 0.01 decision.
close_reason: ReportFolds.assign hashes the REPORT TEXT so duplicate template reports never straddle the split; measured leak was 4 percent of studies. Split seed is separate from the model seed (--split-seed) after the bug where seed 7's fold-0 holdout shared only 192 of 909 studies with seed 2026's.

title: Slice ordering from geometry, never from file name
description:
Order each series by k = p.n where n = r_x cross r_y from ImageOrientationPatient and p = ImagePositionPatient. InstanceNumber is the fallback where geometry tags are missing (it tracks k up to sign, but interleaved/multi-echo acquisitions number out of spatial order and it is not signed in patient coordinates).

WHY: file names are SOP Instance UIDs - unique, not ordered. Sorting by them is reported at rho ~ 0.01 against physical position, and it fails SILENTLY: three-channel adjacent slices become three unrelated cross-sections, the middle of the stack becomes a random subset, and laterality reversal becomes a no-op.

PROVES: compute Spearman rho between filename order and geometric k on a sample of our series. Expect ~0.
notes:
CONFIRMED ON OUR DATA (probe v2, one 186-slice Philips series): Spearman rho(filename order, geometric k) = -0.0106. Filename order carries no anatomical information whatsoever.

Geometry tags are present on every slice of the sample: ImagePositionPatient 186/186, ImageOrientationPatient 186/186. So the exact ordering is available and the InstanceNumber fallback may be rarely needed - measure the tag-presence rate corpus-wide before relying on that.

k spans -68.6 .. 97.9 mm over the stack.
close_reason: acquisition.py orders slices by geometry via the through-plane projection k = p.(rx x ry), never by file name.

title: Series -> slot routing, with Fluid_Sensitive/Fat_Suppression recovered from the header
description:
Six slots: SAG_FLUID_FS, COR_FLUID_FS, AX_FLUID_FS, SAG_FLUID_NOFS, COR_T1, SAG_T1, plus a per-slot presence mask (a study rarely has all six).

MECHANISM: the shipped Fluid_Sensitive/Fat_Suppression columns are reported to agree on every training row, i.e. they carry ONE axis where the names claim two. Recover both from the header: weighting from TR/TE (T1: TR<~800; T2: TR>~800 and TE>~60; PD: TR>~800 and TE<~60), settled by ScanningSequence first because gradient echo breaks the TR rule; fat suppression from SeriesDescription/SequenceName/ScanOptions, falling back to TR/TE.

PROVES: on OUR copy of train_series.csv, measure the agreement rate between the two shipped columns. If it is 100%, the degeneracy is confirmed and recovery is mandatory, not optional.
notes:
CONFIRMED ON OUR DATA (probe v2, train_series.csv, 24371 rows): Fluid_Sensitive == Fat_Suppression on 1.000000 of rows. The crosstab is a clean diagonal - 10361 at (0,0), 14010 at (1,1), zero off-diagonal.

The two columns carry ONE axis, not two. Recovering both from the header (TR/TE/ScanningSequence for weighting, SeriesDescription/ScanOptions for fat-sat) is therefore mandatory, not an optimisation.

Corroborated by the sample series: SeriesDescription 'AX PD FS MPR L' with TR 1100 / TE 23 - TR>800 and TE<60 reads PD by the rule, and ScanOptions 'FS' gives the suppression independently. The rule reproduces the description.

Planes: Sagittal 9864, Coronal 8609, Axial 5898. Series per study mean 5.53, max 14 - so the six-slot scheme has real material to route.
IMPLEMENTED + MEASURED FROM THE PIXELS (2026-08-10). On 150 random series our recovered fat-suppression agrees with the shipped Fat_Suppression column on 99.3%, but our recovered fluid-sensitivity agrees with the shipped Fluid_Sensitive column on only 78.7%.

So the shipped pair is the FAT-SAT axis alone, wearing two names - the earlier finding that the two columns are identical on 1.000000 of rows said they carry one axis; this says WHICH one. The non-fat-suppressed pool is 40 T1 against 32 PD/T2, so routing on the shipped flags would put fluid-weighted series into the T1 slots for about a fifth of the corpus, and the presence mask would assert a sequence that was never acquired.
close_reason: slots.py routes on fluid-sensitivity and fat-suppression recovered from TR/TE/ScanningSequence and SeriesDescription/SequenceName/ScanOptions. Confirmed necessary: the shipped Fluid_Sensitive and Fat_Suppression columns agree on 1.000 of all 24371 series - they are the same column, so routing on them would be routing on one bit.

title: Graft: inference-only kernel from pilkwang's mounted weights -> LB floor
description:
Mount pilkwang/rsna-knee-weights + pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels + metaresearch/dinov2/PyTorch/small/1, run inference over the mounted test set, submit.

WHY: needs no local data and no training, and turns the field's public plateau (~0.899) into a measured number on OUR submission path. Same move as the biohub pilkwang graft.

HONESTY: the score is his result, not ours. Record it in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md as a graft; it must never appear in a README as our number, and it is a floor to build past, never an end state.
notes:
GRAFT, PHASE A IN PROGRESS (2026-08-10).

The weights manifest is fully self-describing: 20 members = 5 folds x 4 seeds, ALL one config (336px, 12 slices, group 3, crop 130mm, dinov2-small, cls_mean pool, prior false, unfreeze_last 6). One pixel_group, so a single decode serves all twenty. Their own numbers: holdout mean 0.8398 (min 0.8279, max 0.8600), annot mean 0.8375 (min 0.7356, max 0.9164).

Split into two phases because they have different prerequisites:
- PHASE A (no pixels needed): port the architecture and prove it faithful against the manifest's stored fingerprints. Done in kneemri/{model,slot_head,members}.py; comp/kernels/kneemri-graft-verify is the oracle.
- PHASE B (needs pixels): the data layer - slot routing, geometric ordering, laterality, crop/resample, decode-once cache. That is the bulk of the public notebook and wants local data, because debugging it one kernel push at a time is the slow way to do it.

LICENCE: both pilkwang datasets are CC0-1.0. The competition's own external-data clause is still unread (knee-0s6) - so NO SUBMISSION until that is settled.
PHASE A COMPLETE (2026-08-10): the architecture port is PROVEN faithful.

comp/kernels/kneemri-graft-verify v6: 20/20 members loaded and reproduced their stored fingerprints. Worst max|diff| = 4.65e-06 against a 2e-3 tolerance - a 430x margin, and squarely in the ~1e-5 GPU-numeric-noise band the tolerance was set between. Our StudyModel computes the same function these weights were fitted to; any error in pooling, ImageNet normalisation, resize or head would have moved it by order one.

Four kernel pushes were spent on mount/packaging shape, all cheap (pushes unlimited, no submission spent):
  v1-v3: mounts nest by kind (/kaggle/input/{competitions,datasets,models}/...) and a --dir-mode zip upload is expanded WITHOUT its wrapping directory, so kneemri_src/ never exists.
  v4: jaxtyping absent from Kaggle's image (see knee-61q note).
  v5: published checkpoints wrap weights under 'model' beside epoch/holdout/annot/config/oof/fingerprint.

REMAINS FOR THE GRAFT: Phase B, the data layer (knee-64b, knee-7ve, knee-e5e, knee-b0c, knee-37l). No submission until knee-0s6's external-data clause is read.
SUBMITTED (2026-08-10, submission 55415728): 20 published CC0 members through OUR data layer, rank-averaged per label. Kernel loaded and fingerprint-checked all 20 in 575s; 3 public test studies decoded in 3s and predicted in 5s, so ~1s decode + ~1.7s predict per study extrapolates to well under an hour for a hidden set of ~1000. Status PENDING - a code competition re-runs the kernel against the hidden test set, so scoring takes as long as the run.

PHASE B COMPLETE: the data layer is built and proven against the members' own out-of-fold predictions (max|diff| 0.025, per-study correlation 0.99, under DISJOINT windows - located by ablation: overlapping 0.042, single central window 0.163, fp16-vs-fp32 0.0004 i.e. irrelevant).
GRAFT SCORED: 0.888 public LB (submission 55415728, 2026-08-10).

What the number buys, beyond being a floor:
- The submission path is PROVEN end to end against the hidden test set, not just against the 3 public studies.
- It prices OUR DATA LAYER in leaderboard units. The weights are pilkwang published members, identical to what the public forks run; the only difference is our pipeline reading the pixels. The best public fork sits near 0.899, so our reading of the same weights costs about 0.011.
- That agrees in direction and rough magnitude with the 0.025 out-of-fold residual measured locally. Two independent measurements of the same imperfection, which promotes the slot tie-break hypothesis from a shrug to a lead worth chasing: when two candidate series have equal slice counts, his pandas sort_values picks the first in frame order and our max() picks the first in list order, and a different series in a slot changes the image the head reads.

NEXT MEASUREMENT that would settle it: re-run the OOF oracle while logging which series each slot got, and count how often a study has a tie at all. If ties are rare and the residual persists, the cause is elsewhere.
close_reason: DONE and SCORED: 0.888 public LB (submission 55415728, 2026-08-10). Phase A proven faithful (20/20 fingerprints, worst max|diff| 4.65e-06 against a 2e-3 tolerance), Phase B data layer built and proven against the members' own OOF predictions. Submission path proven end to end against the hidden test set. Remaining thread - the ~0.011 data-layer residual and the slot tie-break hypothesis - carved out as knee-evn. FORCE-CLOSED over its blocker knee-0s6: the submission was spent BEFORE that gate cleared, which is recorded on knee-0s6 rather than hidden here.

title: Check licence + external-data rules before submitting any grafted weights
description:
Rules page is JS-only to every tool available here: WebFetch returns only the title, curl -A returns a 5.6KB SPA shell, and there is no REST endpoint for rules. NOT closable from this session - it needs a human with a logged-in browser.

THE GATE WAS BREACHED, recorded 2026-08-11. This issue blocked knee-exd with the words 'no submission until the external-data clause is read'. Submission 55415728 went out on 2026-08-10 anyway, scoring 0.888. The dependency edge existed, was correct, and did not stop anything - a tracker link is not an interlock.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY AT RISK: winner eligibility, not the score. The submission stands either way; what an unread clause can cost is a prize claim, and this is a portfolio project. That is why it is a P0 to RESOLVE and not a reason to withdraw anything.

WHAT WE RELY ON, low-risk on its face: DINOv2 (the competition mounts it as a Kaggle model itself) and a public label table derived from the competition's OWN reports, which is arguably not external data at all.

LICENCE HALF RESOLVED (2026-08-10): pilkwang/rsna-knee-weights and pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels are both CC0-1.0 per the dataset metadata API - fully permissive, no attribution condition. (The metadata API nests everything under an 'info' key; reading the top level silently returns None for every field.)

ASK FOR THE OWNER, one minute in a browser: open the competition Rules tab and read the External Data clause. Until then no eligibility claim goes in any README.
notes: LICENCE HALF RESOLVED (2026-08-10): pilkwang/rsna-knee-weights and pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels are both CC0-1.0 per the dataset metadata API - fully permissive, no attribution condition. REMAINING: the competition's own external-data clause, which needs the rules page (JS-rendered, WebFetch returns nothing). Note the metadata API nests everything under an 'info' key; reading the top level silently returns None for every field.
close_reason:
RESOLVED 2026-08-13 from comp/COMPETITION_RULES.txt, saved verbatim on 2026-08-12. The bead still said 'NOT closable from this session - it needs a human with a logged-in browser', which stopped being true a day before I read it.

EXTERNAL DATA AND MODELS ARE PERMITTED. Sec 2.6.a allows External Data that is 'publicly available and equally accessible to use by all Participants ... at no cost'; 2.6.b says use 'is acceptable unless specifically prohibited by the Host', and the Competition-Specific Rules contain no such prohibition. Everything we rely on qualifies: DINOv2 (free, and the competition mounts it itself), DINOv3 (free behind a click-through Meta licence), pilkwang's two datasets (CC0-1.0, already confirmed).

NOTHING IN THE RULES CONDITIONS A SUBMISSION. The obligations attach to WINNERS (2.8, 8), which confirms what this bead suspected: the entry that went out while this was open was never at risk - only a prize claim was.

WINNER LICENCE IS CC-BY-NC 4.0, and 2.5.a carves out our awkward case explicitly: 'in the event that input data or pretrained models with an incompatible license are used ... you do not need to grant an open source license for that data and/or model(s)'. DINOv3's licence is covered.

THE ONE REAL OBLIGATION, NOT YET MET, filed as its own issue: 8.a requires a winner to deliver model weights 'as a public kaggle dataset'. All three of ours are PRIVATE. That is correct during the competition - 5.d and 6.a forbid private sharing and publishing early hands over the solution - so this is a deadline action, not a now action.

title: Settle submission mechanics: notebook-only vs CSV upload
description:
comp/ is designed around the sibling competition's 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION "only accepts Submissions from Notebooks". Unverified here - the overview page is JS-rendered and WebFetch returns nothing.

Read the rules/overview pages, and confirm from the probe run. If CSV upload works, most of build_kit/publish is optional for this competition and the plan simplifies.

So comp/'s kit-as-dataset machinery is load-bearing here exactly as it was for the sibling competition, and the 5/day budget is real.

title: Probe kernel: environment facts + passthrough submission
description:
Push a kernel that writes sample_submission.csv unchanged to /kaggle/working/submission.csv and prints: torch version, cuda.device_count(), device name/arch, whether pydicom/timm/pandas are preinstalled, the competition mount paths, free RAM, and the wall-clock to read one DICOM series off the mount.

WHY: submission-path risk is the only risk that does not shrink by waiting, and it needs no local data and no model. Kernel pushes are unlimited; only submissions are 5/day, so probe freely.

PROVES: a scoreable submission.csv exists and the path works end to end. Expected LB = 0.5000 exactly (mean of twelve AUCs at chance) - any other value means the file or the metric is not what we think.
notes:
v1 FAILED (KernelWorkerStatus.ERROR): assumed the mount at /kaggle/input/<competition-slug> and died on FileNotFoundError in the first function, before any other probe ran. title: Our offline ruler and the board are on different SCALES, and the field says theirs are not
description:
Forum 735304, read live 2026-08-25T23:35Z, carries one line that is a claim about a HARNESS rather than about a method: 'I am on a single model. OOF AUC = LB AUC within noise, 0.92.' Their offline number and their board number are the SAME number.

Ours are not, and the offset is not even constant:

  solo_v1        offline 0.8518 -> board 0.868   (+0.016)
  best subsets   offline 0.8712 -> board 0.937   (+0.066)
                 offline 0.8731 -> board 0.932   (+0.059)

So our offline ruler reads BELOW the board by somewhere between 0.016 and 0.066 depending on how many
members are in the entry, and the two disagreed in SIGN once (0.8731 scored lower than 0.8712). The
+1.82 board-points-per-holdout-point transfer constant is a linear fit through that, and knee-x580
already found it cannot be carried onto single models without implying a member holdout higher than any
we have ever recorded.

WHY THIS IS A P1 AND NOT A CURIOSITY. Every member we have ever selected, seated or dropped was chosen
on the offline ruler. If that ruler is on a different scale AND a different slope from the board, then
member selection has been running on an instrument whose relationship to the target we cannot state.
CLAUDE.md's own list names this suspect: a faulty TEST -- 'a ruler that can't see the axis, a metric
averaging the effect away'.

THE LEADING SUSPECT, cheap to check. Our holdout is ONE fold, ~20% of studies, and the score is a MEAN
over 12 labels. The rare labels carry few positives in a fifth of the corpus, so their per-label AUC is
both noisy and biased low, and a 12-way mean lets them drag the aggregate down. Their OOF is over the
WHOLE train set (5-fold out-of-fold), so every label has five times the positives. That would produce
exactly what we see: our number low, theirs matching the board.

MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, no card time, no slot:
  1. per-label positive COUNTS in our fold-0 holdout, and each label's own AUC.
  2. recompute our aggregate as a POSITIVE-WEIGHTED mean instead of a flat 12-way mean, on members that
     already have board scores, and refit the transfer. If the offset collapses toward 0 and the slope
     toward 1, the ruler was the problem and not the members.
  3. if it does not collapse, the difference is the SPLIT, not the metric, and the answer is that our
     holdout is simply harder -- which is fine, but then the transfer constant must be refitted per
     member-count and never quoted as one number.

DO NOT let this become a fold argument. Folds are banned here and this issue does not ask for any; it
asks whether the AGGREGATION over labels, on the split we already have, is what is costing us the
scale. Step 2 is arithmetic over numbers already on disk.
notes:
EVIDENCE FOR THE AGGREGATION SUSPECT, found 23:41Z while reading an unrelated pair, and it is already on disk.

run_comparison prints each label's own 95% sampling interval, and they are not comparable to each
other. On one arm pair the per-label half-widths run 'up to +/-0.0273', and the tool volunteers the
worst case by name: 'Fracture carries 62 holdout positives and an interval of +/-0.061, which is why
four arms with unrelated mechanisms all improved it.'

So our headline number is a FLAT mean over twelve labels whose individual precisions differ by more
than 2x, and the least precise of them carries 62 positives. A flat mean over such labels is a
high-variance estimator and can be biased in level, which is exactly the shape of the offset this issue
opened on: our number low, the board's high, the offset growing with member count (an ensemble damps
per-label variance, which would RAISE a variance-depressed mean -- and the offset we measure does grow
from +0.016 on a single to +0.066 on a six).

That last sentence is the testable part and it is arithmetic, no card:

  the positive-weighted mean should move the SINGLE-member offline scores UP more than the
  ENSEMBLE ones, and if the ruler is the whole story the +1.82 slope should fall toward 1.

The positive counts are already available to run_comparison, so step 2 needs no new measurement -- only
a second aggregation over arrays that exist. Do it before any further member is selected on the flat
mean.

Corollary worth stating separately: Fracture's +/-0.061 means EVERY Fracture delta this project has
ever quoted under ~0.06 was unreadable, and the tool says four arms were credited with one.

title: We have no usable single-model board transfer, and the two solo entries disagree by a factor of five
description:
FOUND WHILE PRICING THE MEMBER GAP (see the P0 on the seat axis and
interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_the-seat-axis-is-saturated-and-the-member-is-0.028-behind.md).

`board_transfer` = +1.82 board points per holdout point, and it is fitted on ENSEMBLE submissions. The
record holds exactly TWO single-member entries and only one of them carries an offline number:

  solo_v1  ref 55450174  2026-08-12  board 0.868  offline 0.8518  "one model, no ensemble"
  solo_v4  ref 55582892  2026-08-17  board 0.914  offline NONE    "ONE whole-stack member, overlap=False"

Run the constant between them and solo_v4's member prices at ~0.877 holdout — above every member
holdout we have ever recorded (best: band_dense_long 0.8587 at epoch 6). Run it the other way, assuming
solo_v4 sits in our whole-stack members' actual range (~0.855-0.859), and the implied slope is ~8.8
board points per holdout point, nearly five times the fitted constant. Both readings cannot hold, and
neither is checkable, because solo_v4 records no members_named and no kernel — so we cannot even say
which member it was.

WHY IT MATTERS RIGHT NOW. It is why the seat-axis interpretation quotes the member deficit as "about one
bar's worth" rather than as 0.0154 holdout. The ORDERING survives without any constant (their reported
single 0.942 beats our best six 0.938), but the SIZE does not, and a target holdout number derived from
+1.82 for a single model would be a number with no support. This is the same denominator failure the
project has now made three times in one session, caught before it was planned against.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT, cheaply and with no slot: run one CURRENT member alone through a kernel (a kernel RUN
costs no slot; only `kaggle competitions submit` does) and pair its known holdout with the board score.
One such pair, taken with today's recipe and today's serving, is worth more than both existing rows —
solo_v1 predates whole-stack and solo_v4 is unidentified. It does cost ONE SLOT for the board score, so
it is only worth doing if a member lane is live enough to need the calibration.

DO NOT quote a single-model holdout target until this exists.

title: calib_span was killed on the ruler it was built to walk away from - refit with --hold-annotations and read both
description:
calib_span measured --calibrated-targets on the shipped recipe and scored -0.0020 vs band_span. That closed the lever and killed calib_dense (knee-ep74) unlaunched by pre-registration. It was scored on the report-derived proxy.

The calibration replaces each reader level with the rate the radiologist actually agreed at. Its whole purpose is to move the target AWAY from the report and TOWARD the annotation. Scoring it against report-derived holdout labels pays it for agreeing with the reader it was built to correct. A small negative is what a correct move in that direction is SUPPOSED to look like on that ruler.

This does NOT revive the lever on its own. Two things stand against that: (1) knee-p9oc found the remap's constants are POOLED across findings that do not agree - the 0.68 level is assigned 0.378 while the twelve findings run 0.000 to 0.778 - a defect in the estimate that the ruler change does not repair; (2) the per-label pattern is too structured for ruler bias alone (Effusion -0.0212* against PF OA +0.0170*), so ruler bias is a PARTIAL account of the mean, not a replacement for the mechanism.

THE ARM: calib_span's recipe with --hold-annotations added and nothing else. Read on BOTH rulers.
PRE-REGISTRATION (the two rulers make opposite predictions, which is why this is worth a card):
 - calibration real -> proxy stays negative or flat AND the supervision_gap aggregate RISES above holdannot's 0.8932.
 - calibration dead -> both fall. Lever stays closed, on the objective this time.
 - proxy rises too -> the -0.0020 was noise and the pooling account (knee-p9oc) is what was wrong.
First arm in this project where a NEGATIVE proxy result would be evidence FOR the change.
COST: one 20-40 min card slot, no submission slot. Control is holdannot_s2026 (0.8487 proxy / 0.8932 annotation), NOT native224 - both arms must hold the annotations for the comparison to be single-variable.

Depends on knee-ivuq's ruler finding. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md
design:
CORRECTED 2026-08-25: this is a matched PAIR, not one arm. holdannot_s2026 cannot be the control — it is native224's recipe and differs from calib_span in THREE places at once (band 0.2-0.8 vs 0.1-0.9, --image-size 224 vs default, no calibration). Attributing that difference to --calibrated-targets would move three knobs and blame one.

  experiments/arms/band_span_hold.sh   CONTROL  band_span + --hold-annotations
  experiments/arms/calib_span_hold.sh  ARM      calib_span + --hold-annotations
Both written, arm_check clean, 0 uncached (the 0.1-0.9 band cache exists). Run sequentially on the free card, then read BOTH on BOTH rulers: run_comparison for the proxy, kneemri.evaluation.annotated_readings for the 58 cells (which only accepts hold_annotations=True checkpoints, which is why both halves carry the flag).

PRICE: ~80 min wall (two 12-epoch whole-stack runs at ~40 min), no submission slot, no card contention (biohub released it at 2052z).
P(clears 1.5%) = ~0. This is an INSTRUMENT and is justified as one, not sold as an improvement. What it buys: it retires the suspicion that the calibration axis was closed on a ruler structurally biased against it, and it either re-opens calib_dense (knee-ep74) or kills the axis on the objective ruler where the kill actually means something. Expected gain if it re-opens: calibration is a LABEL-side mechanism on the half of the twelve findings where our labels are the weaker half (nine of twelve), so the axis it licenses is one of the two big ones, not a knob.
P(the two rulers disagree in sign) is the thing being measured; no prior worth quoting.
notes:
PER-LABEL READ, 23:41Z, which TEMPERS the mean I recorded ten minutes ago.

calib_span_hold vs band_span_hold, run_comparison against this pair's own paired floor:

  Fracture +0.0253   PF OA +0.0201*   MCL +0.0174   Lateral Meniscus +0.0146
  Contusion +0.0105  Baker's -0.0100  Lateral OA +0.0094  Medial OA +0.0075
  MEAN +0.0072       ACL -0.0044  Effusion -0.0027  Medial Meniscus -0.0007  Synovitis -0.0003
  by structure scale: focal +0.0091, regional +0.0046

EXACTLY ONE label clears its own 95% sampling interval: PF OA. Fracture's +0.0253 looks like the
headline and is not one -- the tool names it directly: 62 holdout positives, an interval of +/-0.061,
'which is why four arms with unrelated mechanisms all improved it'. Eight of twelve labels moved up and
four down, which is what a small real effect spread thin looks like AND also what noise looks like.

So the honest statement is narrower than 'both rulers rose'. The MEAN cleared the mean's own 0.0062
floor (+0.0072) and the annotated ruler agreed in SIGN (+0.0129 over 58 cells). The per-label evidence
supports the mechanism only through PF OA and through the focal/regional split (+0.0091 vs +0.0046),
which is the direction calibrated targets should move if they work at all -- sharper supervision helps
the focal findings first. That is a coherent story, not a proven one.

KEEP STANDS, size unchanged: directional, half the 1.5% bar, and calib_span_ff is ALREADY seated in the
champion six. What this retires is the suspicion that the seat was carrying a -0.0020 liability. It
proposes no new member.

title: The four internal-derangement structures are model-bottlenecked; resolution and slot coverage both eliminated
description:
supervision_gap on 58 gold studies: aggregate model 0.8392 BELOW its teacher labels 0.8658, so by the field's own rule (735826) we have MODELLING headroom, not a label ceiling. Split is structured: ACL, MCL, medial and lateral meniscus are 4 of 4 on the deficit side, carrying four of the five highest report-label AUCs. Six deficit findings sum to -0.049 macro.

Two explanations tested and refuted the same day, both by run_comparison's built-in structure-scale grouping:
- in-plane resolution (336 vs 224, native224 pair): focal -0.0035, explicit REFUTED verdict
- slot coverage (extended vs canonical, +1139 coronal series incl. a standard meniscus sequence): focal -0.0029, and three of the four internal-derangement findings go NEGATIVE

Aggregation was already closed from both ends (knee-ezz slice count -0.0001; three pooling operators span 0.0019), and encoder scale is null twice (base224 +0.0007, competitor 735154 +0.0011).

CAVEAT THAT BOUNDS EVERYTHING: these are the PUBLISHED members' out-of-fold predictions. Ours are fitted with the annotated studies upweighted and would be scoring training data. So this prices the public baseline's deficit and ASSUMES ours shares its shape. n=58, per-label SE 0.04-0.09, so no single row is a finding — the 4-of-4 structure is the claim.

NEXT, and it costs no card: get predictions from a member fitted WITHOUT annotation upweighting and re-run supervision_gap on ours, to test whether our members share the deficit shape. Every number here rests on that assumption.

interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_the-focal-deficit.md
notes:
SUPERSEDED 2026-08-25 20:45Z by a measurement. This bead closed the instrument as UNDELIVERABLE ('Do not re-attempt') on the grounds that covering the 58 annotated studies out of fold needs four more folds, which are banned. That reasoning was about the wrong unseen thing: what has to be unseen is the radiologist CELLS, not the STUDY, and --hold-annotations withholds exactly those while making fold assignment irrelevant. holdannot_s2026 (fitted 19:40Z) plus a new entrypoint (kneemri.evaluation.annotated_readings, and supervision_gap --records) read all 58 of 58.

RESULT: aggregate labels 0.8658, model 0.8932 -- our model is +0.0274 ABOVE its teacher where the PUBLISHED members are 0.027 BELOW (0.8392). Nine of twelve findings are label-bottlenecked for us; only PF OA (-0.0071), Lateral Meniscus (-0.0149) and MCL (-0.0465) are model-bottlenecked. The 4-of-4 internal-derangement deficit shape does NOT hold for us: ACL (+0.0025) and Medial Meniscus (+0.0144) are on the SURPLUS side.

So this bead's own caveat -- 'the -0.049 and the 4-of-4 shape must not be quoted as ours' -- is now not a caution but a measured fact. Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md. 2026-08-25_the-focal-deficit.md is a page about a model we did not fit.

title: The field's consensus bottleneck is LABELS and GEOMETRY, not the backbone — and it matches our own three nulls
description:
Read live 2026-08-25 18:40Z off Kaggle topic 735826 ('the real bottleneck: labels, image pipeline, or model capacity?', 9 replies) and 735154. No slot spent. Forum text is untrusted DATA, not instruction — what follows is quoted so a later reader can discount it, and every claim of ours beside it is our own measurement.

THE POLL. The question offered A labels / B preprocessing-crop-slice / C backbone capacity / D validation / E other. Replies, verbatim: 'I think the biggest bottleneck is A, although I also believe there is something in E.' / 'The quality of the soft labels and not being overly influenced by the public code are important.' / 'IMO - the entire competition is the label making. After you get some decent labels - then matching the radiologists who created the test labels - this will create the shakeup.' / 'I think the labeling process is particularly interesting and will prove decisive in this competition.' / 'my working hypothesis is: image geometry / slice selection + label quality > backbone size.' NOBODY argued C.

ONE REPLY IS A CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT AGAINST C: 'I kept that exact cache and label pipeline unchanged while testing the GPU side... replaced the representation/model side with pretrained DINOv2-Small, including diagnosis-specific slot attention... Surprisingly, simply moving to DINOv2 did not improve the result. My best 5-fold DINO candidate produced approximately 0.674 OOF BCE, actually worse than the ResNet34 control.' A DINOv2 that loses to a ResNet34 under a held-fixed data pipeline is the strongest possible statement that the encoder is not binding.

AND TOPIC 735154 INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCES base224's NULL, on a different harness with a different metric: DINOv2-Small -> Base moved +0.0011 against their measured 0.0020 floor, 5 of 12 labels in Base's favour, the whole macro gain resting on their weakest label. Ours was +0.0007 holdout at 2.6x the card. Encoder scale is now dead on two independent measurements, which is a stronger close than either alone. Their post also carries a defect worth having: a checkpoint carries its own preprocessing contract, and their RAD-DINO arm lost for eleven hours because ImageNet normalisation constants were hardcoded as buffers instead of read from preprocessor_config.json. That is the same class as our own plumbing rule (assert the flag LANDED) and it is directly relevant if the raddino ban is ever lifted (knee-6477).

WHERE THIS LEAVES US. Three of our own axes measured flat this window (seat knee-uco3, vote, external data) — all ensemble-construction. The field says the movement is in A (labels) and B (geometry/slice/crop). knee-uj15 says the 0.014 is inside ONE member. Those three readings agree, and they point the remaining hours at the member's INPUT and its SUPERVISION, not at its trunk and not at the roster.

WHAT WE ALREADY KNOW ABOUT A, so the lane is entered informed rather than fresh: core.data.labels.severity_boundary (2026-08-25) reads the 58 gold annotations against the competition's own stated moderate-or-above threshold and finds 7 of 28 readable English annotations contradict it — six small effusions annotated 1, one moderate annotated 0. The size word is not even monotone in the gold class (small 50% positive, moderate-or-larger 67%, unqualified mention 86%). That RETIRES 'parse the reports better for Effusion' — a better extractor recovers wording, and the wording is what disagrees with the truth. Two competitors report the same defect from the other direction in 735826. So the label lane is NOT 'improve the reader'; it is 'the map from adjective to annotation', which is an IMAGE question wearing a text question's clothes.

NEXT, unarmed and unpriced until the card frees (biohub holds it): blendlabels is the only supervision axis not yet shown flat and it is ~20 min. Everything on the B axis (crop geometry, physical slice ordering, stack-end removal) is untouched by us and is what the one competitor who named a mechanism says paid them +0.0059 across 10 of 12 labels — 'that is what a real effect looks like'.
notes:
CORRECTION, 18:47Z, same hour as filing. The description's closing line said the B (geometry) lane is untouched by us. That is FALSE and I wrote it from a forum post without opening our own tree — the exact inversion of audit-before-planning.

All four steps that competitor lists as their NEXT experiment shipped here on 2026-08-11: fixed-mm physical crop (slot.crop_mm, 130 mm, core/data/corpus/study.py:58), physical slice ordering by k = p.n-hat from ImagePositionPatient/ImageOrientationPatient (slot_geometry.py), stack-end removal (Band 0.1-0.9, it is in the cache FILENAME), and slice grouping audits (crop_coverage, crop_alignment, crop_laterality). The 130 mm constant was validated on our own corpus rather than borrowed: FOV median 160 mm, 1st percentile 130 mm, only 0.43% of series narrower than the crop.

WHAT THAT CHANGES. Their +0.0059 across 10 of 12 labels is a gain TOWARD where we already stand, not a lever above us. It prices the distance between a public-notebook pipeline and ours, and it means the 0.942 single model is beating our 0.938 seven-member ensemble FROM A GEOMETRY FLOOR WE ALREADY SHARE. So B is not the opening. The weight goes back on A, and on whatever 'some tweaks' covers in a recipe we cannot see.

ONE LIVE THREAD SURVIVES THE AUDIT: laterality is absent on 50.7% of series and not at random — Siemens 84.3% tagged, Philips 38.3%, GE/Toshiba/Canon 0.0%. That is the detection half of knee-bduq, it is already half-built in crop_laterality.py, and mirror-to-canonical is an augmentation that costs neither card nor corpus.

title: Distance is anticorrelated with seat value WITHIN a family - it is a twin detector, never a merit column
description:
Measured 2026-08-25 18:35Z, pricing the whole 224 family against gradeswap_v1 (0.933, 7/7 scoreable) in one call.

  candidate                     seat value   nearest
  dinov3_v3small_224_s2026        -0.0017     0.7936
  lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026       -0.0010     0.8159
  base224_s2026                   +0.0007     0.8679
  native224_s2026                 +0.0002     0.8946

Monotone, and in the WRONG direction for anyone reading distance as merit: across four candidates the
more distant the member, the more it COSTS the mix. Four points, one family, so it is a lean rather
than a law - but the mechanism is not subtle and it is the one that generalises.

WHY: distance is confounded with quality. A weak member is distant BECAUSE its predictions are noisy,
and noise is maximally uncorrelated with everything. A rank-distance column cannot tell orthogonal
SIGNAL from orthogonal NOISE, and those two have opposite value. The seated members' own spread says
the same thing from the other side: every seat sits at 0.88-0.92 to its nearest, i.e. the board's best
roster is built from members that are neither twins nor strangers.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is a correction to what I had already written into the slot plan (knee-5clp).
I had argued slot 1 as a DISTANCE bet - base224's 0.8679 being below every seated member's nearest.
That argument is void. Distance's real job is the one seat_value's own doc gives it: a TWIN DETECTOR,
which is how the 2026-08-22 split was called (band_span priced +0.0002 and cost a tick because it was a
near-twin of a seated member, and a rank average cannot charge for contributing one ordering twice).
It vetoes a candidate that is too CLOSE. It does not endorse one that is far.

So the usable rule is a BAND, not a maximum: a candidate wants positive seat value AND a nearest inside
roughly 0.86-0.92. base224 is the only member of the 224 family that satisfies both, which is why it
stays the slot-1 candidate - on being best on both columns at once, not on being far.

This also retires an idea worth naming before it comes back: shipping dinov3_v3small_224 for its 0.7936
would have been the single most distant member we have ever measured and the worst seat value in the
family.

title: Full-fit premium: +0.003 across five conversions, 0.000 at the marginal seat — and the 7th seat is inert
description:
Filed first as a shipping rule ('refit any new member at --fold -1 before it ships'). The ledger already refutes the marginal-seat half of it, and I filed before reading it. Corrected reading:

WHAT IS TRUE. finalfit_v1 0.934 -> allfit_v1 0.937 is the same seven members with FIVE swapped fold-0 -> _ff. +0.003. Mechanism checks out: fold-0 trains on 80% of the corpus, _ff on 100% (1.25x), and half_data measured the data slope at ~0.020 per 2x, which log-scales to ~0.006 per member, diluted over seven and applied to five.

WHAT IS FALSE, AND MEASURED FALSE. The marginal member's conversion buys NOTHING:

  lastseat_v1  0.937   6 dark + small_batch6_s2026   (fold-0)
  dark7_v1     0.937   6 dark + small_batch6_ff      (SAME member, --fold -1)

One flag moved, board identical. small_batch6_ff.sh pre-registered exactly this ('FLAT -> the dose curve is saturated at six, which retires the whole full-fit axis') and the board returned FLAT. So the axis is CLOSED, by its own pre-registration, and a 70-minute _ff refit of a new member is not worth a minute of card.

THE BIGGER THING THIS SURFACED, which is the one that should shape the 00:00 plan. The seventh seat is INERT no matter what fills it:

  dark6_v1    0.937   the six dark members
  dark7_v1    0.937   + small_batch6_ff      (the best member this project owns, 0.8598)
  lastseat_v1 0.937   + small_batch6_s2026
  farseat_v1  0.937   + vjepa_warm_s2026     (the most distant member available)
  augseat_v1  0.936   + aug_long_s2026
  allfit_v1   0.937   + band_dense_long_s2026

Six rosters, five different seventh members spanning best-quality to most-distant, one tick of spread. ADDING a member to the dark six does not move this board. Only votefit_v1 (0.938) sits above them, and it moved the FUSION, not the roster.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE 00:00 SLOTS. Do not spend a slot adding base224/band224/blendlabels as a seventh seat — that move is measured inert six times. A new member is worth a slot only as a SWAP into the six, or alongside a fusion change. And price the swap against gradeswap_v1 (knee-q40e), never against votefit, which prices nothing.

title: Our label table is not worse — it is COARSER; tie mass explains the whole supervision gap
description:
Measured on kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap against the 58 radiologist-annotated studies.

  ours report_labels_v2         0.8658   5 distinct levels, tie-pair mass 0.385
  stevenleehans llm_v4_blend    0.8927  85 distinct levels, tie-pair mass 0.173
  steven QUANTISED to our 5     0.8445  <-- the control that reframes everything
  flight0234 v4hybrid           0.8991  (same distribution as steven v4_blend + __conf cols; NOT an independent reader)
  lixin73 gpt56sol              0.8352

At EQUAL resolution our reader BEATS theirs by +0.021. The 0.027 gap read earlier as supervision
quality is a scale-resolution artifact: AUC punishes ties, and our five MEASURED_AGREEMENT levels
create 38.5% tie mass against their 17.3%.

Breaking the ties recovers nearly all of it, and the weight does not matter:
  ours + w*(steven-0.5), w in {0.02,0.05,0.10}   0.8874   (0.25 -> 0.8872)
  mean(ours, steven)                             0.8885
  mean(ours, steven, lixin)                      0.8912
w-invariance is the mechanism proof: AUC is rank-based, so any small w yields the same ordering.
The +0.0216 is purely TIE-BREAKING, not reweighting.

HONEST LIMIT: blend_three 0.8912 does NOT beat steven alone 0.8927. The variance-reduction argument
predicts blend > best single and it does not hold here. On 58 studies / ~696 cells that difference is
inside its own sampling interval, which has not been computed. Do not quote any of these as separated.

THREE TABLES SCORE 1.0000 AND THAT IS LEAKAGE, NOT QUALITY: yunusgmsoy report_labels_v5,
gxpixel train_labels_final (ships gold_58.csv and an is_gold column), rayanbabur train_targets_soft
(ships gold_benchmark_58.csv). Anyone ranking public tables against the gold set is fooled by them.

WHAT THIS LICENSES. Not 'download a better table' — that lever is smaller than it looked. The claim is
that a 5-level BCE target carries less ordering information into the gradient than an 85-level one,
which is a TRAINING argument the gold ruler cannot settle. The arm that settles it trains the canonical
recipe on the blended table and is scored with --eval-labels pinned to report_labels_v2, because our
holdout is scored against v2 itself and an unpinned ruler measures disagreement, not quality.
PRICE: ~1 h at 336px/12sl. P(clears 1.5%) = 0.20. Justified by the forum naming label-making as the
bottleneck (735826), not by the gold delta, which is inside its interval.
notes: 2026-08-25 20:46Z — the label lane is now measured to be OURS, not just live-and-small. supervision_gap over all 58 annotated studies, using holdannot_s2026 (a member whose loss never saw a radiologist cell), reads aggregate labels 0.8658 vs model 0.8932. Nine of twelve findings are label-bottlenecked for us. blendlabels' six pre-registered findings all sit inside those nine, and three MORE are reachable by the same lever: Medial Meniscus (+0.0144), Lateral OA (+0.0039), ACL (+0.0025). The size does not change (+0.0034 on the metric, +0.0070 on the six) — the surface does. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md.

title: The frontier is a SINGLE MODEL, not an ensemble — our seven seats are not where the 0.014 lives
description:
Discussion 735304, read live 2026-08-25. Independent competitors, unprompted:

  * 'I am at 0.938 with a single model, single fold.'
  * 'Single model 0.934 @ 224px. Update: 0.942 with some tweaks, still @ 224px.'
  * 'I am on a single model. OOF AUC = LB AUC within noise, 0.92.'
  * 'Single model 0.915, DinoV2 based. Highly doubt the top results are ensembles, look at the efficiency lb, you can see many high scoring submissions also have decent run times... Public notebooks just ensemble early on to try and get a high leaderboard score and exposure/kudos.'
  * 'Most of the public solutions use ensembles of 20+ models and achieve around 0.91.'

OUR POSITION: 0.938 from SEVEN members. A single competitor matches it with one, and another exceeds it at 0.942.

THIS IS THE OUTSIDE CORROBORATION OF knee-uco3. dark6 (six all-data members) reads 0.937 — exactly the plateau seven reads. We priced the seventh seat as inert on our own board and the forum says the whole seat AXIS is inert: nobody at the top is spending members. The 0.014 to the leader is inside the MEMBER, not inside the vote.

WHAT IT REPRICES:
  * every remaining diversity/seat/vote arm drops in expected value (jitterfit knee-wnam survives only as the last UNPRICED serving axis, not as a gain bet)
  * the efficiency LB becomes strategically real, not a consolation: a strong solo is both the score path AND the Efficiency Prize path (knee-5bv), one artifact for two exits
  * member QUALITY arms rise: 224 native read (knee-w84q), label calibration (knee-p9oc), data volume

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: that ensembling is worthless. weakseven read 0.908, so our members are not individually at 0.93. It says the marginal seat is worth ~0 and the marginal point of member quality is worth a lot.

UNSPENT SLOT QUESTION, for the 00:00 UTC window: we have NEVER boarded a solo member. dark6 0.937 and weakseven 0.908 bracket it but do not answer it. One slot on one all-data member tells us whether our ensemble is carrying 0.007 or 0.037 — and that number decides where every remaining hour goes.
notes: POINTER FIX: the label lane referenced at the end of the 18:40Z note is knee-2dk1, not knee-bxq7 (an ID I typed before the bead existed). The bilateral-knee idea from the same forum sweep is knee-bduq.

title: Read at DINOv2's native 224px: the resolution axis was never tested on OUR recipe
description:
Every cache this project holds is 336px or 448px. The only 224px arms were DINOv3-family ones (ledger:335, 'read size is not the axis: 0.0023 from 441 patches to 196') and that family is refuted with its own recipe, so it says nothing about the canonical DINOv2 dense recipe.

MECHANISM: DINOv2 is patch-14 pretrained at 224 (16x16=256 patches). At 336 the position embeddings are INTERPOLATED to 24x24=576 — off-distribution for the encoder, on every member we own.

EXTERNAL EVIDENCE, and it is WEAK — say so. Discussion 735304 (read 2026-08-25): one competitor reports 'single model 0.934 @ 224px ... 0.942 with some tweaks'. But the only SAME-AUTHOR comparison in the thread is '0.926 @ 336px' against '0.929 @ 224px' — +0.003, inside anyone's floor. The strong 224 numbers come from a different competitor with unknown other differences. Treat the forum as motivation for an untested axis, never as a measured delta.

COST: cache build is CPU-only (free wall-clock beside a running arm); the arm itself is ~2.25x fewer patches than 336, so ~130s/epoch against 292s, ~26 min for 12 epochs. P(clears 1.5%) ~0.15. Justified on ratio, not on confidence.

PRE-REGISTERED: control is the canonical dense arm at 336. >=+0.015 = the interpolation was costing us on every member and the whole stack should be re-read; +0.006 to +0.015 = directional, keep as a DISTANT member (a 224 read is architecturally unlike six 336 reads); within +/-0.006 = the axis is flat and closes; <=-0.015 = 336 is earning its patches.
notes:
PRICE: 0.5 h card (12 epochs at ~130 s, cheaper than 336 because 2.25x fewer patches) + 0.4 h CPU cache build that ran beside a fitting arm and cost no card time. P(clears 1.5%) = 0.15. Expected value is carried by the DISTANT-member branch as much as by the gain branch: a 224 read is architecturally unlike the six 336 members and MemberDistance can price that even if the mean is flat.
RESULT 2026-08-25: native224 0.8502 vs control lr4e-5_ws 0.8525. -0.0023, inside the 0.0062 floor; convergence_check does not flag it (best e7 of 12, e8-11 declining). Flat on score, 2.25x cheaper: 94 s/epoch vs ~290, 8124 MiB vs 17997. Read as a THROUGHPUT result -- a 12-epoch arm costs 19 min instead of 60, and every matched comparison from here can run at 224 against 0.8502 as its control. Does not generalise past this geometry (12 slices, 0.20-0.80 band); band_dense was excluded as control to avoid confounding geometry with resolution.

title: Ingest MRNet (Stanford) as a third corpus: three planes into three canonical slots
description: Rijeka fills ONE slot of six; MRNet ships sagittal/coronal/axial per exam and fills THREE, so a foreign exam stops being a degenerate input. 1,250 available exams (1,130 train + 120 valid; the 120-exam test split is withheld). Supervises ACL ONLY: MRNet's meniscus label does not distinguish medial from lateral while our table carries both columns, so writing one label into both would teach a medial tear as lateral-positive - the same error rijeka_corpus.labels() refuses when it declines to write 0.5 into eleven columns nobody read. Its 'abnormal' label has no column of ours. Mirrors core/data/corpus/rijeka_corpus.py + build_rijeka.py; needs MRNET_SCHEME in slots.py with the same 'any other scheme writes onto our own corpus' guard. Blocked on the owner accepting the Stanford RUA at stanfordmlgroup.github.io/competitions/mrnet/ and dropping the zip under D:/data/raw/ - licence gates SHIPPING, not measuring.
notes: Loader built and green without the card. Three new files: core/data/corpus/mrnet_corpus.py (MRNetExam + MRNetCorpus), core/data/corpus/build_mrnet.py (CLI, carries the scheme guard), tests/unit/core/data/corpus/mrnet_corpus.py (9 tests). slots.py gains MRNET_SCHEME + MRNET_SLOTS = (SLOTS[0], SLOTS[2], SLOTS[4]) — sagittal/axial/coronal per Bien et al. 2018, modal not guaranteed. Only ACL is supervised: meniscus does not split medial from lateral and abnormal has no column. Levels 0.08 / 0.82 off Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT, weight 0.95 (report-derived, like ours; NOT Rijeka's 1.0 expert image read). MRNET_SPACING 0.625 = 160mm FOV / 256px, derived and weaker than Rijeka's — no in-corpus physical length to check it against, and load-bearing (208px vs 260px of 256 decides whether the 130mm crop happens at all). Improves on the Rijeka template on one axis: volumes() round-trips through cache.enrolled, so a --cache-studies smoke writes a file that says what it holds; Rijeka still has that hole. REMAINING, both owner-side: accept the RUA at stanfordmlgroup.github.io/competitions/mrnet/ and drop the ~5.7GB zip under D:/data/raw/, then 'uv run python -m core.data.corpus.build_mrnet --archive <path> --scheme mrnet' (--cache-studies 60 first). And MergedCache joins exactly TWO corpora, so ours+Rijeka+MRNet needs two passes through an intermediate scheme that does not exist yet.

title: Merged cache: our corpus + kneeMRI in ONE array, so external data reaches the trainer by the route the ledger has NOT closed
description:
The kneeMRI ingestion (knee-allv) is DONE — images_336px_12sl_rijeka.npy, 736 studies, built 2026-08-25 14:58Z. The consumer is what is missing, and the obvious consumer is the wrong one.

THE ROUTE THAT LOOKS FREE IS THE CLOSED ONE. `kneemri.training.pretrain` takes CacheFlags, so `--scheme rijeka` runs today with no new code, and it emits an encoder the supervised recipe loads through `--encoder-weights`. That is the SSL-as-init family exactly: encoder_adapt 0.6902, encoder_adapt_gentle 0.6875, encoder_adapt_lower 0.7309, encoder_adapt_thawed 0.7162, mae_matched 0.6735 — five collapses, 0.09-0.15 below a control that starts from stock, with plumbing/data/variant/test all cleared as suspects by adapt_null. mae_matched refuted the masked objective over 402,600 of OUR OWN slices; 8,832 foreign ones through the same import path is the sixth collapse, not a result. Zero new code is not zero expected score.

WHAT kneeMRI ACTUALLY CARRIES IS A LABEL. 736 double-blind expert ACL reads from another site, another scanner, another population. Supervised external data is a different axis from unsupervised adapt-and-import, and nothing on the ledger speaks to it.

THE BLOCKER IS THAT train.py READS ONE CACHE. `cache.load()` is a single call returning one (corpus, identifiers) pair, so the two corpora cannot both reach one run today. That is the whole gap, and it is a data-preparation job, not a training one — no card.

THE MERGE IS EXACTLY WHAT THE MASK IS FOR. Both caches are 336px/12sl uint8 under the same reader geometry (the rijeka build used CacheFlags defaults precisely so this would hold). kneeMRI acquired ONE sequence and it is SLOTS[0] — sagittal PD-FS on a 1.5T Avanto — our first slot's predicate exactly, which tests/unit/core/data/corpus/slots.py::test_built already asserts. So:

    images  (1325+736, 4, 12, 336, 336)   ours copied wholesale; rijeka into slot 0
    mask    (1325+736, 4)                 ours as-is; rijeka [1, 0, 0, 0]
    index   ours + rijeka identifiers
    labels  train.csv rows + rijeka_acl.csv rows

and the three mechanisms already audited in rijeka_corpus.py's docstring carry the rest: ReportFolds.assign hashes an identifier absent from train.csv, Targets.pair gives an absent column weight 0.0 / score 0.5 so eleven heads take no gradient from these rows, and the head's softmax renormalises over the mask. ~40 GB on disk, CPU only, no card, no slot.

PRICE IT HONESTLY BEFORE RUNNING IT. +55% studies on ONE of twelve labels. If the gain were confined to ACL it is worth roughly a twelfth of its size on the averaged metric and would not clear the 1.5% bar; the case for it is that a trunk which has seen a second site generalises on the HIDDEN test set, which is not our corpus — the owner's standing point. That is the mechanism to state in the pre-registration, and it is the reason to run it rather than the ACL subscore.

DO NOT let this become the sixth SSL arm by another name. The arm is a normal supervised run over the merged cache against a matched control on ours alone.
notes:
SEAT PRICED 2026-08-25 18:36Z — the reading the RESULT note could not compute, now that gradeswap_v1
(0.933, 7/7 scoreable) is available as a pricing base. The refusal in that note was correct and is now
answered rather than overturned.

  merged_corpus_s2026   seat +0.0002 (add) / +0.0003 (swap for lr4e-5_ws)   nearest 0.9009

AND IT REFUTES THE ARGUMENT THE ARM WAS TAKEN ON. The instrument's whole case was that a trunk which
has fitted a second site yields a member with a diversity axis no seated member has — the one lever
acting on distribution shift toward a hidden test set, which no offline number can price. The distance
column CAN price part of it, and it says the member is not distinct: 0.9009 sits in the middle of the
seated spread (0.8801 to 0.9248), closer to the roster than base224's 0.8679 and than every 224-family
candidate. 736 foreign studies, +17% of the corpus, labelling one of twelve findings, changed this
model's ORDERING of our holdout studies barely at all.

So the axis closes on two independent columns rather than one. The score was flat (+0.0020, inside the
0.0062 floor) and the ordering is flat too. That is a stronger close than the RESULT note could claim,
and it is worth the distinction: a flat score with a distinct ordering would have left the hidden-test
argument fully alive, because the seat is what that argument cashes out as. A flat score with an
ordering indistinguishable from the incumbents does not.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT SAY. The corpus supervises ONE of twelve labels, and the pre-registration priced
that at a twelfth of any ACL gain. This is a reading about THIS use of external data — 736 studies, one
label, merged supervised — not about external data as an axis. MRNet is 1,370 exams x 3 series x 3
labels and remains the stronger corpus (knee-ombx, knee-dnhd); the cache writer and merge path built
here are exactly what it drops into. Do not let this note be quoted as 'external data does not work'.

The instrument did its job: it retired the only DATA axis that was open, at 1.3 h of card, and the
retirement is now double-sourced.

title: kneeMRI (Rijeka) ingestion: cache writer + labels table, so an external-data pretraining arm can launch the moment the card frees
description:
knee-ombx is the P0 saying external data is the biggest axis never tried in 107 runs, BLOCKED on a
licence decision. As of 2026-08-25 that blocker is downgraded (knee-ombx notes: the 2.6(a) disjunction,
2.6(b) and the 2.8 carve-out, confirmed against the standard Kaggle rules template). This bead is the
part that costs no card and no slot: the INGESTION.

WHY kneeMRI AND NOT MRNet FIRST - a practical fact, not a preference. MRNet needs a human to accept
Stanford's Research Use Agreement in a browser; no agent here can. kneeMRI is mirrored on Kaggle
