(sohaibanwaar1203/kneemridataset) and pulls with the API we already hold, no slot spent. knee-ombx's
ordering is UNCHANGED - MRNet is the stronger corpus (3 labels x 3 series vs one ordinal label). This is
about what is obtainable today, and the writer is shaped so MRNet drops into the same path later.

DOWNLOADED AND INSPECTED 2026-08-25 14:36Z -> D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/kneemri_rijeka/
kneemridataset.zip, 3.31 GB, 737 entries.

  THE MIRROR IS A SUBSET AND THE DENOMINATOR IS 736, NOT 917. metadata.csv carries all 917 published
  rows, but only vol01..vol08 ship - vol09 and vol10 are absent, so 736 volumes are on disk (80.3%).
  Every .pck joins a metadata row; there are no orphans. The dropped 181 are NOT label-biased:

      aclDiagnosis        0 healthy      1 partial      2 ruptured
      all 917             690 (75.2%)   172 (18.8%)    55 (6.0%)
      present 736         547 (74.3%)   144 (19.6%)    45 (6.1%)
      missing 181         143 (79.0%)    28 (15.5%)    10 (5.5%)

  So the corpus is usable as-is and any figure quoted from it is over 736, never 917. 45 complete
  ruptures is a thin positive class - acceptable for encoder PRETRAINING, and it is not the target task.

FORMAT, measured rather than assumed:
  metadata.csv  examId,seriesNo,aclDiagnosis,kneeLR,roiX,roiY,roiZ,roiHeight,roiWidth,roiDepth,
                volumeFilename
  volumes       pickled numpy arrays, `pickle.loads` -> ndarray (depth, 320, 320) uint16, 12-bit range
                (one sampled volume: shape (32,320,320), min 0, max 1529). Depth varies 21-45.
  So a windowing step to uint8 is required; our cache is uint8. A per-volume percentile window is the
  obvious derivation - fix it from the data, do not pick a constant.

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND, better news than expected: THE TRAINER NEEDS NO CHANGE.
- core/data/corpus/folds.py:36 - `reports.get(identifier, identifier)` falls back to hashing the
  identifier itself, so a foreign corpus absent from train.csv still gets a stable fold assignment
  rather than failing.
- core/data/labels/targets.py:236-251 - a target column ABSENT from the labels CSV gets weight 0.0 and
  score 0.5. A table carrying only `ACL` supervises ACL and contributes exactly nothing on the other
  eleven, with no flag and no code path added.
- kneemri/training/train.py:65-71 - `Targets.pair` reindexes train.csv onto our identifiers; unknown
  ones become NaN, and `supervision.annotations` is off by default, so nothing reads them.

So the work is two artifacts plus one registry entry:
 1. A `StudyCache`-shaped cache: images_<key>.npy [studies, slots, slices, size, size] uint8,
    mask_<key>.npy [studies, slots] float32, index_<key>.json. Written directly rather than through
    `StudyCache.build`, whose `decode_one` calls `Study.from_directory` on DICOMs.
 2. A labels CSV in report_labels_v2.csv's shape: `StudyInstanceUID, ACL, ACL__conf` only.
 3. A slot scheme registered in core/data/corpus/slots.py SCHEMES.

THE SCHEME ENTRY IS A SAFETY REQUIREMENT, NOT A CONVENIENCE. `StudyCache.key` is
`{size}px_{slices}sl{reading.suffix()}{routing.suffix()}{truncation}` and `Routing.suffix()` is EMPTY
for the canonical scheme. A kneeMRI cache at 336 px / 12 slices under the canonical scheme would write
to `images_336px_12sl.npy` - the path the 71.6 GB corpus every member on disk was fitted on occupies -
and destroy it, differing only in its first axis. That is the exact disaster `StudyCache.key`'s own
docstring records narrowly avoiding three times (slot count, physical crop, slice band). A distinct
scheme name makes the collision unrepresentable.

TARGET MAPPING, derived rather than picked. core/data/labels/targets.py holds four reader levels with
measured precisions: 0.08 (0.041), 0.28 (0.136), 0.68 (0.378), 0.82 (0.688). kneeMRI's classes are
double-blind EXPERT reads of the ligament itself, not findings mined from report text, so they are more
trustworthy than any of our levels rather than less. healthy -> 0.08, partial -> 0.68, ruptured -> 0.82
at high confidence. The ORDERING is what carries the mechanism; the exact values matter little for
encoder pretraining.

UNRESOLVED BEFORE THE SCHEME ENTRY IS WRITTEN: sources disagree on the sequence. The Kaggle mirror says
proton-density weighted with fat suppression; several downstream papers say T1-weighted sagittal. It
decides which of our slots this corpus is analogous to and how the domain match is argued. Resolve from
the 2017 paper (Comput Methods Programs Biomed 140, 151-164). The ROI columns also go unused for now -
they are an ACL bounding box and a possible crop-centre signal, which is a separate question.

NOT IN SCOPE: the arm itself, which needs the card - and the card is biohub's, open-ended, until they
write back. This bead ends with a cache on disk and a smoke proving it maps.
notes:
2026-08-25 — INGESTION WRITTEN, gates pending. core/data/corpus/rijeka_corpus.py + build_rijeka.py, mirror tests beside them.

SEQUENCE RESOLVED. Stajduhar et al. 2017 acquired the whole corpus on one Siemens Avanto 1.5T, sagittal, proton-density-weighted with fat suppression. That is SLOTS[0] = SAG_FLUID_FS's predicate exactly — our most-used first slot, so the best possible domain match, and a Rijeka exam occupies the same slot-axis position it would occupy in ours. Hence RIJEKA_SLOTS = (SLOTS[0],), one slot.

SPACING DERIVED AND CHECKED. metadata.csv records none. 160 mm FOV (our own measured median, slots.DETAIL_MM) / 320 px = 0.5 mm/px. Checked against the one physical length the metadata DOES carry: the ACL boxes median 90 x 91 px = 45 x 45 mm at this spacing, right for boxes 'enveloping the wider cruciate ligament area' around a 30-35 mm ligament. 0.4 would make them 36 mm, 0.6 would make them 54.

TARGET MAPPING CORRECTED — this note supersedes the 0.08/0.68/0.82 written when the bead was filed, which came from a four-level reading of targets.py. There are FIVE levels and each is worth its MEASURED agreement rate (targets.py:36-43). healthy -> 0.08 (4.1%), partial -> 0.82 (68.8%), ruptured -> 0.94 (95.8%). These are double-blind expert IMAGE reads, not text-mined findings, so they belong at the confident end; no level below 0.68 fits a confirmed injury.

DENOMINATOR IS 736, NOT 917. The Kaggle mirror ships vol01..vol08 and omits vol09/vol10. Not label-biased: present 74.3/19.6/6.1% against published 75.2/18.8/6.0%.

TRAINER NEEDS NO CHANGE — three mechanisms already admit a foreign corpus: ReportFolds.assign hashes the identifier when absent from train.csv; Targets.pair gives an ABSENT column weight 0.0 (so eleven heads take no gradient, which is why the labels table carries ACL alone and NOT 0.5 fillers); train.py never reads the NaN rows unless annotations are on.

CLOBBER MADE UNREPRESENTABLE TWICE: RIJEKA_SCHEME suffixes the cache key (_rijeka), and build_rijeka refuses any other --scheme. Under canonical a 336px/12sl build would write images_336px_12sl.npy over the 71.6 GB every member on disk was fitted on, differing only in axis 0.

NEXT: run the ingestion (no card, no slot):
  python -m core.data.corpus.build_rijeka --archive D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/kneemri_rijeka/kneemridataset.zip --scheme rijeka --slices 12 --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9
Then the pretraining arm, which DOES need the card and so waits on biohub.
BUILT 2026-08-25 14:58Z, CPU only, ~60s (the card is biohub's until their GPU train ends; they confirmed at 14:26Z they will ping when it is device-empty).

  images_336px_12sl_rijeka.npy   (736, 1, 12, 336, 336) uint8, 997 MB
  index_336px_12sl_rijeka.json   736 identifiers, '<examId>-<seriesNo>'
  mask_336px_12sl_rijeka.npy     (736, 1) all ones — the corpus acquired the one sequence it has
  labels/rijeka_acl.csv          736 rows, StudyInstanceUID/ACL/ACL__conf, levels 547/144/45

GEOMETRY IS THE CANONICAL ONE, NOT THE 0.1-0.9 BAND THE PLAN NOTE NAMED. Built with CacheFlags
defaults — the historic crop, centre and band every member on disk was fitted under — because the whole
mechanism this module exists for is that the two corpora reach the encoder in ONE geometry and ONE
intensity space. A pretraining corpus sampled under a band our members were never fitted on would make
the transfer measure the band difference as well as the dataset difference. Only --scheme is non-default,
and that is the safety flag.

The 547/144/45 in the labels table is the 736-row split exactly (74.3/19.6/6.1%), so the join held all
the way through the build. Our own 35.8 GB images_336px_12sl.npy is untouched — still its Aug 10 mtime.

NEXT: the pretraining arm. Nothing else about ingestion is outstanding.

title: smoke and arm write the SAME log, so a failed smoke's traceback is destroyed by the run it gates
description: experiments/arms/v3lora_dense.sh smoke passes --out v3lora_smoke.pt but run_train still names the arm 'v3lora_dense', so both modes write $PROCESSED/experiments/v3lora_dense.full.log. On 2026-08-25 the smoke exited 1 and the arm that followed overwrote the log before the traceback could be read — the smoke gate produced a FAILURE with no DIAGNOSIS, which is the one thing it exists to produce. The smoke's whole argument is 'two minutes of smoke against 2.5h of arm'; that trade only pays if the two minutes leave evidence behind. Fix in lib.sh run_train: derive the log name from the OUT checkpoint stem rather than the arm name, so v3lora_smoke.pt lands in v3lora_smoke.full.log and can never be clobbered. Applies to every arm with a smoke mode, not just this one.
notes: FIXED 2026-08-25 in experiments/lib.sh: run_train sets ARM_LOG_NAME from the --out checkpoint stem, and the four reads of the arm's log go through _arm_log, which prefers that stem and falls back to the arm name for a run with no --out. The smoke and the arm it gates now write different files because their checkpoints already had to differ -- run_train REFUSES an arm whose --out exists, so two runs sharing a name cannot share a checkpoint path either. Verified: ARM_LOG_NAME=merged_corpus_s2026 resolves to .../merged_corpus_s2026.full.log and the unset case to .../fallback.full.log.

title: board_read read one page, so our rank was invisible: we are 48th of 2373
description: board_read shipped calling competition_leaderboard_view, which returns the first TWENTY rows. A team at rank 48 cannot appear on that page, so 'ours' was never read from the board — it was passed in from champion.json and subtracted from the page's best score. The output (leader 0.952, ours 0.938, gap 0.014) was arithmetically right and answered a question nobody asked; every note since quoted it as though one team stood between us and the top. Forty-seven do, and forty-two of them sit inside 0.936-0.940. Fixed: the read is now the whole board (competition_leaderboard_download, still no slot) and reports a Standing (rank/field/tied), joined on TeamMemberUserNames rather than TeamName. comp/leaderboard.json gained rank/field/tied so champion_check's staleness bound now guards a rank. Also: the CSV carries a BOM, so plain utf-8 gives KeyError 'Rank' against a header that looks correct in a log — utf-8-sig. Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_rank-not-gap.md

title: A checkpoint carries its own preprocessing contract, and rad-dino's is not ImageNet
description: model.py registers IMAGENET_MEAN/IMAGENET_STD as buffers for EVERY encoder. Audited all seven registry encoders against their own preprocessor_config.json (primary source, HF raw + local cache): dinov2 small/base/large, dinov3 vits16/vits16plus/vitb16 and convnextv2-base-22k-224 all declare the ImageNet constants, so six of seven are correct by coincidence -- which is why this never surfaced. microsoft/rad-dino declares image_mean 0.5307 and image_std 0.2583 (greyscale, native 518 px), and we feed it ImageNet. At x=0.5307 the trunk should see 0.0 and sees (0.5307-0.485)/0.229 = 0.200, a 0.20-std offset, with a scale error of 0.2583/0.229 = 1.128 (12.8 percent). raddino_dense scored 0.8137 solo against base_dense_s2026 0.8512 at the same recipe and was read as evidence about medical-domain pretraining; that reading is confounded, and it is a SECOND confound on top of the run being TRUNCATED at epoch 6 of 12. Our mounted snapshot at rad-dino/ carries no preprocessor_config.json at all, so the constants are not even present to read -- which is why the fix belongs on Encoder in the registry (the house pattern params_m already uses) rather than as a checkpoint read. The buffers are persistent so they ride in the state dict: every member already on disk keeps the constants it was fitted with, and only a new fit changes. V-JEPA2 is UNVERIFIED -- no local snapshot and the HF repo answers no readable preprocessor_config.json -- so its constants must be checked before any vjepa arm is armed. Found in kaggle forum topic 735154, verified independently against the primary source.
notes: FIXED 2026-08-25. Encoder.normalization (kneemri/models/backbone.py) now carries the pair per encoder, IMAGENET is the default, RAD_DINO declares 0.5307/0.2583. Consumers moved: StudyModel.__init__ + from_config (registry-resolved from the config's variant, so both inference paths rebuild correctly), run_setup, SpectralMae, pretrain. Buffers stay PERSISTENT, so every packaged member keeps the constants it was fitted under and only a new fit moves. Tests: Normalization.declared/triple/assert_declared, one over the whole registry, and a model-side test that from_config resolves RAD_DINO's pair while an unnamed variant stays ImageNet. raddino_dense's ledger entry now records the second confound. V-JEPA2 left unverified and split into its own bead.

title: The 58-study ruler contradicts its own reports at the severity boundary, and every label-column number rests on it
description:
Read 2026-08-25 from competition discussion topic 735826 via kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read (no submission slot). Two independent competitors report the same defect in the 58 provided annotations, with a check anyone can run:

  - Filter reports whose effusion sentence carries a small-size qualifier ('small', 'minimal', 'trace', or the equivalent in the other languages). That group holds BOTH Effusion=0 and Effusion=1. In one sample two reports used the SAME English template and the SAME sentence and got OPPOSITE labels.
  - Then find a report stating a MODERATE effusion. At least one of those is annotated Effusion=0 - so it is not a 'small=negative, moderate=positive' threshold either, which is what the competition's own introduction lays out as the heuristic.
  - A second poster makes the same point structurally: 'the image label clearly flouts the rules of diagnosis laid out in the introduction ... close to the decision boundary the report label and the image label will often disagree; radiologists will just disagree.'

WHY THIS IS OURS AND NOT THEIRS. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-14_labels-or-pixels.md prices every finding as two AUCs against those 58 annotations - labels 0.8639 vs model 0.8391 aggregate, Effusion 0.8137 -> 0.9453. Both columns are scored against a ruler this claim says is internally inconsistent AT THE BOUNDARY, which is exactly where a report-derived label lands. The claim does not overturn the split (the ordering is over twelve labels and the two largest gaps are far from the noise), but it bounds the LABEL column specifically: a better reader (knee-dbw, knee-bot) cannot recover agreement the annotation itself does not obey.

THE CHECK, CPU-ONLY, NO SLOT, NO CARD:
  1. Over the 58 annotated studies, bucket each report's effusion sentence by severity qualifier (small/minimal/trace vs moderate/large vs none).
  2. Cross-tab against the radiologist Effusion annotation. STATE THE DENOMINATOR - n=58 total, and the count in each bucket, not a rate inside the bucket that happened to parse.
  3. If a qualifier bucket holds both classes, the ruler is subjective at the boundary and the effusion label column has a ceiling below 1.0 that no reader improvement crosses.
  4. Repeat for the other graded findings the intro gives a threshold for; knee-bot already records that we train on 0.68 where the radiologist agrees 38%, which is the same shape measured from the other side.

WHAT IT WOULD CHANGE. If the bucket is mixed: stop spending on the reader for effusion, and treat the graded findings' targets as a distribution rather than a threshold. If it is clean and only OUR extraction is mixed, the defect is ours and knee-dbw pays after all. Either outcome retires a suspicion for the cost of one pandas cross-tab.

CAVEAT ON THE SOURCE: this is a competitor's report of their own sample, not our measurement. It is cheap enough that arguing about it costs more than running it.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 on our own data — the claim holds, harder than the forum reported.

python -m core.data.labels.severity_boundary (CPU, no slot, no card):
  28 English annotated studies of 58 annotated
    small / minimal / trace           12 studies   annotated positive   6
    both, e.g. small to moderate       1 studies   annotated positive   1
    moderate or larger                 3 studies   annotated positive   2
    mentioned, no size word            7 studies   annotated positive   6
    effusion denied                    5 studies   annotated positive   0

The negative side of the stated threshold is a coin flip (6 of 12). The positive side is 2 of 3. Seven
studies are named by the tool with their UIDs. Denominator is 28 English of 58 annotated, NOT 58.

HARNESS SUSPICION PAID: the first run named EIGHT. 'No significant knee effusion', annotated 0, had been
bucketed moderate-or-larger because 'significant' is a LARGE word inside a DENIAL. That row is agreement,
filed as a contradiction by the tool. A DENIED regex now removes denied sentences, and the resulting
'effusion denied' bucket is a free control: 5 studies, 0 positive — the agreement a working ruler shows on
easy cases. Sensitivity: dropping 'mild' from SMALL_WORDS moves 4 studies and leaves the small bucket at
5 positive of 8. Still mixed. Not a vocabulary artefact.

CONSEQUENCE: part of every reader error measured against these 58 is not error, and no better reader
recovers it. Effusion is where supervision_gap shows the biggest label-to-model gap (0.8137 vs 0.9453);
a slice of that gap is annotation noise at the boundary, not headroom. Also prices down LLM-confidence
weighting: confidence over a report measures confidence in applying a crisp rule to a clear word, not in
the finding — 'small' is easy to read while the process that wrote 'small' rather than 'moderate' is the
noisy part.

Written up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_effusion-threshold-ruler.md

title: Frontier reaches our ENSEMBLE score with ONE model at 224px - the gap is member quality, not ensembling
description:
Read 2026-08-25 from the competition discussion via the Kaggle API (kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read; no submission slot). Topic 735304 'Best single-model score', 10 messages, 17 votes.

SELF-REPORTED SINGLE-MODEL SCORES ON THE BOARD:
- 0.942 @ 224px ('Single model 0.934 @ 224px. Update: 0.942 with some tweaks, still @ 224px')
- 0.938 single model, single fold
- 0.926 single model 5-fold @ 336px, LLM-output labels only
- 0.92 with OOF AUC = LB AUC within noise
- 0.915 DINOv2-based

OURS, from comp/board.jsonl: best SINGLE member solo_v4 = 0.914. Best ensemble votefit_v1 = 0.938 over six members. So our ensembling machinery buys +0.024 and is real - but the frontier's ONE model equals or beats our SIX, and does it at 224px against our 392px members, so it is not a compute story.

READ: the 0.014 board gap lives in MEMBER QUALITY, not in ensemble construction. Our ensemble work has been buying back a deficit rather than extending a lead. That is above the 1.5 pct bar as a claim about WHERE to spend, and it is the first evidence this session that localises the gap at all.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT REFUTE: the recorded measurement that diversity beat member quality within OUR pool (interpretations/kneemri, bead knee-eeo). Both hold at once - given members clustered at ~0.91, diversity is the best available lever; the frontier instead has a member that does not need it. Do not re-run that ablation on this.

EVIDENCE QUALITY: unverified self-reports, no way to confirm 0.942. But five independent posts cluster 0.915-0.942 and one anchors OOF=LB within noise, so the cluster is consistent rather than one boast. Treat the LEVEL as soft and the ORDERING (their single >= our six) as the finding.

CHECKABLE FOLLOW-UP named in the same thread: the public Efficiency LB (kaggle.com/code/ryanholbrook/rsna-knee-abnormalities-efficiency-lb) shows runtimes, and a poster argues high scorers there have short runtimes, i.e. are not 20-model ensembles. That is free, independent, non-self-reported evidence for the same claim - read it before acting.
notes:
2026-08-25, from discussion topic 736678 (kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read --topic 736678): the Efficiency LB is the NON-SELF-REPORTED corroboration this bead asked for, and it holds.

  - As of Aug 22 only ~32% of the public-LB top 50 also appear in the Efficiency-LB top 50. A high score bought with a long runtime is a score bought with ensembling.
  - The poster is Efficiency LB 22nd and Public LB 78th at 0.926 with 'preprocessing plus a single model trained with 5-fold', total runtime ~20 minutes.
  - A second poster is currently Efficiency LB #1 with NO ensemble.
  - A third notes the top two public-LB submissions also sit on the Efficiency LB, so the very top is not runtime-heavy either.

That is a public board rather than a forum claim, and it says the same thing the self-reports did: a single model reaches ~0.926-0.942 while our six-member ensemble reads 0.938. The ensembling we do is real (+0.024 within our pool) and it is buying back a member-quality deficit, not extending a lead. Efficiency also bears on knee-5bv.
2026-08-25, kneemri.kaggle.efficiency_read (new tool, live read, no slot): the Efficiency-LB corroboration this bead asked for is now MEASURED rather than quoted, and it is stronger than the forum version - but it is bimodal, which the forum version was not.

The poster's overlap claim verifies: public top-50 and efficiency top-50 share 17 teams (34.0%), against their '~32% as of Aug 22'. Top-10 overlap is 20%, top-100 is 32%.

WHAT THE BOARD SHOWS THAT THE FORUM DID NOT. Joining the public top-20 to their efficiency rank, the same accuracy is reached by two completely different builds:
  public 4  Scott Willis   0.947  efficiency rank    1   (0.947 - same entry)
  public 5  Matteo Vitali  0.946  efficiency rank    8   (0.946 - same entry)
  public 14 Tucker Arrants 0.944  efficiency rank    5   (0.944 - same entry)
  public 8  CloseAI        0.946  efficiency rank 1678
  public 20 Pizza Boy      0.943  efficiency rank 1856
  public 16 Ignat          0.943  efficiency rank 1350
So ~0.943-0.947 is reachable BOTH at efficiency rank 1 and at efficiency rank 1856. Two routes to the same number, differing by orders of magnitude in runtime.

THE DATUM THAT MATTERS, and it is a board fact rather than a self-report: the efficiency-#1 team scores 0.947 on the PUBLIC board with the SAME entry. A cheap build reaches 0.947. This bead's finding was 'their ONE model equals our SIX' from unverified posts clustering 0.915-0.942; the board now says a fast build reaches 0.947, which is 0.009 ABOVE our six-member 0.938 and above every self-report in the thread. The ordering this bead called the finding is confirmed by non-self-reported evidence, and the LEVEL it called soft is, if anything, understated.

THE EXCEPTION WORTH NAMING: the actual public leader, Brandon Low at 0.952, sits at efficiency rank 41 with a SEPARATE 0.922 entry. So the very top is not on the cheap route - the forum's 'the top two public entries are on both boards' does not hold for #1 as of this read. The cheap route's demonstrated ceiling is 0.947, not 0.952.

WHAT THIS SETS UP, and it is a SUM rather than a choice: our ensembling buys a measured +0.024 within our own pool and a cheap frontier member reaches 0.947 solo. Those compose. The target is a replicated member at frontier quality FEEDING our existing ensemble machinery, not a choice between replicating theirs and building ours. GPU-blocked at the time of writing.

EVIDENCE CAVEAT: the efficiency board is a snapshot with newest submission 2026-08-23 22:30 while the public board is live - see knee-5bv, where that lag was found to have inflated a different measurement by 14 points. It does not touch the rows above, whose two scores agree, but any efficiency figure quoted from this read is as of Aug 23.

title: board_check should join unnamed rows on NAME and refuse an empty members_named
description:
Three board rows were recovered by hand on 2026-08-25 (chosen_v2, onedecode_v2, weakseven_v1) after two earlier passes left them unnamed, and each was missed by a mechanism a check can hold.

1. NAME JOIN. The earlier recovery offered a row a script only through the row's own `kernel` field, so a row with `kernel: null` was never handed one. Joining on the entry id instead (chosen_v2 -> comp/kernels/kneemri-chosen) finds a surviving script for THIRTEEN of the fourteen rows the file called unrecoverable. The note said 'no script survives'; that was true of fusion25_v2 alone.

2. ABSENT, NEVER EMPTY. weakseven_v1 carried `members_named: []`. A consumer asking `'members_named' in row` reads that as recovered, one asking for truthiness reads it as missing. It had a kernel AND a literal tuple and was still skipped.

3. THE REAL BLOCKER IS SELECTION STYLE, not a missing script. The eleven that stay unnamed call KernelRun(members=N) - strongest(N) over recorded holdouts - which a parse cannot replay against a package that has since changed. Worth recording per row so nobody re-audits them.

Proposed: board_check grows an assertion that no row has an empty members_named, and that any row lacking members_named either has no matching kernel directory or selects by rank. Recovery must read the AS-SUBMITTED commit, not HEAD: kneemri-chosen was edited 2026-08-17 after chosen_v2 shipped (tuple unchanged, but checked rather than assumed - the sixfresh caveat is this exact hazard).

title: champion.json pins allfit 0.937 while votefit_v1 holds the board at 0.938
description: The pin lags the board by one entry, which is the exact failure its own principle #39 names verbatim ('A PIN THAT LAGS THE BOARD SILENTLY MISPRICES EVERY CANDIDATE UNDER IT ... champion_check asserts the pinned entry can be REBUILT; it cannot know the entry is still the best one'). seat_value reads the roster from the pin precisely so no arm header holds a stale copy. Not a significance claim -- 0.938 over 0.937 is one tick and the record already says it is not a result -- the pin is a board-max reproducibility record, and 0.938 is the max. Blocked on the board row repair: votefit's kit is aa79cd3 DIRTY, so the pin cannot claim a clean sha and must carry the DIRTY. Its six members are a subset of allfit's, so the roster already packages them. Moving the pin does not lose allfit, whose board row is one of the 17 complete ones.

title: board.jsonl: the five best entries carry no members_named, so from_board raises on the top of the board
description: 31 of 48 rows in comp/board.jsonl have no 'members_named' (and mostly no 'kit'). Champion.from_board reads row['members_named'] and row['kit'] directly, so it raises a bare KeyError -- not its own 'no board entry named X' message -- on every one of them. The rows it fails on include dark6_v1, dark7_v1, farseat_v1 (0.937) and votefit_v1 (0.938): the pricing door that exists so a member can be scored against a non-champion entry is shut on exactly the entries worth pricing against. Repair the recent scored rows from the two sources champion.json's own 'why' names: the kernel's 'chosen' tuple and the kernel log's 'kit <sha>' line. votefit_v1's log reads 'kit aa79cd3 DIRTY' -- record the DIRTY, do not drop it. Also make from_board name the missing field instead of KeyError.
notes: DONE: the five top rows only (dark6_v1, dark7_v1, v3seat_v1, farseat_v1, votefit_v1), members_named recovered via Champion.named_by_kernel and kit read from each kernel log's own 'kit <sha>' line. Cross-checked: each recovered tuple's length equals the row's existing 'members' count, which was recorded independently. v3seat_v1's kernel log does not survive, so its kit is recorded null rather than guessed. votefit_v1 and farseat_v1 both read 'kit aa79cd3 DIRTY' -- recorded with the marker. from_board now names the missing fields instead of raising a bare KeyError. The remaining 26 rows are knee-ykny.

title: DeviceBudget prices a frozen block at zero: unfreeze4 under-capped by 35.7%
description:
MEASURED over 74 recorded runs by `python -m kneemri.experiments.budget_residuals` (commit 1f79eca), which prices every run whose epoch rows carry the corrected reserved peak.

THE DEFECT. `DeviceBudget.needed()` multiplies the WHOLE slice cost by `trainable_blocks / FITTED_TRAINABLE`, i.e. it prices a FROZEN block at exactly zero memory. A frozen block still runs its forward and still holds the activations the blocks above it read; only its gradients and optimiser state go away. So the model is wrong in BOTH directions, and both are measured:

  unfreeze4_s2026        measured 14.79, derived 10.90  (+35.7%)  CAP UNDER DEMAND — allowed 11.79
  encoder_adapt_thawed   (killed earlier this axis, in the OVER direction)

A cap under a measured demand is the one failure this model calls fatal: it prevents nothing and guarantees the OutOfMemoryError.

THE FORM THE DATA SUPPORTS. Per-slice-per-batch unit cost, backed out of three recorded points at u = trainable blocks:
  u=4  -> 1.2142
  u=6  -> 1.3350   (the fitted point, GB_PER_SLICE)
  u=12 -> 1.7730
A two-parameter line a + b*u fitted on u=4 and u=6 gives a=0.9726, b=0.0604, and predicts u=12 at 1.697 against 1.773 measured — 4.5% off, on a HELD-OUT point that also differs in batch and slice count. The current pure ratio predicts 2.67 at u=12, 51% over. The intercept a is the frozen forward: 0.97/1.335 = 73% of a fully-open block's cost is the forward pass, which is the right order for bf16 activations against fp32 grads+Adam.

WHY THIS IS THE SHAPE, NOT A FUDGE. It is the same failure as knee-kwdh, knee-ylp0 and knee-bj90 one term further along: a term fitted at one configuration and handed to another. The difference is that this time there are three measured points on the axis and a held-out check, rather than one point and an invented constant.

FIX: `GB_PER_SLICE * (slices + 1) * step` where step's trainable factor becomes (FROZEN_SHARE + (1 - FROZEN_SHARE) * trainable / depth)-shaped, derived from the two fitted points rather than assumed. Re-run `budget_residuals` after: the three CAP UNDER DEMAND rows are the acceptance test, and it graduates into nox when `--assert` passes clean.
close_reason: Fixed in 3b4d2e6. The trainable-blocks term is now affine (TRAINABLE_FLOOR 0.9726 + TRAINABLE_PER_BLOCK 0.0604 per open block, normalised at 6) instead of a pure ratio. Fitted on the four-open and six-open ledger points, twelve-open held back: both held-out twelve-open runs (encoder_adapt_thawed -32.8% -> +4.3%, band_dense_llrd -32.7% -> +4.5%) land inside 4.5%. unfreeze4_s2026 goes +35.7% -> -0.0% but it is a fit point, so that is construction not evidence. budget_residuals: 3 runs capped below measured demand -> 2. Only those three rows move; every arm at the default unfreeze_last derives what it derived before, because the line's value at six IS GB_PER_SLICE.

title: models/model.py is 731 lines against a 750 god-file gate, and StudyModel holds two responsibilities
description:
`kneemri/models/model.py` is the largest file in the tree at 731 lines. `[tool.structure]` file_max is 750 and ENFORCED, so the next feature that touches this file blocks the gate — the same way arm_check.py did at 789 on 2026-08-23, which is what forced the ArmHeader extraction mid-change rather than on purpose.

The split is already visible in the method list. StudyModel does two things:

FORWARD (the architecture): per_slice, check_whole_stack, forward, slot_features, over_depth, slice_features, supervised, fingerprint, _tokens, _pool.

ENCODER SURGERY (the optimisation plumbing, roughly lines 397-708): load_trained, _blocks, low_rank, applied, _opened_blocks, _base_parameters, parameter_groups, _readout_parameters, _open_blocks, _opened, _last_blocks, compile_encoder, recompute_activations. That is ~310 lines about LoRA wrapping, block freezing, parameter groups, torch.compile and activation recompute — none of which the forward pass reads.

DESIGN: lift the second group into `kneemri/models/encoder_surgery.py` as an `EncoderSurgery` holding the backbone (and whatever readout parameters it needs). StudyModel keeps THIN DELEGATING methods for the six names consumers actually call — low_rank, parameter_groups, compile_encoder, recompute_activations, load_trained, applied — because a caller reaching `model.surgery.low_rank(...)` is exactly the chained-call-into-a-stranger the demeter gate exists to refuse. Delegation costs ~25 lines back and nets ~250 out.

CONSUMERS (audited, all through StudyModel and so unchanged by this): run_setup.py:332-337, serve_bench.py:206, holdout_predictions.py:63, members.py:638, landed.py:146.

CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT: model.py drops well under 750, the surgery module gets its own mirror tests, and a smoke recipe (`arm_check --smoke`-sized, 60 studies 1 epoch) trains and reports the same `applied()` dict — landed.py reads that dict to assert a flag actually fired, so it is the one output that proves the surgery still runs rather than merely imports.

title: TrainingOptions is a 666-line god-config with 55 flags and six disjoint responsibilities
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25. kneemri/training/options.py: 666 lines, 55 add_argument calls, LCOM4 = 6 - the
highest in the tree by a factor of 1.5 (next is CropAlignment at 4). The cohesion detector names the six
components itself, so the seams do not need to be invented:

  {band, crop, reading} · {routing} · {cache} · {supervision} · {sampled} · {thinned}

Six groups sharing one class means every consumer of one flag imports all fifty-five, and every new arm
flag lands in the same file regardless of what it configures. It is also the reason the arm scripts pass
long undifferentiated flag strings that arm_check then has to re-parse to price.

PROPOSAL: keep TrainingOptions as the composition root, move each component to its own frozen dataclass
beside its consumer (per the repo rule that a supplementary type lives beside its producer, not in a
types bucket). The parser stays one parser - what splits is the STATE, not the CLI surface.

CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT: every arm script in experiments/arms/ must produce a byte-identical
invocation before and after, and arm_check --switches must report the same switch set. That is the
equality check; without it this is a rewrite with a chance of silently dropping a flag, and a dropped
flag is a run that reads as a fact about an architecture.
notes:
AUDITED AND PARTLY REFUSED 2026-08-25 (e2e7f7f).

The proposal in this bead - nest each cohesion component into its own dataclass - is REFUSED, and the
refusal is the finding. `TrainingOptions.parse` is `cls(**vars(parser().parse_args()))`, so argparse's
dest names and this dataclass's field names are one set. FIVE separate guards walk that set FLAT, each
against a defect that already happened:

  switch_coverage.py:80,84   - proves no flag is left unarmed by every arm
  landed.py:315,322          - proves no write-off names a flag TrainingOptions no longer has
  tests/integration/argv_to_checkpoint.py:495 - proves every declared field is READ by a run
  tests/unit/kneemri/training/options.py:103  - asserts dests == field names, exactly
  tests/unit/kneemri/runs/member_record.py:144 - a new field lands in exactly one of three places

Nesting makes all five recurse. That is MORE code guarding the same defects, which is the opposite of
what this bead wanted. And the split it asks for already exists in the shape this repo chose: crop,
band, reading, routing and supervision are each scalar fields plus a grouping property.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and is now fixed: `sampled` and `thinned`. Two numpy methods on a config
object, called from exactly one place, taking and returning exactly the tuple `ReportFolds.holdout`
produces. They are the next two steps of the SPLIT, not a statement about a recipe. Moved to
`core/data/corpus/folds.py` as `FitPositions`, together with the two disclaimers train.py spelled out
inline (`caveats`). options.py no longer imports numpy at all.

WHY LCOM4 WENT 6 -> 5 AND NOT 6 -> 4: the new `positions` property is itself a component, exactly as
crop/band/routing are. LCOM4 on this class is MEASURING THE ACCEPTED PATTERN, not a defect - it cannot
drop below about 5 while scalar-fields-plus-grouping-property stands, and driving it lower means
nesting. Do not chase that number here.

The equality constraint this bead asked for was met: the field set is byte-identical at 63 either side,
so every arm invocation and every switch the coverage walk reports are unchanged.

REMAINING, IF ANYTHING: the file is ~625 lines of which the large majority is argparse help text - i.e.
documentation, and the most valuable thing in it. Each field's default is spelled in two homes (the
dataclass and the flag), but that drift is already caught totally by options.py test_defaults, which
asserts whole-object equality. Generating the parser from the fields would remove ~55 duplicated
defaults at the cost of a reflection machine and would have to re-home the help text anyway. Not worth
it. Closing.

title: 68 CLI entrypoints hand-roll the same six-line preamble; ~300 lines of it are pure duplication
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 over kneemri/ + core/ (163 modules, 36.9k lines):

  ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)   55 modules
  logging.basicConfig(...)              60 modules
  --paths default paths.yaml            45 modules
  DataRoot.from_config(arguments.paths) 45 modules
  if __name__ == '__main__': main()     61 modules
  'for line in X.report(...): logger.info(line)'  24 modules
  add_argument calls, total             308

Three read in full (core/data/corpus/band_coverage.py, kneemri/evaluation/label_stability.py,
kneemri/evaluation/paired_floor.py) open with the SAME five statements in the same order before any
module-specific line appears. That is not a coincidence of style: it is the repo's only CLI contract,
written out 45-60 times instead of once, and it is why main() is the complexity hotspot in the tree
(arm_check.main CC 21, report_prices 14, slot_ties.main 13, mount_check.main 12).

There is NO shared CLI helper today. kneemri/commands.py is an index GENERATOR (it parses modules for a
top-level main and rewrites kneemri/README.md); it does not run anything.

PROPOSAL: core/cli.py holding the contract once - the parser seeded from __doc__, --paths declared once,
logging configured once, DataRoot resolved once, and a report(lines) sink for the 24 modules that print a
line iterator. A module then declares only its own arguments and its body.

THE RISK, stated up front so the work is judged on it: a CLI framework trades explicit lines for
indirection, and a bad one makes every entrypoint harder to read than the six lines it replaced. The bar
is that a module using it must be SHORTER and no less obvious, and that argparse stays visible rather
than being wrapped in a decorator DSL. If the first three ports do not read better, the finding stands
and the framework does not.

Do NOT port all 68 in one commit. Port three (one per package), measure the delta, then decide.
notes:
36 entrypoints ported to core.cli.Command in 519a396 (91 lines net, argparse leaves 30 modules) and 18 report loops collapsed to command.report in aa12a10. Every ported entrypoint smoked with --help and answers with --paths in its options. Three modules built their logger inside main() below where the preamble needs it; the definition moved up. STILL HAND-ROLLED, deliberately, each for a different reason worth its own read: arm_check (no --paths in the preamble block), label_probe and protocol_prior (statements between parse_args and basicConfig), run_comparison, holdout_backfill, teacher_readings (no canonical ArgumentParser line). Six left of 42.
41 of 42 ported (c7f5ca0). Only arm_check left, and DELIBERATELY: its parser has no --paths (an arm's paths travel inside TrainingOptions) and Command always adds one, so porting it would add a dead flag. That one belongs to knee-eydz.

title: Rigid test-time views on the shipping roster — the last unmeasured serving axis
description: Serving.views has never been exercised on any roster we would ship. votefit's log reads 'views=identity only (default)', and that default has held for every board entry on the all-data roster. The only three attempts (kneemri-views, topviews, rateviews) rode two- and four-member fold-0 rosters from before the all-data era, and kneemri-views came back COMPLETE with a BLANK public score from a warp OOM that WARP_CHUNK=512 has since fixed. kneemri-jitterfit (pushed 2026-08-25) serves dark6's identical six under SpatialViews(degrees=(0.0,-6.0)) with RankAverage and overlap=False held, so the single variable is the view set. Two views not three: six members at 3x forward is 18 member-passes against the 9h ceiling that 2 members at 3x once failed to clear. HAZARD: Ensemble.mitigate gives up views FIRST on a projected overrun, so a long run degrades silently into dark6 and reads 0.937 for an unrelated reason. The free run must be checked for the absence of a 'giving up test-time views' line BEFORE any slot is spent. Pre-registered against dark6 0.937: >=0.940 members are pose-brittle, license the third view and serve everything under views; 0.935-0.939 flat, both serving axes closed on board numbers and nothing serving-shaped remains; <=0.934 the warp destroys information at slice edges, retire TTA on this pool.
notes:
PRECONDITION CLEARED 2026-08-25 12:14Z, no slot and no card spent. Pulled the completed free run with `kaggle kernels output dimiturnt/kneemri-jitterfit` (note the owner is dimiturnt, not dimiturtrz - the wrong slug returns a 'Permission kernels.get was denied' that reads like a private-notebook problem and is not one).

The log answers the hazard this bead raised:

  loaded and fingerprint-checked 6 of 6 members
  overlap=False requested, INERT - all 6 members are whole-stack
  serving: vote=RankAverage (default) views=SpatialViews(degrees=(0.0, -6.0), shifts=((0.0, 0.0),)) precision=each member's own (default)

and `grep -ic 'giving up'` over the whole log returns 0. Ensemble.mitigate never fired, so this entry did NOT degrade into dark6, and a score from it would be a reading of the view set rather than of an unrelated budget event. Status is COMPLETE and the run converted its notebook normally, so it did not die late either.

The single variable against dark6 (0.937) is intact: identical six members, RankAverage held, overlap held and inert, views the only difference. The pre-registration stands as written - >=0.940 means members are pose-brittle, 0.935-0.939 means flat and both serving axes close, <=0.934 means the warp destroys information at slice edges.

What the free run CANNOT give: submission.csv holds three studies plus a header, the public stub a non-submitted run sees, so there is no score to read here. This still needs a real slot. Five were spent today and the reset is 00:00 UTC.

One observation for whoever reads the scores: every value in the stub is a twelfth (0.0833, 0.25, 0.9167), which is RankAverage over six members behaving exactly as it should on three rows - not a defect.

title: Per-label reader agreement measured: rho=+0.53 vs per-label AUC, and per-label recalibration is worth 0.000
description:
core.data.labels.reader_agreement.by_label was in the tool and never in the ledger. Ran it card-free 2026-08-25 (logs/reader_agreement_20260825.log).

Agreement on the reader's POSITIVE calls, per finding: Synovitis 81.2 (16 calls), Medial Meniscus 78.1 (32), ACL 71.9 (32), Fracture 68.4 (19), Baker's 68.8 (16), Effusion 68.0 (50), PF OA 66.7 (24), Lateral Meniscus 66.7 (30), Medial OA 63.6 (22), Lateral OA 56.2 (16), MCL 50.0 (18), Contusion 44.4 (36). DENOMINATOR: 311 positive calls over 57 annotated studies, 684 cells. Per-label n is 16-50, so each rate carries roughly +/-20pp and no PAIR of labels is separated.

Paired against band_dense's per-label AUC table (experiments/README.md:411), Spearman rho = +0.53 (sum d2 = 134.5, n=12, p~0.08). Moderate, NOT established. The residual is two trauma findings pulling opposite ways: Contusion is 6th by AUC and LAST by agreement; Fracture is 11th by AUC and 5th by agreement.

TWO CONSEQUENCES.

(1) FREE KILL, and it needs no resolution at all. The error census is lopsided 3.4:1 - 108 false positives against 32 misses, Synovitis the only inversion at -11 - which looks like a calibration lever. It is not one. The metric is a per-label rank AUC, so a monotone per-label recalibration cannot change it by construction. Any arm that corrects the reader's over-call rate is worth exactly 0.000 on this board. Retired before proposal. Consistent with calibrated_targets at +0.0038, inside the floor.

(2) The twelve-label deficit target is OVER-PRICED. farseat's FLAT branch hands off to 'lifting Lateral Meniscus 0.7981, PF OA 0.8165, MCL 0.8166, Lateral OA 0.8215 to 0.87 is +0.0189'. MCL at 50.0 and Lateral OA at 56.2 are the worst reader precision after Contusion, so that arithmetic prices headroom the label table may not contain. NOT refuted - Contusion scores 0.8705 on 44.4 precision, which proves a label can - but not licensed as a target either. Anything built against the label deficit must state which labels it targets and what their agreement is.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. Agreement here is precision on the reader's positives only, not full agreement; recall is the separate 32-miss column. And the board scores radiologist annotations while we train on report-read labels - experiments/README.md:2356 and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-11 line 644 do not agree on how far those two diverge, and this measurement does not settle it.

title: [bug] witness_check reported 22 of 40 members and was silent about the 18 it skipped, all seven shipped members among them
description:
RUN 2026-08-25 02:11-02:26Z, comp/witness_check.py --device cpu over the whole package. It printed 20 'ok' and 2 'UNVERIFIED - no witness'. The manifest holds 40. The other 18 produced NO line of any kind.

The 18 unreported: aprior_dense_s2026, base_dense_ff, calib_span_ff, crop80_span_s2026, final_ws_e12, focal_dense_s2026, grade_ladder_ff, lr4e-5_ws_ff, margin_seat_s2026, severity_weight_s2026, sided_pool_s2026, small_accum_s2026, small_batch6_ff, small_batch6_s2026, through_dense_ff, through_dense_s2026, v3base_dense_s2026, vjepa_warm_s2026.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A COSMETIC GAP. That list contains ALL SEVEN all-data --fold -1 members, and those are the only members on the last four board entries (dark6, dark7, farseat, and the armed votefit). It also contains vjepa_warm_s2026, submitted in farseat 40 minutes before this run, and v3base_dense_s2026, sitting in a PENDING v3seat. CLAUDE.md names witness_check as a pre-submission gate 'which found three defects on first use'. As invoked here it was silent about 45% of the package and about 100% of what has actually shipped.

SUSPECTED CAUSE, and it is MY invocation before it is the tool's: I ran it under 'timeout 900 ... > log 2>&1; echo "EXIT 0"'. That is the exact trap CLAUDE.md documents — the echo's status is what the harness reports, so a timeout kill at member 22 reads back as a clean exit 0. The member loop is unordered with respect to importance, so a truncation lands wherever it lands. VERIFY THIS FIRST: re-run scoped and timed generously (launched 02:27Z as logs/witness_six.log over votefit's six) and see whether they verify at all.

IF THE TRUNCATION EXPLAINS IT, the tool still owns two defects: (1) it prints no per-member progress against a total, so a truncated sweep is indistinguishable from a complete one; (2) it exits without reconciling reported-vs-manifest, which is the same structural hole MountCheck.absent() just closed on mount_check — a per-item loop that cannot state what it did not reach.

IF IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT, then --fold -1 members are being dropped from the loop silently, which is worse: witness_check would be structurally unable to check the only members that ship, and knee-52mu (a --fold -1 member taking its witness from a holdout it does not have) would be only half-fixed — reporting UNVERIFIED for two members while dropping seven.

FIX EITHER WAY: reconcile the loop against the manifest and fail loudly on any member that produced no verdict, so 'checked' means 'checked all of them'.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-25 02:37Z, and it is BOTH branches, not one.

BRANCH A (my invocation) CONFIRMED. The task output's first line is `EXIT 124` — the 900 s timeout killed it at member 22 of 40, and my `; echo "EXIT $?"` reported the echo. So the 18-member silence was mine. The tool still owns the two defects that made it invisible: no progress-against-total, and no reconcile of reported-vs-manifest at exit. A cut sweep must not be indistinguishable from a complete one.

BRANCH B (the --fold -1 hole) ALSO CONFIRMED, and it is the P0 half. Re-ran scoped to votefit's six all-data members (logs/witness_six.log, 3000 s cap, ran to completion):

    final_ws_e12:     UNVERIFIED - no witness
    calib_span_ff:    UNVERIFIED - no witness
    grade_ladder_ff:  UNVERIFIED - no witness
    through_dense_ff: UNVERIFIED - no witness
    lr4e-5_ws_ff:     UNVERIFIED - no witness
    base_dense_ff:    UNVERIFIED - no witness
    0 ok, 6 unverified, 0 refused

So knee-52mu is NOT fixed, it is only DIAGNOSED. Every --fold -1 member still fails to record a witness, because the witness is taken from a holdout the member does not have. And --fold -1 members are 100 percent of what ships: dark6, dark7, allfit, lastseat, farseat and the armed votefit are all six-or-seven all-data rosters. The pre-submission gate CLAUDE.md describes as having 'found three defects on first use' is a NO-OP over every roster this project has put on the board since 2026-08-24.

THE FIX IS NOT 'skip them'. A witness only needs studies whose predictions can be compared between the fitting process and the serving process; it does not need HELD-OUT studies. Nothing about the check is a generalisation measurement. For --fold -1, take the witness from a fixed, seeded slice of the TRAIN studies. Same comparison, same tolerance, same meaning: does inference read this checkpoint the way training wrote it.

Splitting this bead: A (reconcile-and-fail-loudly) stays here; B gets its own P0.
CORRECTION 2026-08-25 02:40Z, to my own note above. Branch B is WRONGLY STATED there and the wrong version must not be the one that survives.

witness_check is NOT structurally unable to witness a --fold -1 member. The fix already landed, at kneemri/training/fitting.py:172-176: when `predicted is None` the witness is taken from `fold.training[:WITNESS_STUDIES]` and replayed through Trainer.predict. Seen studies, on purpose — the witness pins the READING (image size, slot list, decode resolution, window, precision), and a memorised study exposes a consumer-side default disagreeing with a recorded value exactly as well as an unseen one.

So the six all-data members read UNVERIFIED for a TEMPORAL reason, not a structural one: they were fitted before 2026-08-24. Re-fitting them to earn a witness costs roughly seven card-hours and buys nothing, because their reading is already proven end-to-end by a stronger instrument than the witness — dark6, dark7, allfit and lastseat are four board entries built from exactly those six members, all four reading 0.937. A member that serves wrong does not land on a plateau with three siblings; weakseven demonstrates the board resolves member quality at twenty-nine points. NOT re-fitting is the decision, and it is recorded rather than left implicit.

That leaves only branch A as a real defect, and it is FIXED in this commit. comp/witness_check.py now logs 'checking N members' before the loop and indexes every verdict '[i/N]', so a run cut by a timeout says so in its own log instead of looking like a complete one. A reconcile against the loop's own membership raises SystemExit on any member that produced no verdict — unreachable while the loop is exhaustive, kept so that 'checked' is arithmetic rather than a property a later edit is trusted to preserve.

Closing on the fix. The UNVERIFIED-for-all-data-members state is expected and documented, not open work.

title: sided_tissue: sided pooling on an anatomically centred crop, the suspect sided_pool's row named and did not clear
description:
sided_pool read 0.8561 vs band_dense 0.8578, middle band, three side-defined targets moved a mean of -0.0004 with every interval spanning zero. Its ledger row verified the mechanism FIRED (head.proj.1.weight is (256,1152)=384x3 parts) and then named one live alternative to 'the idea is wrong': the config reads centre=image, crop_mm 130, so the centre column of the patch grid is the anatomical midline only if the crop is anatomically centred.

sided_tissue is that test: sided_pool's exact recipe plus --centre tissue. Fold 0, so the per-label columns can be read.

PRICE: ~75 min card + an UNDECODED cache axis (336px_20sl_tissue_0.1-0.9band) whose build cost is being measured before the arm is queued. Zero submission slots.

THE CONFOUND IS PARTIAL AND MEASURED: crop_centre.py has tissue-centroid-vs-image-centre at median 7mm, p90 18mm, max 32mm over 60 studies. Against a 130mm crop the half-width is 65mm, so the median study is off by 11% of a half. That blurs the worst tenth, it does not destroy the median split. Honest prediction is a partial recovery of a small effect. The 0.8500-0.8579 band (flat) is pre-registered as the most likely outcome.

WHY IT IS WORTH THE CARD ANYWAY: the pot is the largest lever written down in this repo and the only one clearing the 1.5% bar. 2026-08-14_the-ruler-was-five-times-too-small measures the four weakest labels over the full corpus (Lateral Meniscus 0.7981, PF OA 0.8165, MCL 0.8166, Lateral OA 0.8215) and prices lifting them to 0.87 at +0.0189 on the twelve-label mean. Three of the four are side-defined.

AND IT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE: dark6 read 0.937 with six all-data members and nothing else, tying allfit/lastseat which are those six plus a seventh, so the marginal member is inert and ensembling is saturated. Per-label profiles correlate +0.92 within a fold, so every member is weak on the same labels and no vote can fix a deficit they all share. It has to be trained out.

NOT TRIED, on policy: the small-weight side regulariser side_dense deferred to 'a head that sees position'. That is loss-engineering aimed at a named weakness.
notes:
PRICE: ~75 min of card plus a one-off cache build on the undecoded axis 336px_20sl_tissue_0.1-0.9band, and ZERO submission slots. P(clears the 1.5% bar on the twelve-label mean) ~ 0.05. P(the three side-defined columns move together by more than their intervals) ~ 0.25 — that is the reading this arm is actually bought for, and the pre-registration's most likely band is the flat one.
KILLED BEFORE RUNNING, on arithmetic over measurements the repo already had — and this is the reason to state the price out loud before starting.

The full price was not the ~75 min of training. sided_tissue lands on the undecoded reading axis 336px_20sl_tissue_0.1-0.9band, and experiments/README.md records a full cache build at about TWO HOURS. Real price ~3.25 h of card.

That forced the question of whether the suspect is even large enough to be the explanation, and it is not:

  336 px at ViT patch 14 = 24 patch columns, 12 per half, across a 130 mm crop = 5.4 mm per column.
  crop_centre.py measured the tissue centroid against the image centre over 60 studies at median 7 mm,
  p90 18 mm, max 32 mm. That is 1.3 columns at the median and 3.3 at p90.
  Contamination of each half is 1.3/12 = 11%, and a difference-of-means contrast attenuates by (1-2c),
  so about 78% of the true contrast survives for the median study and about 56% for the p90 study.

A confound that preserves 70-78% of the signal cannot flatten a real effect to -0.0004 with all three side-defined intervals spanning zero. So the image-centred crop is NOT why sided_pool read flat.

WHAT THIS PROMOTES: sided_pool's own reading stands, and it is stronger than its row claimed. Its docstring argued that a flat result is informative here in a way other pooling arms' were not, because the halves partition the grid so the head could form the patch mean and ADDITIONALLY the difference - one extra part, nothing removed. The head could have ignored the split and did. With the crop suspect now quantitatively excluded, head-sees-position is REFUTED AT HALVES on this data rather than merely unconfirmed.

WHAT IT DOES NOT KILL: the finer grid (quadrants / compartment columns) rests on the same premise that just failed at halves, so it needs a NEW argument rather than a rerun. And it says nothing about the +0.0189 four-weak-label pot itself, which stays the largest lever in the repo and now has one fewer approach.

The arm script and its cache smoke are kept - the smoke wrote the truncated cache and read ok sided_tissue, 0 refused, so the axis is proven decodable if a later argument wants it.

title: mount_check --live reads only the first page of the members dataset, so it refuses valid kernels
description:
mount_check --live refused nearly every kernel in the tree tonight, including kneemri-allfit, whose members produced a COMPLETE 0.937 board entry earlier the same day. The refusals named members the LIVE dataset supposedly does not hold.

The dataset holds them. 'kaggle datasets files dimiturnt/kneemri-members' returns ~20 entries against 38 members because 20 is the CLI default page size; with --page-size 200 all 38 appear, small_batch6_ff included. The live check is comparing kernel tuples against page one of a paginated listing, so any member sorting past the first page reads as absent.

This is the gate written after the 2026-08-19 incident specifically to be the authoritative one - the local package check was green while Kaggle held something else, so --live was added to ask Kaggle directly. It asks, and then believes a truncated answer.

Two failure directions, and the quiet one is worse. Loud: a correct kernel is refused, which costs a submission window to diagnose (it cost one tonight). Quiet: the pagination happens to include the members a bad kernel names, and the check passes a kernel that should have been refused. A gate that is wrong in both directions is worse than no gate, because it is trusted.

Fix: request the full listing (page size high, or follow the next-page token until exhausted) and assert the returned count against the number of files the local package holds before comparing anything. If the listing cannot be shown to be complete, the check must say UNKNOWN rather than REFUSED.

title: mount_check is silent about a kernel directory that has no kernel-metadata.json
description:
kneemri-dark7 held a .py and no kernel-metadata.json. mount_check walked comp/kernels/ and reported '45 ok, 4 skipped, 1 refused' — dark7 in none of the three buckets, no line at all. It was found by grepping for a kernel that should have REFUSED (its tuple names small_batch6_ff, which the package does not yet hold) and finding no mention of it whatsoever.

A metadata-less directory is not an exotic state: it is exactly the state a kernel is in between being written and being pushed, which is the moment the check is run. Silence there reads as 'nothing to say about it' when the truth is 'this cannot be pushed at all' — push.sh kernel would have failed at the reset window with the slot clock running.

Fix: a directory under comp/kernels/ with a code file and no kernel-metadata.json is a REFUSAL, not an omission. Make the totals line account for every directory walked, so ok+skipped+refused equals the directory count and a missing bucket is arithmetically visible.

title: Add a convergence check to the arm harness: refuse to record a peak that lands on the last epoch run
description:
An audit of every metrics.jsonl on disk (2026-08-24) found 21 runs whose best epoch is at or one before their LAST epoch. Two of them - raddino_dense and vjepa_member - are outright crash readings that entered the ledger as facts about their architectures. A third, cnx_dense, peaked at e11 of 11 with loss still falling and was written up as 'the first non-transformer trunk, weak'; refitting its rate returned +0.0259 and produced a curve that peaks at e6 and DECLINES, which is what convergence looks like.

So the repo has three instances of the same defect and no gate against it, while it has nine gates against shipping defects. The asymmetry is the point: we check hard that a submission will BUILD and not at all that a number is FINISHED.

WHAT THE CHECK IS. After a run, compare the best epoch against the last epoch actually recorded, and against the epochs the recipe ASKED for. Three outcomes:
  - best epoch < last recorded, and last recorded == epochs asked -> CONVERGED, record normally.
  - last recorded < epochs asked -> TRUNCATED. The arm crashed or was killed. Refuse to write the score into the ledger as the recipe's number; label it a floor.
  - best epoch == last recorded == epochs asked -> UNDERTRAINED. The budget bound the result, not the recipe. Flag for a longer run or a fitted rate before the number is quoted.

The one_cycle=True schedule is what makes TRUNCATED distinct from merely short: stopping early stops in the high-LR portion, so the anneal that does the fine convergence never runs. A truncated run is not a shorter version of the same experiment.

Fits beside the existing nine checks (kneemri/experiments/*_check.py) and follows their convention: it guards a failure that has already happened, three times.
notes:
Built and in use: kneemri/experiments/convergence_check.py, documented in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as the check that guards a NUMBER rather than a shipment.

The bead's three outcomes are all in, plus two the build found necessary. STOPPED was added because the check's own FIRST corpus run reported ten truncations, three of which (res392_lr8e-6_ws, focal_pool, calibrated_targets) carry patience=3 and stopped at exactly e10 of 12 - the stopper working, not a kill. One of those is the res392 resolution refutation, so without reading the patience key the check would have re-opened a correctly-closed family. UNSCORED was added for --fold -1 members, which hold nothing back and so have no epoch to peak on.

Only TRUNCATED exits non-zero: an undertrained run is an honest measurement of a budget and its score is real; a truncated one is a crash whose score is a floor. Smokes (a studies cap) and one-epoch throughput probes are excluded - six of the fifteen the first reading reported were timing probes that never produced a member and diluted the actual finding.

Corpus today: 83 runs, 56 converged, 8 truncated, 3 stopped, 9 undertrained, 7 unscored. The three runs this bead was filed over read as filed: raddino_dense TRUNCATED (best e6 of 7 run, 12 asked), vjepa_member TRUNCATED (e9 of 10, 12 asked), cnx_dense UNDERTRAINED (e11 of 12, 12 asked).

title: raddino_dense 0.8137 is a CRASH READING, not RadDINO's score - the run died at epoch 7 of 12
description:
logs/raddino_dense.log and the arm driver both end mid-epoch-7 with 'ARM FAILED raddino_dense (trainer exit 1)'. The full log shows step 248/583 of epoch 7 at 448 img/s with loss still falling, no traceback, no OOM (27.14 GB peak on a 32 GB card). The process was killed externally on 2026-08-23 23:29, during the card-handoff window - it did not fail on its own merits.

The recorded 0.8137 is therefore the AUC at epoch 6 of a 12-epoch schedule, and it entered experiments/README.md as a fact about the RadDINO architecture ('raddino_dense ~0.82 extrapolated', line 2682).

WHY THE TRUNCATION IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT JUST A SHORT RUN. The recipe sets one_cycle=True over 12 epochs. Stopping at 7 stops in the high-LR portion of the schedule, so the anneal - where one-cycle does its fine convergence - never ran. Contrast v3base_dense, which also peaked at e6 but then RAN its remaining five epochs and never beat that peak: that is a converged measurement. RadDINO has no such evidence.

Its own curve (0.7247 0.7439 0.7852 0.7944 0.8000 0.8119 0.8137) is decelerating, so the honest estimate of the remaining gain is modest and uncertain, NOT the naive slope extrapolation.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. RadDINO is pretrained on medical images and is the most pixel-distant trunk in the pool. The champion pin's one surviving selection rule is that a pixel-distant seventh seat did best of five tried (0.932). kneemri-farswap, queued for the 00:00Z reset, tests exactly that hypothesis with a WEAK non-DINOv2 member (lora_r8, 0.8215). If farswap pays, a STRONG RadDINO is the follow-up member and it needs to exist.

COST: kneemri/training/fitted_encoder.py exists precisely for this - it converts a member checkpoint into an encoder another arm can start from, so the finish is a warm start from the e6 .pt rather than 12 epochs from scratch. ~1.65h warm (6 x 993s) vs ~3.3h cold.

DO NOT ARM WHILE THE CARD IS BIOHUB'S. logs/YIELD_CARD is on disk by agreement; gate this on farswap's board number first.

title: Seventh dark member: is the all-data dose saturated at six?
description: Three consecutive board entries (allfit 0.937, lastseat 0.937, augseat 0.936) exchanged the ONE fold-0 seat in a six-dark-plus-one ensemble and moved at most one tick. Seat identity, seat offline quality (a -0.0076 member bought the same number) and seat regularisation are all measured flat. The variable those entries HOLD FIXED is the count of dark members: exactly six exist, so no entry has ever had a seventh to offer, and count-at-fixed-dose and dose-at-fixed-count are the same unmeasured axis. small_batch6_ff converts the best member this project owns (0.8598) - and the exact member that held that seat in lastseat at 0.937, so its fold-0 behaviour in this ensemble is a measured control. Pre-registration lives in experiments/arms/small_batch6_ff.sh against lastseat's 0.937: >=0.939 dose still pays, 0.936-0.938 flat and the full-fit axis is CLOSED with a number instead of an extrapolation, <=0.935 indicts --ema/all-data and the harness is first suspect. Cost ~95 min of otherwise-dead overnight card. NOTE band_dense_long_ff stays unrun: allfit's own board entry pre-registers it null on the sub-linear dose reading, at 24 epochs / 7.3h.
notes:
PRICE: 95 min GPU (12 epochs x ~361 s x 4406/3497), in overnight wall-clock that is otherwise dead. GAIN if the dose still pays: +0.002 to +0.003 on the board, extrapolating the finalfit->allfit step (+0.003 for one seat -> six) onto a curve that has already read sub-linear. P(clears the 0.0015 board-resolvable) = 0.3. The ratio only prices as worth running because the wall-clock is free and because the FLAT outcome is itself the deliverable: it closes the only axis that has ever moved this board with a measurement instead of an extrapolation, and it is the prerequisite checkpoint for an eight-member all-dark entry that cannot be built until a seventh dark member exists.

STILL LIVE AFTER THE 2026-08-24 22:12Z GREEDY MEASUREMENT, and it is worth saying why, because that
measurement retired two other beads and looks at first glance like it retires this one too. The greedy
curve is flat within noise from seat 4 to seat 36, so member SELECTION is not a lever. It cannot speak to
this axis at all: greedy ranks members by a HOLDOUT record, and a dark member is fitted at --fold -1 with
no holdout, so no dark member has ever appeared on that curve. Count-of-dark-members is the one variable
every board entry has held fixed, and it stays unmeasured. Arming small_batch6_ff tonight on the freed
card.
RESULT 2026-08-25: dark7 = 0.937 against dark6 0.937. FLAT, the middle band this arm pre-registered, so the all-data dose is SATURATED AT SIX and the full-fit axis closes on a measurement rather than on allfit's sub-linear extrapolation.

The arm did what it was built to do. Its whole case was that COUNT-at-fixed-dose and DOSE-at-fixed-count are the same unmeasured axis and both needed one more _ff checkpoint; the checkpoint now exists and the axis is measured and closed. small_batch6_ff is the best member this project owns and adding it as a seventh all-data member moved the board zero.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the valuable half: this arm's own pre-registration said 'queue the second conversion immediately' ONLY on >= 0.939. 0.937 is not that, so band_dense_long_ff is NOT converted and roughly three hours of card (24 epochs) is not spent. A flat result that spends its own follow-up budget correctly is worth more than the 95 minutes it cost.

WIDER: four board entries now read exactly 0.937 - dark6 (6 dark), dark7 (6+1 dark), allfit and lastseat (6 dark + 1 fold-0). Member count, member identity and the seventh member's fold status all vary across them and the number does not. Recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_the_seventh_seat_is_inert_and_four_slots_measured_it.md.

title: Run an ACTUAL multilingual reader over the reports, locally, and gate it on the 58 annotations
description:
THE ONLY UNRUN SIZED LEVER LEFT. Every other axis is closed on this repo's own measurements: member selection (0/33 append, 0/19 displacement, peak8 board 0.932 under champion 0.937), per-label weighting (oracle ceiling +0.0002), slice depth (2 of 12 clear zero, chance predicts 0.6), slot coverage (extended_slots +0.0002), pooling operator (0.0019 span), SSL-as-init (five collapses), encoder capacity (base_dense 0.8512 vs small 0.8578 at 2.5x the card time), and the cheap severity/confidence proxies (knee-mxj, closed 2026-08-24, both read out backwards).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNRUN. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_the-corpus-is-not-english.md sizes it: 33.1% of the corpus carries severity vocabulary the current extraction path cannot see AT ALL, English is 40.1% of reports, and Spanish/Croatian/German/Dutch are 35.1% of reports converting at 1.5/0.0/2.7/2.6 percent. Its own closing line: 'whether better supervision on it clears the 1.5% bar is a training question, unrun.' knee-dbw states the repo runs NO language model at all - report_labels_v2.csv is a consumed rule-engine table whose __conf column is constant per verdict.

WHY IT COMPOUNDS. Our local ruler IS these labels, so a better table raises both what we train on and what we measure with. And the metric is a RANKING metric while severity is a ranking signal, which is the argument knee-mxj made and then could only test through regex proxies over the sentences the reader had already read.

NO CREDENTIAL NEEDED. There is no LLM API key on this machine. Run a multilingual instruct model LOCALLY on the 5090 instead - the HF token exists, the card is ours between arms, and 4,407 reports is a single-digit-GB pass.

THE GATE, BEFORE THE CORPUS PASS. Read only the 58 radiologist-annotated studies first. reader_agreement must beat the incumbent's 65.3%, and ordinal_signal must beat 0.741 mean over 12 labels. Both CLIs already exist and run in seconds. A candidate table is judged before anything is retrained on it.
close_reason: REFUTED before any card time, 2026-08-24. The premise was that report_labels_v2.csv is an English-pattern read leaving 33.1% of the corpus ungraded. Measured the severity spread of the three YES levels (0.68/0.82/0.94) BY REPORT LANGUAGE over all 4,407 studies: en .401/.399/.199, hr .435/.342/.223, es .331/.498/.170, tr .400/.412/.188, el .369/.404/.227, de .481/.326/.193, bg .456/.338/.207, nl .370/.379/.251. Every language grades at essentially the English rate. The table is already a multilingual read and there is no language gap in it to close. What 2026-08-17_the-corpus-is-not-english.md measured was report_language.SEVERITY - OUR English regex - not the labels we train on, so it read the TOOL's blind spot as a property of the DATA, which is the mistake its own Limits section names. Denominator discipline: the rate that matters is over the shipped label table, not over what a regex could locate.

title: The peak-8 was never shippable and no gate could see it
description: Every shipment gate passed while the uploaded dimiturnt/kneemri-members held only 5 of the 8 members of our best measured ensemble (0.8731 holdout): margin_seat was rostered-but-unpushed, sided_pool was in no roster line at all, crop80_span only inside a comment. champion_check guards the 0.937 entry's members; mount_check guards declared-vs-required encoders; kit_check guards the kit's commit distance. None of them asks whether the BEST OFFLINE SET is buildable. Fixed on 2026-08-24 (2cc4fc8) by rostering the two and repackaging. The GATE HOLE remains: add a check that the current greedy peak's members are all packaged, so the next peak cannot go unshippable silently.

title: Non-DINOv2 trunks were starved 189:1, and cnx_dense's own pre-registration was overruled by its write-up
description:
THE OWNER ASKED FOR THE DISTRIBUTION OF EFFORT ACROSS ARCHITECTURES. Counted 2026-08-24 over the 202 trained checkpoints on disk, by the variant stamped in each checkpoint's own options blob:

  131  small     DINOv2-small
   45  <unstamped, early; every filename reads adapt_small_* / *_small_*>  DINOv2-small
   11  base      DINOv2-base
    2  large     DINOv2-large
   10  v3small / v3base / v3splus   DINOv3   (9 real, 1 smoke)
    2  cnxbase   ConvNeXtV2   (ONE real run, cnx_dense_s2026; the other is cnx_smoke)
    1  vjepa2l   V-JEPA-2-large   (one run)

DINOv2 family ~189. ConvNeXt 1. V-JEPA 1. Ratio 189:1.

Arm scripts agree: 93 arms, 70 of which never set --variant at all and inherit the default .

WHY THE RATIO IS THE FINDING AND NOT A CURIOSITY. The 189 DINOv2 runs are where every recipe knob in this
project was tuned: read size, backbone LR, schedule, slice band, sampling, augmentation, batch, pooling.
The standing recipe is therefore a 189-run local optimum around DINOv2-small. It was then handed unchanged
to ConvNeXt once and to V-JEPA once, and their scores were written up as properties of those
architectures. They are not. They are measurements of our own tuning, charged to the trunk. Any trunk
would fail that test, DINOv2 included had the recipe been fitted to a CNN.

THE SPECIFIC OVERRULING, which is worse than the count. experiments/arms/cnx_dense.sh pre-registered four
outcomes before it ran. Verbatim:

  THE EXPENSIVE NEGATIVE - solo below 0.80. The head, the band and the slice pooling were all settled on
  token sequences from a patch-14 ViT; a 121-token grid may simply be too coarse for the slot head's
  spatial pooling, in which case the reading is about RESOLUTION and the retry is 448 px (a 14x14 grid)
  BEFORE THE TRUNK IS JUDGED.

cnx_dense scored 0.7927. That is below 0.80. The arm's own protocol fired the branch that says the result
is about resolution and the trunk is NOT yet judged. The 448 retry was never run. Instead
experiments/README.md:1607 titles the entry 'the first non-transformer trunk, and it closes encoder
diversity as an axis', and that sentence has since been quoted forward into an interpretation and into two
answers given to the owner. A pre-registration that is discarded when it fires is not a pre-registration.

SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME ARM: --backbone-lr 4e-5 is DINOv2's adapter rate handed unchanged to a
convolutional trunk. Convolutional trunks fine-tune at rates roughly an order of magnitude higher. LR was
never varied on this family - one point, one rate, chosen for a different architecture.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED ABOUT NON-DINOv2 TRUNKS: that they are FAR. knee-y59c measured distance
ordering exactly by architectural distance from DINOv2 across seven points with zero exceptions, and
cnx_dense is the most distant thing we own (nearest 0.7941 against a seated roster whose own spread floors
at 0.8724). The distance half of the owner's thesis is measured and holds. The quality half has never been
tested at a fair budget.

ACTIONS:
  1. Correct experiments/README.md:1607 - the title claims a closed axis on n=1 against n=189, and the
     entry must print that denominator and its own unrun retry branch.
  2. Run the pre-registered 448 px retry (knee-y59c).
  3. Run a CNN learning rate, which nothing has ever done.
  4. Do not quote 'encoder diversity is closed' anywhere until 2 and 3 have run.

title: Architecture diversity is a tradeoff CURVE, not a closed axis - and every non-DINOv2 trunk was trained on the DINOv2 recipe
description:
Every non-DINOv2 trunk this project has trained was trained on the DINOv2 recipe. Of 202 checkpoints on disk ~189 are DINOv2-family, one is ConvNeXt, one is V-JEPA. Read size, backbone LR, schedule, band, sampling, augmentation, batch and pooling were all tuned across those 189, so the standing recipe is a 189-run local optimum around DINOv2-small. Handing it unchanged to a convolutional trunk measures our tuning and charges the result to the architecture. See knee-zfgn for the count and for the pre-registration cnx_dense overruled.

Owns experiments/arms/cnx_own_recipe.sh: 448 px (a 14x14 grid, the retry cnx_dense itself pre-registered) and --backbone-lr 4e-4 (an order above the ViT adapter rate, and deliberately below ConvNeXtV2 published 6.25e-4 with layer decay), everything else the control.

PRICE: ~2.6 h of card for the arm, plus the smoke that writes the 448 truncated cache. P(clears 1.5% bar) 0.10-0.15. P(confirms the starvation, solo >= 0.83) 0.45-0.55. Justified as an INSTRUMENT first rather than as an improvement: either branch retires the 189:1 confound, which currently sits under every statement this repo makes about encoder diversity, including two answers already given to the owner. A refuting run licenses setting the convolutional family aside with the denominator printed next to it, which nothing today licenses.
notes:
Raised because the owner asked, for at least the second time, whether ensembling DIFFERENT ARCHITECTURES
is the better lever. Both previous answers were given from memory and quoted SOLO SCORES. This one was
measured: every non-DINOv2 trunk with a holdout record, priced against greedy7_v1's seven members on
BOTH rulers, card-free.

  member                trunk                 nearest   solo
  mae_matched           MAE pretraining       0.4333    0.6735
  cnx_dense             ConvNeXt (CNN)        0.7941    0.7927
  vjepa_warm            V-JEPA 3D tubelet     0.8212    0.8337
  lora_r8_v3small       DINOv3 + LoRA         0.8455    0.8217
  dinov3_base_lora      DINOv3 + LoRA         0.8467    0.8268
  v3base_dense          DINOv3 full fine-tune 0.8829    0.8512
  distill_pairs         DINOv2 self-distill   0.9159    0.8594

  roster of 7, its own nearest-neighbour spread: 0.8724 .. 0.8893

THE FINDING. Distance orders EXACTLY by architectural distance from DINOv2, across seven points with no
exception: a different pretraining objective is farthest, then a different inductive bias, then a
different input geometry, then a frozen base of the same family, then a fine-tuned base of the same
family, then the same family distilled from itself. That is not scatter around a mean; it is a curve, and
