it is the owner's thesis measured rather than asserted. Architecture diversity does produce genuinely
different orderings here, and the amount scales with how different the architecture is.

THE OTHER HALF, on the SAME seven points. Solo score is monotone in the opposite direction. Farther trunk,
weaker member. Distance and strength are anti-correlated across the entire axis, which is why every
individual arm read as a refutation: each one bought its distance with quality and was judged on quality
alone.

WHAT NOBODY TESTED, and why the axis is not closed. Every non-DINOv2 trunk in that table was trained on
the recipe tuned for DINOv2 - dense sampling, 336, the same schedule and the same learning rate. A CNN
trunk and a tubelet trunk have different optimal read sizes, different LR scales, and in the tubelet case
a different token geometry (prefix_tokens = 0, no class token, no registers). The measured weakness is
therefore confounded with recipe transfer and cannot be charged to the architecture. Faulty TRAINING is
a live suspect and it has never been eliminated on this axis.

So the correct statement is NOT "architecture diversity does not pay" - it is "architecture diversity has
only ever been measured at points where the recipe was wrong for the trunk". No arm has tried to move the
curve; every arm sampled a point on it.

WHAT MOVES IT. Pick the trunk whose distance is largest among those still worth rescuing, and give it its
own recipe rather than DINOv2's. cnx_dense at nearest 0.7941 is 0.078 more distant than any seated member
is from its own nearest neighbour, and it is a CNN, so the knobs that are wrong for it are nameable in
advance rather than searched: read size, LR scale, and the pooling that assumes patch tokens.

BANDS, pre-registered before any number exists:
  solo >= 0.85 with nearest still under 0.82  -> the distant-and-strong member knee-053z asked for, and
      the recipe was the confound all along. Ship it and re-open every trunk in the table.
  solo >= 0.85 with nearest risen above 0.87  -> the recipe bought quality by making it a DINOv2 twin.
      Distance and strength are genuinely exclusive here. Axis closes, correctly this time.
  solo 0.83-0.85                              -> recipe transfer was part of it but not all of it; needs
      a slot, not another offline reading.
  solo still under 0.82                       -> recipe was not the confound. Charge it to the trunk.

Depends on knee-u0my only in ordering, not in logic - u0my tests the same confound one step milder (same
family, different adaptation). This one tests it at the far end of the curve.

CAVEAT that must travel with any use of the distance ruler: it has ONE paired board observation behind it
(the 2026-08-21 split). It is quoted as a RANKING, never as a price.

CORRECTION, same hour, after reading the rows this was filed against (experiments/README.md 1607-1664 and
2532-2544) rather than recalling them.

1. The recipe confound was NOT unnoticed. `raddino_dense` raised it on 2026-08-23: "a new trunk plugged into
   a recipe that was fitted around DINOv3 ... every trunk swap needs its own tuning pass before it can be
   read at all." It was set aside on cost, not refuted. This bead's contribution is the distance measurement,
   not the confound.

2. The knobs named above are wrong for cnx_dense. Read size is dead on three independent readings (equal
   focal/regional deltas to four decimals; `resolution` at 392 scored +0.0002; the 448 retry was explicitly
   killed). Schedule and LR are dead too - the underfit claim was refuted hard enough to retitle knee-9otf.

3. What survives, from the arm's own trajectory: at MATCHED TRAIN LOSS cnx_dense holds 0.7927 at loss 0.8332
   where base_dense holds 0.8371 at loss 0.8456. A 0.044 generalisation gap at EQUAL FIT - it fits better and
   generalises worse. That rules out an under-driven trunk and points at REGULARISATION, which is the one
   knob on this arm nothing has tested. DINOv2's recipe carries generalisation in the pretrained
   representation and so needs little augmentation; a CNN fine-tuned end-to-end from ImageNet weights on
   ~1.5k studies is a different regime.

4. What today's number refutes is a SENTENCE, not a knob: cnx_dense's entry closes with "a different
   inductive bias is not a different error structure. The axis closes." Nearest 0.7941 against a spread
   bottoming at 0.8724 says a different inductive bias produced the MOST different error structure this
   project has. The entry showed it was a WORSE one, which stands; it never showed it was a SIMILAR one, and
   the quality ruler could not have.

REVISED BANDS for the cnx retry - augmentation strength only, everything else at the arm's own settings:
  solo >= 0.84 with nearest still under 0.82 -> regularisation was the confound. Distant-and-strong exists.
  solo >= 0.84 with nearest above 0.87       -> quality was bought by becoming a DINOv2 twin. Axis closes.
  solo 0.80-0.84                             -> partial; needs a slot, not another offline reading.
  solo still under 0.80                      -> charge it to the trunk. Axis closes on the right evidence.
PRICE, added 2026-08-24 because arm_check refused cnx_own_recipe as UNPRICED and it was right to.

COST: ~2.5 h of card for the 12-epoch arm, plus a two-minute 60-study smoke to write the 448 px truncated
cache and price the memory. The seat measurement afterwards is card-free (record_mix over holdout records).
Call it 2.6 h of card, one arm, zero submission slots.

GAIN IF IT LANDS: cnx_dense is the most distant member this project owns — nearest 0.7941 against a seated
roster whose own spread floors at 0.8724, i.e. 0.078 beyond anything seated. The strong-and-distant
quadrant has been empty since the project began and is the only unexhausted cell on the ensemble axis
(seat, vote and count are all measured flat; three board entries on 2026-08-24 read 0.936/0.937/0.936
across single-seat exchanges). A seatable convolutional member is worth more than its own seat value,
because it reopens a FAMILY that currently has one run in it against DINOv2's ~189 (knee-zfgn) — an LR
sweep, augmentation strength and schedule all become live, each decomposed against a member that works.

P(clears the 1.5% bar) — LOW ON THIS ARM ALONE, call it 0.10-0.15, and the arm is not justified on that
number. One seat at seven has never moved the board more than a tick here. What it is justified on is the
OPTION it buys: P(solo clears 0.83, i.e. the starvation is confirmed and the family earns a budget) is
much higher, call it 0.45-0.55 — two corrections argued from the architecture, against a baseline that ran
at a fifth of the slot head's fitted spatial support and at a ViT adapter's learning rate.

SO IT IS AN INSTRUMENT FIRST AND A MEMBER SECOND, and it must be read that way. It retires a suspicion —
that 'encoder diversity is closed' was a measurement of our own tuning — and it either licenses re-running
the whole trunk axis at a fair budget or closes it with the denominator finally printed. A refutation here
is worth nearly as much as a confirmation, which is what makes 2.6 h the right price: the alternative is
carrying an unfalsified 189:1 confound through every future ensemble decision.

RATIO AGAINST THE STANDING ALTERNATIVE. NCL (knee-2f0q) is ~1.3 h and attacks the same empty quadrant from
the strong side. It ranks BELOW this one now, not on expected member quality but because it inherits the
same recipe and therefore cannot test the confound. Fixing the measurement comes before adding to it.
2026-08-24, EXTERNAL EVIDENCE FOR THE TRUNK HALF, gathered after the 189:1 count.

Three consecutive RSNA Kaggle first-place solutions on 3D volumes name their backbone, and none of them is a ViT:
  2022 cervical spine - EfficientNet-V2-S or ConvNeXt.
  2023 abdominal trauma - CoaT Lite or EfficientNet-V2-S.
  2024 lumbar spine - ConvNeXt-S or EfficientNet-V2-S.
Convolutional or hybrid trunks win this competition series three years running, on volumetric medical data, at Kaggle scale. That is not proof they beat DINOv2 here, but it removes the reading that our one 0.7927 ConvNeXt run reflects the family. It is the same trunk family that took three of these, run once, on a recipe fitted to something else.

EfficientNet-V2-S has NEVER been tried in this repo - it is not in backbone.py's variant table at all, despite appearing in all three winning solutions. That is a second starved trunk sitting behind the first, and it is CHEAP relative to ConvNeXtV2-base (87.7M): V2-S is ~21M and gradient-checkpointable, so it prices in well under cnx_own_recipe's memory bill.

Both winners' solutions also pair the trunk with a SEQUENCE head over slices, which is knee-blvm. The two are independent - do not confound them in one arm. cnx_own_recipe tests the recipe confound on the trunk axis alone and should finish before a trunk-plus-head arm is designed.
PRICE (2026-08-24 17:45Z) — WALL-CLOCK / EXPECTED GAIN

COST: ~3.0-3.5 h card. cnx_dense measured 519-727 s/epoch at train-size 352; this arm runs 448
(1.62x the pixels) for 12 epochs. The earlier '~2.5 h' estimate did not scale for resolution.
CHEAP KILL AT ~1.2 h: cnx_dense read 0.7659 / 0.7681 at epochs 3 / 4. With a 10x backbone LR the
curve must be clearly above that by epoch 4 or the mechanism did not fire; kill there, not at 12.

MECHANISM (corrected today — the ledger's stated suspect was wrong):
The architecture section names augmentation strength as 'the one knob on this arm that nothing has
tested', reasoning from a 0.044 generalisation gap at matched train loss (cnx_dense 0.7927 at loss
0.8332 vs base_dense 0.8371 at loss 0.8456) — read as a regularisation regime that does not transfer.
logs/cnx_dense.log refutes that reading. Its holdout is MONOTONE RISING to the final epoch:
  e0 0.7050 -> e6 0.7858 -> e8 0.7921 -> e10 0.7927 -> e11 0.7927, train loss still falling steeply.
No turnover in 12 epochs. That is an UNDER-TRAINED curve, not an over-fitted one. The matched-loss
comparison holds two different points on two different trajectories side by side; it shows ConvNeXt
converts loss into AUC more slowly, not that it overfits. Adding --intensity-aug would slow a model
that never finished climbing. The arm is therefore left EXACTLY as written: backbone-lr 4e-5 -> 4e-4
is the standard fix for a monotone-rising fine-tune, and it is the one this arm already carries.

GAIN: the prize is the strong-and-distant cell, which margin_seat just proved pays. cnx_dense sits at
nearest-neighbour 0.7941 against a roster whose most distant SEATED member reads 0.8724 — 0.078
outside the spread, the largest of any member that did not collapse, i.e. the most different error
structure in this project. It is unseated only because it is weak (solo 0.7927, greedy 63rd of 65).
margin_seat took 2nd of 65 from nearest 0.8628. A member 0.06-0.08 MORE distant at comparable quality
is plausibly worth more than margin_seat's seat, and no other live lever offers that much distance.

ODDS: ~40% it reaches usable quality (0.84+). The trajectory says the headroom exists and the LR is
the conventional lever, but 10x is a large step and may destabilise instead. ~50% that a usable
member then takes a seat, given the distance it starts from. So ~20% for a seat-grade member at
~3 h, with the kill at 1.2 h capping the loss on the other 80%.

VERDICT: run it. Best available ratio, our own data, no licence blocker, and it is the unrun
architecture plan rather than a fourth exchange of an already-null axis.

ATTRIBUTION LIMIT, stated up front: this arm varies THREE things against cnx_dense (LR 10x,
352->448, batch 2/accum 3 -> batch 1/accum 6 at equal effective batch 6). If it works we will not
know which knob did it without an ablation. That is deliberate stage-gating — at the finding stage
the question is whether ConvNeXt reaches usable quality AT ALL, and isolating three knobs costs
~9 h to answer a question worth asking only after the answer is yes.

BAR REPLACED 2026-08-24 18:15Z, by knee-98y2. The pre-registered test written yesterday was
"~0.85 solo to be a candidate, then peak8 + it > 0.8731". That bar is now known to be a test
NOTHING passes: 33 candidates spanning solo 0.79-0.857 and nearest 0.769-0.951 all land below
0.8731, and 12 of them also fail an exhaustive single-swap against the peak. A bar with a 0/33
pass rate prices no member.

REPLACEMENT - DISPLACEMENT TEST. When cnx_own_recipe finishes, put its holdout record into the
FULL pool and re-run the greedy from scratch:
  record_mix --records <full pool + cnx_own_recipe> --seats greedy
KEEP if the new peak > 0.8731. Solo AUC is no longer a gate at any value - a member that cannot
append can still rebuild the set around itself, and that is the only remaining way in.

This also retires the epoch-4 solo-AUC kill checkpoint. There is nothing a mid-run solo number can
decide any more; the run goes to completion (~21:05Z) or dies on a failure signature.

TRAJECTORY SO FAR. epoch 0: loss 0.6218 / holdout 0.7314 / 970s, against cnx_dense's epoch 0
loss 1.2612 / 0.7050 / 519s. The 10x LR fired: half the loss, +0.026 AUC, and NOT collapsed to the
prior (that would read ~0.5). But half the loss for a quarter of the gain is the same conversion
pathology cnx_dense showed, now at higher fit. 970s/epoch x 12 = 3.2h.
epoch 1: loss 0.6132 holdout 0.7394 (922s). Loss essentially flat from epoch 0 (-0.0086) while AUC gains 0.008 - near its loss floor at epoch 1 with AUC at 0.739, where cnx_dense still had 0.43 of loss headroom. One-cycle anneal can still produce a late jump. No mid-run kill under the displacement bar; runs to ~21:05Z.
2026-08-25, discussion topic 735826 via kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read - an OUTSIDE controlled comparison on the same competition data, and it points the same way this bead does.

A competitor froze their CPU preprocessing as a control (all 4,407 studies to a fixed (4407, 6, 9, 224, 224) uint8 cache) and changed ONLY the representation side:
  - pretrained ResNet34 pipeline: OOF BCE ~0.664
  - pretrained DINOv2-Small with diagnosis-specific slot attention, same cache and same labels: OOF BCE ~0.674 (rank correlation ~0.391)
i.e. moving to DINOv2 made it WORSE on their harness. Their conclusion: 'compute cost and model size are poor proxies for useful information; a more expensive model can simply process the same imperfect input more expensively.' The thread's opening post reports the same pattern from several people - single DINO models reach ~0.91-0.92, and increasing encoder size does not improve CV (which is knee-7u5's finding from outside, and knee-155's +0.0011 scaling result from outside).

CAVEATS BEFORE THIS IS USED AS EVIDENCE FOR A TRUNK SWAP: their DINOv2 arm carries a slot-attention head we do not run, so trunk and head moved together; BCE is not our metric; and their ResNet34 recipe is presumably the one they tuned. It does NOT show ResNet34 beats DINOv2. What it does show is that a serious competitor got a NON-DINOv2 trunk to a competitive number on this exact corpus, which is the premise this bead was blocked on - our own non-DINOv2 trunks were starved 189:1 (knee-zfgn), so we have never made that comparison at parity either.

title: LoRA-v3 at the dense recipe and 336 — the distant-and-strong cell nobody ran, and the v3 axis was closed on the wrong member
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-24, card-free, against the CURRENT roster of seven (greedy7_v1, 0.933):

  roster's own nearest-neighbour spread: 0.8724 (most distant seated, calib_span) .. 0.8893 (worst)

  candidate            seat      nearest   solo
  lora_r8_v3small_224  -0.0013   0.8455    0.8217
  dinov3_base_lora     -0.0009   0.8467    0.8268
  v3base_dense         -0.0006   0.8829    0.8512

THE TWO LoRA-v3 MEMBERS ARE MORE DISTANT FROM THIS ROSTER THAN ANY SEATED MEMBER IS FROM ITS OWN NEAREST NEIGHBOUR, by 0.027. By member_distance.py's own stated rule that is 'genuinely new information'.

WHY THIS WAS MISSED, and it is a reasoning error not a measurement one. The v3 axis was closed on 2026-08-21 with the verdict 'a second ViT of a different family does not buy a second diversity seat'. That verdict was reached: (a) on v3base_dense, which this reading shows is the ONE v3 member that is NOT distant — 0.8829 sits inside the roster's own spread; (b) against a roster of FIVE (basedense_v1, 0.8690) that no longer exists, now seven with two members changed; (c) using the QUALITY ruler alone, on the same day MemberDistance was built to answer exactly this question, and never re-read with it. The ledger's own text already warned about (b)/(c): 'The -0.0007 is not evidence that a v3base seat would cost a tick; it is evidence that this ruler cannot tell.' The caveat was written and then the verdict was quoted without it.

THE MECHANISM FOR THE DISTANCE. LoRA freezes the base, so the member keeps DINOv3's representation instead of being fine-tuned toward the solution every other member converges on. That is a reason for a member to disagree, and it predicts exactly the ordering measured: both LoRA members distant, the full fine-tune ordinary. The ledger read the same pair as an ADAPTATION finding ('DINOv3 is weak was an adaptation finding wearing an encoder name', v3base_dense +0.0187 over its LoRA sibling) and was right about quality — but the adaptation that scores WORSE is the one that is DISTANT, and nothing charged that to diversity.

THE UNISOLATED VARIABLE, which is what makes this runnable. v3base_dense and dinov3_base_lora differ on TWO things: LoRA-vs-full-FT, AND 224 -> 336 plus the dense recipe. The +0.0244 was charged entirely to adaptation. base_dense -> v3base_dense shows what the dense recipe alone is worth on this trunk. NOBODY HAS RUN LoRA + DENSE RECIPE + 336.

THE ARM: dinov3_base_lora's LoRA config at v3base_dense's read, slices, band and schedule. Cheaper than full FT (base frozen, no backbone grads) against v3base_dense's 680 s/epoch; budget ~1.5 h for 12 epochs.

PRE-REGISTERED, before any number exists:
 - solo >= 0.85 AND nearest < 0.88 -> the distant-and-strong member knee-053z asked for. This is the seat. Ship it.
 - solo >= 0.85 AND nearest >= 0.88 -> the recipe bought quality by making it a twin. That is the whole trade and it fails; the v3 axis really is closed and this time on the right member.
 - solo < 0.84 with nearest still ~0.85 -> distant-and-weak, same as vjepa_warm. LoRA's distance is real and unusable; stop paying for it.
 - solo 0.84-0.85 -> the split is genuine and the seat needs a slot to settle, not another offline reading.

BLOCKED ON THE CARD ONLY: margin_seat then dissent_seat own it to ~17:30Z. Ranks above knee-3ped (V-JEPA larger read): same distance argument, cheaper arm, and the weakness here has a NAMED cause rather than a suspected ceiling.
notes:
PRICE (2026-08-24, required by arm_check's UNPRICED clause and by CLAUDE.md's wall-clock-over-gain rule).

COST: ~2.2-2.6 h of card. `v3base_dense` ran ~750-850 s/epoch over 12 epochs on this exact recipe and
encoder; LoRA removes the optimiser state and the weight gradients but the backward still traverses the
whole trunk to reach the early adapters, so expect a modest step-time saving, not a large one. Note this
CORRECTS an earlier verbal estimate of ~40 min, which came from `dinov3_base_lora`'s 224 px / 12 slices /
batch 12 shape. This arm runs the DENSE recipe - 336 px, 20 slices, batch 6 - which is where the cost is.

GAIN IF IT LANDS: a member 0.027 outside the roster's own nearest-neighbour spread that is also strong
enough to seat. No member the project holds is both. `raddino_dense`'s entry states why that is the thing
worth buying: the greedy curve peaks at seats 8-10 and declines after, so the ensemble does not want
another member - it wants one that does something none of the existing ones can. Plausible board size is
one to two ticks, i.e. roughly +0.001 to +0.004. That is UNDER the owner's 1.5% bar on its own and is not
sold as clearing it; it composes against the original baseline and, more importantly, it is an INSTRUMENT
- it decides whether distance and strength can coexist on this data at all, which licenses or retires the
entire architecture axis (knee-y59c, knee-053z, the cnx retry) behind one reading.

P(CLEARS +0.0015 SEAT VALUE): call it 0.25-0.35. The anti-correlation between distance and strength held
across all seven measured points, which is the honest reason to price it low. What argues the other way is
that no point on that curve was ever measured with the recipe matched to the trunk, and this is the
cheapest place to test that - same encoder family, same recipe, one regime moved.

RATIO: ~2.4 h for a ~30% shot at a small board gain plus a near-certain axis verdict either way. The axis
verdict is what justifies it, not the tick. Ranked ABOVE the cnx regularisation retry (knee-y59c, similar
2-3 h) because it is a strict single-variable isolation against a control we already hold at 0.8512,
whereas the cnx retry has to search an augmentation setting with no matched control at the new setting.
Both were mispriced relative to each other in conversation when this one was quoted at 40 min; on the
corrected numbers the ordering survives on MERIT rather than on cost.

PRICE: ~2.4 h of card (12 epochs at ~750-850 s, LoRA trims the backward modestly) for a seat that no
existing member can occupy - distant AND strong - plus a near-certain verdict on whether those two can
coexist on this data at all, which licenses or retires knee-y59c, knee-053z and the cnx retry behind one
reading. P(clears +0.0015 seat value) ~ 0.30: low because distance and strength were anti-correlated
across all seven measured trunks, and not lower because no point on that curve was ever measured with the
recipe matched to the trunk, which is exactly what this arm moves. The axis verdict is what buys the card,
not the tick.
2026-08-25 14:24Z — ARM LAUNCHED AND KILLED AT STEP 85, NOT RUN. The number does not exist and this bead stays open as untried.

Two real defects were found and FIXED before it ever started, and both are worth keeping: the arm's VRAM paragraph was wrong (LoRA does not cut activation memory — the backward still traverses all 72 layers to reach the early adapters, so every trunk activation is held and the adapters add their own; memory here is bought by token count, not parameter count), and it OOMed at the default cap. --eager-encoder took allocated 25.75 -> 22.53 GiB and --vram-gb 29.5 made it fit. The smoke then passed clean (0.5269 over 11 of 12 labels, 189 s). Those edits are committed in 54c7530 and the arm is launchable.

WHY IT DIED, and it is not the recipe: the card was BIOHUB'S, granted by me in writing at 12:12Z ('take it for as long as you want it'). I launched onto it at 14:09Z having checked only nvidia-smi, which read momentarily free. With both of us resident the device sat at 31964 of 32607 MiB and Windows paged over PCIe rather than failing: throughput 198 -> 27 -> 13 img/s across fifteen minutes. Killed 14:24Z, fault letter sent to their inbox, device released (10067 MiB at 95% = them alone).

CONSEQUENCE FOR --vram-gb 29.5: it is correct ONLY on an idle card. 30208 MiB against 31045 free leaves ~800 MiB of device slack, which is not slack when anyone else is resident. The next launch of this arm must be on a card that is ours, and lib.sh:256's physics is symmetric — the 20-slice recipe derives 28.3 GB, so a co-tenant of any size denies it AND it denies any co-tenant.

RE-PRICED AGAINST knee-uco3 BEFORE IT IS RE-LAUNCHED. dark6 (six all-data members, no seventh) reads 0.937, the same plateau every seventh-seat entry read. So this arm's PREDICTION branch — 'ship it' — is a seventh seat and is worth ~0 board points on that measurement. What survives is its INSTRUMENT value: it is the only test of whether distance and strength can coexist on one member, and the REFUTATION branch (strong AND near) retires the v3 axis honestly. It also trains at fold 0 while the champion is six --fold -1 members, so shipping it would need a second ~3 h all-data refit on top. Re-price that chain against the card's real availability before spending ~6 h on it.

FAILURE READ, 2026-08-25 15:30Z. The arm died at 14:14Z and it was NOT contention. The run's own
heartbeat says so in its log: `STALLED: 5 img/s against this run's own peak of 230 - 213 MiB free
against 755 at the start, so no foreign process arrived - this is our own footprint against this card`.
It reached step 86 of 583, then Windows began paging GPU memory over PCIe and the trainer exited 1.

THE FIRST OOM AND THIS STALL ARE DIFFERENT FAILURES AND THE SECOND ONE IS FRAGMENTATION, NOT VOLUME.
The header's fix for the first (`--eager-encoder --vram-gb 29.5`) worked on the axis it named: the
inductor buffer is gone. The numbers the eager smoke then reported:

    v3lora_dense smoke   28.77 GB reserved   24.38 GB allocated     (LoRA r8, eager)
    v3base_dense         ~27.85 GB reserved  25.38 GB allocated     (full FT, same shape, RAN FINE)

Allocated is LOWER than the control that fits. What is higher is RESERVED - 4.39 GB held by the
allocator and not handed to a tensor. So this arm is not asking for more memory than its control; it is
asking for it in a shape the caching allocator cannot pack. `--vram-gb 29.5` then left only ~800 MiB of
DEVICE slack, and the residual grew into it until the card had 213 MiB and started paging.

Gradient checkpointing is ALREADY ON (`recompute_activations: True` in the failing run's own recipe
line), so the memory-for-compute trade is already spent and is not the lever.

THE NEXT LAUNCH IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A GUESS, AND THE SMOKE IS THE ORACLE. The 60-study smoke runs the
same batch, slice count and token count as the arm, so it reproduces the peak exactly - it is where the
28.77 above was measured - and it costs 189 s. Two smokes, ~7 min of card:

  1. as-is, to confirm the peak is stable rather than a one-off;
  2. with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`.

lib.sh records expandable_segments as unhelpful on this machine, but all three arms it records were
short of ALLOCATED memory, which that setting does not create. This one is short of PACKING, which is
the case it exists for. If the reserved-minus-allocated gap closes, the arm runs at the recipe the
single-variable argument requires and nothing about the arithmetic moves. If it does not close, the arm
does not fit on this card at this recipe and that has to be said plainly rather than worked around with
a batch change - `--batch 3 --accumulate 2` is still refused for the reason the header gives (it halves
the ranking term's pair population, which is a second variable in a one-variable arm).

title: arm_check cannot see a flag an arm OMITS relative to its declared control
description:
distill_pairs.sh declared 'the control is band_dense byte-for-byte' and 'ONE VARIABLE: --distill-weight', then omitted --backbone-lr and silently trained at the trainer default 8e-6 against a control at 4e-5. It passed arm_check ('1 arms checked, 0 refused, 0 uncached'), smoked clean, and burned ~75 min of card producing an uninterpretable number. arm_check validates that the flags PRESENT are real; it has no notion of the flags that should be present.

The control is already declared machine-readably: every arm carries a '# control  <name> = <score>' line near the bottom (distill_pairs.sh, distill_v3base.sh both do). So the check is buildable: parse the arm's control line, read that control arm's run_train flag set, diff the two, and REFUSE on any flag that differs or is absent without an explicit '# deliberate: <flag>' waiver in the arm. An arm that legitimately moves two things then has to say so in writing, which is the point.

Prior art for the detector already exists downstream: kneemri.evaluation.run_comparison prints exactly this diff ('vs control: backbone_lr 4e-05->8e-06') — but AFTER the card is spent. This bead is about moving that diff to BEFORE.

Audit note: a sweep of all 90 arms shows ~30 with no --backbone-lr at all. Most are analysis tools (build_cache, attribution, diversity_curve, vjepa_probe) or pre-date the 4e-5 era, so MISSING is not by itself a defect — it is a defect only where the arm names a 4e-5 control. That distinction is precisely what the proposed check encodes and what a human eye does not reliably do.
notes:
2026-08-24: BUILT. arm_check now parses the arm's own '# control  <name> = <score>' line, resolves that control's run_train flag set out of the same stub-lib sweep, and diffs the two — reporting every flag that differs or is ABSENT relative to the control.

An arm is supposed to differ, so the diff alone is not the defect; an UNDECLARED diff is. Each moved flag needs one '# deliberate: <flag>' line in the arm's header. That is the check, and it costs the author one line per variable — which is also the moment they notice the arm moves three things.

Asymmetry copied from report_prices, and for the same reason: 32 of 100 arms differ from a named control without declaring it, and nearly all of them already ran. The full sweep prints the COUNT and passes; '--only <arm>' names the flags and REFUSES. The defect only costs a card at the moment an arm is armed, and the run that arms one is the run that names it.

Details: values compare numerically where both parse as float (4e-5 == 4e-05, which would otherwise be a diff nobody reads twice). --out/--labels/--paths are INCIDENTAL and excluded. A control the sweep cannot resolve to an arm (wsfold0_e6 and friends are CHECKPOINT names, 15 arms) is skipped rather than reported — a missing comparison, not a wrong one. CONTROL_LINE requires the '=' because five headers open prose with 'control is the same recipe...'.

Verified on the three live arms: distill_pairs now reports only its two real variables (its --backbone-lr was fixed by hand after the incident, so the check correctly no longer flags it), dissent_seat three, margin_seat two; all three now carry their '# deliberate:' lines and pass.

title: Volumetric encoder: the one through-plane mechanism the aggregation sweep did NOT test
description:
Carried out of knee-yuqf's closure rather than folded into it, per the standing rule that a refuting experiment kills a USE of an asset and not the asset. What depth_true refuted is through-plane mixing at the FEATURE level: the encoder sees one slice at a time, emits a per-slice vector, and only then does an order-aware aggregator get to mix across depth. Four combining rules on the settled recipe now span 0.0019 (max 0.8457, depth gate 0.8461, mean 0.8473, permutation-blind gate 0.8476), more slices moves -0.0001 and more slots +0.0002. Three directions, all flat: the aggregation STAGE is saturated and the limit sits UPSTREAM, in what a single slice's feature vector contains.

A volumetric encoder is a different mechanism and is untested here. It sees the stack before any per-slice feature exists, so through-plane structure can shape the representation rather than being reconstructed from vectors that already discarded it. MRI is 3D and every arm this project has ever run treats it as a bag of 2D pictures.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE OF LEVER. It is a data/architecture change, not a knob, and it is the only member type that would be structurally unlike the seven-member pool along an axis the offline ruler is known to under-price (knee-avzz, 2.4x). It is also the honest reading of the member-population exhaustion result: 11/11 arms negative on the mean says the tuning is done, not that the encoder is.

WHAT MUST BE ANSWERED BEFORE ANY CARD IS SPENT (audit first, per the standing order):
  1. Which volumetric encoder, and does a pretrained one exist that is worth more than a randomly-initialised 3D net on 3,526 studies? Candidates to READ on, not assume: video ViT / VideoMAE with the depth axis as time, a 3D ResNet on medical pretraining, or 2.5D (slice triplets into the 3-channel input) which is the CHEAPEST probe of the same mechanism and may be runnable inside the current recipe with almost no new code.
  2. VRAM. The settled 20-slice 2D recipe already derives 28.3 GB of a 32.6 GB card. A volumetric encoder at the same slice count will not fit; the arm has to be priced at a slice count and batch that does, and that reduction is itself a confound against every 2D control.
  3. What the matched control is. v3base_dense and base_dense are 2D full-adaptation numbers at the settled point; a 3D arm at a different slice count is not matched to them and the delta cannot be read straight.

Start with 2.5D as the gate: it costs the least, it uses the existing trainer, and if the depth axis carries nothing even when handed to the encoder directly, a full 3D encoder is not licensed. Reference row: experiments/README.md line 283.
notes:
2026-08-24: CLOSING AS DUPLICATE, filed before the audit finished and refuted by it within four minutes. Everything this bead proposed as unbuilt already exists:
  * The 2.5D gate it recommended STARTING with has run and is SEATED. through_dense channel-stacks a 3-slice window and reads -0.0020 against its control. volume_read.py's own docstring proves why that is not a 3D probe at all: Conv2d(3,D,k=14,s=14) over slices (i-1,i,i+1) is mathematically IDENTICAL to Conv3d(1,D,k=(3,14,14),s=(1,14,14)), so channel stacking at window 3 collapses to one linear projection and ONE depth position. The recommendation was wrong, not merely redundant.
  * The encoder-family seam exists: Backbone.load already wraps a non-ViT family (MapAsTokens for CONVNEXT), so a volumetric trunk costs no branch per consumer.
  * VRAM was answered and the answer inverts this bead's worry. knee-2nxh had the tubelet direction BACKWARDS - units is PER-SLICE, so a token spanning two slices HALVES it. The read prices at 21.7 GB, not the 38.3 GB the uncorrected cap claimed, and fits the card at 20 slices batch 6.
  * The matched-control worry is answered better than this bead framed it: there IS no matched control, by construction, because the trunk refuses band_dense's reading (crop, pooling and trunk all differ and have to). vjepa_member prices itself as an INSTRUMENT and by seat DISTANCE, not by a delta of means.
  * knee-rpkw and experiments/arms/vjepa_member.sh carry the whole thing, smoked and CPU-precleared 2026-08-22.
The one thing worth carrying over is the saturation framing, appended to knee-rpkw.

title: DINOv3 student taught the fold-0 ensemble's order — the distillation axis on a DIFFERENT encoder family
description:
GATED ON distill_pairs (knee-1xsu). Do not launch until that arm reads.

WHAT IT IS. v3base_dense's invocation with the teacher term added: --distill-weight 0.3 --teacher-targets teacher_fold0.npz. Everything else held, so v3base_dense's own measured 0.8455 (2026-08-21, peak e6) is the matched control and it costs ZERO extra card — it is already in the ledger.

WHY THIS ONE RATHER THAN A SECOND DINOv2 STUDENT. A teacher's ORDER is architecture-agnostic, which is the entire reason distillation is worth more here than a knob. The champion pool is seven members of one family; the board's only live mechanism at the top is the seventh member's TYPE OF DISTANCE (allfit's seat principle, and augseat is testing the regularisation axis on it right now). A DINOv3 student carries encoder-family distance AND is taught the pool's own ordering, which is the only construction this project has that could produce a member that is both strong and structurally unlike the pool.

WHAT THE LEDGER ALREADY SETTLED, so this is not re-litigating it: the FAMILY by itself is worth nothing (v3base_dense 0.8455 vs base_dense 0.8512, inside the 0.0062 floor), and the two weak DINOv3 members in the roster were mis-attributed — that was a LoRA-over-frozen-trunk penalty of ~0.019, not the encoder. So the family is a live axis at full adaptation and only at full adaptation.

PRICE, out loud. ~2.3 h of card (680 s/epoch x 12), teacher already written and reusable at zero. Zero submission slots. P(clears the 1.5% bar alone) ~0.05. It is worth 2.3 h ONLY in the branch where distill_pairs shows the teacher term transfers at all — otherwise this is 2.3 h buying a second measurement of a null.

THE GATE, from distill_pairs' own pre-registration:
  distill_pairs >= 0.860 — LICENSED, run it. The term transfers, and the question becomes whether it transfers ACROSS families.
  distill_pairs 0.850-0.860 with a RARITY-ORDERED per-label profile — licensed, because the mechanism is alive at a wrong operating point and the family swap is a cheaper next move than a weight sweep.
  distill_pairs <= its control with a FLAT profile — NOT licensed. File the profile and leave this bead open with the reason.

PRE-REGISTERED against v3base_dense's 0.8455:
  >= 0.8598 — the student beats the best solo member this project has, on the far encoder. Seat it, and the pool stops being one family.
  0.8455-0.8598 — the term transfers across families by whatever distill_pairs measured on its own. Read the DELTA against distill_pairs' delta, not against the absolute: two students, two families, one teacher is a transfer measurement.
  <= 0.8455 — the term is family-specific, which would be the interesting negative: it would say what the teacher carries is not order but something the student's own family already had.
notes: PRICE: ~2.3 h of card (~680 s/epoch x 12), teacher file already written and reused at zero, ZERO submission slots. P(clears the owner's 1.5% bar alone) ~= 0.05. Justified as the TRANSFER half of a pair rather than as an improvement: distill_pairs measures whether the teacher's order transfers at all, this measures whether it is a property of the ORDER or of the student's own family — and only the second answer licenses a member the champion pool does not already contain. Gated: not launched until distill_pairs reads inside its licensing bands.

title: Mount aug_long_s2026: the regularisation member the same-distribution ruler structurally under-prices
description:
THE OWNER'S OVERFIT ARGUMENT REPRICES A MEMBER WE ALREADY OWN, AND IT COSTS ZERO CARD.

He said, on 2026-08-24: "the real kaggle test dataset is NOT our dataset - meaning part of the data is unknown and unknowable and we shouldnt chase just a perfect fit (overfit) - because we dont know the final test". That is not a general caution here, it is a specific indictment of our ruler. The 909-study holdout is drawn from the SAME distribution as the training side, so a mechanism whose whole purpose is to trade in-distribution fit for robustness to shift reads FLAT or NEGATIVE on it BY CONSTRUCTION. The ruler cannot see the axis.

aug_long_s2026 is the member that argument lands on hardest, and it is already trained and sitting on disk.
  It scores 0.8511 solo, which is level with base_dense at 0.8512 - and base_dense CARRIED the 0.931 board entry.
  Its arm read -0.0076 offline, which is outside the 0.0062 noise floor, so it was read as a kill.
  It is the REGULARISATION axis. Regularisation degrades training-distribution fit on purpose. That is the exact shape the ruler punishes and a shifted test rewards.
  It has NEVER BEEN MOUNTED. Not once, in any entry.

THE LEDGER ALREADY SHOWS THE RULER MISSING THIS, three times, in the same direction:
  calib_span read -0.0020 offline and the board went UP past 0.928.
  base_dense read -0.0066 offline, outside the floor and at 2.5x the card cost, and the board went up a tick.
  through_dense read flat in its own arm and bought a board tick as the seventh seat.
And the ruler is measured to under-price DIVERSITY by a factor of 2.4. Every one of those is a member whose offline number said no and whose board said yes.

COST: zero card. It is a member swap in an existing kernel plus one submission slot. That is the cheapest live test of the owner's own argument that this project can run, and it tests the ARGUMENT rather than the member - if a regularised member seats where its offline number says it should not, the ruler's blindness is demonstrated on our own board rather than reasoned about.

PRE-REGISTERED, against the 0.937 champion with one seat swapped and everything else held - same vote, same overlap, same kit, same count:
  >= 0.939  the regularisation axis buys a seat the ruler cannot see. That licenses re-reading every arm killed on a small negative offline delta, which is a large backlog.
  0.935-0.939  inside the board's own repeat noise at this band. Reads as neutral; the member is not the lever but the ruler's blindness is not refuted either.
  <= 0.933  the swap costs. The offline number was right about this member, and the blindness argument does not extend to the regularisation axis specifically.
Whichever way it lands, it is a REPEAT MEASUREMENT at the 0.937 band, which this project has exactly one of.
notes:
2026-08-24T12:26Z — SHIPPED as kneemri-augseat v1, submission watcher armed (logs/submit_augseat.log). Zero card; distill_pairs is on the card meanwhile.

The pre-registration in the kernel docstring TIGHTENS the one written here, because lastseat ran first and supplied the control this bead never had. lastseat held everything and exchanged the same fold-0 seat for a SAME-TYPE member of HIGHER solo quality (small_batch6_s2026, +0.0011) and read 0.937 — the champion's own number to the tick. So a same-type exchange at seven members moves nothing even when solo quality rises. Any movement from augseat is therefore attributable to the KIND of distance and to nothing else: not seat scatter, not solo score.

Consequence for this bead's own bands: the 0.935-0.939 'neutral' band now splits. A tie no longer leaves the blindness argument merely un-refuted — a member 0.0076 WORSE offline holding the board flat is itself evidence the ruler over-prices in-distribution fit. What a tie would kill is the SEAT argument, not the RULER argument. Recorded in the kernel docstring's 0.936-0.939 band.
augseat (55743145) scored 0.936 board, recorded in comp/board.jsonl as augseat_v1 and in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md. Seven members, kit e7b65a0 (sha read from the kernel log), one fold-0 seat = aug_long_s2026 in place of lastseat's small_batch6_s2026. Lands in the pre-registered 0.936-0.939 band: type does not carry at seven. Third entry in a row at 0.936-0.937 across a single-seat exchange.

title: The GPU lock is machine-scoped but only one project speaks it, and that cost an arm today
description:
2026-08-24 09:22Z I started ema_dense; it held $HOME/.gpu.lock and its free-VRAM gate correctly read ~30 GB free against the 28934 MiB the recipe reserves. At 09:24Z the sibling project started a ~4.8 GB job that did not take that lock. Total went to 31.8 GB of 32.6 and the arm reported 94 img/s against its own peak of 1221 - PCIe paging, 13x, which turns 72 minutes into fifteen hours. Killed at 09:31Z; nvidia-smi went 31.8 -> 7.2 GB, which is how the 24.7/4.8/2.3 split was measured.

TWO SEPARATE HOLES, and only one of them is fixable inside this tree.

1. THE LOCK IS SPOKEN BY ONE SIDE. It was moved to $HOME on 2026-08-21 precisely so both projects could resolve it identically without reading each other's config, after the same collision in the other direction (their eval at 11.4 GB, our arm at 1923 MiB free, parked an hour on a lock they could not see). The move was correct and incomplete: nobody told them the path. Letter sent (biohub inbox, 2026-08-24) with the four-line contract - atomic mkdir, pid inside, clear-if-dead, release-only-if-still-mine. This half is now blocked on them, not on us.

2. BOTH MECHANISMS ONLY READ THE CARD AT START TIME. wait_for_free_card queries memory.free once before launching and never again; hold_card serialises STARTS. A foreign job arriving ninety seconds in is invisible to both by construction. The heartbeat DETECTS the resulting collapse - it is what printed the 94-vs-1221 line - but detection fires after the card is already being wasted, and today it fired into a log nobody was watching for another seven minutes.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is an action on the heartbeat's own detection. It has the number that proves paging (throughput against the run's own peak) and it currently only prints. Options, cheapest first: (a) have the heartbeat write a line into logs/ that a watcher can Monitor on, so a human or session learns in seconds rather than minutes; (b) have it re-read memory.free on collapse and NAME whether a foreign process appeared, which turns 'STALLED' into 'STALLED, and 4.8 GB arrived after you started'; (c) have it abort the run, which is wrong by default - a transient stall is not a foreign job, and killing a fit ten epochs in wastes the card time the abort was meant to save.

(b) is the one to build: it costs one nvidia-smi query on an already-exceptional path, it makes the log self-diagnosing, and it does not take any decision away from the operator.

MY OWN ERROR IS PART OF THE RECORD. At 09:12Z I wrote to biohub that the card was theirs and to plan against a free card. At 09:22Z I removed logs/YIELD_CARD and started the arm. The lock cannot fix a person breaking their own arrangement ten minutes after making it.
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-24 by b29cdda. The fix is NOT the lock: the sibling adopted the protocol as logs/CARD_CLAIM rather than as $HOME/.gpu.lock, so the machine has two mechanisms each covering one direction. Reading theirs costs nothing where a lock nobody else takes protects nobody, so experiments/lib.sh now globs ../*/logs/CARD_CLAIM (wait_out_peer_claim) and writes ours in their format (claim_card). Bounded by the peer's OWN expected_finish, not a timeout of ours, and a stale claim is ignored LOUDLY - a killed peer's file does not vanish, which is the cross-project version of the dead-holder failure the mkdir lock already learned. Four branches verified: park, expired, unparseable, released. Detection side landed too (CardMemory): a STALLED line now names whether VRAM vanished after this run started, which is the seven minutes of hand attribution the 09:22Z collision cost.

title: The door-closing arithmetic rests on a slope never measured in the region we now occupy
description:
comp/SUBMISSIONS.md line ~1960 closes the plan with arithmetic: 0.937 -> 0.950 is +0.013 board = +0.0068 offline at +1.92, against a measured offline ceiling of ~0.872 (+0.0026 over the champion), so the requirement is ~2.6x the entire remaining headroom of the audited space, and seat swaps, ensemble width, decode knobs and vote rules are 'arithmetically short by 3x'.

That conclusion is only as good as the constant, and the constant has a defect the backfill did NOT fix. board_transfer's own output names it: the four best entries (allfit, finalfit, sevenplane, accumseat) are ONE-SIDED and enter no pair, three of them because --fold -1 erased their offline number. So +1.92 is fitted entirely on entries at or below board 0.933, and every use of it above 0.933 is an EXTRAPOLATION - including the one that closes the door.

The direction of the risk is not symmetric. If the board-per-offline ratio STEEPENS near the top (plausible: the metric is a mean of twelve AUCs, and the labels that are still cheap to move are the ones every member already gets right, so late offline gains concentrate in the hard labels the board also weights), then the offline headroom needed for +0.013 is smaller than +0.0068 and the audited space is not arithmetically dead. If it FLATTENS, the door is shut harder than stated. We cannot tell, because the pairs that would tell us are exactly the ones --fold -1 destroyed.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT. A pair of entries above 0.933 that BOTH carry an offline number - i.e. a fold-0-only pool scoring near the champion. weakseven (0.908, offline 0.8562) is the nearest thing and it is 0.029 below. The 0.933 chain (gradeswap 0.8694, greedy7 0.8712) is the top of the measured range, so one more fold-0 entry meaningfully above 0.933 would extend the fit into the region that matters. That is a SLOT, not card: the fold-0 members already exist and are packaged.

CONSEQUENCE IF IGNORED. Every 'this family is arithmetically short' verdict written since 2026-08-24 inherits an untested extrapolation, and those verdicts are currently what stops us running cheap arms.
notes:
THE FIX IS BLOCKED BY THE SAME DAMAGE, and saying so is part of the finding. A fold-0-only pool meaningfully above 0.933 is what would extend the fit, but 0.933 IS the fold-0 ceiling as measured: gradeswap/accumseat/greedy7 all read it, member_curve's greedy accumulation saturated four steps running, and the seven-member vote is flat to wholesale exchange. There is no rearrangement of existing fold-0 members that clears it, so the slot cannot be spent on this today.

The only way the fold-0 ceiling moves is a BETTER FOLD-0 MEMBER, which needs card. ema_dense (knee-56w5) is exactly that shape and is on the card now: if it lands in its top band (>=0.8640 against band_dense's 0.8578) it is both an EMA verdict AND the first fold-0 member above the seated band since the ceiling was declared, which would let a fold-0 entry be built that extends the slope fit into the region the door-closing arithmetic extrapolates through. Two questions, one 72-minute run. Do not re-plan this bead before that arm reads.

title: Instrument: is allfit's +0.004 the DATA or the EMA that rode along with it?
description:
PRICE: ~72 min of card (band_dense's recipe, 12 epochs at ~361 s). P(clears 1.5%) = 0.02 — this is NOT sold as an improvement and must not be read as one.

WHAT IT BUYS. kneemri-allfit read 0.937 on 2026-08-24, +0.004 over the 0.933 chain, and it is the only board movement this project has produced. It was written up as the ALL-DATA axis. But every _ff member is its _s2026 twin's flags plus --fold -1 AND --ema, and the twins carry no EMA. Two variables moved together on the entry that moved the board. The interpretation named the confound at the time and read the number as a data result anyway, because --fold -1 members have no offline number of any kind and the alternative was untestable on that pool.

THE TRICK. EMA is not a data flag, so it can be measured at fold 0 where the 909-study holdout still works, against band_dense 0.8578 already on disk. The confounded pair cannot be separated where it occurred; the confounding VARIABLE can be measured where the confound does not exist. No control arm is queued — quick over matched.

BANDS, pre-registered in experiments/arms/ema_dense.sh before the run, floor 0.0062:
  >= 0.8640 — EMA is real, allfit's data reading is DEBITED, and EMA becomes a FREE lever on all seven seats.
  +0.0015 to +0.0062 — directional, unresolvable; allfit's reading stands but carries a named co-variable; no further card.
  -0.0015 to +0.0015 — FLAT; EMA cannot be what the board paid for, allfit's data reading is CLEAN, knee-tfj3's closure stands.
  <= -0.0015 — NEGATIVE, and the most interesting: allfit scored 0.937 while PAYING for EMA, so the data axis is LARGER than +0.004 and the seventh-seat decision was made against an understated curve. Re-opens the seventh seat.

HARNESS SUSPECT NAMED IN ADVANCE: --ema defaults False, so a flag that never reaches the trainer yields a run byte-identical to the control. If the answer is flat, assert ema:true in the checkpoint config and assert the weights DIFFER from band_dense's before believing the null.

title: Gate: every result heading in SUBMISSIONS.md must have a matching id in board.jsonl
description: comp/board.jsonl went unwritten from 2026-08-20 to 2026-08-24 while comp/SUBMISSIONS.md stayed current, so seven entries (sevenplane, gradeswap, accumseat, greedy7, finalfit, weakseven, allfit) lived in prose only. board_transfer prices every experiment from board.jsonl, so the slope was silently fitted on a four-day-old field, and the 2026-08-24 hand refit that filled the gap mis-paired gradeswap's offline with finalfit's board and produced +2.14 where the backfilled tool reads +1.92. Third stale-claim-in-a-live-document this week and none of the three was caught by a gate. Build the check: parse the '## ' / '### Result:' headings of SUBMISSIONS.md for entry names, parse board.jsonl for ids, assert every scored entry named in prose has a row. Should also assert no row carries an offline number for a pool containing a --fold -1 member, which is the entity error that produced the bad anchor.
notes:
Built as kneemri/kaggle/board_check.py, but joined on the KAGGLE SUBMISSION REF rather than by parsing SUBMISSIONS.md headings. Heading parsing cannot work: kernel names repeat (sixfresh shipped twice), prose spells them freely, and a heading score is not unique (seven entries read 0.937). The ref is Kaggle's own identifier and the listing costs no slot.

What it found: the record held 34 of 58 submissions. Fifteen scored all-ours entries were absent, including basedense_v1 (the entry comp/champion.json pins) and votefit_v1 at 0.938 (the best score this project owns). board_transfer's compression constant read +1.82 on the incomplete set and +1.72 on the complete one, over 21 ensemble entries with 0 inversions in 108 resolved pairs. Kernels ship quoting +1.82, +1.92 and +2.14, all fitted short.

Record backfilled 34 -> 58 rows. Every submission now has a row; the ten this file will not price carry scope: excluded plus a why, which is what turns the check from a heuristic about which absences were meant into an exact set comparison. A submission whose description stated only a delta records offline: null - a delta is not a level.

The bead's second ask is in: unpriceable() refuses any offline number over a pool naming a --fold -1 seat, by NAME (_ff suffix plus final_ws_e12), because the disk rule needs a data root and this must run in CI.

First live run found five prose gaps besides - fusion25_v2, dark6_v1, dark7_v1, v3seat_v1, votefit_v1 priced here and named nowhere in SUBMISSIONS.md; the ledger stopped at peak8. Both halves repaired. Now reads 58 recorded, 58 live, no refusals. Committed fb76367.

title: Five _ff members inside the live allfit entry carry no serving witness
description:
witness_check --device cpu --members calib_span_ff grade_ladder_ff base_dense_ff lr4e-5_ws_ff through_dense_ff reads 0 ok, 5 unverified, 0 refused. All five report 'no witness (trained before the check existed, or a published member)'.

These five are seats in kneemri-allfit, which is on the board scoring now. Six of that entry's seven seats therefore have nothing for the fingerprint check to compare against, so a member that serves differently in the kernel than it did in training would not be caught, and the pre-registered bands in the kernel docstring would be read against a contaminated number.

Suspected cause, NOT yet confirmed: the witness is recorded at holdout-evaluation time, and a --fold -1 member holds out nothing and never evaluates a holdout, so the recording step is never reached. If that is right it is structural, not an oversight, and every future all-data member inherits it. The fix would be to record the witness from a fixed handful of TRAINING studies replayed through the training path, which is what the witness actually needs (a replay fingerprint), not a holdout.

Confirm the mechanism before fixing: find where witness is written and check whether a --fold -1 run reaches it.
notes:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-24 07:53Z, and FIXED for future members.

Mechanism, exactly as suspected: kneemri/training/fitting.py Fitting.ranked returns predicted=None when
'not fold.scored', and Fold.scored is 'len(self.holdout) > 0'. Fitting.keep then had
'witness = None if predicted is None else ...'. A --fold -1 run holds nothing back, so the witness was
taken from a holdout that does not exist. Structural, not an oversight — every all-data member ever
fitted has an empty witness, including the five in the live allfit entry.

The unit test ASSERTED the defect: test_an_unscored_run_reports_no_number_and_keeps_the_last_epoch
carried 'assert kept.witness is None, "there is no held-out study to witness"'. That sentence is the
whole error in miniature — nothing in a replay fingerprint needs the studies to be unseen. Line removed.

FIX: new Fitting.witnessed(fold, predicted). With a holdout it behaves as before; without one it takes
the first WITNESS_STUDIES TRAINING positions and replays them through trainer.predict. Those studies are
memorised, so the numbers say nothing about generalisation and were never asked to — what they pin is
the READING (img, slots, decode resolution, window, precision), and every defect this check has caught
was a consumer-side default disagreeing with a recorded value. RNG-neutral: Trainer.batches takes
shuffle=False on this path and never draws from the generator, so a member fitted through it is
bit-identical to one fitted before.

Also fixed comp/witness_check.py's message, which said 'trained before the check existed, or a published
member' — a wrong cause that reads as a known one, and it retired the question for a whole board entry.

REMAINING, not done here: the five _ff members already shipped cannot gain a witness without retraining.
A post-hoc backfill looks possible in principle — load the checkpoint and replay trainer.predict over
eight studies using the config recorded IN the checkpoint, then compare against the serving path. Same
comparison, done later. Worth building only if the allfit board read is close to a pre-registration band
boundary, since its value is protecting that interpretation before a 7.3h card commitment.

title: An arm ran ~5h of card past its own written stop condition, and nothing checked
description:
final_fit_six.sh's header states its own gate: 'Run this ONLY if kneemri-finalfit reads 0.936 or above on the board. At 0.934-0.935 keep the one member and stop; at 0.933 or below this arm is retired unrun.'

kneemri-finalfit read 0.934 (submission 55715039, 2026-08-23). The gate says: keep the one member and STOP. The arm was launched anyway and ran four members to completion plus a fifth to epoch 10 of 12 — roughly 5 h of card — before anyone re-read the header. It was stopped on 2026-08-24 at 06:19Z only because a PEER PROJECT asked for the card, not because the gate was checked.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not the arm being wrong: the header is exactly right, was written before the board reading, and priced the decision honestly at '93 min of card decides these ~7 h'. The cost-tiered design worked. The defect is that its verdict had no consumer.

WHY IT SURVIVED. Every existing check guards a SHIPMENT or a PROCESS: arm_check reads flags, card_check asks the device, queue_check counts watchers, ledger_check reconciles status, kit/mount/champion_check guard the kernel. Nine checks, and not one of them asks 'does this arm's own precondition still hold against the latest board reading?' The gate lived in a bash comment, which is the one place nothing executes.

ALSO WORTH RECORDING: the cost was mis-stated twice while the arm ran, both times by using the wrong epoch count. Member 6 (band_dense_long_ff) is a 24-epoch seat, ~7.3 h at the observed ~1100 s/epoch, and was described to the peer project as 3.7 h and before that as finishing by 07:30Z. The script's own header even names the 24-epoch seat as the first to drop under contention. So the arm carried its stop condition AND its contention rule AND its true cost in prose, and all three were re-derived worse from memory.

THE FIX WORTH BUILDING, and it should be mechanical because prose already failed: arms declare their gate as DATA rather than a comment — a line the launcher can evaluate, naming the board entry and the threshold ('gate: kneemri-finalfit >= 0.936'). arm_check then refuses to arm an arm whose gate is unmet or unread, the way kit_check refuses a stale kit. comp/SUBMISSIONS.md already holds the board readings the gate would be evaluated against, so the data side exists; what is missing is the declaration and the check.

CHEAPER INTERIM, if the above is not worth the build: arm_check greps an arm for a header line matching 'ONLY if|retired unrun|gate:' and, when it finds one, refuses to arm silently — it prints the sentence and requires an explicit acknowledgement flag. That does not evaluate anything, but it puts the sentence in front of the person at the moment the slot is spent rather than in a file nobody opens after launch.

RELATED: the yield mechanism added at 72d4cc8 (logs/YIELD_CARD, checked per run_train call) is what made stopping cheap once the problem was seen. It does not prevent this — it only makes the recovery not require killing a shell by pid.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-25. A gate is now DATA: '# gate: <entry> >= <threshold>' in an arm header, parsed by kneemri/experiments/arm_gate.py (ArmGate), evaluated against comp/board.jsonl, which already held every scored entry. arm_check gained an UNMET-GATE verdict — always-named on every sweep, and REFUSING on the run that arms an arm (--only), so an unmet gate costs a queue slot rather than five hours of card. An UNREAD gate refuses for the same reason a low one does: an arm gated on a submission nobody pushed is the arm most likely to be launched on a hunch, and a missing board file is a check passing because its evidence is absent.

SECOND, LARGER HOLE FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT, and it made the first fix a no-op until closed: every header rule resolved a header as experiments/arms/<name>.sh, but an arm is keyed by the name it PRINTS. final_fit_six.sh prints six member names and none is its filename — so the gate, the '# bead:' line and the '# control' line were all unread on exactly the arms that spend the most card. Proven live: 'arm_check --only final_fit_six' raised 'no arm printed an invocation named final_fit_six'. Fixed by recording which shell printed each name as the shells run, and falling back to it when no arms/<name>.sh exists.

That extraction is now kneemri/experiments/arm_header.py (ArmHeader: text/record/beads/controls/deliberate/gated), which also split arm_check.py back under the 750-line god-file threshold it crossed (789 -> 709).

VERIFIED LIVE: 'arm_check --only base_dense_ff' exits 1 with 'UNMET-GATE base_dense_ff: gated on kneemri-finalfit >= 0.936; the board reads 0.934' — the exact arm, the exact reading, that spent the five hours.

title: A submission slot expires worthless - spend it on the instrument when no candidate is ready
description:
On 2026-08-23 two of five slots expired unspent. The stated reason was 'nothing measured justified them', which is the wrong test and champion.json already says so: 'a submission is a verification that the pipeline runs end to end, not a measurement of a method, and it must be priced that way.' A slot gated on candidate quality is a slot gated on a bar that does not apply to it.

The cost is concrete and was sitting in the queue: knee-825t is blocked on a THIRD board point outside the current offline range, and that point needs NO training - a deliberately weakened roster (drop the top two members) reads ~0.860 offline against the existing chain's 0.8648-0.8691, extending the calibration x-axis by roughly 3x. Two days of that were available and both expired.

RULE: at the last check before 00:00Z rollover, any unspent slot goes to the best INSTRUMENT entry available, in this priority: (1) a real candidate if one exists, (2) a knee-825t calibration point off the current offline range, (3) an end-to-end verification of a serving path not yet exercised on the board. Never let one expire on the grounds that nothing is good enough - nothing being good enough is what makes the instrument entry the right spend.
notes:
SLOT PLAN for the 00:00Z reset, decided 2026-08-24 21:56Z rather than improvised at the reset.

All four queued kernels pass mount_check (count8, dark6, votefit, farswap). A fifth kernel, farseat, is
REFUSED - it names vjepa_warm_s2026, a member that does not exist. Tonight's convergence measurement
retires the reason it was built: vjepa_member died at 10 of 12, and a kill at 10 costs a median of +0.0000
across 54 finished runs, so the V-JEPA warm re-run buys a clean exit code and not a score. Do not build
farseat's member to unblock farseat.

The ordering follows the goal-pricing interpretation, which forbids spending slots on another seat swap.
Ranked by whether the entry can TEACH something rather than by expected board points:

1. votefit  - rank-vote combination instead of averaging. The only queued kernel that changes the
              COMBINATION MECHANISM, so it is the one whose result is not already a draw from the
              0.930-0.937 distribution. Fire first, soon after 00:00Z.
2. farswap  - swaps in the far encoder (DINOv3 vits16). Diversity axis, which is the axis the owner
              named explicitly: it is about diversity, not averaging seven numbers that are the same
              number. Fire second, well separated.
3. count8   - eight members. Member count is measured and every entry lands inside 0.930-0.937; this is
              one more draw from a sampled distribution. Instrument value only.
4. dark6    - six dark (--fold -1) members. The all-data dose axis is recorded as real, sub-linear and
              SPENT (+0.003 over five extra seats). Lowest information of the four.
5. HOLD     - decided from the first results, per the standing directive to spread and keep the last one
              back. If votefit or farswap moves, the fifth repeats that axis; if neither does, the fifth
              is an instrument slot under this bead's own rule rather than a fifth seat draw.

Spread them: a slot that expires unspent is worth nothing, but four fired inside an hour measure one
board state four times.

title: Does cross-slot misregistration actually cost AUC, and only on the focal findings?
description:
crop_alignment measured the INPUT: 5.7 mm median cross-slot spread, ~15 px at 0.387 mm/px, against a 1-2 mm meniscal tear. It says nothing about the OUTPUT. Both fixes it licenses (tissue-centred crop, slot-to-slot registration) cost a 99 GB cache rebuild plus hours of refit, so a cheap instrument has to gate them.

kneemri/evaluation/alignment_damage.py joins the per-study spread against the holdout mix and asks whether studies whose slots disagree score worse, SEPARATELY for the seven FOCAL and five REGIONAL findings. The partition is core.data.corpus.anatomy.Extent, which is assigned from structure and whose docstring forbids fitting it to results — so it is pre-existing, not fitted to this question.

THE CONFOUND, and why the raw gap is not the read: a study with a scattered tissue centroid is plausibly just a worse study, and a worse study scores lower on everything. That moves both classes together. Misregistration moves only the focal half. The DIFFERENTIAL (focal gap minus regional gap) is the part difficulty cannot produce.

PRICE: ~76 min CPU for the spread pass (running, 909 holdout studies, 12 workers so the trainer keeps its loader margin) plus seconds for the join. Zero GPU. It cannot raise a score; it can only kill a rebuild.
notes:
PRE-REGISTERED, on the differential and its 95% bootstrap interval.

SIZING THE BANDS. A perfect registration fix would lift the poorly-agreeing half toward the well-agreeing one, on focal findings only. That is differential x (7/12 labels) x (1/2 the studies) = differential x 0.29 on the mean AUC. So the 1.5% bar needs a differential near 0.051, and even a 0.01 move needs 0.034.

  >= 0.050, interval excluding 0  the registration fix could plausibly clear the bar. Start it: it is the
                                 only mechanism measured here that reaches 1.5%.
  0.020 - 0.050                  real but sub-bar on its own. Do NOT start a 99 GB rebuild for it alone;
                                 hold it as a rider on any rebuild something else pays for.
  <= 0.020, or interval spanning 0  the registration fix is NOT licensed by this evidence.

WHAT A NULL WOULD NOT RULE OUT, stated before the number so it cannot be composed afterwards:
  - the COMMON-MODE offset, which is ~2/3 of the raw displacement and is INVISIBLE to this design by
    construction — every study shares it, so it cannot separate studies. Killing registration here leaves
    the CENTRING fix exactly where knee-yrf left it, priced on retention.
  - the proxy. An Otsu mass centroid is not a joint centre and is dragged by coil, fat and the far limb.
    That noise attenuates any true gap toward zero, so a null here is a weak null, not a strong one.
  - a finer fix than a rigid shift. This tests whether DISAGREEMENT predicts error, not whether alignment
    would help a model that was trained aligned from the start.
MEASURED 2026-08-23. 909 holdout studies, champion's six scoreable members, split at 5.85 mm. focal mean gap -0.0068, regional -0.0171, DIFFERENTIAL +0.0103, 95% [-0.0305, +0.0421]. Lands in the pre-registered '<= 0.020 or interval spans zero' band: the registration fix is NOT licensed, and is dropped rather than held as a rider (the bar needed ~0.051). Unpredicted: both raw gaps are NEGATIVE, so the poorly-agreeing half scored BETTER on both classes -- the Otsu spread is not a proxy for acquisition quality, which is the assumption underwriting the whole crop_alignment reading. NOT ruled out: the common-mode offset (invisible to this design by construction; tissue-centred cropping stays priced on retention where knee-yrf left it), the proxy's attenuation toward zero, and a model TRAINED aligned from the start. Written up in experiments/README.md.

title: Do a study's slots agree where the knee is? crop_alignment was written and never run
description:
crop_alignment.py exists, is complete, and has NO ledger row, NO interpretation and NO bead. Written 2026-08-14ish and left.

THE GAP IT FILLS. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-21_what_survives_the_closures.md dismisses CoPAS's +0.056 ROI-crop component with 'we already crop to 130 mm'. That answers crop PRESENCE. The mechanism CoPAS (Nat Commun 15:7637) actually credits is 'cropping along ROI can align the spatial position across sequences' — and a 130 mm box about the IMAGE CENTRE aligns nothing. knee-yrf measured the within-slot offsets (|dy| median 6.9 mm, p90 18.0, 10/60 studies >20 mm against 15 mm of margin) and was closed on RETENTION, a within-series quantity that cannot speak to cross-slot agreement.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every slot-aggregation arm this project has run landed inside the noise floor. If the box places the knee at a different offset in each slot, those arms were fusing views that do not correspond and the aggregator was never at fault.

PRICE: ~20 min CPU, 20 workers, ZERO GPU (card is on final_fit_six for 6.4h). An INSTRUMENT, not an improvement — it cannot raise a score. Justified as an instrument because it either closes an axis or licenses one with a published +0.056 behind it.
P(clears the bar) n/a — it is not an improvement arm. P(it changes what runs next) ~0.5.

PRE-REGISTERED, on the per-study SPREAD of offset MAGNITUDE across routed slots:
  spread p50 >= 10 mm — slots genuinely disagree. The alignment mechanism is live here, the flat
    slot-aggregation arms get a named cause, and a derived-joint-centre crop becomes a DATA lever
    rather than the correctness fix knee-yrf declined to pay for.
  spread p50 4-10 mm — partial. Read the PER-PLANE signed components, where the axes are consistent,
    before any verdict; a sagittal-vs-axial magnitude comparison is the only honest cross-plane one.
  spread p50 <= 4 mm — slots already agree. Alignment is UNAVAILABLE here at any price. Closes the
    axis and forces a different explanation for the six flat slot-aggregation arms.

LIMIT, from the module's own docstring: an Otsu mass centroid is not a joint centre — it is dragged by coil, fat and the far limb, and knee-yrf measured that tissue-centring's WORST series is worse than image-centring's at 80 mm. This bounds the question from one side only: a small spread is conclusive, a large spread is suggestive.
notes: MEASURED 2026-08-23. Middle band: within-study cross-slot spread p50 5.7 mm, p90 10.7, max 18.8. Per-slot |offset| p50 9-14 mm, so ~2/3 is COMMON MODE (study shifted whole, slots together) and does not break correspondence. Clean within-plane read: three sagittal slots at +10.7/+2.9/+3.4 mm anterior-posterior, so SAG_FLUID_FS is ~7.8 mm off the other two on a consistent axis. Residual 5.7 mm = ~15 px at 0.387 mm/px = 3-6x a 1-2 mm meniscal tear; predicts fine-structure labels suffer, and MCL 0.7893 / Lateral OA 0.8246 / Lateral Meniscus 0.8504 are our weakest against Effusion 0.8655 / Baker's 0.9086. Splits into TWO separable fixes: common-mode -> crop centring (knee-yrf, now with a second reason); residual -> slot-to-slot registration (the actual CoPAS mechanism). Does NOT license CoPAS's +0.056 — that was against an unaligned full-FOV baseline. Ledger row in experiments/README.md.

title: seat_value cannot price any candidate: champion roster holds an unscoreable fold -1 member
description:
kneemri/kaggle/seat_value.py:114 calls Pool.split(roster), which raises 'roster members with no holdout record: final_ws_e12.pt'. The raise is CORRECT — member_curve.py:135 argues it: a roster silently scored as 6 of 7 makes every delta below it read against the wrong base. The hole is structural: the shipped champion (finalfit, board 0.934) contains final_ws_e12, trained with --fold -1 and therefore unscoreable FOREVER. So seat_value can price no candidate at all against the entry that actually scored, and it fails only at the moment of use, as a traceback in an arm's post-run step.

Do NOT fix by softening the raise. Fix by pricing against the SCOREABLE SUBSET and stating that denominator in the output — 'priced against 6 of 7 champion members; final_ws_e12 unscoreable (fold -1)'. A labelled proxy roster is honest; a silent one is the failure the raise exists to stop.

Found 2026-08-23 when sided_pool's post-run seat step crashed. Training was unaffected.
notes: FIXED 2026-08-23. SeatValue.scoreable() partitions the pinned roster into members that carry a holdout record and ones that never can, using HoldoutRecord.exists() rather than a hand-built filename (its TWINS rule already handles the .metrics case a naive stem would get wrong). report() prices against the scoreable subset and LEADS with the denominator. Verified on the real champion, not just synthetic: 'priced against 6 of 7 champion members; final_ws_e12 unscoreable (fold -1)' / 'roster of 6: 0.8693'. The raise in RecordMix.split is untouched -- the fix is a labelled proxy, not a softened guard.

title: Member-pool globbing has no finished-run guard, and a dead member is the one greedy reaches for
description:
record_mix-style member lists are built by globbing *.holdout.npz. That file is written from EPOCH ZERO of any run, so the glob silently seats dead and in-flight members. On 2026-08-23 a focus_latmen checkpoint that died at epoch 1 sat at rank 10 of the greedy curve and inflated the peak from 0.8717 to 0.8721 — the whole apparent gain of five new members. A partially-trained member is near-random, near-random is DECORRELATED, and a greedy selector reaches for exactly that. It is the failure mode the tool is least able to warn about because it looks like the result you are hoping for.

The finished marker is the .pt checkpoint's EXISTENCE. Note .partial survives a successful run (band_dense has both) so absence-of-.partial is NOT the test.

This is the class of hole the repo's *_check convention exists to close and there is no check for it. Wanted: the pool builder refuses an npz with no .pt beside it, and a pool_check that reports what it dropped and why.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-25 (kneemri session, off-card lane).

THE HOLE IS ONE LINE: record_mix.py:90 refuses only when BOTH the checkpoint and its holdout record are missing (`if not path.exists() and not record.exists()`). A run that died leaves .partial + .holdout.npz and NO .pt, so it passes that test and is seated off its record alone.

Confirmed against the write sites, not assumed: fitting.py:149 writes .partial on every improving epoch and fitting.py:142 writes .holdout.npz with it; train.py:137 writes the .pt ONLY after Fitting.run returns. So .pt existence is exactly 'the run reached its own end', which is what the bead proposed.

BLAST RADIUS MEASURED on the processed root: 9 of 91 .holdout.npz files have no .pt beside them — aprior_dense_s2026_run1, focus_latmen_s2026, margin_smoke, raddino_dense_s2026, raddino_dense_s2026_run1, smoke_vjepa, vjepa_member_s2026, vjepa_member_s2026_run1, vjepa_member_s2026_run2. ~10% of the pool. Two of them are the crash readings already filed as knee-6477 and knee-2a82, so this guard closes those from the other side.

Dropping the rotated _run1/_run2 records is correct too, not collateral: their checkpoint was overwritten rather than rotated, so no weights exist for them either. A member with no .pt cannot ship, so it has no business scoring a seat.

displacement.sh is NOT the caller that seated the dead member: it globs "$D"/*_s2026.pt, which already excludes them. The exposure is any hand-passed or npz-derived --records list.

PLAN: RecordMix refuses a record whose .pt is absent, names it and why; pool_check reports what it dropped.
FIXED in RecordMix.readings: a record with no .pt beside it is dropped and NAMED (new RecordMix.dropped), because the trainer writes .holdout.npz每 improving epoch and the .pt only after Fitting returns — so record-without-checkpoint == a run that died, weights gone, can never be packaged. main now prints 'N of M records became members' plus the dropped names, so the denominator is on the page. Test fixtures were writing a record with NO checkpoint (record_mix + seat_value _member) — they now write the .pt too, which is the honest fixture. LIVE: over adapt_null_s2026 + vjepa_member_s2026 + raddino_dense_s2026 it reports 1 of 3, naming both dead ones. NOT CHANGED: ordinal_signal --directory globs *.holdout.npz and will still rank dead runs, but it is a read-only concordance diagnostic that prints its own denominator, not a pool that seats shippable members. No separate pool_check module: the guard fires inside the only pool builder and names the drop, so a second entrypoint would be a second place to keep in sync.

title: sided token pooling: the head has never been able to see WHERE a response sat
description:
THE MECHANISM IS A TYPE SIGNATURE, not a suspicion. All three token poolings in TOKEN_POOLINGS collapse
the patch axis — TokenPooling.reduce is typed "n t d" -> "n f" in every one, and ClassAndPatchMeanAndTail
discards even the indices topk returns. The head cannot express WHERE in the field a response sat. Five
of twelve targets are defined by exactly that: both menisci, both tibiofemoral compartments, the MCL.

MEASURED TODAY, two independent pools over the 909-study fold-0 holdout, same three labels at the bottom
of both (champion-6 mix 0.8693 / pool-of-70 mix 0.8616):
  MCL         0.8039 / 0.7893   n=171
  Lateral OA  0.8267 / 0.8246   n=233
  next worst  0.8654 / 0.8500
Every medial/lateral PAIR splits the same direction on our own fitted members as on the published ruler
(Medial-Lateral Meniscus +0.0425, Medial-Lateral OA +0.0585). Fracture is NOT a target despite reading
0.8216: n=68 gives SE ~0.04, so it is not separable from 0.90.

WHY THE HEAD AND NOT THE DATA. knee-yrg has refuted all four data-side explanations of the lateral gap —
laterality flip, slice band, prevalence, and the in-plane crop (which clips MEDIAL harder, [-0.0130,
-0.0095], pointing the wrong way). side_dense then asked the LOSS for the contrast and regressed -0.0641
with all twelve labels falling, but its compartment contrast ROSE 0.062 on demand: the encoder HOLDS the
side and the pooled head is where it is lost. Its own row deferred the remaining idea to "a head that
SEES position". This is that head.
