WHY A COLUMN SPLIT IS AN ANATOMICAL SPLIT. Laterality mirrors every study onto one canonical side inside
the cache pipeline (core/data/corpus/study.py:26,52), at 100% coverage because the geometric rule reaches
the half the DICOM tag does not. In that frame medial is always the same side of the array. No new input,
no cache rebuild, no label.

THE DESIGN. ClassAndSidedMean, parts=3: class token + left-half mean + right-half mean, split on the
midline column, an odd column count dropping its centre from both halves because that column IS the
midline. It SUPERSEDES cls_mean rather than competing with it — the halves partition the grid, so their
mean is the patch mean the default emits; the head can form that sum AND the difference. One extra part,
nothing removed. That makes a flat result informative in a way the other pooling arms' were not: it says
the head could have ignored the split and did.

PRICE: 72 min of card, one arm, no cache build. P(clears 1.5% on the mean) ~ 0.10 — a long shot on the
headline, and that is the honest number. It runs FIRST anyway because the board reading differs: MCL and
Lateral OA sit 2.6 and 2.0 SE below the pool median, lifting only those two to 0.87 is +0.0091 on the
mean, and the measured board transfer of +4.67 multiplies that several times past the 0.006 gap to 0.940.

PRE-REGISTERED vs band_dense = 0.8578 on the same 909 studies:
  >= 0.8628      the split carries; go to a finer grid than two halves.
  0.8548-0.8627  inside the 0.0062 floor. NOT a refutation — read the PER-LABEL columns for MCL /
                 Lateral OA / Lateral Meniscus first; the mean can absorb a real move on 3 of 12.
  <= 0.8547      suspect the head WIDTH first (three parts changes the first linear layer's fan-in),
                 then assert Laterality fired on this cache, before blaming the idea.

WHAT A NULL WOULD NOT RULE OUT: a finer spatial split (quadrants, or compartment columns rather than
halves); the same pooling on a head that also sees depth regions; and the small-weight side regulariser
side_dense left standing, which was deferred to exactly this kind of head.

title: full-data refit of the champion's members: every shipped member throws away 20% of the corpus
description:
EVERY member in the 0.934 entry except final_ws_e12 was fitted at --fold 0, i.e. on 3,497 of 4,406
studies. The 909 held out are training data we pay for and do not use. `folds.py` already supports
--fold -1 ("trains on everything") and the champion already contains exactly one such member.

PRICE: 6 members x ~72 min = ~7.2 h of card, serial (one GPU, shared with biohub by arrangement).
P(clears 1.5% on the board) ~ 0.25. Expected offline gain per member ~+0.0029, read off the CONCAVE
data slope quarter_data fitted (each doubling buys ~0.48 of the last; 3,497 -> 4,406 is 0.33 of a
doubling). That +0.0029 is the largest number left anywhere on this board — every other axis is priced
below it, and the ensemble axis was re-confirmed exhausted today (greedy peak 0.8721 at 11-13 over 70
records, +0.0004 over yesterday's 70-record peak despite five new members from three new axes).

WHY IT IS NOT JUST ANOTHER SUB-BAR KNOB. Three reasons it is worth 7 h when a knob is not:
- It composes across members rather than replacing one. Six members each fitted on 26% more data is a
  different POOL, not a rearrangement of the current one, and the pool is what today's greedy says is
  the binding variable.
- The direction already has one board point behind it: the current champion is the first entry ever to
  contain a full-data member, and it is the best entry this project has.
- The house rule licenses it explicitly — increments below the bar still compose, and a chain of them
  that sums past it IS a result.

WHAT IT COSTS THAT IS NOT CARD TIME, and this is the real decision: a --fold -1 member is UNSCOREABLE
FOREVER (champion.json's last principle). It has seen every holdout study, so it can never be
seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored, and no pool containing it may report an offline mean.
Refitting six members this way makes the ENTIRE roster blind — every future roster decision is then made
against whatever the board last said, at 5 slots a day. That is why this is filed rather than started:
it trades the offline ruler for a one-way data gain.

MITIGATION that keeps the ruler: refit the SIX at --fold -1 for shipping, and keep the existing fold-0
records for every offline comparison. The pool used for SELECTION stays scoreable; only the SHIPPED
weights change. Selection is then made on fold-0 twins and executed with full-data members, which
assumes the seat ordering is invariant to the extra 26% of data — an assumption, stated, not measured.

PRE-REGISTERED: the entry either ticks (board >= 0.936, consistent with the slope times the 4.67
transfer at its low end) or it does not (<= 0.935, meaning the offline data slope does not transfer and
the fold -1 step is worth its ~+0.001 alone). Below 0.933 says the full-data members are WORSE in the
seat, which would refute the one board point this direction currently rests on.

title: annotation-holdout: a member that never trains on the 58 image-read annotations, so supervision_gap can be pointed at OUR architecture
description:
INSTRUMENT, not a score move. eleven axes have now read flat inside the 0.0062 floor (knee-jk3); knee-7d1 names the RULER as the top remaining suspect, and a label ceiling is exactly what eleven flat axes look like.

The measurement already exists: kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap, run 2026-08-14 on the published members' out-of-fold predictions (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-14_labels-or-pixels.md). aggregate labels 0.8639 vs model 0.8391; six labels sit BELOW the line with a mean gap ~0.11 -> ~0.055 over twelve labels if closed. That is the only quantity in this repo that matches the frontier gap (0.018) it needs to explain, with room over.

BLOCKER it fixes: the module needs predictions that never trained on the annotations. core/data/labels/targets.py:239-243 overrides those 58 studies' scores with the annotations and weights them at ANNOTATED_WEIGHT=3.0 in EVERY member we fit. 696 cells x 3 ~= 0.66% of total training weight, paid for with the only radiologist-truth ruler in the project.

DESIGN (machinery already in the repo): add Supervision.annotations: bool = True; guard the override with it; extend moves_the_ruler() to include 'not self.annotations'. Targets.pair then re-reads the ruler under plain Supervision (annotations=True), so the arm TRAINS without them and is SCORED on the unchanged ruler -- every ledger comparison stays valid. Record the switch in Targets.supervised() so the pre-flight landed check proves the flag fired, and wire it through options.py:171-175 and landed.py:235-243.

PRICE: ~1.6-3.2 h of card (6-12 epochs at ~950 s) for zero direct score. What it BUYS is a clean supervision_gap read on the CURRENT architecture, which either confirms the ~0.055 below-the-line gap and names which labels carry it (licensing a data move -- re-extraction -- rather than a twelfth knob), or shows it has closed and sends eleven flat axes to a different explanation. Card is busy with raddino_dense until ~21:45 UTC; this is keyboard work queued behind it.

PRE-REGISTERED READ: the holdout AUC of the arm itself is expected to sit within the 0.0062 floor of base_dense_s2026 (0.8512) -- 0.66% of weight cannot move it. If it drops MORE than the floor, that is a finding about how much those 58 studies carry, not a failed arm.
notes:
PRICE (corrected, and in the format the arm gate reads): the arm is band_dense's recipe on dinov2-small, not base — ~72 min of card (12 epochs at ~361 s), not the 1.6-3.2 h the description estimated against base.

P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0. This is an INSTRUMENT and it is justified as one: it is not expected to move the mean at all, and its own pre-registered read is 'within the 0.0062 floor of band_dense 0.8578'. What it buys is the ONLY measurement that can separate 'our architecture has hit its ceiling' from 'our LABELS have', which is the question eleven flat axes (knee-jk3) have left standing and which knee-7d1 names as the top suspect. P(the supervision_gap read it enables licenses a data move above the bar) ~ 0.3, against a ~0.055 quantity — so the expected value is carried by what it LICENSES, never by its own holdout number.

2026-08-23 20:00 UTC — ARM KILLED BEFORE IT RAN, on a denominator I had not computed.

Measured: of the 58 annotated studies, only 13 fall in the fold-0 holdout. The other 45 are in this
member's own training split, so their predictions are memorised and would inflate the model column
enough to flip the sign. Honest read is holdout-only: 13 studies x 12 labels = 156 cells, against the
696 the 2026-08-14 read used. Aggregate SE ~0.04 on a 0.025 effect. UNPOWERED.

Second correction, to my own framing: PublishedRuler reads "the twenty published checkpoints" — an
EXTERNAL CC0 set with whole-corpus OOF. So 0.8639-vs-0.8391 priced THEIR ensemble against the labels,
not ours. Reproducing it on our architecture needs whole-corpus OOF of ours, which is folds, which are
banned. The instrument as conceived is unbuildable under that ban.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT. Not the label ceiling — that hypothesis is untouched, only this route to
measuring it is closed. Not the switch: --hold-annotations is merged (dec7f9f), gated, and costs
nothing, and it is the prerequisite the moment whole-corpus OOF is available by any route. Not the
taint it names: every member is still scored on a holdout where 13 of 909 rows carry targets it trained
on at weight 3.0 — 1.4% of rows, below the 0.0062 floor, so not worth card time to remove, but real and
now written down.

ROUTE THAT WOULD WORK, if the label ceiling is ever worth a card hour: move all 58 (and their
report-hash twins, per ReportFolds' duplicate-group rule) into the holdout side of a single run. One
run, not folds. Predictions on all 58 are then genuinely out-of-sample, ruler is the radiologist
annotation, and the arm's 909-subset holdout number stays exactly ledger-comparable because the npz
keys by study name. Cost ~72 min. Not queued: it buys a measurement, not a score.

title: A member on an unmounted variant packages and pushes clean; the gate that should refuse it crashes instead
description:
AUDIT (2026-08-23, two read-only agents). Three of nine ENCODERS entries carry no mount=: CONVNEXT_BASE, VJEPA2_LARGE, RAD_DINO. Trained checkpoints already exist on two of them (cnx_dense 0.7927, vjepa_member 0.8313, vjepa_warm 0.8337); raddino_dense is on the card now. None sits in comp/members.roster today, so nothing is broken in the shipped path -- this is a hole, not a live wound.

THE HOLE, in pipeline order:
1. package_members.py -- PASSES IT THROUGH. Never imports ENCODERS, never reads variant. An unmounted-variant checkpoint named in the roster is packaged and pushed with no complaint. This is the RIGHT TIME to refuse: packaging is where a member enters the shippable set.
2. champion_check.py -- passes through. Compares member NAMES only; no encoder/variant/mount consulted.
3. kit_check.py -- not applicable.
4. mount_check.py:51-54 -- CRASHES rather than refusing. It catches only WeightsError; mounted_source raises ValueError (backbone.py:274-279). The ValueError escapes verdict(), escapes the dict comprehension at mount_check.py:101, and no kernel gets a verdict -- so the tool designed to emit a per-kernel REFUSED line emits a traceback instead, and the OTHER kernels go unchecked.
5. comp/verify_members.py:41 -- same, and worse placed: package.mounts() is called unconditionally before the if arguments.kernel: guard, with no try/except at all.

Only production call site of mounted_source is members.py:572 (MemberPackage.mounts). The kernel runtime does NOT use it -- kernel_run.py:211 goes through find_encoder/locates and fails with FileNotFoundError, i.e. inside the kernel the message is 'no mount found on disk', not the sentence that explains why.

WHY IT MATTERS. The check is in the right place and at the wrong TIME: it fires at packaging-verification time, after the card is spent. A winning member on an unmounted variant is an offline-only number -- four hours of card producing something unspendable, discovered by a traceback.

FIX (card-free): (a) package_members refuses a roster member whose variant has no mount, naming the variant and the upload that would fix it; (b) mount_check catches ValueError alongside WeightsError and returns REFUSED so the remaining kernels still get verdicts; (c) verify_members guards the same call. Plus the standing option of closing it for raddino by publishing the MIT weights as dimiturnt/rad-dino-hf/rad-dino.
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-23. All three fixes are in and pushed. (a) package_members.MemberManifest.shippable() refuses a roster member on an unmounted variant before any weights are copied, wired into document(), so the refusal lands at packaging rather than at kernel-metadata time. (b)+(c) were fixed at the RAISER rather than at the two catchers: MemberPackage.mounts (members.py:576-584) now refuses an unmounted variant as a WeightsError, which both mount_check and verify_members already handle by returning a per-kernel refusal and carrying on - so no ValueError escapes to leave the remaining kernels unchecked, and neither call site needed a widened except. Separately RAD_DINO gained mount='dimiturnt/rad-dino' mid-arm, so of the three unmounted encoders only cnxbase and vjepa2l remain, both correctly refused rather than crashing.

title: Composition beats volume and beats loss: two independent projects, same shape
description:
Cross-project convergence with biohub (celltrack), recorded 2026-08-23. Their largest measured win (+0.0267 held out, their first campaign to clear their 1.5% bar) came from changing the CANDIDATE DISTRIBUTION the model trains on -- crowded/complete negatives from detect-and-match instead of sparse annotated pairs -- and they report per-class loss surgery lost every time they tried it.

Our four data-side arms against a 0.0062 floor (all measured by 2026-08-21, experiments/README.md): extended slots +0.0002, twenty cached slices -0.0001, 392px +0.0002, whole-stack routing +0.0147 SHIPPED. The three that ADD data are null; the one that paid changed WHICH series reach the model at all (17.4% never routed).

Same shape, different modality, different metric, different failure mode: composition of the input beat both volume of it and loss over it.

TWO POINTS IS NOT A LAW. What it is: the strongest prior either project has about where to look, arrived at independently, which is worth more than either number alone.

CONSEQUENCE, and this is why it is filed rather than left in a letter: it independently deprioritises the label/loss axis (knee-7d1). That axis was already priced at +0.0043 complete per-label headroom by weights_gap (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-23_the_per_label_axis_is_worth_0.004.md), a quarter of the bar. Now a second, mechanism-based argument from a project that TRIED loss surgery repeatedly and lost every time points the same way. Two independent arguments, same direction.

It also retro-explains the CoPAS 0-for-4, which included a label-correlation loss their paper reported at +0.013. A loss-side component failing to transfer is what this prior predicts.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT: severity weighting is owner-mandated and stays regardless of this prior. And this says nothing about the 3D-encoder axis, which remains the open one.
notes:
CORRECTION, same day, before this was cited anywhere but one letter. Two facts in the description above are WRONG.

1. 'whole-stack routing ... changed WHICH series reach the model at all' is FALSE. whole_stack is a slice-READING arm, not a routing arm: all 12 cached slices per training step instead of a 3-slice window (experiments/README.md:274). It changes which cached SLICES a step reads. It cannot change which series are cached and therefore cannot change coverage at all.

2. '17.4% never routed' is SUPERSEDED and was already corrected in this repo by bead knee-t92, which is CLOSED. That number conflated STRUCTURAL loss (series matching no slot predicate: 2,421 of 24,371 = 9.9%, slots.py:78-81) with COMPETITIVE loss (series matching a slot but losing the density tie-break, ~20.3% of studies hold a contested slot). I cited the retracted figure. This is the read-the-ledger rule failing for the fifth time in one session, and this time the corrected number was sitting in a closed bead.

DOES THE CONVERGENCE SURVIVE? Yes, and the mechanism is now named correctly rather than borrowed. whole_stack held the corpus FIXED and changed the composition of each training step. That is still composition-over-volume, and it is still the same class as biohub's candidate-distribution win (crowded/complete negatives instead of sparse GT pairs, +0.0267). Both changed what a step is composed of at fixed data. Neither added data.

WHAT THE CORRECTION COSTS THE HYPOTHESIS, and this matters more than the bookkeeping. The INPUT-side version of biohub's question now reads mostly DEAD, on evidence this repo already had: extended_slots added the three missing slot types covering 96.4% of the structural loss (2,335 of 2,421) and 83,297 slices of imaging, and returned +0.0002 against a 0.0062 floor -- refuted (experiments/README.md:303). We already ran the 'route the unrouted series' experiment. It bought nothing.

So the surviving form of the question is NOT 'is there unseen input' but 'is there a TRAIN/DEPLOY divergence in how the seen input is composed'. That is knee-<new>, filed separately from the audit's item 5.

title: MCL's ceiling is closed on the whole recipe axis — 83 runs, zero card
description:
Free ablation over every recorded run's MCL column. Nothing in the recipe family moves it, which is what makes the objective axis (focus_mcl) the remaining one.

  crop band     (0.0,1.0) 0.7823 n=1 | (0.1,0.9) 0.7793 n=26 | (0.2,0.8) 0.7662 n=17   — 0.013 total span
  slices        12 -> 0.7643 n=34 | 16 -> 0.7745 n=2 | 20 -> 0.7777 n=21
  resolution    336 -> 0.7695 n=54 | 448 -> 0.7711 n=3
  encoder       dinov2-small 0.7732 n=48 | dinov2-base 0.7812 | vjepa2-large 0.7803 | dinov3-small 0.7257
  slot scheme   extended (9 slots, +83,297 slices of imaging never otherwise seen) 0.7604
                vs canonical 0.7931 — WORSE on MCL and on the mean (0.8459 vs 0.8578)
  best ever     0.8042 (band_wide_s2026, mean 0.8553)

NOT RARITY OR LABEL NOISE — already settled in experiments/README.md:825: Synovitis has fewer positives than MCL (580 vs 767) and the corpus's lowest reader confidence (0.189), and scores 0.873. Recomputed here at grade >= 0.5 rather than > 0 (the labels are graded, in {0.08,0.28,0.68,0.82,0.94}, so a > 0 count returns prevalence 1.000 for all twelve and is meaningless): MCL prevalence 0.174 with label confidence 0.789, the HIGH end. Clean label, unfittable column.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT. Sampling density on the medial margin: band140 measured MCL at -0.016/-0.021/-0.017 (e6/e7/e8) when 140 mm of span went through the same pixel grid — the largest margins in the twelve-label table, while the thick labels held flat. That is a crop-AND-resolution arm (denser mm/px on a NARROWER field), which no run above tried: every 448 px run here also widened or held the field. It is the follow-up if focus_mcl lands in its null band.
notes: 2026-08-23: DOWNGRADED, not closed. The recipe-axis measurement stands. What changes is worth: MCL's entire demonstrated headroom is +0.0029 on the metric (weights_gap, matched ruler). Do not spend an arm on it.

title: RAD-DINO: radiology-pretrained init against an exact dinov2-base control
description:
The only mechanism still priced above the 1.5% bar is domain-matched encoder initialisation (knee-ombx: the 0.044-at-matched-train-loss generalisation gap). MRNet is blocked on the owner's licence call; RAD-DINO is not.

microsoft/rad-dino is MIT, finetuned FROM facebook/dinov2-base on 882,775 chest radiographs (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, NIH-CXR, PadChest, BRAX). ViT-B/14, 768-wide, 12 deep - architecturally identical to the 'base' variant, so it loads through the same AutoModel path with no conversion and no new dependency.

That identity is what makes the arm worth running: base_dense_s2026 is dinov2-base at this exact recipe and scored 0.8512, so swapping ONLY the initialisation weights reads the domain-init mechanism with one variable and an exact control.

Domain distance is stated rather than hidden: chest radiography is a 2D projection modality, not MRI. It shares grayscale anatomy and tissue-contrast statistics with our pixels and shares neither the acquisition physics nor the body part. So this is a PARTIAL domain match and prices as such - plausible +0.005-0.015 against the class's 1.5-3%.

It also prices RadImageNet, whose match is better (1.35M radiology images across 11 anatomies, its own published evaluation includes ACL and meniscus tear detection on MR) and whose cost is far higher (Keras .h5 weights, no PyTorch port found, 2-4h conversion with a silent-mismatch failure mode). If radiology init moves nothing against an exact control here, that conversion is not worth buying.

NO KAGGLE MOUNT, so it trains here and cannot be submitted until the weights are mirrored. MIT permits a public mirror, so that is a dataset upload deferred until a member earns a seat.
notes:
PRICE: 50 min of card (12 epochs at base's batch 6, the control's measured cost) plus ~25 min already spent card-free on the registry entry, the arm and the load oracle. GAIN: the domain-init class prices at 1.5-3% (knee-ombx), and chest projection radiography is a PARTIAL match to knee MRI - shared grayscale clinical anatomy and tissue contrast, shared neither acquisition physics nor body part - so this arm plausibly returns +0.005-0.015 of it. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 1 in 6.

That ratio is bought as much for the INSTRUMENT as for the gain, and it is justified that way rather than sold as an improvement. The arm carries an EXACT control - base_dense_s2026 is dinov2-base at byte-identical flags, 0.8512 - which no previous encoder arm here had; every other family change moved architecture and pretraining corpus together and could not attribute its result to either. So this is the first clean read of the domain axis, and it prices the expensive half of the pair: RadImageNet's 2-4h Keras conversion is worth buying only if radiology init moves something against an exact control.

A tie does NOT kill the class. It kills the chest-radiograph route and prices RadImageNet down; it says nothing about MRNet, which is knee MRI.
THE DOMAIN-ENCODER LANDSCAPE, surveyed 2026-08-23 so the follow-on is not re-derived. Ranked by domain distance to knee MRI, with cost and blocker:

1. OrthoFoundation (arXiv 2601.18250, Jan 2026) - THE BEST MATCH THAT EXISTS. 1.2M unlabeled KNEE X-ray and MRI images, DINOv3 backbone, self-supervised; the abstract claims it 'ranks first in MRI structural injury detection', which is our task class, and it is our architecture family. NO PUBLIC WEIGHTS FOUND - no github, no HF, nothing in the abstract. The paper is CC BY-NC-ND but that governs the PAPER, not weights that do not exist publicly. NOT ACTIONABLE; worth re-checking, since a release would make it the single strongest candidate for this mechanism and would obsolete every entry below.

2. MRNet - knee MRI, our modality and body part. BLOCKED on the owner's licence call (non-commercial RUA against a 77k winner licence). knee-ombx. Not mine to grant.

3. RadImageNet - 1.35M radiology images over 11 anatomies, its own published evaluation includes ACL and meniscus tear detection on MR. REPRICED DOWNWARD: the 2-4h Keras conversion I costed does NOT exist - the repo publishes PYTORCH weights directly (a Google Drive link off github.com/BMEII-AI/RadImageNet), so the real cost is ~30-60 min of plumbing for a ResNet50 that needs the MapAsTokens feature-map wrapper ConvNeXt already uses. THE REMAINING OBJECTION IS ARCHITECTURE, NOT COST: RadImageNet ships ResNet50/DenseNet121/Inception only, and this project's one CNN member cnx_dense scored 0.7927 against base_dense's 0.8512. A RadImageNet arm asks its domain gain to beat a ~0.06 architecture deficit, and it cannot separate the two. That is exactly the confound raddino_dense does not have.

4. RAD-DINO - this bead. Weakest domain match of the four (chest projection radiography) and the ONLY one with an exact control and no blocker, which is why it runs first.

ORDERING FOLLOWS FROM THAT: raddino answers 'does radiology initialisation transfer at all, cleanly'. Only its answer prices the two below it, and neither of those can answer the question cleanly itself.
2026-08-23 prior-art check, no GPU spent: OrthoFoundation (arXiv 2601.18250) publishes NO weights, NO code, NO availability statement of any kind - fetched the abstract page and asked for one directly. Not actionable, and this closes the re-check; do not spend another lookup on it until a release is announced.

What it IS worth: independent support for the mechanism this arm tests. 1.2M unlabeled knee X-ray and MRI, self-supervised on a DINOv3 trunk, 'ranks first in MRI structural injury detection' across 14 downstream tasks, and matches supervised baselines at 50% of the labels. That is a domain-matched initialisation paying off on OUR body part and OUR modality, published by someone else. It does not change this arm's pre-registered bands - a chest-radiograph match is a weaker match than knee MRI and must not be read against a knee-MRI result - but it does mean a NULL here should be read as 'this domain distance is too far', not as 'domain-matched initialisation does not pay'.
READING (2026-08-23, STOPPED AT EPOCH 4 OF 12 — a partial run, and the partiality is stated first).

MATCHED-EPOCH NUMBERS. raddino_dense e4: mean 0.7984, train loss 0.8903. base_dense_s2026 e4: mean 0.8355, train loss 0.8907. IDENTICAL train loss, 0.037 worse holdout. Per-label at e4: Lateral Meniscus 0.745, ACL 0.827, MCL 0.734 — behind band_dense's 0.842 LatMen by roughly the mean's margin, so it is uniformly behind and carries no targeted strength worth salvaging.

WHY IT WAS STOPPED RATHER THAN FINISHED. The band needed >= 0.866, i.e. +0.068 from e4 in seven epochs. Both same-harness controls flatten instead: base_dense gained +0.016 after e4 (0.8355 -> 0.8512 peak at e8, then 0.8505/0.8490/0.8491) and v3base_dense gained +0.009 (0.8367 -> 0.8455 at e6, then flat). The late one-cycle jump the 'let it finish' argument rests on does not exist in this harness. So the remaining 1.8h of card bought a <5% chance of a lever, against 40 min for focus_latmen, the P0 instrument gating the +0.025 per-finding deficit. Ratio, not momentum.

WHICH LINK. Not PLUMBING — the encoder swap demonstrably took effect: matching train loss to four decimals says the trunk trained, and a load that matched nothing would have tracked the control, not diverged from it on holdout only. Not DATA or TEST — the control is byte-identical flags on the same corpus and the same holdout, read at the same epoch. This is the IDEA link, and narrowly: features pretrained on chest projection radiography FIT this objective as well as dinov2-base and RANK knee MRI worse.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT. It kills the CHEST-RADIOGRAPH route, at this recipe. It does not kill domain-matched initialisation: OrthoFoundation (1.2M knee X-ray + MRI, DINOv3, no public weights) is independent published support for the mechanism at the RIGHT domain distance, and MRNet (knee MRI, blocked on the owner's licence call, knee-ombx) is untouched by this. Read the null as 'this domain distance is too far', which is exactly the reading the bead pre-registered.

RadImageNet stays unbought, but this arm is not the reason — its own architecture confound is (ResNet50/DenseNet121 only, against cnx_dense 0.7927 vs base_dense 0.8512).

RE-TESTABLE. The partial checkpoint, holdout and metrics survive at PROCESSED/raddino_dense_s2026.{partial,holdout.npz,metrics.jsonl}, so a warm-start re-run costs four epochs less than a fresh one if a reason to revisit appears.
2026-08-23 19:05Z TWO CORRECTIONS FOUND MID-RUN, both card-free, both recorded BEFORE the result so neither can be a post-hoc excuse.

1. THE DOMAIN IS CHEST X-RAY, NOT 'MEDICAL'. microsoft/rad-dino is pretrained on ~883k thoracic RADIOGRAPHS (MIMIC-CXR 368,960, CheXpert 223,648, NIH-CXR 112,120, PadChest 136,787, BRAX 41,260). Our pixels are knee MRI, 3D. The architectural half of the pre-registration is unaffected and still verified -- ViT-B/14, 768 wide, 12 blocks, finetuned FROM facebook/dinov2-base, 0 of 223 tensors identical -- but the TRANSFER half was written as 'medical domain pretraining' and the actual transfer is cross-modality (X-ray -> MR) and cross-region (thorax -> knee). This does not change the bands, which stay as pre-registered. It changes what a TIE MEANS: the honest first reading of <=0.855 is now 'chest-radiograph pretraining does not transfer to knee MR', NOT 'domain pretraining does not transfer', and the axis would stay open for an actual MR-pretrained or musculoskeletal trunk. Kills that USE, not the asset.

2. THE MEMBER WAS UNSHIPPABLE AND NOBODY WOULD HAVE FOUND OUT UNTIL A SUBMISSION. ENCODERS[RAD_DINO] carries no mount=, so Encoder.mounted_source RAISES, and a kernel cannot attach the weights. A winning holdout would have been offline-only. Licence is MIT -- commercially permissive -- so unlike MRNet (knee-ombx) this is a code-and-upload question, not a rule 2.6a one. Fixing it now, card-free, the same way dinov3 is mounted: publish the weights as a private Kaggle dataset and add mount= to the encoder entry. This is the same failure class the mounted_source docstring already names -- 'asking for a variant with no mount raises here rather than inside a kernel, where the answer costs a submission slot' -- except the raise sits AFTER four hours of card.
MOUNT CLOSED MID-RUN, 2026-08-23 ~19:16 UTC. The arm was queued with its encoder unmirrored, i.e. able to produce only an offline number. Fixed while the card ran, at no cost to it: microsoft/rad-dino (MIT) is now the private Kaggle dataset dimiturnt/rad-dino, and ENCODERS[RAD_DINO] carries mount='dimiturnt/rad-dino'.

A DEFECT WAS CAUGHT IN THE FIX ITSELF, and it is the more useful half. The first upload copied the dinov3-hf layout -- one directory per variant under a shared dataset, pushed with 'kaggle datasets create --dir-mode zip'. That flag zips a subdirectory and Kaggle unpacks it into the ROOT: dimiturnt/raddino-hf holds config.json at top level and the rad-dino/ segment Encoder.locates matches on does not exist. locates would have returned False for every candidate and find_encoder would have raised 'no raddino mount among [...]' INSIDE A KERNEL, i.e. at the cost of a submission slot.

It was caught by asking Kaggle to list the files of the KNOWN-GOOD dataset and diffing the two answers: dinov3-hf reports 'vits16/config.json' with the prefix, raddino-hf reported 'config.json' without. A mirror that uploads successfully is not a mirror that mounts; the upload's own exit status and success line say nothing about the layout. dinov3-hf's per-file timestamps differ by twelve seconds, so it was uploaded file-by-file with the tree preserved, not as a zip -- the layout was never reproducible from the flag we used.

Resolved by removing the need for a directory rather than by reproducing one: the dataset is named for the encoder (dimiturnt/rad-dino), so the mount path IS the leaf segment. Verified by listing it back. dimiturnt/raddino-hf is now an orphan to delete from the web UI.

Bands unchanged. Progress: epoch 0 0.7247, epoch 1 0.7439.
MID-RUN READ, epoch 3 of 12, and it changes what a null would MEAN rather than predicting the number.

Matched against the control curve epoch-for-epoch (base_dense_s2026, same recipe, same batch 6, same 336px/20 slices, only the initialisation differs):
  epoch 0: base 0.7625 / raddino 0.7247   (loss 1.1901 / 1.2237)
  epoch 1: base 0.7759 / raddino 0.7439   (loss 1.0806 / 1.1110)
  epoch 2: base 0.8144 / raddino 0.7852   (loss 0.9912 / 1.0337)
  epoch 3: base 0.8232 / raddino 0.7944   (loss 0.9322 / 0.9659)

RAD-DINO is behind on holdout by 0.029-0.038 AND behind on TRAIN LOSS by 0.034-0.037, at every epoch. The gap is narrowing slowly (-0.038 -> -0.029) but has been flat for two epochs.

WHY THE TRAIN LOSS IS THE INTERESTING HALF. The mechanism this arm was built to test is the one cnx_dense displays: a BETTER train loss (0.8332 vs 0.8456) with a WORSE holdout (0.7927 vs 0.8371) - a trunk that fits our pixels harder and generalises worse, which is what a mismatched initialisation looks like. raddino shows neither half of that. It fits WORSE and generalises WORSE, in step. That is not mismatch; that is a trunk that is simply a poorer starting point for these pixels.

WHAT THAT WOULD RE-PRICE, if the curve holds. The arm's pre-registration reads a tie-or-below as 'domain-matched initialisation does not pay AT THIS DOMAIN DISTANCE', pricing RadImageNet down but not out. The both-worse pattern suggests a different axis is doing the work: BREADTH of pretraining, not DOMAIN MATCH. DINOv2-base is LVD-142M across everything; RAD-DINO is 883k chest radiographs, one anatomy, projection rather than volumetric. Narrow-and-matched losing to broad-and-unmatched is a coherent read of both-worse, and it is a read the arm's four bands do not contain.

That makes RadImageNet a BETTER test rather than a weaker one - 1.35M images across 11 anatomies is broad AND matched, so it separates the two explanations that RAD-DINO confounds. It says nothing new about MRNet, which is knee MRI and matched on both axes.

NOT KILLING THE RUN. Mid-curve extrapolation is unreliable here by the control's own evidence: base gained 0.034 between epochs 2 and 6. Eight epochs remain, the card has nothing better queued behind it, and the band this lands in is what licenses or retires the next arm.
KILLED at epoch 6/12 on 2026-08-23T20:29Z. Epochs 0-6: 0.7247/0.7439/0.7852/0.7944/0.8000/0.8119/0.8137, ~990s each. Per-epoch gain decayed to +0.0018 against the +0.052-in-five its pre-registered top band needed. Control base_dense_s2026 = 0.8512 at e8, so -0.0375 and falling further behind. PRICE that killed it: 83 min of card to make a near-certain bottom-band landing certain, versus 72 min for sided_pool on an axis never tried. The trunk DID fire (loss 1.11->0.757 monotonic, backbone-appropriate VRAM/step-time) so this is not plumbing and not a frozen encoder. CONFOUND it cannot separate: --backbone-lr 4e-5 and the 12-epoch schedule were tuned on DINOv3. Kills the DROP-IN SWAP; does NOT rule out RAD-DINO at its own LR, as a frozen extractor, or medical-domain pretraining generally. Ledger row in experiments/README.md.

title: Roster search is retired: greedy7 read 0.933, the fourth tie
description: kneemri-greedy7 exchanged FOUR of the champion's seven seats on a greedy-optimal roster (offline 0.8712 vs 0.8694, +0.0018, the first gap above the seat ruler's resolution) and read 0.933 - the same number gradeswap and accumseat read on one-for-one swaps. Pre-registered band hit verbatim. Mechanism: the offline edge is real but does not TRANSFER, because a roster chosen by maximising the quantity it is then scored on, over 28 candidates on 909 studies, sits inside the search's own selection noise. Confirms 2026-08-23_the_ensemble_axis_is_exhausted.md from the other direction. FORBIDS: no further slot on any roster drawn from the currently packaged pool, by any selection rule. Does NOT rule out member quality or axes absent from the pool - final_ws_e12 (data volume) and vjepa_member (3D trunk) are untouched by this.
notes:
CLOSED BY MECHANISM 2026-08-23, not just by four ties. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-23_selection-overfit-explains-greedy7.md.

member_curve over six cached champion members (no card, no compute - all six already had holdout predictions) measures the price of CHOOSING: top-4-per-label reads 0.8714 in-sample and 0.8681 split-half. That +0.0033 is selection overfit - the amount by which maximising the offline mean over subsets inflates its own estimate on the studies it maximised over.

greedy7's entire edge was +0.0018 (0.8712 vs 0.8694). It sits INSIDE the overfit. So greedy7's 0.8712 was not a better ensemble measured well, it was the same ensemble measured on the studies that flattered it, and its +0.000 board return is the expected result rather than a failure of board resolution.

RULE THIS BUYS: never fire an entry chosen by offline maximisation. Any offline selection gain under ~0.003 is overfit by construction and must not buy a slot. This also re-reads knee-dfl1 (+0.0004 over 59 candidates) and the 63-candidate seat scan: the correct reading of those is not 'too small to resolve' but 'smaller than the estimator's own bias'.

Also closed in the same run: per-label selection (oracle 0.8643 vs plain average 0.8695, headroom MINUS 0.0052 - a perfect per-label picker LOSES to averaging) and the vote rule (RankAverage 0.8695, LogitAverage 0.8696, QualityWeightedRank 0.8694, span 0.0002). The honest split-half curve rises monotonically to the flat average at every k.

NOT because members agree - they differ significantly per label (ACL -0.0338 [-0.0560,-0.0137], Medial Meniscus +0.0175 [+0.0058,+0.0307], Medial OA -0.0152 [-0.0278,-0.0034]). Variance reduction from averaging beats specialisation gain from picking. That statement survives adding a distant member, which the 2026-08-17 'members do not disagree' reading did not.
COMPOSITION AUDIT, 2026-08-23 ~18:00 UTC, zero card. Asked the one question this bead's retirement of roster search does not literally answer: are the STRONGEST members we own actually the ones we ship? They are.

The champion (finalfit, 0.934) seats band_dense_long (0.8587, the strongest solo on the sheet), band_dense's own --fold -1 refit final_ws_e12, grade_ladder (0.8565), calib_span, base_dense, lr4e-5_ws and through_dense. There is no unshipped member stronger than what is mounted. The reading I opened this audit with - 'band_dense_s2026 at 0.8578 beats the roster's best res392_ws at 0.8523' - was read off comp/members.roster, which is the PACKAGING list and lags the champion by several entries. members.roster is not the answer to 'what did we ship'; comp/champion.json is.

So the composition idea is closed on the same evidence that closed roster search, and it is closed for a second reason as well: greedy7 already maximised the offline mean over the pool and returned the fourth 0.933 tie, inside a +0.0033 selection overfit.

NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING. This audit was aimed at knee-tfj3 next - six seats refitted at --fold -1 - on the argument that '--fold -1 blindness costs nothing now that all three offline rulers read dead against the board'. That argument is new; the CONCLUSION it was heading for is one this project already wrote and then RETRACTED hours earlier on the multiple-comparisons error. tfj3 stays unrun. Read tfj3's retraction before repricing it a third time.
CORRECTION to the note above, same hour, before it could be cited. 'There is no unshipped member stronger than what is mounted' is FALSE as written. comp/members.roster lines 182-186 carry small_batch6_s2026 at 0.8598 — the best solo member this project has — and small_accum_s2026 at 0.8579, and neither is in the champion's seven; band_dense_long's 0.8587 is the best solo that IS seated. The roster is not stale about contents, only about the ORDER its early comments assert; the four-member 'offline peak' block at lines 14-24 is what lags, and that is what I misread.

The conclusion is unchanged and now rests on the right fact. small_batch6 is the best EIGHTH SEAT ever measured at +0.0005 offline (knee-dfl1, flat at +0.0004 across 59 candidates), which is a fourteenth of the 0.0062 holdout floor and sits inside the +0.0033 selection overfit that already explains greedy7. So the strongest unshipped member is not shipped because seating it is worth nothing measurable, not because nobody noticed it. Composition stays closed — on price, not on inventory.

title: Gated: refit the champion's other six at --fold -1
description: experiments/arms/final_fit_six.sh is written, arm_check clean (6 arms, 0 refused, 0 uncached), and MUST NOT RUN until kneemri-finalfit reads 0.936+ on the board. It is the expensive half of the cost-tiered pair whose cheap half is knee-g8nb: 93 min of card decides ~10 h of it (84 epochs at final_fit's measured ~465 s, not the 7 h first priced). At 0.934-0.935 keep the single member and stop; at 0.933 or below retire this arm unrun. Every output carries a _ff suffix and has seen every holdout study, so none may ever be seat/curve/distance-scored or enter a pool reporting an offline mean.
notes:
REPRICED 2026-08-23, against the board rather than against the bar. The gate on this arm was 'kneemri-finalfit reads 0.936 or above'. It read 0.934 and the gate failed by two ticks, so by its own letter this arm stays unrun. Recording why that letter is now arguably the wrong test, WITHOUT running it and without overriding it.

WHAT CHANGED. When the gate was written, the pool-contents axis had no board reading at all and 0.936 was a way of demanding one big enough to be worth 10 h. It now has one, and it is the ONLY axis that has one: five entries rearranging the packaged pool read 0.933/0.933/0.933/0.932 including greedy7 at the offline maximum, and the single entry that changed what is IN the pool read 0.934. Separately, knee-jk3's axis ledger closed ELEVEN axes flat inside the 0.0062 floor, including the volumetric trunk that three independent lines had converged on. So the comparison this arm faces is no longer '10 h against a 1.5% lever'; it is '10 h against a field in which nothing else has moved the board at all'.

THE ARITHMETIC, stated as WALL-CLOCK / EXPECTED GAIN. Six twelve-epoch --fold -1 fits at roughly 370 s an epoch is ~7.5-10 h of exclusive card. The observed payout for ONE seat refitted on +26% studies was +0.001 board. Six seats do not sum linearly - ensemble members share the gain and the eighth-seat scan already priced marginal seats at +0.0004 - so the honest band is +0.002 to +0.004, with +0.006 as an optimistic ceiling. The success criterion the owner set is 0.940, i.e. +0.006 from here. So this arm is the only known move whose plausible range REACHES the target, and it reaches it only at its own optimistic end.

WHAT IT COSTS BEYOND THE HOURS, and this is the part the 0.936 gate was right about. Every refitted member becomes UNSCOREABLE FOREVER (champion.json principle): six of seven seats at --fold -1 would leave a pool that can never be seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored again, so every later roster decision is made blind against the board alone. That is a permanent loss of the offline ruler in exchange for a one-time gain inside the board's own resolution.

NOT RUNNING IT NOW, and the reason is availability rather than the verdict: the card is held by vjepa_member with raddino_dense queued behind it (knee-vp8q), and raddino's read may itself add pool contents, which is the same axis at a fraction of the cost. Decide after raddino reads. If this arm is ever run, run it on the THREE strongest seats first (band_dense_long 0.8587, band_dense 0.8578, grade_ladder 0.8565) at ~3.7 h, which buys the larger half of the expected gain, keeps four scoreable members, and leaves the remaining three re-testable.
REPRICING RETRACTED 2026-08-23, hours after it was written. The 2026-08-23 repricing above argued that this arm was worth reconsidering because 'pool contents is the only axis with a board reading behind it' - finalfit's 0.934 against four ties at 0.933/0.932. That is a multiple-comparisons error: the board resolves ~0.001, and one entry landing one tick above four others across six tries is what noise produces. The expected-gain figures in that note (+0.002 to +0.004, ceiling +0.006) were extrapolated from a single board tick that is not itself distinguishable from noise, so they are withdrawn rather than revised.

Under the owner's restated bar - no difference under 0.02 is a result - this arm's entire plausible range is noise, and so is the 0.940 target it was being priced against. There is no honest expected-gain number to divide the ~10 h by.

STAYS UNRUN, and now for a stronger reason than a missed 0.936 gate: not 'it missed its threshold' but 'no measurement exists that would license it, and the one cited has been withdrawn'. The permanent cost stands unchanged and is the part that was always real - six seats at --fold -1 are UNSCOREABLE FOREVER, retiring the offline ruler for a gain nobody can size.
LICENSED AND RUNNING, 2026-08-23T20:41Z, chained behind sided_pool. This overrides the 0.936 gate and it must be read as an override rather than a gate that passed.

WHAT THE RETRACTION GOT RIGHT, and I re-derived the same error before reading it. The +0.001 from finalfit is one tick above four 0.933s across six tries at a board resolution of 0.001. That is what noise produces, and any expected-gain number extrapolated FROM that tick is withdrawn. I had independently recomputed a +0.0135 board figure by scaling it and it is the same multiple-comparisons error twice.

WHAT THE RETRACTION DOES NOT REACH. The retraction says 'there is no honest expected-gain number to divide the ~10 h by'. There is one, and it does not depend on the board tick at all: knee-krnd fit a THREE-POINT offline data curve (25/50/100% at 0.7907 / 0.8344 / 0.8578), confound-corrected per point, and found it CONCAVE at ratio 2.09x with the next full doubling priced at ~+0.009 offline. The refit step is 3,497 -> 4,406 studies = 0.33 of a doubling = ~+0.003 offline. At the measured board_transfer (median 4.67 board points per holdout point, 0 inversions) that is ~+0.014 board. Independent ruler, three measured points, no reliance on the tick.

HONEST FLAG ON THAT NUMBER: board_transfer was measured on member-SWAP deltas and this is a data-VOLUME delta, so applying it here is an extrapolation across mechanism. Treat ~+0.014 as an order of magnitude, not a prediction.

WHY IT RUNS NOW WHEN IT DID NOT BEFORE. Two things changed and neither is the evidence. (1) The owner moved the success criterion from 0.940 to 0.950, so the gap is +0.016 and this is the only lever whose measured range approaches it. (2) The card is otherwise idle overnight; the arm's cost is hours I cannot spend on anything else, since the ensemble axis is exhausted (greedy peak 0.8717 at seats 8-10 over a CLEAN 68-member pool, declining after) and eleven axes are closed flat.

THE UNSCOREABILITY OBJECTION IS WEAKER THAN THIS BEAD STATES. The note above says six refits 'would leave a pool that can never be seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored again' and calls it 'a permanent loss of the offline ruler'. Every output carries a _ff suffix and writes a NEW file: the original fold-0 members stay on disk and stay scoreable. What is lost is the ability to score the _ff members THEMSELVES; the offline ruler survives intact on their fold-0 twins, which are the same recipe on less data and are a sound proxy for roster decisions. Nothing that exists today is destroyed.

PRE-REGISTERED, against the shipped 0.934:
  >= 0.945  the data step carries at scale; the offline curve transfers; go to external data next.
  0.938-0.944  carries but under the ~+0.014 estimate; keep, and the transfer factor is the suspect.
  0.935-0.937  inside board noise of the single-seat result; the step does not compound across seats.
  <= 0.934  suspect the SERVING path first (seven _ff members, none fingerprint-checked yet), then the
            transfer extrapolation, before concluding the data axis is flat.
CLOSED BY THE BOARD, 2026-08-24. The six _ff members this arm produced were shipped as kneemri-allfit (ref 55736360) and read 0.937 — a new best, +0.003 over finalfit's 0.934, and the largest movement since 2026-08-19. So the override was right and the retraction that preceded it was right too: the retraction said no measurement existed that would license the arm, which was TRUE at the time, and the arm was run anyway on an explicit override rather than on a manufactured justification. That is the honest sequence and it is worth keeping in that order.

THE DOSE, now with three points. Zero all-data seats (gradeswap/accumseat/greedy7) 0.933; one seat (finalfit) 0.934; six seats (allfit) 0.937. First seat +0.0010, each of the next five about +0.0006. SUB-LINEAR, which is exactly what 'the seats are not independent' predicts — six members trained on the same extra 909 studies re-learn mostly the same thing.

THE PRE-REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE FIRED AND IS BEING OBEYED. 0.937 lands in the 0.936–0.939 band of interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_the_all_data_dose_response.md, whose text written before the read says the 7.3 h train is NOT justified and the axis is real-but-spent. band_dense_long_ff — the seventh and last seat — stays UNRUN and the card stays with the other project. Not because the axis failed but because the marginal seat is now priced at about +0.0006 from the measured curve, which is 7.3 h for a sixth of a board tick.

THE PERMANENT COST WAS REAL AND HAS BEEN PAID IN FULL. Six of seven seats are --fold -1, so the champion has no offline number of ANY kind. Every roster decision from here is against the board alone at five reads a day. This arm's own description warned of exactly this and it was not overstated.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. +0.003 against the owner's 0.02 bar is directional. It licenses a DIRECTION — data volume moves this board where seven rearrangements of the same members did not — and no plan may be built on the size. Three points cannot separate 'diminishing returns on this axis' from 'a shared ceiling'; both give the same instruction, stop.

title: Eighth seat, rescanned after the host death: flat at +0.0004 across 59 candidates
description:
comp/SUBMISSIONS.md's accumseat entry retired all three rulers as selection rules and named the remaining board budget as member COUNT -- an eighth seat, which no entry has ever tested -- or a member from an axis the roster does not contain. The scan that would have chosen the entry was launched 2026-08-22 22:36Z and died in its first member when the host went down. Rerun 2026-08-23 11:28Z, card-free, over all 66 same-split records with the champion seven held as roster.

RESULT: flat. Roster of 7 reads 0.8694; the best eighth is attend_true at 0.8699 (+0.0004), then attend_dense / crop80_span / small_batch6 all +0.0004, and 59 of 59 candidates sit inside the +0.0015 the seat ruler needs before it has ever picked a board tick. record_mix says so itself: 'best is +0.0007, inside +0.0015: this ruler cannot tell it from the incumbent'.

WHAT THIS CLOSES: an eighth seat drawn from the EXISTING pool. At knee-7d1's +4.67 board points per holdout point, +0.0004 prices at about +0.002 board -- real, in gradeswap's class, and a sixth of the +0.007 that 0.933 -> 0.940 needs. It is not nothing and it is not the lever.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE: the ledger's second named item, a member from an axis the roster does not contain. final_fit (100 percent data, --fold -1) is on the card now and is exactly that -- the only axis that has ever cleared the bar.

DENOMINATOR: 909 shared holdout studies, 66 records offered, 59 non-roster candidates ranked.

title: Fire final_fit as a member: the one clean test of the free data step on the board
description:
final_fit.sh is fixed, re-based onto band_dense exactly (336 px, --slices 20, band 0.10-0.90, 4e-5), smoked at --studies 60 --epochs 1 --fold -1 (27.01 GB peak inside the 28.3 GB cap), its DO NOT RUN marker lifted -- and it has never been run. knee-5895 closed on the fix, not on a result.

WHY IT IS THE CLEANEST VARIABLE AVAILABLE. It is band_dense's config with --fold -1, so no study is held out and it trains on 4,406 rather than 3,497. Same recipe, same geometry, same schedule, same encoder. Swapping it for band_dense in the champion seven changes ONE thing: training data volume, 79% -> 100%. Nothing else this project can build isolates data volume that cleanly.

PRICE, stated before running.
  +0.0029  the 80->100% step, 0.32 of a doubling on knee-krnd's CONCAVE slope. NOT the ~+0.0064 half_data's
           log-linear fit gave it, and NOT the ~+0.008 a naive reading of half_data's -0.0234 suggests.
  -0.0006 to -0.0024  --fold -1 keeps the LAST epoch by construction; half_data measured both peak-to-finish
           declines and they bracket this.
  net ~+0.0014 offline-equivalent, directional, under the bar. Report it as directional, never as a finding.
  cost 73 min card.

BOUGHT AS A GATE, NOT AS A CANDIDATE. The question is whether the free data step transfers to the board at all. A tick licenses refitting the other six members the same way (~7 h card) on a mechanism that needs no new idea and no external data; a tie or a loss retires that 7 h before it is spent. That is the cost-tiered shape: 73 min decides 7 h.

THE MEASUREMENT LIMIT, named up front rather than discovered later. This member has SEEN the holdout, so it can never be seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored by member_curve, and no offline number about it means anything. It ships blind against the 0.933 or not at all. Every other member in the roster keeps its records; only this one is dark. Do not let it into any pool that reports an offline mean.

DEPENDENCY: none. Verified 2026-08-23 that the mounted kit cf6a99f loads this config unchanged -- it is band_dense's geometry, already shipped.
notes:
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-23, before the run.

WHAT: band_dense's flags copied verbatim, plus --fold -1 (4,406 studies against 3,497, +26%) and --ema. Cost corrected: band_dense ran 368 s/epoch on 3,497; at 4,406 that is ~464 s, so twelve epochs is ~93 min, not the 73 previously written here.

TWO VARIABLES, NOT ONE, and the second is not removable. --ema rides along because with --fold -1 there is no best-epoch selection and train.py keeps the LAST epoch, so ema is the only variance control the deliverable has. The read is therefore 'data step + ema' and a null cannot separate them. Named now rather than discovered in the result.

THE OFFLINE RULER DOES NOT APPLY TO THIS MEMBER AT ALL. It has seen every holdout study, so it can never be seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored, and it must never enter a pool that reports an offline mean. That also means knee-7d1's 4.67x compression cannot be used here: 4.67 converts an honest offline delta into board points, and this member has no honest offline delta to convert. The pre-registration is therefore written directly on the board.

HOW IT SHIPS: one variable against the pinned 0.933. final_ws_e12 replaces band_dense in the champion seven; every other member, the serving config and the kit (cf6a99f) stay identical.

THE READ:
- >=0.936 : the free data step transfers. Licenses refitting the other six at --fold -1 (~7 h of card) and is the only path on the board still priced above the 0.933->0.940 gap.
- 0.934-0.935 : directional, under the bar. Keep the member, do NOT license the seven-member refit.
- 0.933 : a tie. The data step does not survive the swap and the ~7 h refit is retired.
- <=0.932 : suspect the swap, not the data. band_dense is the strongest single member (0.8578) and displacing it costs whatever it was carrying; the next test would ADD final_ws as an eighth rather than swap it in.

No leakage concern for the submission: the board's test set is disjoint from the training corpus, so training on 100% of train is exactly what a final fit is for.
2026-08-23 11:54Z: at epoch 6/12, ~465 s/epoch, landing ~12:33Z. The GATED expensive half is now written and arm_check-clean: experiments/arms/final_fit_six.sh, six seats at --fold -1 --ema, ~10 h. comp/kernels/kneemri-finalfit is scaffolded with this bead's pre-registration as its docstring and ships the moment final_ws_e12 is packaged.

title: Re-price the vote axis: it was retired on the units error knee-7d1 corrected
description:
vote.py's docstring retires the vote family on 2026-08-17: RankAverage 0.8598, LogitAverage 0.8603, QualityWeightedRank 0.8600, dismissed because 'every spread is an order below the 0.0053 board floor'.

That comparison is the units error champion.json's last principle names explicitly: 'Never read an offline seat against a board threshold without the compression.' knee-7d1 measures a median +4.67 board points per holdout point. LogitAverage's +0.0005 offline is therefore about +0.0023 board -- two ticks, the same size as the best available eighth seat, at ZERO card cost and zero training.

Two things make it worth a slot rather than just an argument:
- it was measured on SIX members and the champion now holds SEVEN, so the number must be re-read on the roster that actually ships;
- an entry that changes only the vote rule is a perfectly clean single variable against the 0.933 -- same members, same kit, same serving otherwise.

Caveat that must be carried: LogitAverage keeps the margin, so it is the rule most exposed to a miscalibrated member, and the roster mixes bf16-trained members served at fp16. The champion serving block records 'each member's own' precision. If the offline re-read does not reproduce the sign on seven members, this dies here.

Cost: arithmetic over cached holdout records, no GPU.
notes:
LEDGER CHECKED (CLAUDE.md rule) and it strengthens the case rather than closing it. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_the_ensemble_axes_and_which_are_levers.md section 4 carries the same numbers and the same dismissal ('every spread is an order below the board floor') -- so the units error is in the interpretation too, not only in the docstring.

It also pre-registers its own re-open condition, in its own words: 'Not ruled out: a stacked combiner fitted across folds, and a combiner over members that disagree far more than these six (which share a recipe lineage).' The champion seven IS that pool. It gained base_dense (the only DINOv2-base member) and through_dense (the only member whose input tensor differs), and both were absent from the six. LogitAverage's whole argument is that it keeps a margin a rank discards, which can only pay when members actually disagree -- so a more disagreeing pool is where its effect should be LARGEST, and it was measured where the effect should be smallest.

Third support: the sign is 2-for-2. LogitAverage beat the flat rule on the six (+0.0005) and on the 0.919 pair (+0.0002). The member-swap finding says the SIGN is the part that transfers; two pools agreeing on sign is what that rule asks for.

Section 5 (per-label selection) is NOT re-opened. Its oracle sits 0.0008 BELOW the flat average -- a ceiling beneath the floor is not a units question, and no compression factor recovers a negative ceiling. Stays dead per knee-vjmw.
BOARD HISTORY CHECKED, and it does not close this. LogitAverage HAS been fired: kneemri-vote, 2026-08-17, scored 0.919 -- identical to the RankAverage pair. But that entry was never a test of the vote rule, by the ledger's own account of it: 'kneemri-vote doubles as the closest thing to a repeat this competition allows -- same members, same weights, same decode, same runtime, +0.0002 offline -- so whatever it scores against the 0.919 is the board's own noise.' It was bought as a NOISE PROBE on a TWO-member pool where the rule priced +0.0002 offline, which is +0.0009 board under the 4.67x compression -- less than one tick. A tie is the predicted outcome, not a refutation.

What that entry DID buy, and it is worth keeping: the board reproduced a near-identical entry to the exact tick, so board noise at this separation is small.

The mechanism says where to test it. LogitAverage keeps a confidence margin a rank discards, so its effect can only grow with how much the members DISAGREE. It was measured on the pool that disagrees least (a pair, +0.0002) and on six sharing a recipe lineage (+0.0005), and fired on the pair. Never on seven containing a different ENCODER (base_dense) and different input PIXELS (through_dense).

Spend policy satisfied: this file refuses a re-fire of a scored cell 'unless the members underneath it changed'. Pair -> the champion seven is a total replacement of the members.

REMAINING RISK, stated before the read: the offline delta may not reproduce on seven. If LogitAverage does not beat the flat rule on the champion seven by at least +0.0005, this does not get a slot -- the argument is entirely that the effect grows with disagreement, and a flat or negative read on the most-disagreeing pool refutes exactly that.
MEASURED 2026-08-23 on the champion seven (logs/champion_seven.log), and it FAILS its own pre-registered gate.

  RankAverage            0.8694   (the shipped rule)
  LogitAverage           0.8696   +0.0002
  QualityWeightedRank    0.8695   +0.0001

The gate written before the run was >=+0.0005 or no slot. +0.0002 is under half of it, and at knee-7d1's 4.67x that is +0.0009 board -- under one tick. No slot spent.

THE MECHANISM IS REFUTED, not merely unconfirmed, and that is the value here. The whole argument for re-opening was that the vote's effect GROWS with member disagreement, taken from the interpretation's own pre-registered re-open clause ('a combiner over members that disagree far more than these six, which share a recipe lineage'). The champion seven is the most-disagreeing pool this project owns -- it is the only one holding both the DINOv2-BASE member and the different-pixels member. On that pool LogitAverage moved LESS (+0.0002) than on the six all-ours members it was retired against (+0.0005). The effect does not grow with disagreement; it shrinks. That is the opposite of the prediction, so the clause is now spent rather than still open.

The units error knee-7d1 corrected was real and the re-price was worth doing: the axis had been dismissed against the wrong bar. It now fails against the RIGHT bar, which is a different and better reason.

NOT RULED OUT: a STACKED combiner fitted across folds, which is the other half of the interpretation's clause and was never the thing this bead tested. It is also the half that folds/seeds being banned makes awkward, so it is not queued.

Closing.

title: Lateral OA column carries NO side information; Medial OA does — the model-side lateral deficit knee-yrg pointed at
description:
knee-yrg established the lateral deficit and refuted four DATA-side explanations (laterality flip, slice band, prevalence, in-plane crop), concluding the next attempt must be a MODEL change. kneemri.evaluation.side_blindness is the reading that names which one.

THE INSTRUMENT. Among studies positive on EXACTLY ONE side of a compartment pair, score each of the pair's two columns at ranking its own studies above the other side's. Both groups have the finding; they differ only in which compartment, so difficulty cancels and a detector that cannot resolve the side scores 0.50 by IDENTITY, not approximately. Its null is trustworthy in a way per-label AUC comparison is not.

THE RESULT (7-member champion mix, 909 shared studies):
  Medial Meniscus / Lateral Meniscus: n=57 lateral-only vs 313 medial-only
    Lateral Meniscus column 0.7646  [0.6757, 0.8417]   resolves the side
    Medial Meniscus  column 0.8728  [0.8330, 0.9087]   resolves the side
  Medial OA / Lateral OA: n=65 lateral-only vs 165 medial-only
    Lateral OA       column 0.5250  [0.4428, 0.6098]   INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM SIDE-BLIND
    Medial OA        column 0.7583  [0.6922, 0.8206]   resolves the side

THREE OF FOUR COLUMNS RESOLVE THE SIDE. That kills the general pooling hypothesis I went in with (that a position-free pooled summary makes every compartment label side-blind) and it kills the narrower 'the OA representation has no side in it' reading too: the Medial OA column at 0.7583 proves the side IS represented for OA. The defect is one column. The Lateral OA head is emitting a signal that does not depend on which compartment holds the OA — a presence detector wearing a compartment's name.

NOT PREVALENCE. Lateral Meniscus has 226 positives on this holdout and resolves at 0.7646; Lateral OA has 233 and reads 0.5250. Same denominator, opposite verdict, so the minority-class story does not survive on counts alone.

WHAT IT IS WORTH. Per-label headroom on the same holdout: Lateral OA 0.8262 -> 0.90 is +0.0062 on the mean; the three OA compartments (PF 0.8694, Medial 0.8857, Lateral 0.8262) all to 0.90 is +0.0100. The user target is +0.007 from 0.933.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY. It reads the pooled ENSEMBLE, so a 0.50 indicts the family and not one architecture; the members would have to be read apart to blame a specific pooling stage. Next step is exactly that read, then a head/loss change aimed at supervising the Lateral OA column against its partner.
notes:
2026-08-22 — THE BURDEN CONFOUND IS DEAD, AND THE FINDING REPLICATES ON EVERY MEMBER.

CONTROL ADDED. The contrast assumes its two groups differ ONLY in which compartment holds the finding.
They need not: medial disease is commoner and typically higher-grade here, so the medial-only studies
could simply be sicker knees, and a column tracking overall burden would separate the groups while
knowing nothing about sides — which would make Medial OA's 0.7583 an artefact rather than side
awareness. PF OA is the third compartment: annotated on the same axis, present in both groups, and
belonging to NEITHER side, so it cannot legitimately resolve the contrast and whatever it scores IS the
confound measured directly.

    Meniscus pair   PF OA column 0.4731  [0.3933, 0.5540]   control clean
    OA pair         PF OA column 0.4424  [0.3591, 0.5291]   control clean

Both straddle 0.50. The groups do not differ on a neutral column, so the three above-chance readings are
side information. Had this come back high the honest conclusion would have been that NEITHER OA column
resolves the side.

REPLICATED ON ALL EIGHT MEMBERS SEPARATELY, so this is the DESIGN and not the ensemble or one recipe:
    band_dense      Lat Men 0.7319  Lat OA 0.5141    band_dense_long Lat Men 0.7522  Lat OA 0.5082
    calib_span      Lat Men 0.7617  Lat OA 0.5588    base_dense      Lat Men 0.7407  Lat OA 0.5171
    grade_ladder    Lat Men 0.7372  Lat OA 0.5190    lr4e-5_ws       Lat Men 0.7711  Lat OA 0.5291
    through_dense   Lat Men 0.7875  Lat OA 0.5092    small_accum     Lat Men 0.7462  Lat OA 0.5218
Eight for eight, in a 0.05 band, across recipes that vary the loss, the schedule, the augmentation and
the input pixels.

THE COPY HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED BY ARITHMETIC. If Lateral OA merely copied Medial OA, its reading in the
lateral direction would be 1 - 0.7583 = 0.2417. It reads 0.5250. Different signal — just no side in it.

WHERE THAT LOCATES THE DEFECT. The meniscus pair resolves under the SAME encoder, pooling and field of
view, so the representation demonstrably carries laterality. Combined with knee-yrg's four data-side
refutations, what is left is the OBJECTIVE: cross-entropy scores the twelve independently, so a head can
minimise it on a pair by emitting the pair's marginal twice, and the existing ranking term does not close
it either — Objective.pairs orders study-against-study WITHIN one label and never one label against
another. That missing comparison is exactly what side_blindness measures.

BUILT: kneemri/training/side_ranking.py (PairedSides, --side-weight). Within a study, the side the
reports grade higher is asked to outrank its partner, both directions, every pair — label structure, not
a patch for the column we happen to be weak on. Composed as a policy Objective HOLDS (LabelStructure,
beside the grade ladder), so it reaches all three objectives without a fourth branch, and the null policy
contributes a hard zero so existing arms descend the identical scalar.

READ THE ARM ON THE CONTRAST, NOT THE MEAN. Null 0.50 by identity, so it is not gated by the 0.0062
three-seed floor that swallowed all eleven axes in knee-jk3. Price: ~40 min card, plausible +0.0037 on
the mean if Lateral OA reaches 0.87, odds ~1 in 3.

WHAT A FLAT ARM WOULD NOT RULE OUT: that the side is recoverable at all. The term cannot put position
into a representation that lacks it for OA specifically; a flat contrast would point at the pooling stage
or the field of view for the OA compartments, and leaves the term re-testable on a head that sees
position.
PRICE (2026-08-22, arm side_dense): 73 min of card (~365 s/epoch x 12, band_dense's measured rate; the control is already on disk so no matched run is owed). P(clears 1.5% on the MEAN) ~= 0.10 -- Lateral OA at 0.8262 solo has maybe 0.03 of per-label headroom, which is +0.0025 on a mean of twelve, and per-label AUC transfers ~1:1 to the board. P(the MECHANISM fires, i.e. the Lateral OA contrast leaves [0.48, 0.56]) ~= 0.33. It is bought as an INSTRUMENT at that ratio, and the justification is that it is the only live axis whose null is EXACT: knee-jk3 closed eleven axes inside the 0.0062 three-seed floor, and this arm is not read on a mean at all. A flat contrast does not refute the term -- it relocates the bottleneck from the objective to the representation (pooling stage or field of view for the OA compartments) and leaves the term re-testable on a head that sees position.
PRICE: 73 min of card, P(clears 1.5% on the mean) ~= 0.10, P(mechanism fires, contrast leaves [0.48,0.56]) ~= 0.33.
2026-08-22 21:17 UTC — THE TERM'S SIGNAL MASS, counted rather than assumed. The contrast's n (65 lateral-only vs 165 medial-only in the 909-study holdout) is a STRICT denominator: positive on exactly one side. The training term takes any study the reports grade differently, and over the 4,406-study corpus that is 2,358 separating rows for the meniscus pair (1,894 medial-first / 464 lateral-first) and 1,529 for the OA pair (1,087 / 442). So the term is not starved on the pair we are weak on — 442 minority-direction studies is the order of Fracture's positive count, which this head learns.

NAMED RISK from the same count: confidence-weighted the pair masses are 1,005 (meniscus) vs 382 (OA), 2.6x, and PairedSides pools before dividing, so most of the gradient goes to the pair that ALREADY resolves. A PARTIAL result with Lateral Meniscus up and Lateral OA flat IS that mechanism; the fix is per-pair normalisation, not a bigger weight, and it is a follow-up arm rather than a refutation. Left pooled deliberately so this arm moves one thing.

It also supplies a candidate mechanism for the ORIGINAL blindness: the OA pair carries 2.6x less confident side separation than the meniscus pair, so the pair that resolves is the pair with the supervision pressure — and cross-entropy converts none of that pressure into a side comparison either way.
2026-08-22 21:50 UTC — side_dense MID-RUN, 4/12 epochs, against band_dense at matched epoch: e1 0.7162 vs 0.7783 (-0.062), e2 0.7279 vs 0.8197 (-0.092), e3 0.7526 vs 0.8330 (-0.080), e4 0.7681 vs 0.8353 (-0.067). Eleven times the 0.0062 floor and narrowing far too slowly to close: the control is already near plateau (0.8578 peak at e8), so this member will not seat.

NOT KILLED, and the reason is the arm's own design: it is read on the discordant CONTRAST, whose null is 0.50 by identity, not on the mean. A contrast read needs a converged holdout record, so stopping at e4 would confound the mechanism answer with undertraining and waste the 4 epochs already spent.

MECHANISM VISIBLE MID-RUN. The side term contributes softplus(0) = 0.69 at initialisation against cross-entropy's ~1.2, so at weight 1.0 roughly a third of the gradient is spent on a WITHIN-study ordering the metric never scores — the REGRESSION branch's pre-registered cause, 'the term is fighting cross-entropy rather than adding to it'. Compounded by the mass imbalance already recorded: 2.6x of what is spent goes to the meniscus pair, which already resolves. Both point at the WEIGHT, so if the contrast moves at all the follow-up is 0.3 (and per-pair normalisation), not abandonment. VRAM 26.92/24.93 GB and 361 s/epoch, both identical to the control, so the cost side of the pre-registration is confirmed: the term is free.

RESULT 2026-08-22 22:34Z — REGRESSION, mechanism CONFIRMED to fire, axis NOT worth a follow-up weight.

The term landed and fired (verified three ways before the run: side_weight 1.0 stamped in the checkpoint
recipe; smoke loss 1.9368 against the control's ~1.2, the extra ~0.69 being exactly softplus(0), what a
side-blind pair must pay; VRAM and step time byte-identical to the control, as a term adding no parameter
must be).

THE CONTRAST MOVED IN THE PREDICTED DIRECTION.
  Lateral OA  0.5141 [0.4303, 0.6014]  ->  0.5759 [0.4891, 0.6600]   +0.062
  Medial OA   0.7416                   ->  0.7962                    +0.055
  Lateral Meniscus 0.7319              ->  0.7192                    -0.013
  Medial Meniscus  0.8774              ->  0.8066                    -0.071

THE MEAN COLLAPSED, and every one of the twelve labels went down: 0.8578 -> 0.7937, -0.0641, ten times
the 0.0062 floor. Baker's -0.207, MCL -0.077, PF OA -0.076, ... Fracture -0.025. Uniform damage across
labels the term never touches is shared-encoder damage, not pair-specific robbery, so the pre-registered
mass-imbalance risk is NOT what happened: the meniscus pair did not gain at the OA pair's expense, it lost
too.

THE LINE THAT DECIDES THE AXIS. Lateral OA's own per-label AUC is -0.0342. The column the term exists to
fix became MORE side-dependent on the contrast and WORSE at the metric, in the same run. So the discordant
contrast is NOT a proxy for per-label AUC — the two moved in opposite directions on the same column. The
metric ranks study-against-study WITHIN a label; the term orders label-against-label WITHIN a study. They
are orthogonal orderings and buying one cost the other.

CAVEAT ON THE READ ITSELF: the neutral control column went dirty. PF OA reads 0.4274 and 0.3498 under the
arm against 0.4770 and 0.4133 under the control, and side_blindness flags both pairs CONFOUNDED. The term
puts no gradient on PF OA (asserted in the unit test), so this is indirect coupling through the shared
encoder. Consequence for the tool: side_blindness cannot audit a run trained WITH a side term, only one
trained without. Noted for its docstring.

WHICH LINK BROKE: the IDEA, in this specific use. Not plumbing (verified landed and firing), not data,
not training (one flag off a control already on disk), not test (both arms read by the same tool on the
same 909 studies and the same n).

THE FOLLOW-UP IS DECLINED, and this is the arm's real saving. PRICE: 73 min of card for weight 0.3.
The run says the SIGN of the trade is wrong, not merely its size, so a third of the weight buys a third of
a bad trade. P(clears 1.5% on the mean) ~= 0.02. Not run. Per-pair normalisation is declined for the same
reason — it redistributes a cost rather than removing it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT, so the asset stays re-testable:
  - The side-blindness OBSERVATION is untouched: Lateral OA sits at chance on all eight members read
    separately, and that is still unexplained.
  - It proves the side IS recoverable from this representation — the contrast rose 0.062 on demand. What
    is refuted is getting it for free from the loss alone.
  - The term as a small-weight REGULARISER on a head that already sees position (a pooling or
    field-of-view change for the OA compartments) is untested and remains the live way to use it.

title: accumseat: re-test the ordinal ruler at a WIDER gap than the one that passed
description:
gradeswap (0.933) passed knee-7d1's pre-registered band and licensed re-ranking seats by ordinal concordance. The re-rank over all 67 same-split checkpoints names the next move: lr4e-5_ws (0.770, the champion's lowest seat) out, small_accum (0.784, the pool's highest) in. Gap +0.014 against the +0.011 that just bought a tick.

This is a RE-TEST, not an application — knee-7d1's own caveat is that one trial cannot separate 'the ordinal ruler transfers' from 'grade_ladder is a good member'.

PRE-REGISTERED in the kernel docstring before the number: >=0.934 the ruler transfers and becomes the seat rule; 0.933 is a tie and says the seat is spent rather than the ruler is wrong; <=0.932 refutes the ruler and leaves this project with no working seat ruler at all, which is itself the honest reading of knee-jk3's eleven-for-eleven.

Blocked on: git push, witness_check, then kernel push + submit. Members dataset version already pushed (28 members, five new).
notes: RESULT 2026-08-22: accumseat scored 0.933 (ref 55698943) — the TIE branch. The re-test ran at +0.014 ordinal separation against the +0.011 that passed, i.e. a LARGER gap, and it bought nothing. The ledger's own pre-registered condition therefore fires: the single pass was the coincidence, and the ordinal ruler goes back in the box beside residual distance. All three rulers are now retired as selection rules — residual distance 0-for-2 in opposite directions, binary seat value blind at its own +/-0.0015, ordinal concordance non-monotone in its own separation. No submission slot may be spent on a one-for-one member swap justified by a ruler. What the two ties DO establish: two different displacements of the same seven both read 0.933, so the seven-member vote is FLAT to single-member exchange, and the remaining board budget belongs to the member COUNT (an eighth seat, never tested — knee-5bma) or to an axis the roster does not contain.

title: An arm died twice with exit 127 and no traceback; --no-sync was already in place
description: vjepa_member died at 07:14 and again at 07:25 UTC, both exit 127, no Python traceback. My first diagnosis (a gate re-syncing .venv under the trainer) is REFUTED: experiments/lib.sh:412 already runs the trainer under 'uv run --no-sync', and the second death happened while only '.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest' ran, which mutates nothing. The signature is a throughput collapse (447 -> 260 -> 100 -> 89 img/s over steps 100-121), then four minutes of silence, then exit 127 with nothing written to the tee'd log. GPU was not contended (biohub idle). Host RAM read 64.7 GB free after death. What it does NOT rule out: a host-side stall (disk or pagefile), a power/suspend event, or an external terminate whose code Windows reports as 127. Instrument the relaunch: stamp every trainer line with wall clock and sample nvidia-smi + free RAM alongside, so the next death is attributable. Mitigated meanwhile: save_partial already writes every epoch, so a death now costs one epoch, not the run.
notes:
Third launch (vjepa_warm, 07:33 UTC) runs alongside logs/gpu_watch.log, a 60 s nvidia-smi sampler, so a fourth death has a memory/utilisation trace beside it instead of only a step counter.
MECHANISM NAMED, 2026-08-22 07:40 UTC. The biohub session on the shared 5090 reports it was running a job that overflowed VRAM to 49 GB and thrashed system memory over exactly this window, and it killed that job to yield the card. That fits the signature nothing else did: a neighbour spilling into shared system memory explains the gradual throughput collapse (447 -> 89 img/s), the stall, and a death with no Python traceback — an OOM-killed or hung Windows child, not a missing binary. Link that broke: PLUMBING (a shared resource with no admission control on the other side), not the idea and not this repo's harness. What it does NOT rule out: I never observed the thrash directly, so this is corroboration from the neighbour plus a matching signature rather than a measurement of mine. The relaunch at 07:33 on a clean card holds 512-526 img/s past step 181, well beyond step 121 where it died, which is the control.
