Asked biohub to derive their reservation up front the way DeviceBudget.needed() does, so an over-large run parks in a headroom wait instead of taking the neighbour down.

title: Warm-start an arm from a fitted member (FittedEncoder)
description: A member checkpoint and the file --encoder-weights reads were different shapes, so 23 fitted members on disk could not seed any arm. kneemri/training/fitted_encoder.py converts one: strips _orig_mod. and backbone., folds LoRA (base + up@down*alpha/rank, rank read off the adapter shape) and writes the {encoder,variant,cache,config} file PretrainedEncoder already reads. Proven end to end against vjepa_member_s2026.partial: loads into a stock vjepa2l with no refusal, 96 of 587 tensors changed = exactly the 6 opened blocks.

title: uvx nox re-syncs .venv and kills any arm training from it
description:
On 2026-08-22 the vjepa_member arm died at epoch 6 step 528/583 with trainer exit 127 (command not found), no Python traceback, after five clean epochs. Nothing was wrong with the recipe: 0.7396 -> 0.7737 -> 0.7935 -> 0.8027 -> 0.8177 -> 0.8313, still climbing +0.014 an epoch and already inside the 0.83-0.845 tie band at half the schedule.

The cause was a gate run. 'uvx nox -s gates' invokes 'uv run --extra devtools', which re-resolves and rewrites .venv. The trainer was executing .venv/Scripts/python.exe at the time, so its interpreter was replaced underneath it. The gate run's own pytest child died the same way, mid-collection at tests/unit/kneemri/kaggle/kit_check.py, which is what makes the mechanism unambiguous rather than a guess: one action, two processes, both losing the same binary.

Cost: 100 minutes of GPU and no checkpoint, because the arm writes a member only at the end.

Two independent fixes, and the arm's own one is the bigger win:

1. Per-epoch checkpointing in the arm path. An arm that has proved five epochs should not be able to lose them to anything at all - a crash, a reboot, or this. It also makes the warm-start bridge worth more.
2. A guard so a gate run cannot start while an arm holds the venv, in the shape of queue_check: ask the process table, not a flag. An arm could take a lock file naming its pid, and nox could refuse (or wait) while one is live.

Until either lands the rule is manual: do not run 'uvx nox' or 'uv run' while an arm is training.
notes:
RETRACTED 2026-08-22 — the diagnosis in the description is wrong, and so is its cost estimate. Three
things were checked and all three refute it.

1. THE TRAINER DOES NOT RUN FROM A SYNCED VENV. experiments/lib.sh:412 already invokes it as
   `uv run --no-sync --project "$REPO" python -u -m kneemri.training.train`, and the comment on that
   line names the 2026-08-13 incident `--no-sync` was added for. A gate run cannot rewrite an
   environment the arm was told not to resolve.

2. THE SECOND DEATH HAD NO GATE RUN AT ALL. vjepa_member died again at 07:25:41 UTC, step 121 of epoch
   0, while the only other process was `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest`, which mutates nothing.
   One mechanism has to cover both deaths and this one covers neither.

3. NOTHING WAS LOST. `save_partial` writes every epoch — fitting.py:153 calls it, trainer.py:451-454
   writes `<dest>.partial` via a .tmp then replace. The file was on disk holding epoch 5 at holdout
   0.8313367353652542, 600 tensors. "No checkpoint, 100 minutes gone" was false when written; the
   partial is what vjepa_warm now warm-starts from.

THE REAL MECHANISM is on knee-sx3a: a co-tenant filled 31.1 of 31.5 GB dedicated VRAM and spilled
23.4 GB into shared system memory across exactly the death window. That fits the signature nothing
else did — throughput decaying 447 -> 260 -> 100 -> 89 img/s over twenty steps, a four-minute stall,
then death with no traceback and nothing in the tee'd log.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT. The gate run's pytest child did die mid-collection on the first
occasion, and the VRAM story does not explain a CPU-only process dying. That remains unexplained and
is one observation, not a pattern; if it recurs without a co-tenant on the card, reopen on THAT
evidence rather than on this description.

The manual rule this bead ended with — "do not run uvx nox or uv run while an arm is training" — is
WITHDRAWN. It cost real serialisation for a mechanism that does not exist. Proposed fix 1 (per-epoch
checkpointing) already shipped long before this bead. Proposed fix 2 (a venv lock) guards nothing.

title: Extract core/data/: corpus + labels + findings move below kneemri
description:
Adopt cardiac-seg's layering: core/ is the kernel that holds the data layer, the named package is the science on top.

MEASURED, not assumed (2026-08-22):
  kneemri/corpus/   imports only kneemri.corpus (57 internal) + core.paths - zero outward deps
  kneemri/labels/   imports kneemri.findings (4 sites)
  kneemri/findings.py  imports nothing at all - pure leaf
  kneemri/runs/     imports kneemri.models - stays ABOVE the data layer, does not move

So the data layer is exactly corpus + labels + findings, and it already obeys the direction. Nothing to untangle.

Moves:
  kneemri/corpus    -> core/data/corpus
  kneemri/labels    -> core/data/labels
  kneemri/findings.py -> core/findings.py   (shared vocabulary several producers speak, per the house rule)

Blast radius: 131 python files, experiments/arms/*.sh, experiments/lib.sh, docs/architecture/graph.json, and the [tool.importlinter] contracts.

WHAT IT BUYS: the four forbidden-import contracts inside kneemri (corpus is the base layer, models sit on corpus alone, embeddings are a cache, runs sit on corpus and models alone) collapse toward one package-level contract import-linter enforces directly, instead of four hand-maintained module lists that have to name every sibling.

RISK, stated before starting: comp/kernels/* ship to Kaggle and the kit is pinned at cf6a99f, already 3 commits stale. This rename means the next kit rebuild carries the rename plus those 3 fixes. Gate the next rebuild on kit_check --mounted, mount_check, and witness_check before any submission.

title: core/config.py: paths become a real config (per-kind override, translate-or-raise)
description:
Port cardiac-seg's core/config.py + core/paths.py hardening.

paths.yaml today holds ONE key (data:) and DataRoot hardcodes raw/ and processed/. Two gaps:

1. No per-kind override. cardiac-seg's Config.data_root(kind) reads a top-level yaml key named for the kind, so 'processed: /big/scratch/processed' redirects the cache off the data root without a code change. We cannot.

2. A foreign or missing path goes SILENTLY RELATIVE. Six empty dirs were found at repo root on 2026-08-22 named after CLI values and arm names (1, 60, 336px_20sl_140mm_0.1-0.9band_first60, encoder_adapt_thawed, half_data, vjepa_member) - a relative mkdir landing in CWD. cardiac-seg hit the same class and its paths.py docstring records it leaked dataset metadata into git. Their fix: Paths.resolve_data_root translates a Windows drive path to/from its WSL mount and RAISES on an untranslatable one. Never silently relative.

DataRoot keeps its constructor and from_config signature so the ~40 call sites are untouched.

title: Aim an arm at DISTANT-AND-STRONG: nearest-neighbour under 0.88 and solo over 0.85
description:
Both submission rulers were run over all 16 mounted-but-unseated members against the true champion (sevenplane, 0.932, seven members) on 2026-08-22. Seat value: 0 of 16 clear the +0.0015 BOARD_RESOLVABLE threshold, best +0.0005. Distance: the four most distant candidates (lora_r8_v3small_224 0.8235, dinov3_base_lora 0.8286, crop80_tissue 0.8422, deep24 0.8428) are the bottom four by seat value.

Every mounted candidate is either STRONG AND A TWIN or DISTANT AND WEAK. The board has priced both halves: sixstrong seated a strong twin and lost a tick; crossenc and maxdiv seated distant weak members and lost four and five. So an eighth seat from this pool is negative-expectation, not a coin flip.

The one member that was both is the one that won: through_dense, 0.8558 solo with nearest neighbour 0.8922, carried sevenplane's +0.001.

WHAT THIS ISSUE IS: no arm in this repository has ever been aimed at the PAIR. Arms are pre-registered against a matched control on solo score, which selects for twins by construction -- a recipe one flag from the control produces a member correlated with it. The target to pre-register instead is nearest-neighbour under ~0.88 AND solo at or above ~0.85, measured with kneemri.evaluation.member_distance alongside the holdout.

CAVEAT ON THE RULER, recorded so it is not over-trusted: label-free correlation does not order the three tested sevenths monotonically (through_dense 0.8922 -> 0.932, band_span 0.9188 -> 0.930, grade_ladder 0.9248 -> 0.931). grade_ladder is the least distant of all sixteen and beat the more distant band_span. Distance in the MECHANISM is what sevenplane measured; the correlation column is a proxy on three points.
notes:
2026-08-22 09:18Z -- vjepa_warm is the first ARM to test this clause at the extreme, and it splits it. Nearest seated neighbour 0.8210 against a seated spread topping out at 0.8801: maximum measured distance, 0.059 clear of anything on the roster, and NOT the broken-representation kind (mae_matched's 0.4333 is what uncorrelated-because-broken looks like). Solo 0.8337, so it misses this bead's over-0.85 clause by 0.017. Seat value +0.0002, 0 of 1 clearing +0.0015.

Verdict for this bead: DISTANCE IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. The clause was written as an AND and the AND is what carries it -- a distant-and-weak member buys nothing, so no future candidate may be seated on distance alone. The distance ruler itself is NOT refuted; its reading was correct. What failed is the inference from distance to seat. Ledger row: experiments/README.md, 'vjepa_warm -- the re-test lands in the TIE band'.
2026-08-22 09:33Z -- HARDENED FROM n=1 TO n=63 on a second ruler, see knee-5bma and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-22_the_pool_is_exhausted.md. record_mix priced every same-split record against the shipped seven: vjepa_warm, the most distant member this project owns, adds +0.0001, while small_batch6 (+0.0005), crop80_span (+0.0004) and aug_long (+0.0004) all beat it and none of them is remarkable on any diversity axis. So the ordering itself refutes distance-as-a-seat-predictor, not just the one extreme case. This bead's AND remains the right shape; what is now measured is that no member in the pool satisfies either clause well enough to matter -- best eighth seat of 63 is +0.0005 against a +0.0015 board-resolvable threshold.
Second failure of the residual-distance INFERENCE, same day, opposite direction. vjepa_warm: most distant member ever produced here (nearest seated neighbour 0.8210 vs a seated spread topping at 0.8801), priced +0.0001 as a seat. gradeswap: grade_ladder called the MOST redundant of 23 for its strength (+0.0187 corrected, pearson 0.890), predicted to lose a tick, and it took the board from 0.932 to 0.933. Distant-and-weak buys nothing; redundant-and-strong bought a tick. The ruler measures residual geometry correctly; the inference from that geometry to seat value has now failed twice, independently, in both directions. It is not a selection rule. Ordinal concordance is the one that passed its forward test.
MEASURED 2026-08-24, and this bead is now the ONLY open cell on the axis. MemberCurve.diverse (forward selection by disagreement, parameter-free) run against the greedy over 70 same-split records / 909 shared studies, card-free: diverse peaks 0.8624 at 62 seats, greedy peaks 0.8719 at 9, and at matched nine seats diverse reads 0.8331.

Distance alone is refuted as a seat rule. But the mechanism of its loss is what makes THIS bead live: diverse's first five seats include quarter_data and half_data, members trained on a fraction of the corpus. Distance and weakness are CORRELATED in this pool. Every distant member we own is distant partly by being bad, so the greedy has never been offered the distant-and-strong trade it would have to refuse for the axis to be honestly closed.

Also corrected: the greedy is not blind to distance. It seats vjepa_warm 12th and mae_matched (most distant, solo 0.6735) 18th, on a plateau flat to four decimals. It takes them late, not never.

knee-u0my (v3lora_dense) is the arm built to break the correlation. Falsification is now cheap and does not need a seat value: re-run --seats diverse with the new member in the pool. Ledger: experiments/README.md 'DISTANCE AS A SEAT RULE'. Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_architecture_diversity_is_closed_and_the_empty_cell_is_strong_and_distant.md
OCCUPANT FOUND 2026-08-24, and it came from the OBJECTIVE, not from a trunk swap. margin_seat (band_dense's recipe, --auc-margin 1.0 --rank-weight 0.0, single variable verified in the checkpoint stamp) reads:

  SOLO 0.8525 vs control band_dense 0.8578 = -0.0053, INSIDE the 0.0062 floor. Converged (peak e10, 0.8524 at e11, no turn-down), so quality is not distinguishable from the control by this ruler -- which satisfies this bead's 'at or above ~0.85' clause.
  DISTANCE nearest 0.8628, mean 0.8314, against the greedy roster's own nearest-neighbour spread of 0.8717-0.8893. It is further from every seated member than any two of them are from each other -- this bead's 'nearest-neighbour under ~0.88' clause, cleared.
  SEAT priced card-free with record_mix over 65 fold-0 records: add +0.0015 (exactly BOARD_RESOLVABLE), best swap +0.0013 displacing crop80_span. Greedy takes it SECOND of 65 (small_batch6 0.8598 -> margin_seat 0.8669, +0.0071 to the pair).

WHY THIS IS NOT A FOURTH FAILURE OF THE SAME INFERENCE. The three failures recorded above (vjepa_warm, gradeswap, diverse) all tested distance produced by ARCHITECTURE or by DATA STARVATION, and the note above named the confound exactly: 'every distant member we own is distant partly by being bad'. margin_seat breaks that confound -- same trunk, same data, same recipe, distance bought by the loss. The per-label profile is a redistribution of about +/-0.03 with a near-flat mean (MCL +0.0272*, Fracture +0.0250, Baker's +0.0163* against Lateral Meniscus -0.0546*, PF OA -0.0288*, Medial Meniscus -0.0277*), i.e. a DIFFERENT error structure rather than a worse one.

LIMITS, so this is not over-read: greedy selection on the holdout is in-sample, +0.0015 is at the edge of what this ruler has ever resolved (0 of 3 clear it by the tool's own line), and the pinned champion cannot be priced against at all because six of its seven members are --fold -1.

CONSEQUENCE: the loss axis outranks the trunk axis for seat-hunting. dissent_seat is on the card now testing whether this is a property of AUC-margin specifically or of moving the objective at all. Ledger row + full write-up: experiments/README.md, 'margin_seat -- a losing solo that greedy picks SECOND of sixty-five'.

title: Domain-matched MAE pretrain: pre-register the read BEFORE the fine-tune arm, because the pixel loss is already near-flat
description:
The arm: pretrain_matched_e8 (logs/pretrain_matched_e8.log), 8 epochs, 4193 steps/epoch, ~490 s/epoch, ~820 slices/s. Then a ~25 min read arm — fine-tune with --encoder-weights pretrain_small_matched_e8.pt, byte-identical to band_dense otherwise, 4 epochs.

CONTROLS (already on the ledger, not re-run): adapt_null 0.8240 @ e3, band_dense 0.8232 @ e3. Collapsed arms sit at ~0.63-0.73, so the floor that says 'the weights loaded but broke the trunk' is far below the band this will land in.

PRE-REGISTRATION, written while epoch 2 of 8 is still running so it cannot be fitted to the answer:
  epoch 0  pixel 0.9859  spectral 1.2171
  epoch 1  pixel 0.9704  spectral 0.7760
Pixel moved 1.6% in two epochs; spectral fell 36%. The objective is being carried almost entirely by its spectral term. So whatever this arm measures, it is NOT 'reconstruction pretraining' in the plain sense — it is a spectrally-shaped initialisation. Name that before reading the number, because the obvious wrong verdict is 'MAE pretraining does not transfer' when what was actually tested is a trunk that never learned to reconstruct pixels.

READS:
  >= 0.838 (+1.5% over adapt_null): the axis is real, harden it.
  0.824-0.838: directional at best, and per the house bar not a finding. Do NOT spend a submission slot.
  < 0.824: the arm failed. Before any verdict, check WHICH LINK — did --encoder-weights actually land (assert the trunk's first-block weights differ from the fetched DINOv2, do not assume), is 4 epochs enough for a differently-initialised trunk to catch up to one that starts pretrained, and is the pixel-flatness above the whole explanation.
WHAT A NULL DOES NOT RULE OUT: a pixel-weighted or longer MAE, and volume-native pretraining (CoPAS's surviving component) which is a different asset entirely.
notes:
ARM WRITTEN 2026-08-22 03:33 UTC: experiments/arms/mae_matched.sh, arm_check-clean. Byte-identical to band_dense except --encoder-weights, 4 epochs, ~25 min. It takes the card the moment pretraining releases it (epoch 5 of 8 at 03:32, ~490 s/epoch, so ~03:57 UTC).

The pre-registration above is now stronger, not weaker: three more epochs of pixel-flatness have landed since it was written — 0.9704 @ e2, 0.9708 @ e3, 0.9702 @ e4, against spectral 0.7218 -> 0.5755 -> 0.4878. So 'spectrally-shaped initialisation' is not an inference from two points any more; the pixel term has not moved in FIVE epochs while the spectral term halved again. That is the thing the arm actually measures, and it is written into the arm's own header so the verdict cannot drift off it.
RESULT 2026-08-22: mae_matched = 0.6735 at epoch 3, against adapt_null 0.8240 and band_dense 0.8232 at the same epoch. Delta -0.1505. That is not a null, it is the FIFTH COLLAPSE in this family, and it lands inside the 0.63-0.73 band the arm's own header named as the floor meaning 'the weights loaded and broke the trunk' while asserting a null would not be that. The header was wrong about which band this would land in.

WHICH LINK BROKE, worked before the verdict, and the answer is NOT the harness:
  PLUMBING  cleared. adapt_null is the same --encoder-weights path with a null adaptation and reads
            0.8240, so the load path is clean; the ledger already says so at line 308.
  DATA      cleared. Same cache key as the control (336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band, stamped in the checkpoint).
  TRAINING  cleared on variant. PretrainedEncoder.into RAISES on a variant mismatch and did not fire;
            checkpoint variant 'small' equals TrainingOptions().variant default 'small', and band_dense
            names no --variant either, so the arm's byte-identity claim against the control holds.
  TEST      cleared. Matched epoch, matched control, both on the ledger, not re-run.

THE FIX I REACHED FOR WAS ALREADY RUN. pretrained_encoder.py:47-58 documents the mechanism (pretraining
rewrites the TOP block -- block 11 moved 55% and 21% of its own norm where supervision never moves it
more than 0.8% -- and the head reads that block), and argues the axis only ever concerned the BOTTOM
blocks, which is what --encoder-adapt-depth 6 states. encoder_adapt_lower IS that arm: 0.7309, and the
ledger records its diagnosis as refuted. encoder_adapt_thawed 0.7162. encoder_adapt_gentle 0.6902/0.6875.

So the family now reads across TWO pretraining objectives (SSL-adaptive and spectrally-shaped MAE) and
TWO import depths (all blocks, bottom six): 0.6735 / 0.6875 / 0.6902 / 0.7162 / 0.7309, every one of
them 0.09 to 0.15 below a control that simply starts from stock DINOv2. Consistent with knee-jk3's board
re-read, which already listed SSL-as-init CLOSED. I flagged that prior before this arm ran and ran it
anyway because the 65-minute pretrain was already spent -- correct call on sunk cost, but the arm should
have been priced as an INSTRUMENT retiring the axis, not as an improvement.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT, kept re-testable: (a) volume-native pretraining, a different asset entirely
-- the trunk is pretrained by someone else on video volumes and imported whole, so it never passes
through this repo's adapt-and-import path at all (knee-rpkw, on the card now). (b) a pixel-weighted or
much longer MAE -- but five collapses across two objectives and two depths makes this a poor bet, and it
should not take a card ahead of anything on knee-jk3's surviving list.
MECHANISM NAMED: an encoder adapted by ANY reconstruction-shaped objective in this repo hands the
classifier a top block shaped for reconstruction, and importing less of it does not help because the
damage is not additive -- encoder_adapt_lower took only blocks 0-5 and still lost 0.13.
2026-08-24 AUDIT, ledger not bead: this is already REFUTED and the bead should not have stayed P1. experiments/README.md line 309 records mae_matched (DINOv2-small, 8 epochs masked reconstruction over 402,600 knee-MRI slices, the only encoder that has seen nothing but this domain) at 0.6735 @ e3, -0.1505 vs adapt_null at matched epoch, and calls it 'the FIFTH collapse, closing the SSL-as-init family across two objectives and two import depths'. Every suspect was cleared before the verdict (plumbing: adapt_null is the same --encoder-weights path and reads 0.8240). Domain-matched MAE pretrain as an INIT is spent. What is NOT covered by that verdict: a 3D encoder that sees the volume before any per-slice feature exists (named untouched by depth_true's row). Closing this as refuted; that clause belongs in its own bead.

title: VolumeRead / the tubelet trunk is wired into model.py and has ZERO arms in the ledger
description:
AUDIT FINDING, 2026-08-22, unmeasured asset. kneemri/models/model.py:26,202,204-205 wires a VolumeRead / tubelet path — the trunk reads the stack as 3D tubelets rather than as independent slices. grep of experiments/README.md returns ZERO hits for it across 107 runs. It is the only ARCHITECTURE-SCALE axis this project has BUILT and never measured, and the owner's standing note that 'the data is 3D' points straight at it.

WHY IT MATTERS RELATIVE TO WHAT IS LEFT. Every axis measured this week landed inside a floor: encoder diversity closed (cnx_dense), FOV closed (band140), batch closed (batch_teardown, two arms), resolution flat twice at 336, adaptation closed (adapt_null + the frozen-bottom reading), the label-correlation head refuted (knee-w8h6). Data volume is the only axis that has ever cleared the bar and its slope is CONCAVE (quarter_data: each doubling buys ~0.48 of the last). A slice-independent trunk cannot represent through-plane extent at all, which is the mechanism class that could plausibly deliver 1.5% rather than a knob-sized delta.

BLOCKED BY, AND THIS IS THE REAL COST: knee-2nxh. The VRAM cap's activation_units is 2D-only — it computes (size/stride)^2 and a tubelet trunk's token count is (size/stride)^2 x frames/tubelet, so the cap under-reserves and the arm dies in the attention backward exactly as final_fit did at 392 px. Fix knee-2nxh FIRST or the arm's failure is the harness's, not the idea's.

BEFORE ARMING: python -m kneemri.experiments.arm_check, then a --studies 60 --epochs 1 smoke. Price the arm out loud before it takes the card.
PRICE: stated out loud before the card, 2026-08-22. COST ~2 h wall for 12 epochs of ViT-L at 20 slices a
study; the truncated cache and the CPU build check are already paid. GAIN if it lands: this is the last
surviving axis on knee-jk3's ledger whose mechanism is a REPRESENTATIONAL claim rather than a routing
one, and the frontier gap is 0.054, so the mechanism could plausibly deliver 1.5% where ten measured
knob axes could not. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.15, and that is the honest number: vjepa_probe already read a TIE
on frozen features, which is weak evidence against, weakened in turn because a latent-prediction
objective is not expected to be linearly separable and the probe spent the depth axis on a 3-slice
window. EXPECTED VALUE is therefore ~0.15 x 1.5% for 2 h, which does NOT beat a knob on arithmetic
alone. It takes the card anyway as an INSTRUMENT: it retires or licenses the whole 3D-trunk family that
every remaining backlog idea is downstream of (knee-pq8u, knee-ec0p, knee-jucq), and there is no cheaper
question that does that. Priced as an improvement it would be a bad buy; priced as the thing that
decides where the next ten hours go, it is the best buy on the board.
notes:
CORRECTION + UNBLOCKED, 2026-08-22. Two things in the description above are wrong and both moved the price:

1. The blocker's direction was backwards here too. The cap does not UNDER-reserve a tubelet trunk; DeviceBudget.needed multiplies by (slices + 1), so `units` is per-slice and a tubelet trunk costs grid^2/tubelet per slice — LESS. The cap OVERSTATED it 2x, so the arm would have parked in await_headroom, not died in the attention backward. knee-2nxh is now fixed (Stage/Encoder carry an explicit tubelet divisor; VJEPA2_LARGE declares tubelet=2).

2. There is no read-size choice to price. VolumeRead.check_tokens (kneemri/models/volume_read.py:87-95) asserts the read is the trunk's NATIVE crop, 256, because the spatial grid is not free the way depth is — 3D RoPE derives depth position ids at run time, the spatial weights were fitted at native//patch. So 336 was never an option, and the earlier 'does not fit even corrected' reading was pricing a size the code refuses.

DERIVED, at the only read that exists (256 px, 20 slices, batch 6, 6 blocks open):
  uncorrected  38.3 GB  -> refused on a 31.8 GB card

The arm is now armable. Next: python -m kneemri.experiments.arm_check, then --studies 60 --epochs 1 smoke, then price the full arm out loud before it takes the card.
ARMED AND PRICED, 2026-08-22 03:31 UTC. experiments/arms/vjepa_member.sh written and arm_check-clean.

THIRD CORRECTION, and it is larger than the first two: the tubelet path was UNARMABLE from any flag combination. Trainer.whole_stack is the only path to a window wider than GROUP = 3, and its guard demanded self.model.per_slice — which a volumetric read is not, by definition. Without it the window stays 3, which tubelet 2 does not divide, so VolumeRead.check_tokens would raise. So every number this trunk has produced here (vjepa_probe: 0.7620 vs a DINOv2-large control's 0.7669) was taken with its depth axis SPENT ON A WINDOW TOO NARROW TO CARRY IT. Fixed by moving the guard onto the model as StudyModel.check_whole_stack, which names the two different reasons a model can take a whole stack (per-slice pooling; a tubelet the window divides) instead of testing a proxy for one of them. Same bug class the per_slice docstring already recorded once (the guard tested != 'max' and silently rejected attention pooling the model supported).

FLAGS, all derived: --variant vjepa2l --pool mean --slice-pooling channels --whole-stack --slices 20 --train-size 256 --batch 6. No --vram-gb: arm_check reports a hand-typed 26 as OVERSTATED by 4.30 GB, i.e. DeviceBudget derives 21.7 — the corrected number to four figures, against a 31.8 GB card. 256 px is not a knob (native crop assert); 20 slices because tubelet 2 must divide the window; channels because it is the only non-per-slice pooling and VolumeRead.of requires one.

PRICE, out loud: ~2 h wall for 12 epochs. This is an INSTRUMENT, not an improvement — it retires or licenses the whole volume-pretraining axis that every 3D-trunk idea in the backlog sits downstream of. As a member it is priced by DISTANCE: the only candidate whose PRETRAINING DOMAIN differs from all six seated members, which is the third diversity axis after objective (sevengrade, 0.931, tie) and pixels (sevenplane, pending).

PRE-REGISTERED READ: >=0.845 says the depth axis carries what the frozen probe could not see, and the member earns a seat_value pricing against the champion five. 0.83-0.845 is the tie again, taken with the advantage actually spent, and RETIRES THE AXIS rather than the trunk. <0.82 means suspect the harness first, in this order: did --whole-stack land (trainer logs its window — 20, not 3), did VolumeRead.of build at all (it returns None SILENTLY when the config lacks tubelet_size, and the model then reads as an ordinary 2D ViT-L at 256), did six blocks open.

That branch cannot fire for this trunk, and the failure mode as written is the wrong shape anyway: on a wrong config VolumeRead.of RAISES. Asked for the default pool cls_mean it says 'a tubelet trunk emits no class token'. So --pool mean in the arm is not a preference, it is the only pooling this trunk admits, and a mis-specified arm dies at construction rather than quietly training a 2D ViT-L. SMOKE CAUGHT A DEFECT, AND IT WAS NOT SUSPECT #1 (2026-08-22).

The smoke died with 'a 256x256 read over 3 frames predicts 256 tokens and the trunk emitted 256'. That
reads as '--whole-stack did not land', which is failure mode #1 in this arm's own header. It is not.

Read the traceback's frames, not its message: fitting.py:153 keep -> member_record.py:375 payload ->
model.fingerprint(read_size, GROUP, device). The training epoch had already SUCCEEDED; the 3 frames are
the FINGERPRINT's synthetic bag, whose depth is the module constant GROUP = 3 by design. Three slices is
one and a half tubelets, so check_tokens refused it. --whole-stack landed fine.

Two things made the message misleading. The guard ORs three clauses and only 'frames % tubelet' fired,

title: adapt_null: does --encoder-weights reproduce control when the adaptation is stock?
description:
Four fine-tunes on the SSL axis collapsed (0.6902 / 0.6875 / 0.7162 / 0.7309) against band_dense 0.8578. The written verdicts blame the adaptation. The evidence does not support that attribution, and the reason is a magnitude argument nobody has made: encoder_adapt ran lr 1e-4 and moved blocks 0-5 by 3.4-8.3 percent; encoder_adapt_gentle ran lr 1e-5 and moved the same blocks by 0.46-1.79 percent, a 4x smaller perturbation. Their scores are 0.6902 and 0.6875 - a 0.0027 gap, well inside the 0.0062 floor. A cost that does not scale with the size of the change is not representational damage. It is something COMMON to both paths: the --encoder-weights load, or a preprocessing mismatch between pretrain.py and train.py.

THE CONTROL, which the axis never got: fine-tune from a NULL adaptation - stock DINOv2-small written through pretrain.py's own save path at --epochs 1 --max-steps 1 --lr 0, so AdamW's update and its decoupled decay (both scaled by lr) leave the weights bit-identical. Already written to $PROCESSED/adapt_null.pt and CONFIRMED null: encoder_drift reads 0.0000 on the stem and all twelve blocks, which validates the drift instrument against a known zero at the same time.

WHY THIS IS AN INSTRUMENT AND PRICED AS ONE. It cannot raise the score. It decides whether four collapsed arms are evidence about SSL or evidence about our harness, which is the difference between the only remaining axis with a >1.5 percent mechanism being CLOSED or REOPENED. Every knob family (decode, pooling, seats, resolution, capacity, span, calibration) is measured flat, so there is nothing else of that size to spend the card on.
notes:
PRICE: ~25 minutes of card (4 epochs at ~370 s), plus the null checkpoint and its drift read, both already spent and both clean.

P(clears 1.5%) = 0, STATED DELIBERATELY. This arm cannot move the score and is not offered as an improvement. It is an INSTRUMENT, and the base rule licenses one only when it retires a suspicion or re-opens a whole axis. It does both. Four arms and one interpretation currently attribute -0.14 to -0.17 to on-domain SSL; if the null collapses, that attribution is void and the only remaining axis with a >1.5% mechanism reopens with a named bug in front of it. If the null tracks the control, the attribution is confirmed and the axis closes on measurement rather than on suspicion, which frees the card from an axis that would otherwise keep drawing arms.

EXPECTED VALUE is therefore not this arm's own delta but the delta of what it gates: the SSL axis is the last unclosed lever priced above 1.5% (knee-c5n), and every knob family - decode, pooling, slot/seat count, resolution, capacity, span, calibration - is measured flat inside 0.0062. 25 minutes to decide the disposition of the largest remaining lever is the best ratio on the board.
ANSWERED 2026-08-22. adapt_null 0.8240 at epoch 3 against band_dense's 0.8232 at the same epoch: +0.0008, an eighth of the floor, against the ~0.19 separation the arm was written to detect. Training loss 1.2042 -> 0.8631 is the control's own trajectory, where all three collapsed encoder arms floored near the control's epoch-ZERO loss.

VERDICT: the load path is CLEAN. --encoder-weights and the preprocessing on either side of it cost nothing. Plumbing is removed as a suspect for the whole SSL family and the four collapses stand as evidence about the adaptation.

SECOND RESULT, and it keeps its value regardless: encoder_drift reads the null at 0.0000 on the stem and all twelve blocks. That is the drift instrument's first negative control, and every gate on this axis had been steered by that reading without one.

AGAINST MYSELF. The magnitude anomaly that bought the slot -- two adaptations differing FOURFOLD in blocks 0-5 drift and scoring 0.0027 apart -- is already in experiments/README.md at encoder_adapt_gentle, and there it is RESOLVED rather than merely noticed: blocks 0-5 are the wrong blocks, block 11 moved 0.5510 and 0.2144 against supervision's 0.0080 ceiling, and encoder_adapt_lower then refutes even that and lands on the frozen-bottom reading the family carries. I read lines 1320-1370 and 1455-1500 when arming and not 1401-1440. CLAUDE.md says read the ledger before filing a finding; the cost of not finishing that read is ~25 min of card, twice now.

STILL OPEN on knee-c5n, untouched by a null control: the MAE ran 6 epochs with both loss terms still falling steeply, and it was fitted on the DEFAULT 12-slice 0.20-0.80 cache while every consumer trains on 20 slices at 0.10-0.90.

title: Is the score DATA-limited? The one quantity 107 arms never varied
description:
Every measured axis is saturated: slice aggregation closed from three directions, ensemble seats capped at ~1 board tick, unfreeze depth flat past six blocks, all four CoPAS components priced out, volume-pretrained trunk ties frozen, knee-jk3's nine axes all inside 0.0062. That pattern is the finding. The one quantity never varied is how much data there is.

Every arm shows the same shape underneath: peak at epoch 5-9, then decline while train loss keeps falling. aug_long is the sharpest evidence it is not the ordinary kind -- the intensity regulariser demonstrably fired (train loss higher at every epoch past 4) and the decline did not move, -0.0169 against the control's -0.0182.

MEASUREMENT: experiments/arms/half_data.sh. band_dense's recipe on HALF the training studies, holdout untouched, read straight against the ledger's 0.8578. Costs ONE run (~36 min) because the 100% point already exists. New --train-fraction flag cuts the training side only, drawn at random and seeded by --split-seed.

READ IT ON: within the 0.0062 floor = data is not the lever, which LICENSES the expensive representation work (fine-tuned V-JEPA, larger encoder) currently unjustifiable. Below by 0.02+ = still on the steep part, data is binding, and knee-ombx's licence question gates the schedule. Above the control = a harness statement about label noise, not a result.

It is an INSTRUMENT and justified as one: it decides which family every remaining hour goes to. Both branches actionable.
notes:
PRICE: ~36 min of card (band_dense is 361 s an epoch on 4,407 studies; half the studies is ~180 s, 12 epochs). The 100% control costs nothing -- it is the ledger's band_dense 0.8578 row, same recipe, same holdout.

P(clears 1.5%) = 0, DECLARED, because this arm cannot raise the score at all. It is an INSTRUMENT and must be justified as one rather than sold as an improvement. What it buys is the DECISION about where the remaining hours go, at a moment when every other axis this project has measured is saturated and the alternative is picking the next arm by momentum.

Its instrument value: P(the reading is actionable) ~ 1, because both branches are. Flat licenses the expensive representation work (fine-tuned volume-pretrained trunk, larger encoder) that is currently unjustifiable on its own evidence -- that is hours of card released, not spent. Steep promotes knee-ombx's licence question from backlog to schedule-gating. A third outcome, above the control, would be a label-noise finding, which is a defect report rather than a result.

Against the alternative use of the same 36 min: another recipe knob on an axis already measured flat, whose own pre-registration would predict a null. This is the better ratio on the project's own rule -- a ~0-expected-score run is worth it ONLY as an instrument that retires a suspicion or licenses a whole axis, and this one does the second.
2026-08-22 00:52 UTC — TWO THINGS REGISTERED BEFORE THE NUMBER EXISTS.

(1) A CONFOUND I DID NOT NAME WHEN I PRICED THIS, and it is in the harness rather than the idea.
Half the training studies is also HALF THE OPTIMIZER STEPS PER EPOCH, and --one-cycle is defined over
total_steps — so this arm compresses the schedule as well as shrinking the corpus. recipe.sh records
the size of that effect from schedule_8: compressing the schedule cost 0.0028. The bias is DOWNWARD,
which means:
  * a WITHIN-FLOOR reading is STRENGTHENED by it — the arm was handicapped and still tied, so 'data is
    not the lever' survives a priori the objection.
  * a BELOW reading of order 0.005-0.010 is UNINTERPRETABLE as stated, because roughly 0.003 of it is
    schedule rather than data. Only a drop of order 0.02+ — the size the pre-registration already
    demanded before it would call data the binding constraint — is large enough that the schedule term
    cannot explain it.
The de-confound, if the middle case happens: rerun at --epochs 24, which matches total steps at half
the data, and costs ~72 min. NOT run pre-emptively, because two of the three branches do not need it.

(2) A SECOND READING THIS RUN GIVES FOR FREE, and it bears on the one signature nobody has explained.
Every arm in the ledger peaks at epoch 5-9 and then declines while the training loss keeps falling, and
aug_long showed an input-space regulariser that demonstrably FIRED does not touch that decline. The
control's own curve (band_dense.full.log) peaks 0.8578 at epoch 8 and finishes 0.8554.
  * If the decline is MEMORISATION of a finite corpus, half the corpus should be memorised SOONER: the
    peak epoch moves EARLIER and the peak-to-finish decline gets LARGER.
  * If the peak epoch and the decline size are UNCHANGED at half the data, the decline is not about how
    much data there is at all — which, with aug_long, would rule out the two ordinary explanations at
    once and make the signature a property of the optimisation or the objective.
Registered now because it costs nothing to read afterwards and proves nothing if written afterwards.
Note the schedule confound above applies here too: a compressed one-cycle moves the peak epoch by
itself, so the peak-epoch reading is the WEAKER of the two and the DECLINE SIZE is the one to trust.
ANSWERED 2026-08-22. half_data best 0.8344 @ epoch 6 vs band_dense 0.8578 @ epoch 8 = -0.0234, 3.8x the 0.0062 floor. The BELOW-BY-0.02+ branch landed: DATA IS BINDING. Registered schedule confound charged at its maximum (schedule_length prices step compression at 0.0028; scaled per doubling of steps, 0.0028-0.0048) leaves ~0.019 attributable to data -- 3x the floor, above the 1.5% bar.

Second reading, memorisation: peak moved 8 -> 6, the predicted direction. Decline sizes -0.0024 (control) vs -0.0006 (arm) are both sub-floor and UNREADABLE, reported as such rather than as a refutation. What the half-data curve does after its peak is not decline but PLATEAU: six epochs inside 0.0021 while train loss keeps falling 0.8015 -> 0.5973. Fitting continued, generalisation stopped -- the shape of an exhausted corpus.

SLOPE: 1,763 -> 3,526 training studies buys ~0.020. Bar needs ~1.7x the corpus. One point is not a curve; a 25% point (~18 min) prices the knee and is now worth running, filed separately.

CONSEQUENCE: knee-ombx's licence question promotes from backlog to the decision that gates the schedule, exactly as pre-registered. Ledger section + summary row written to experiments/README.md.

title: The mounted kit is 5 commits behind, so any member fitted with newer code cannot ship un-confounded
description:
dimiturnt/kneemri-kit is pinned at e3c884e; HEAD is 9 commits ahead in the 30 files the kernel loads (kit_check --mounted, 2026-08-21). One of the nine, ba76fd1 through_plane, IMPLEMENTS THE READ through_dense_s2026 was fitted with, so mounting that member on the current kit is a hard failure on the card, not a degraded score.

The trap is the fix: refreshing the kit changes model.py (198 lines), kernel_run, live_dataset and study_cache under EVERY member of an entry at once. The champion 0.931 (basedense_v1) and both six-member entries were produced at e3c884e, so the first entry shipped on a fresh kit has two variables and its reading cannot be attributed.

RESOLUTION, in order:
1. Refresh the kit.
2. Re-ship a kernel with a KNOWN score and no other change - sixfresh (0.931) is the natural one - and confirm the fresh kit reproduces it. That one slot buys the right to attribute every later reading.
3. Only then spend slots on members that need the new code (through_dense_s2026, and every V-JEPA member knee-jucq produces).

Until step 2 passes, new entries must be built from members the OLD kit can already construct. kneemri-sevengrade was chosen under exactly this constraint: grade_ladder_s2026 needs none of the nine commits, so it ships against the same kit that produced the 0.931.
notes:
2026-08-21 23:28 UTC - steps 1 and 2 in flight. Kit rebuilt at cf6a99f (11 commits on from e3c884e) and pushed as a new dataset version; kneemri-sixfresh re-pushed UNCHANGED as v2 so the only variable between its 0.931 and this reading is the kit. Its code, its members and its vote are byte-identical.

READ IT AS: 0.931 reproduced = the refresh is transparent, and through_dense_s2026 plus every V-JEPA member knee-jucq produces become shippable. Anything else = the refresh moved serving, and the delta is measured on a known entry rather than discovered under a new member, which is the whole reason this slot was spent.
2026-08-21 23:33 UTC: step 2 SHIPPED. sixfresh v2 (kernel v2, refreshed kit cf6a99f, byte-identical code+members to the 0.931) submitted as slot 4. PENDING; code submissions take hours, so the reading lands 2026-08-22. Step 3 (seating through_dense_s2026 and any V-JEPA member) stays blocked until it reads back. Slot 5 deliberately unspent: the through_dense entry is uninterpretable before step 2 reads, and no other question was ready.
2026-08-22 00:48 UTC — BOTH PENDING ENTRIES RESOLVED, both on their middle branch.

sixfresh v2 (55678708) = 0.931. The kit refresh (cf6a99f, was e3c884e) is TRANSPARENT to serving,
measured on an entry whose score was already known. through_dense_s2026 and every V-JEPA member are
now shippable, and a future bad reading on a fresh-kit entry is attributable to the candidate.

sevengrade (55678597) = 0.931. Seven seats tie six. The seventh was not a weak pick — grade_ladder
carries the only axis no seated member varies (the objective) — so the seat count is now saturated
from a third direction: five 0.925, six 0.931/0.930, seven 0.931. Future members must DISPLACE.

The distance ruler's registered prediction (the least distant candidate should NOT exceed 0.931)
survived. Not a validation: a tie was available to two other explanations, and only a BEAT would have
refuted it. One out-of-sample call, not wrong. Still a tie-breaker only.

kneemri-sevenplane WITHDRAWN as an addition. It is a seventh seat and a seventh seat is worth 0.000
regardless of which member fills it; shipping it would re-measure the axis sevengrade just closed.
Held as a DISPLACEMENT question instead — through_dense keeps the mechanism argument no other
candidate has (only member whose input tensor differs), so the slot-worthy question is whether it
displaces a seated member at six.

BLOCKED UNTIL ~15:45 UTC 2026-08-22, on a constraint that is not about the kit itself.

kneemri-gradeswap was submitted 08:07 UTC and projects 7.7 h over the hidden set. Pushing a new
kneemri-kit version while that rerun is in flight is only safe if Kaggle pins the dataset version
captured when the kernel ran, rather than resolving the latest at rerun time. I do not know which, and
the cost of being wrong is asymmetric: the wrong answer swaps the code underneath a scoring submission,
which loses the slot AND corrupts the three-ruler arbitration that slot was spent on (knee-7d1). A P1
housekeeping task is not worth learning that on a live entry.

So the ordering is forced: gradeswap scores first, kit refreshes after. Anyone picking this up before
15:45 should stop.

WORTH RESOLVING PROPERLY rather than waiting each time. The question is answerable off the critical path
- push a trivial kit version while nothing is scoring, then read whether an already-submitted kernel's
rerun log names the old or the new version. Doing that once turns a recurring blocker into a known fact.
Until then the conservative ordering stands.

Count is now 5 behind, not the 9 in the title: f485791 (core/data rename), 5aa01f6 (paths config),
15eaae8 (fingerprint), 3300d38 (whole_stack), a7a4a9f (budget). The last three were already deliberate;
the first two arrived with the data extraction. Note that a refresh now carries the core/data rename,
so the rebuilt kit must pass kit_check --mounted, mount_check AND witness_check before anything ships on
it - the rename touches import paths every kernel reaches through kernel_run.
NOT ON THE CRITICAL PATH for 2026-08-23. Checked what the pending members actually need: the vjepa/tubelet member (knee-rpkw) loads on the mounted kit cf6a99f unchanged -- both vjepa2l in backbone.py and VolumeRead in volume_read.py are present at that commit. The eighth-seat entry and the vote entry (knee-769f) also need nothing newer; Serving.vote landed in 42d2ae1, which IS an ancestor of cf6a99f.

Keeping the kit at cf6a99f is therefore the ACTIVE choice today, not neglect: every entry fired on it varies one thing against the 0.933, and refreshing would add the kit as a second variable to all of them. Refresh when a member needs code the kit lacks, and pair it with a reproduce-the-champion entry the way sixfresh v2 did.

title: The VRAM cap ignores the depth-axis stride: a tubelet trunk's per-slice cost is (size/stride)^2/tubelet, so the cap OVERSTATES it 2x
description:
Encoder.activation_units(size) sums Stage.units(size) = blocks * (size/stride)^2 * width, which assumes one token grid per SLICE. That is true for every 2D trunk this repo has fitted and false for a tubelet transformer: V-JEPA 2 (facebook/vjepa2-vitl-fpc64-256, hidden 1024, 24 layers, patch 16, tubelet 2, crop 256) tokenises TWO slices per token, so the same window costs (size/16)^2 / 2 per slice.

THE DIRECTION. The first reading of this bead said a tubelet trunk carries 6x MORE than the cap computes and would OOM mid-arm. That is wrong, and the arithmetic that makes it wrong is one line: DeviceBudget.needed multiplies by (slices + 1), so `units` is a PER-SLICE quantity. A tubelet trunk emits grid^2 * slices/tubelet for the whole window = grid^2/tubelet per slice — LESS, not more. The cap therefore OVERSTATES a tubelet trunk by exactly the tubelet factor.

So the failure mode is knee-bj90's, not an OOM: the run parks in await_headroom waiting on memory it would never have allocated, and never starts. Loud rather than expensive — but it is what makes the whole tubelet axis look unreachable on this card when it is not.
notes:
2026-08-22: UNBLOCKED FROM DEFERRAL by knee-jucq. The frozen probe paid no backward pass and no optimiser state, which is why this was safe to defer. The next arm fine-tunes a tubelet trunk and pays both, so activation_units undercounting by frames-per-tubelet (6x at a 12-slice window, tubelet 2) will size the VRAM cap on a number 6x too small. Fix BEFORE the arm, not after the OOM.
2026-08-22 00:54 UTC — THE DIRECTION IN THIS BUG'S OWN DESCRIPTION IS BACKWARDS, verified card-free.

The description says a tubelet trunk 'carries 6x the activations the cap would compute' and would
therefore ADMIT a run that OOMs. That reasoning assumes the cap computes one token grid per STEP. It
does not: DeviceBudget holds `slices` as its own field and needed() is
    GB_PER_SLICE * (slices + 1) * (units / FITTED_UNITS) * (batch/FITTED_BATCH) * (trainable/FITTED_TRAINABLE) + optimiser
so `units` is a PER-SLICE quantity and the slice loop multiplies it. A 2D trunk emits grid^2 tokens per
slice; a tubelet-2 trunk emits grid^2 * slices/2 for the whole window, i.e. grid^2/2 PER SLICE. The cap
therefore OVERSTATES a tubelet trunk by the tubelet factor — it does not understate it.

That is knee-bj90's failure mode, not an OOM: the run parks in await_headroom on memory it will never
allocate, burns the wait bound and never starts. Still blocking, still P1, but a fix built from the
description as written would have added capacity to a cap that is already too large.

THE NUMBERS, at vjepa2l as the registry already states it (depth 24, patch 16, dim 1024, 326M params,
size 256), against a 31.8 GB card:

  slices  batch | cap as written | tubelet-corrected
      6      12 |      27.2 GB   |     16.2 GB
     12      12 |      46.2 GB   |     25.7 GB
     20      12 |      71.5 GB   |     38.3 GB
     20       4 |      27.2 GB   |     16.2 GB

AND THE PLANNING FACT THAT FALLS OUT, which is worth more than the fix. Even CORRECTED, the settled
recipe (20 slices, batch 12) derives 38.3 GB and does not fit this card. A fine-tuning arm on this
trunk is only runnable at a reduced batch (20 slices at batch 4 = 16.2 GB) or a shorter window (12
slices at batch 12 = 25.7 GB), and either is a second variable against every 20-slice/batch-12 row in
the ledger. That has to be designed for, not discovered on the card.

FIX SHAPE, revised: Encoder gains `tubelet: int = 1` and activation_units divides by it. One field, one
divide, and the 2D default is unchanged for every trunk on disk.

NOT IMPLEMENTED YET, deliberately. The bead's own gate was 'decide when the probe says the trunk is
worth fine-tuning at all', and the probe TIED rather than beat (see
interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-22_vjepa_frozen_probe.md). Writing the fix now would be building for an
arm that is not yet justified. The analysis above is the part that had to exist before that decision,
because it changes what the arm would cost and what it could be compared against.
FIXED 2026-08-22. Stage gains an explicit `tubelet` divisor and Encoder carries one for the shorthand path (a tubelet transformer states no `stages`, so depth-axis stride had no way to reach the derivation). VJEPA2_LARGE declares tubelet=2 (fpc64 tokenises two frames per token).

THE FIX FLIPS THE PLANNING VERDICT, which the audit did not expect. vjepa2l at its NATIVE 256 px, 20 slices, batch 6, 6 blocks open:
  uncorrected  38.3 GB  -> refused, parks in await_headroom on a 31.8 GB card
  corrected    21.7 GB  -> fits under a 26 GB cap with room
The 38.3 GB in this bead's own audit note is exactly the uncorrected 256 px figure. So the earlier reading -- 'even corrected it does not fit' -- was measuring the 336 px read, which vjepa2l has no reason to take: it is pretrained at 256. The encoder was never too big for the card; the cap was double-counting the depth axis.

This unblocks knee-rpkw (the tubelet trunk, the only architecture-scale axis this project has built and never measured) and makes the vjepa2 frozen-embedding probe reachable without a recipe compromise. Test: tests/unit/kneemri/models/backbone.py::test_units asserts the halving directly, test_activation_units asserts the shorthand path carries it.

title: queue_check verifies the watcher but not the sentinel WRITER: a killed wrapper reads as OK
description:
FOUND 2026-08-21, live, on band_dense_llrd.

WHAT HAPPENED. The background shell running experiments/arms/band_dense_llrd.sh was killed at epoch 9.
The TRAINER survived as an orphan and kept training normally -- log advanced 1470 -> 1567 steps in 20 s,
python pid 46876 alive at 65.9 GB working set -- so no epoch was ever at risk. What died was the bash
wrapper, and run_arm (experiments/lib.sh:415-437) does three things in that wrapper AFTER the trainer
returns:

  release_card       -> the GPU lock would stay held by dead pid 120448 forever
  ARM DONE <name>    -> the sentinel the next chain's watcher greps for
  _seat_value        -> the second ruler the ledger quotes

All three were gone. The trainer would have finished, written its checkpoint, and the queue would have
sat with a locked card and a watcher waiting on a line nobody was left to write.

THE GATE MISSED IT, AND THIS IS THE ACTUAL BUG. queue_check was run in exactly this state and returned:

  after_band_dense_llrd.log  waits on 'ARM DONE band_dense_llrd'  0/1 started  live
  OK: every arm still owed is gated by exactly one live process

Both halves of what it checks were TRUE. Exactly one watcher was live, and it was not double-owed. The
check's model of the queue is 'is someone waiting, and is exactly one someone waiting' -- it has no
notion of whether anything is still alive to SATISFY that wait. A watcher waiting on a sentinel whose
only writer is dead is indistinguishable, to this check, from a watcher waiting on a healthy arm.

That is the same SHAPE as the hole queue_check was built for and the opposite END of it. Its docstring
records two holes: a dead watcher owing an arm (queue looks armed, nothing will run) and two live
watchers owing one arm (it runs twice on one card). This is a THIRD: a live, correctly-single watcher
owing an arm no surviving process can complete.

THE FIX, and it is small because the signal already exists. For each owed arm the check already knows
the log it greps. Add: is a process still alive that will write that sentinel? The honest test is not
'is the trainer alive' -- an orphaned trainer is alive and still cannot write it -- but 'is the WRAPPER
alive', i.e. is there a live shell whose recorded pid matches the arm's. The gpu.lock already stores
that pid (120448 here), which is why the recovery could be written at all. So: if a watcher owes an arm
whose log is still growing but whose lock pid is dead, report it. Growing log + dead holder is precisely
the orphan state and it has no other cause.

INTERIM: experiments/orphan_recovery.sh hand-finishes an arm in this state. It waits for the trainer's
own 'best holdout' artefact (replicating run_arm's refusal to advance the queue on an arm that exited
without one), THEN releases the lock only if the recorded holder is still the dead pid, THEN writes the
sentinel. That ordering is not incidental -- releasing earlier hands the card to the next chain while
the orphan is still on it, which is the two-arms-on-one-card overflow drop_own_card exists to prevent.

NOT FIXED IN queue_check YET. The recovery is the instance; this bead is the class.
notes:
WITHDRAWN 2026-08-21, same hour it was filed. THE PREMISE WAS MY MEASUREMENT ERROR, not a defect.

Nothing was orphaned. The arm's wrapper (experiments/arms/band_dense_llrd.sh) was alive throughout, so
release_card, the ARM DONE sentinel and _seat_value were all going to run normally. What was killed was
only the harness's own tracking shell -- the 'timeout 12000 bash ...' task wrapper -- which owns none of
those three. The card lock was correctly held by a LIVE shell the whole time.

under git-bash is an MSYS pid. I checked whether that pid was alive with PowerShell Get-Process, which
enumerates WINDOWS pids. The two namespaces are unrelated and numerically disjoint, so the lookup
returned empty and I read empty as dead. It is not a stale-lock detector at all; it is a category error

title: Registered orthogonal reformats: our six slots are unregistered acquisitions, so attention has never had two views it could align
description:
Child of knee-pq8u, component (A) - the headline mechanism, and the one that most directly attacks the
axis the aggregation chapter closed as saturated.

MECHANISM. CoPAS rotates each PDW volume into its two orthogonal planes, producing 6 SYNTHETIC volumes
alongside the 5 real ones, then runs cross-plane attention with Q from the native volume and K/V from its
own rotations: F = sum_n softmax(Q K_n^T / sqrt(d_Kn)) V_n. The synthetic views are the SAME TISSUE,
pixel-aligned by construction.

THAT REGISTRATION IS THE WHOLE POINT AND IT IS WHAT WE LACK. Our six slots are different acquisitions -
a sagittal slot and an axial slot are separate scans of the same knee with no voxel correspondence, no
shared grid, and no guarantee of coverage overlap. Every attention and pooling arm we have run over the
slot axis has therefore been fusing UNALIGNED views, which is a plausible reason the slot-aggregation
axis kept landing inside the noise floor while looking like it should not: attention across two views
that do not correspond has nothing to attend TO. A reformat gives attention, for the first time, two
views where position means the same thing in both.

It is also the only through-plane operation we have that is FREE OF EXTERNAL DATA and free of a licence
question - it manufactures new views from volumes we already hold.

RELATION TO knee-40wh (through_dense), which is queued and must be read first. through_dense puts (i-1,
i, i+1) into the encoder's three channels. That is through-plane information INSIDE one slice's feature
vector, at pixel level, over a three-slice window. This bead is through-plane information as a WHOLE
RESLICED VOLUME the encoder reads end-on. They are the small and the large version of the same claim, so
through_dense is a genuine cheap gate on this: if a three-slice window at pixel level moves nothing, a
full reformat still might (different scale), but if through_dense lands BELOW its control that is
evidence the 2D ImageNet stem cannot be asked to read depth at all - which pushes this bead toward
needing (B), the volume-pretrained trunk, first.

BUILD NOTE, from the audit: the reformat need not touch the cache. A slot arrives as (group, p, q);
transposing to (p, group, q) and interpolating the group axis up to the in-plane size produces the
orthogonal stack ON THE FLY, inside the model, with no cache rewrite and no new preprocessing pass. The
honest caveat is that our cached slices are already resized to a common matrix, so the reformat is
geometrically CRUDE - slice thickness and in-plane spacing are not reconciled, and the synthetic view is
anisotropic in a way a real acquisition is not. CoPAS reformatted from properly spaced volumes. Whether
a crude reformat carries the mechanism is itself the first thing to test, and it is cheap to test.

PRICE. ~4h dev (reformat + a cross-plane attention block + the wiring the three plumbing ratchets
demand), then one ~45 min arm. Plausible gain: this is the largest single component of a stack measured
at +0.031 over an MRNet-shaped baseline, so 1-2% is a defensible expectation and it is the only lever
currently on the board priced near the bar by someone else's measurement. Odds of clearing 1.5%, ~1 in 3.
Roughly 5h for a one-in-three shot at a bar-clearing result, against a board where every other axis is
priced at <=0.006 with high confidence. Best ratio available that needs no owner decision.

GATE: do not start the build until through_dense has been read, and fetch the CoPAS supplementary
ablation table first - one web fetch that could tell us what fraction of the +0.031 this component owns,
and would either double or halve this bead's price.
notes:
PRICE CUT 2026-08-21 by knee-f6u4's measurement. The in-plane half of this bead's premise is refuted: slot tissue centroids disagree by only 5.7 mm p50 / 10.7 mm p90 within a study, which is under one encoder feature cell (12.4 mm at 336 px over a 130 mm box, stride 32), and our aggregator pools H and W away before slots meet at all. So 'our six slots are unregistered acquisitions' is true in-plane but the residual is too small to be the thing suppressing the aggregation axis.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT WAS ALWAYS THE POINT: through-plane. Nothing has measured whether two acquisitions sample the same anatomy at the same slice positions and orientations - that is a different statistic (slice-position overlap and normal-vector agreement from the DICOM geometry, not a centroid), and it is what a reformat would actually fix. Rewrite the bead's mechanism around that before pricing it again.

GATE UNCHANGED: do not start until through_dense (knee-40wh) is read.
MEASURED 2026-08-21, second half. slot_geometry (header-only, 400 studies / 1848 slots / 3465 within-study pairs, logs/slot_geometry.log):
- normal angle between slots p50 87.3 deg, p90 90.0; 2711/3465 (78.2%) within 20 deg of orthogonal. The planes ARE the orthogonal set a reformat assumes.
- centre distance p50 42.6 mm, decomposed into a through-plane leg 27.3 mm and an in-plane leg 21.2 mm.
- the IN-PLANE leg is not new: crop_alignment already measured 5.7 mm p50 of between-slot disagreement in tissue centring, and two slots each ~10 mm off their own matrix centre in roughly opposite directions produces ~21 mm of centre separation with the tissue landing at the same patient point.
- the THROUGH-PLANE leg is the new quantity, and 27.3 mm is meaningless without the stack span it sits inside. SlotFrame.covers() supplies it: in 6219/6930 ordered pairs (89.7%) the first slot's stack CONTAINS the second slot's centre.

READING. Both halves of the premise now read the same way: the slots are already orthogonal views of one volume, displaced by less than the volume they each span. A reformat would carry a shift the data does not need. The 10.3% tail where coverage fails is a per-study minority, not a corpus-wide defect, and is the only thing left on this axis worth re-testing.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT. Coverage is a centre-in-stack test on the MIDDLE slice's geometric centre, not a joint landmark, so a series that ran long in one direction moves its centre without moving the knee. It also says nothing about SAMPLING: two slots can cover the same volume at 3 mm and 0.4 mm through-plane resolution, and that difference survives everything measured here. If the through-plane axis is revisited, revisit it as a RESOLUTION question, not a registration one.

title: Label-correlation head: twelve independent sigmoids have never been told that ACL tear and effusion co-occur
description:
Child of knee-pq8u, component (C), and deliberately the FIRST of the four because it is the only one
that is head-only. (A) and (B) are trunk surgery and cost a full arm each; this one can be warm-started.

MECHANISM. Our twelve outputs are independent sigmoids over one pooled study feature. In 107 runs
nothing has ever modelled the joint structure of the label set, and that structure is large and clinical,
not statistical noise: an ACL tear drags effusion and bone contusion with it, the three OA subscores move
together, a Baker's cyst rides with effusion. CoPAS gets at this by forming the outer product of its
three plane-branch predictions, x_ijk = sag_i * cor_j * ax_k, and mining the resulting 12x12x12 tensor
with a 12-channel convolution, taking the diagonal as the base prediction.

WE CANNOT COPY THAT LITERALLY and should not pretend to. CoPAS has three PLANE BRANCHES; we have six
SLOTS whose identity varies per study, so there is no fixed triple to take an outer product over. The
separable part of the mechanism is the label-correlation refinement, not the plane triple. So: keep the
existing twelve logits, then refine them with a learned interaction over the label axis - a 12x12
label-attention block or a small MLP on the logit vector - so each label's final score can read the
others. This is 'build upon', not replication, and the bead says so on purpose.

WHY IT IS THE CHEAPEST INSTRUMENT ON THE BOARD. The trunk does not move. Fit the refinement on features
cached from an existing checkpoint (band_dense or grade_ladder), which is minutes of card rather than a
40-minute arm, and the control is the same checkpoint's raw logits - a perfectly matched A/B with no
retrain, no new seed, and no confound. If the refinement cannot beat its own frozen logits on holdout,
the mechanism is dead for near-free and (A)/(B) are unaffected.

PRICE. ~1h dev, under 10 min of card. Plausible gain 0.005-0.015 - label-correlation refinement in
multi-label medical imaging is usually a small-to-borderline effect, so honestly this is priced AT OR
UNDER the 1.5% bar, not above it. It is justified by the RATIO, not the size: near-zero cost, a matched
control for free, and it is a prerequisite reading for whether CoPAS's +0.031 lives in the plane
machinery or in the label machinery. If the label half is worth ~0, that RAISES the expected value of
(A), which is the expensive one - which is exactly what an instrument is for.

RISK, named up front: refining logits against the training set's own label co-occurrence is a way to
overfit the label prior rather than learn anything about the image. Read it on holdout only, and check
the per-label breakdown - a gain that lives entirely in the RARE labels (fracture, synovitis) is the
prior leaking, not correlation being used.
notes:
REFUTED 2026-08-22 for zero card. The gate was built instead of the head: kneemri/evaluation/residual_coupling.py (LabelCoupling — does structure survive in the residual) + kneemri/evaluation/label_probe.py (HeldOutProbe — is it usable out of sample). Ledger section: experiments/README.md, '### residual_coupling / label_probe'.

MEASURED. Residual coupling is real: Medial OA/Lateral OA 0.3068 (563 studies), Contusion/Fracture 0.2742 (358), over DECIDED pairs only (7712 of 10908). The held-out probe — the proposed head with its nonlinearity removed, fit on half the holdout, scored on the other half against the label's own raw logit on the SAME rows — LOSES AUC in all 15 measured cells: 3 members (band_dense, base_dense, calib_span) x 5 ridge penalties spanning 10^5. Best cell -0.0125, worst -0.0291.

HARNESS SUSPECTED FIRST AND CLEARED. HeldOutProbe.alone restricts the same machinery to the label's own logit; a ridge on one monotone feature is monotone, so it must reproduce raw AUC. null_control_max_abs = 0.0 on all three members. The loss is mechanism, not arithmetic.

MECHANISM NAMED. The twelve heads share ONE pooled study feature, so every correlation the IMAGE predicts is already available to all twelve. What survives in the residual is SHARED STUDY-LEVEL ERROR — when a study is hard, all twelve logits are wrong in the same direction, so label A's logit points the same wrong way as B's and cannot correct it. Correlated errors are not recoverable errors.

THE PRE-REGISTERED LEAK FIRED EXACTLY AS THIS BEAD WROTE IT. The only two labels that improved are the rarest (Synovitis, 65 scored studies of 909) — 'a gain that lives entirely in the RARE labels is the prior leaking, not correlation being used'.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT. It kills the LINEAR label-interaction refinement of FROZEN logits on our twelve-head, one-pooled-feature architecture. It does NOT kill label structure as a SUPERVISION signal — a joint loss shapes the shared feature during fitting, which is a different intervention and is left re-testable. It does not touch (A) or (B).

title: CoPAS: its +0.031 is bought by preprocessing we already have — two big components refuted on transfer, the volume-pretrained trunk survives
description:
SOTA GATHER (2026-08-21, card-free). Qiu et al., "Learning co-plane attention across MRI sequences for
diagnosing twelve types of knee abnormalities", Nature Communications 15:7637 (2024). HKUST + Third
Affiliated Hospital, Southern Medical University. Code: https://github.com/zqiuak/CoPAS, APACHE 2.0 -
fully permissive, no owner decision, nothing to negotiate. Data: restricted, email + MTA, non-commercial
academic only, so it FAILS rule 2.6a and is NOT a data source. We take the METHOD, not the corpus.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS AND THE other papers did not. It is multi-sequence knee MRI, TWELVE abnormality
labels, multi-label, exactly our task shape - not ACL-only like MRNet/ELNet/Rijeka. And it reports the
number that prices a build: on their own internal test set, CoPAS 0.812 vs MRNet 0.781, MPFuseNet 0.754,
ELNet 0.760. That is +0.031 for the CoPAS stack over an MRNet-style per-plane-CNN-then-pool baseline,
measured on one dataset with one split - and OUR architecture is an MRNet-style per-plane-CNN-then-pool.
+0.031 is 2x the project bar. It is the first lever on the board whose plausible size comes from someone
else's measurement instead of from my hope, and knee-jk3's nine axes all landed inside a 0.0062 floor.

DO NOT read 0.812 against our 0.858. Different corpus, different twelve labels (they have PCL, LCL,
plica, infrapatellar fat pad, patellar retinaculum; we have three OA subscores, fracture, Baker's). The
transferable quantity is the DELTA over the MRNet-shaped baseline, not the level.

THE STACK, DECOMPOSED - four mechanisms, none of which we have, each priced separately below. The +0.031
belongs to the whole stack; a partial replication buys a fraction, and the ablation table is in
supplementary materials I have not read yet (worth one fetch before committing to the expensive parts).

(A) REGISTERED SYNTHETIC ORTHOGONAL REFORMATS + CROSS-PLANE ATTENTION. They take each PDW volume and
    ROTATE it into the two orthogonal planes, making 6 synthetic volumes on top of 5 real ones, then run
    attention F = sum_n softmax(Q K_n^T / sqrt(d)) V_n with Q from the native volume and K/V from its own
    rotations. The point is REGISTRATION: the synthetic views are the same tissue, pixel-aligned by
    construction. Our six slots are DIFFERENT ACQUISITIONS, so nothing in our stack has ever given
    attention two views it could actually align. This is the deepest difference between their model and
    ours and it needs no external data.

(B) A TRUNK PRETRAINED ON VOLUMES. ResNet3D-18, i.e. video weights, not an ImageNet 2D stem. Every
    encoder in 107 runs was pretrained on natural still images. This is precisely the branch knee-40wh
    pre-registered for its BELOW-control outcome ("the pretrained colour-channel stem cannot be asked to
    mean depth, so a 3D trunk must be PRETRAINED on volumes"), so through_dense's result reads directly
    onto whether to spend here.

(C) PLANE-AWARE PROBABILITY MATRIX / LABEL-CORRELATION MINING. Three branch predictions combined by
    OUTER PRODUCT, x_ijk = sag_i * cor_j * ax_k, then a 12-channel convolution mines the correlation
    structure and the diagonal is the base prediction. Our twelve heads are independent and have always
    been. Nothing in 107 runs has modelled that ACL tear and effusion co-occur.

(D) FOCAL LOSS ON THE FINAL HEAD + BCE DEEP SUPERVISION ON EACH BRANCH. Adjacent to the severity-loss
    chapter the owner kept alive.

Two of their choices CONFIRM ours rather than challenging them, which is worth recording because it
means the replication is not a rewrite: their pooling collapses H and W only and keeps depth (C x D x H x
W -> D x C), which is exactly our per-slice slice_features; and they crop to an anatomical reference
found by a U-Net, which is what anatomical_prior does.

PLAN. Split into child beads, cheapest-instrument-first, because (C) is head-only and warm-startable
while (A) and (B) are trunk surgery. Do NOT start with (A) just because it is the headline.
notes:
Children filed: knee-w8h6 (C, label-correlation head, cheapest instrument, do first), knee-vigl (A, registered orthogonal reformats + cross-plane attention, the headline, gated on through_dense). (B) volume-pretrained trunk and (D) focal + deep supervision not yet filed - (B) is gated on through_dense's outcome, (D) overlaps the live severity-loss chapter.

ABLATION TABLE READ 2026-08-21 (supplementary PDF, Table 10, Center A, mean AUC-ROC over the 12 labels).
This is the number that prices every child, and it REORDERS them - the headline attention is not the
biggest component.

  (i)   MRNet baseline (12 separate nets, ROI-cropped)   0.781
  (ii)  Baseline WITHOUT the ROI crop                    0.725
  (iii) Baseline, multitask (one net for all 12)         0.705
  (iv)  + CPA  (cross-plane attention, built on (ii))    0.774
  (v)   + CPA + CSA (cross-sequence attention)           0.799
  (vi)  + CPA + CSA + CRM  = CoPAS                       0.812
  (vii) CoPAS as single-task, 12 duplicated models       0.808

DECOMPOSED, and each delta is now measured rather than guessed:
  ROI CROP        0.725 -> 0.781   +0.056   <-- LARGEST SINGLE COMPONENT IN THE PAPER
  CPA             0.725 -> 0.774   +0.049   (measured on the no-ROI basis, so it is an ALTERNATIVE
                                             route to the same alignment, not additive on top of ROI)
  CSA             0.774 -> 0.799   +0.025
  CRM             0.799 -> 0.812   +0.013
  multitask       0.808 -> 0.812   +0.004   (their own word: "marginal")

THE AUTHORS' OWN EXPLANATION OF WHY ROI WINS IS THE KEY SENTENCE, quoted: "cropping along ROI can align
the spatial position across sequences". So ROI and CPA are the SAME MECHANISM - spatial correspondence
between views - bought two ways, one by preprocessing and one by attention. That is why CPA is measured
against the no-ROI baseline and why the two cannot simply be added.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE CHILDREN:
- knee-w8h6 (label correlation, = CRM) is priced at +0.013 by their own ablation. That is UNDER the 1.5%
  bar, which is exactly what the bead guessed before this table was read. Keep it as the cheap
  instrument, correctly priced; do not sell it as a result.
- knee-vigl (cross-plane attention) is priced at +0.049 - above the bar - but the ROI reading says a
  large part of what it buys may be obtainable far more cheaply by fixing the crop.
- NEW CHILD, now the highest-ratio item on the board: anatomy-centred cropping. See below.

PREPROCESSING DETAILS WORTH HAVING (supplementary sec 2.1), several of which differ from ours: resample
to 0.28 x 0.28 x 3 mm and scale to 576x576 with slice count unchanged; zero-mean/unit-sd intensity
standardisation; crop 448x448 on the U-Net meniscus ROI then interpolate to 224x224 (we run 336);
augment by crop/translate +/-10 px, in-plane rotation +/-25 deg, contrast/brightness x1.5, class
resampling, 4x expansion to 3092 samples; Adam 1e-5, 500 epochs with early stopping, alpha 0.3.
NOTE their "isotropic" voxel is 0.28 x 0.28 x 3 mm, i.e. about 10x coarser through-plane - so even
CoPAS's synthetic orthogonal reformats are strongly anisotropic. That de-risks knee-vigl's stated worry
that OUR reformat would be too crude to carry the mechanism: theirs is crude too, and it bought +0.049.
POST-MORTEM ON THE PRICE 2026-08-21, after both large children closed on our own measurements the same day. The parent's headline (+0.031 over an MRNet-shaped baseline) must NOT be re-quoted as an available lever. Their ablation attributes it as ROI crop +0.056, cross-plane attention +0.049, label-correlation matrix +0.013 (components overlap; they are measured against different baselines and do not sum).

WHAT WE MEASURED, AND WHY THE TWO BIG ONES DO NOT TRANSFER.
- ROI crop (+0.056) - knee-f6u4, CLOSED. Their number is against a full-FOV 576-matrix baseline with NO crop. Ours is a 130 mm box already. crop_alignment (400 studies, 1848 slots) puts between-slot tissue-centroid disagreement at 5.7 mm p50 / 10.7 mm p90, under ONE encoder feature cell (12.4 mm), and the aggregator pools H and W away before slots meet. The residual is below the granularity anything downstream could act on. Separately knee-yrf priced tissue-centring at +0.029 RETAINED TISSUE, not worth a 99 GB cache rebuild.
- Cross-plane attention (+0.049) - knee-vigl, CLOSED. Its premise was that our slots are unregistered. slot_geometry (3465 within-study pairs) says otherwise: normals p50 87.3 deg apart with 78.2% within 20 deg of orthogonal, and in 89.7% of ordered pairs one slot's stack CONTAINS the other's centre. The slots are ALREADY the orthogonal set a reformat manufactures, displaced by less than the volume they each span. A reformat would carry a shift the data does not need.

THE HONEST READING, and it is a statement about our stack rather than about theirs: CoPAS's edge over MRNet is bought largely by preprocessing and view-alignment that our corpus already has. That is why the number does not transfer - not because the method is wrong, but because we are not the baseline it was measured against. This is the third time a frontier component has been priced high and then found already-present here; the lesson for the next external method is to measure OUR distance from THEIR baseline before pricing THEIR delta.

WHAT SURVIVES, in price order. knee-jucq (P2, volume-pretrained trunk) - the one component whose premise our measurements did NOT touch, since every encoder in 107 runs was pretrained on natural still images; gated on knee-40wh (through_dense). knee-w8h6 (P1) - priced +0.013 by their own table, i.e. UNDER our 1.5% bar, so it is an INSTRUMENT (does label correlation carry anything at all here) and must not be sold as a candidate. knee-afz6 (P3) - smallest component, half-owned by the live severity chapter.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT. Nothing here refutes CoPAS. Both closures are about transfer, and both are IN-PLANE/registration statistics. knee-vigl's own close names the axis left open: SAMPLING RESOLUTION, not registration - two slots can cover one volume at 3 mm and at 0.4 mm through-plane, and that difference survives every statistic taken today.
2026-08-22: knee-jucq CLOSED as a TIE, which retires the last surviving component of this parent. V-JEPA2-large frozen reads 0.7620 against a matched DINOv2-large control at 0.7669 (-0.0049 inside a 0.0062 floor). The tubelet path is verified to have fired (cache depth 1 per slot against the control's 12).

So all four CoPAS components are now priced on OUR data: ROI crop refuted on transfer (knee-f6u4), cross-plane attention refuted on transfer (knee-vigl), label-correlation priced +0.013 by their own table i.e. under our bar (knee-w8h6, instrument only), volume-pretrained trunk ties frozen (knee-jucq). The parent's +0.031 is fully accounted for and NONE of it is an available lever here.

That is a clean result for the parent's own closing lesson -- measure OUR distance from THEIR baseline before pricing THEIR delta -- and it is now backed by four independent measurements rather than one.

WHAT STAYS OPEN, and it is not a CoPAS component: knee-vigl's close named SAMPLING RESOLUTION (3 mm vs 0.4 mm through-plane) as the axis every registration statistic leaves untouched. And knee-jucq's own close names the bigger one: frozen probes read 0.76 while fitted members read 0.85+, so fine-tuning carries ~+0.09 and every trunk question is really a question about the fitted number.
REPRICED 2026-08-22 after component (C) was refuted for zero card (see knee-w8h6, and experiments/README.md '### residual_coupling / label_probe'). The label-correlation head loses AUC in all 15 measured cells with an exact null control, and the mechanism is named: shared study-level error is not recoverable error.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE STACK'S PRICE. The +0.031 belongs to the whole four-component stack.
