(C) was the cheap component and it is now measured at ~0 on our architecture, so the whole of any remaining gain has to come from (A) and (B) — the expensive ones. That RAISES (A)'s expected value rather than lowering it, which is exactly what an instrument is for: the same +0.031 ceiling now divided over fewer surviving components. It also removes the cheapest way to buy a fraction of the stack, so a partial replication is no longer cheap.

NEXT READ BEFORE COMMITTING CARD: the supplementary ablation table, still unfetched. If it attributes most of the +0.031 to (C), the stack's transferable delta for us drops sharply and (A) should be repriced down too.
2026-08-23: CLOSING. All four components are priced on our data and none is an available lever (ROI crop refuted on transfer, cross-plane attention refuted on transfer, label-correlation ~0 with an exact null control, volume-pretrained trunk a frozen tie AND a fitted loss — vjepa_warm 0.8337 against roster members 0.8525-0.8578). The two axes this bead's close named as still open are both now measured too: through-plane feature mixing died with depth_true (0.8461, seat -0.0002) and the fitted volume trunk is the vjepa_warm row. Nothing here refutes CoPAS; we are not the baseline it was measured against.

title: queue_check reads a marker, not a queue — it misses duplicate watchers and stale logs
description:
Found 2026-08-21 while rewiring the ladder ahead of band_dense_llrd. Two after.sh watchers were live on the SAME marker ('ARM DONE depth_true'), both owing experiments/arms/band_dense_llrd.sh — one of them carrying a malformed watch path ('/experiments/depth_true.full.log') that could never fire. queue_check reported 'OK: every arm still owed is gated by a live process' for both.

Two defects, one cause: liveness is decided by MARKER, not by (marker, arm list).

1. DUPLICATE WATCHERS ARE INVISIBLE. Two processes owing the same arm read as one healthy queue. Had the marker fired, band_dense_llrd would have launched twice on one card — 2.5 h of slot, and two arms of that geometry together drove the card to 31.5 GB of 32 (the measurement after.sh's own header cites). This is the expensive one.

2. A DEAD WATCHER'S LOG READS LIVE whenever any OTHER live watcher shares its marker. That is exactly backwards: the check exists because watchers die with the session that launched them, and a shared marker is the common case when a queue is rewired.

Fix: match a log to a process by the arm list it owes, not by the marker alone; report a count per (marker, arm) and flag any arm owed by more than one live process as BLOCKING. A stale log with no process of its own stays a warning, as today.
notes:
Fixed 2026-08-21, and the fix needed a second correction the first one caused.

WHAT CHANGED. Liveness is now (marker AND the exact arm tuple), read off the process line the same way the log header is read — by the .sh suffix, so an arm carrying its own argument loses it on both sides. A new doubled() counts, per arm still owed, how many live after.sh processes will start it; >1 is BLOCKING. faults() collects both, and main() now exits 2 on either (it exited 0 on a strand before — the same reads-as-a-pass trap the module docstring was already written against). UNREADABLE=1 stays distinct.

THE CORRECTION. A naive count of after.sh lines called the healthy queue DOUBLE-QUEUED: a watcher is started as 'nohup bash experiments/after.sh …' from a harness shell whose own -c string embeds that whole command, so ONE queue leaves TWO lines carrying the same argv. Now a line that is the PARENT of another watcher line is dropped — exactly the wrapper, while two genuinely separate watchers (neither one's parent) both survive. That needed pids from both probes, so the PowerShell probe now prints ProcessId/ParentProcessId ahead of the command line; parentage is read as the first two whole-number tokens, which is the one thing ps -ef and it agree on.

VERIFIED. 20 unit tests, including the two regressions by name: a superseded watcher's argv being a SUFFIX of the chain that replaced it, and the launching shell. Live run on the real table reads OK with one chain owing grade_ladder then band_dense_llrd.
close_reason: Fixed in 89fac2f and now exercised on a live queue: queue_check reads OK: every arm still owed is gated by exactly one live process against the real depth_true chain, with the launching-shell parentage case in the listing it parsed. Both holes are covered by named regression tests (test_alive_is_not_vouched_for_by_the_chain_that_replaced_it, test_watchers_drops_the_launching_shell, test_doubled) and main now exits 2 on a fault.

title: An arm cannot be queued against a bead with no wall-clock/gain price
description:
MY OWN FAILURE, 2026-08-21: I launched the 140 mm build without ever computing expected gain, then defended it with retention numbers that are not a gain argument. The rule (CLAUDE.md: price every experiment as wall-clock / expected gain BEFORE running, out loud) had fired that same morning on the LLRD candidate I was suspicious of, and did not fire on the build because the build was a CARRIED-OVER task and read as already-decided. Three causes: next-on-the-list momentum, sunk cost from the work spent making it safe, and two letters already publicly arguing for it.

A rule I have to remember is a rule that fails on exactly the runs momentum picks. Make it mechanical:

1. A price field on the bead, filled AT FILE TIME: hours of card/CPU, the gain the mechanism could plausibly deliver, P(clears 1.5 percent). knee-yuqf already carries one in its description as the format to copy.
2. arm_check REFUSES an arm whose bead has no price. arm_check already reads the arm shell and validates flags; the missing link is arm -> bead. Cheapest binding: a '# bead: knee-xxxx' line in the arm shell, which arm_check resolves via 'bd show' and rejects when absent or unpriced.

Not a documentation change. The documentation already says it.
design:
DESIGN, 2026-08-21, shaped to arm_check's existing grain (ArmCheck holds pure functions plus one disk read; the unit gate refuses tests that shell out, so the bd call cannot live inside the detector).

Two methods on ArmCheck, split on WHO touches the outside world:

  unbeaded(self) -> dict[str, str]
    Arms whose shell carries no '# bead: knee-xxxx' line. Reads the shell files off disk, exactly like
    carriage_returns() already does, so it stays testable against a fixture directory.

  unpriced(self, descriptions: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]
    PURE. Takes bead id -> bead description text and returns the arms whose bead has no price. Detects
    the knee-yuqf format by requiring both 'PRICE:' and 'P(clears' -- two markers rather than one so a
    bead that merely mentions the word price in prose does not pass.

main() resolves the ids with 'bd show' and hands the text in. That keeps the subprocess at the edge and
leaves both detectors unit-testable, which is the same shape refused()/carriage_returns() already have.

REFUSAL, not a warning: an arm with no bead, or a bead with no price, fails arm_check the way a flag typo
does. The whole point of the bead is that a rule I have to remember fails on exactly the runs momentum
picks, so an advisory line would be the documentation that already exists.

attend_true.sh already carries its '# bead:' line, so it is the first arm the check will pass.

title: Depth-ordered slice aggregation — every arm this project has run is permutation-invariant over the slice axis
description:
PRICE: proxy ~1.5h (mostly coding) + ~6 min card; confirm ~1h card. PLAUSIBLE GAIN 1-3%; P(clears 1.5%) ~25-30%. Best ratio on the board.

MECHANISM. slice_features encodes every slice alone. over_depth takes amax within depth regions then a MEAN ACROSS regions, symmetric under swapping them. SliceAttention is attention-MIL: it scores each slice independently and softmax-weights, so it is order-blind too. Max pooling, depth regions, slice attention, whole-stack reading and three encoders are therefore ALL permutation-invariant over depth. On 3D MRI the model has never been able to represent that a finding extends across consecutive slices.

WHY THE ENCODER CLOSURE DOES NOT REFUTE IT. v3base_dense and cnx_dense closed encoder diversity, but all three encoders sat behind this same order-blind aggregator. Those arms varied the trunk, never the aggregator's access to order. Supporting sign: depth_regions_narrow, the one crude gesture at depth structure, is in the champion roster.

PROXY. kneemri/embeddings caches per-slice features precisely so pooling stays a free choice (its own docstring says so), and head_trial answers such a question in seconds against 320s for a full arm. Train an order-aware aggregator (learned positional embedding + 1-2 attention layers over <=20 slice tokens, kept to SliceAttention parameter scale because this task is supervision-limited) against the order-blind incumbent on IDENTICAL cached features, so the delta reads clean.

THE PROXY MUST BE VALIDATED BEFORE IT IS BELIEVED, on its own terms: embedding_cache states that a frozen encoder is a different function, and that the harness is trustworthy only once head variants with known fine-tuned scores are ranked on it and the ORDERING survives. Do that first; if it fails, the harness answers a different question and the arm goes to the card instead.
notes:
2026-08-21: DepthAttention landed in kneemri/models/slice_attention.py — depthwise conv of span 3 over the slice axis, identity-tap init so it IS `attend` at step zero, then the existing attention-MIL pool. Registered as slice_pooling 'depth'. SLICE_POOLINGS became a record (per_slice + aggregator factory) instead of a bool table plus an '== ATTEND' branch duplicated in model.py and head_trial.py — that duplication meant a pooling added to the model would have been accepted by head_trial's parser and silently built as the maximum. Absolute position deliberately NOT supplied: it is a different claim (where in the band a finding sits) and mixing them would leave a positive unattributable. Tests pin both halves: SliceAttention is permutation-invariant over depth, DepthAttention is not.
2026-08-24: CLOSING — this was answered on 2026-08-21 and the bead never caught up. depth_true ran DepthAttention on the settled recipe and read 0.8461: -0.0015 against attend_true, -0.0012 against the plain mean, +0.0004 against max. Four operators on one recipe now span 0.0019 (max 0.8457, order-aware gate 0.8461, mean 0.8473, permutation-blind gate 0.8476) and the ORDER-AWARE one lands second-worst, so the extra structure is not merely flat but slightly costly. Seat value -0.0002, which the board charges at ~3x. It does not mount.

The frozen-feature proxy called BOTH signs in advance (trained gate +0.0027, through-plane mixing -0.0007) and the pixel model reproduced them — the first time that proxy was checked against a full arm on this axis, which makes it usable to gate future pooling work at ~2 min instead of ~45.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT, and it is the part worth carrying forward: through-plane mixing at the FEATURE level is what died. A 3D encoder that sees the volume before any per-slice feature exists is a different mechanism and remains untouched. The aggregation stage is now saturated from three directions at once — more slices -0.0001, more slots +0.0002, every combining rule within 0.0019 — so the limit is UPSTREAM, in what one slice's feature vector contains. Full row: experiments/README.md line 283.

title: study_cache.build must be resumable — a kill costs the whole decode
description: open_memmap(mode="w+") recreates the images file zeroed, so an interrupted build restarts from zero however far it had got. On 2026-08-11 a build sharing the machine with a trainer was killed by the OS with neither process leaving an error; the cost was the entire multi-hour decode. That no-resume property is also what forces every build to demand the machine alone, which is a scheduling cost paid on every build forever. Flush a partial mask plus per-study done flags periodically and reopen the existing memmap when the index matches exactly, bounding a kill's cost to the studies since the last flush.

title: 140 mm is the FOV knee: 94% of series served, +5.6pp tissue retained
description:
Corpus-wide over 1822 series from 400 studies (kneemri.corpus.crop_coverage --sample 400 --tight-mm 140):

crop        median    p10   worst  series
image@130   0.8495 0.7299 0.4537    1822
image@140   0.9052 0.8073 0.5254    1718
tissue@130  0.8860 0.7576 0.4524    1822
tissue@140  0.9375 0.8336 0.5232    1718

The shipped 130 mm crop discards a median 15% of imaged tissue (p10 27%, worst 55%), and the discarded ring is the PERIPHERY - where MCL (medial margin), ACL and Baker's (posterior) live. That is exactly the per-label gradient crop80_span measured when the crop tightened further: MCL -0.0265*, ACL -0.0263*, Baker's -0.0164*.

WHY 140 AND NOT 150/170. SlotReader._crop does NOT pad - it returns the stack untouched when the window does not fit, so a wide crop is honoured only on the subset wide enough and breaks the constant-mm/pixel invariant for the rest. Served share: 130mm 1822/1822 (100%), 140mm 1718/1822 (94.3%), 150mm 1489/1822 (81.7%), 170mm 358/1822 (19.6%). 140 buys +5.6pp median tissue for 5.7% of series falling back to native extent; 150 buys a little more and breaks 18%.

DEPENDS ON: knee-7zw7 (the direction), and on deciding whether the 5.7% fall back or get PADDED - padding is the change that would make 150 readable too.
notes:
DECODE COST MEASURED 2026-08-21: the 140 mm cache built in 34m59s wall clock (09:44:44 -> 10:19:43 UTC), 4407 studies x 6 slots x 20 slices at 336 px, 0.1-0.9 band, uint8, 0/4407 studies with no slot. ~126 studies/s at this geometry; scale roughly linearly in slices x pixels, so a 448 px build of the same corpus prices at ~1h05.

CONTENTION, the half that matters for the shared card: it ran ALONGSIDE attend_true holding 16.24 GB of the 5090 and neither slowed the other measurably -- the arm's epochs across the build window were 274 / 266 / 258 / 260 / 247 / 254 s, a warm-up trend, not contention. A decode is CPU + NVMe bound, so a cache build is not a reason for either agent to wait for the card; only TRAINING queues against the lock. Sent to biohub as inbox/2026-08-21_140mm_build_wallclock.txt.

PRICE: ~52 min of card (band_dense geometry -- 20 slices, 12 epochs at ~250 s an epoch). The decode is SUNK, so the card time is the whole cost. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.05 on the mean; P(clears the 0.0062 floor) ~ 0.4.

WHY THAT PRICE AND WHY THE ARM IS STILL WORTH IT. The mean is not where this arm's expected value lives, and pretending otherwise would be the unpriced-arm mistake. What is measured is a PER-LABEL GRADIENT along this exact axis, in the opposite direction: crop80_span tightened the crop and cost MCL -0.0265*, ACL -0.0263*, Baker's -0.0164* -- the periphery labels, each clearing its own interval. 140 mm loosens the same axis by a comparable step (+5.6pp median tissue, 0.8495 -> 0.9052 image coverage). Three of twelve labels recovering half of that is ~+0.005 on the mean, i.e. inside the floor. A 1.5% mean needs all twelve to move and they will not.

The seat, not the mean, is the return: MCL / ACL / Baker's are labels NO seated member resolves, and the decode axis is the one measured to transfer to the board at 2.4x. So this is a DIVERSITY arm priced as one -- keep it if the periphery group goes positive against band_dense even with a flat mean, kill it if the periphery group is flat, which would say the crop80_span losses were resolution and not field of view.

CONTEXT THAT RAISES IT ABOVE THE KNOB QUEUE: six consecutive knobs on band_dense have now gone negative (attend -0.0009, focal -0.0044, aprior -0.0021, depth_regions -0.0029, calib -0.0020, aug -0.0076). band_dense is a local optimum under knobs; the data recipe is the remaining lever, and this is the only arm on the board whose mechanism carries a measured per-label gradient.
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-21 while band140 is at epoch 2, so the follow-up is chosen before the number rather than after it.

THE CONFOUND IS REAL AND IT IS IN THE READER, verified at kneemri/corpus/slot_reader.py:264. window() takes round(crop_mm / spacing) NATIVE pixels and the stack is then resized to image_size. So a crop is a fixed PHYSICAL extent rendered into a fixed PIXEL budget, and widening it spends resolution:

  130 mm / 336 px = 0.3869 mm/px   (band_dense, the control)
  140 mm / 336 px = 0.4167 mm/px   (band140)

band140 is therefore not 'more field of view'. It is 7.7% more field bought with 7.7% coarser pixels, at identical compute. That is the right FIRST arm -- it is free, and if coverage matters more than resolution it wins outright -- but it cannot separate the two, and its refutation clause was written knowing that.

THE DECOUPLING ARM, gated on band140's periphery group rather than on its mean. 140 mm at 362 px holds mm/px at the control's 0.3869 exactly (140 / 0.3869 = 361.9), so field of view moves and resolution does not. Cost is (362/336)^2 = 1.16x, about 420 s an epoch, 84 minutes.

  RUN IT IF band140's MCL / ACL / Baker's group moves POSITIVE while the mean is flat or down. That reads as coverage helping and resolution hurting, which is exactly the case a fixed-mm/px arm resolves and the only case worth 84 minutes.
  DO NOT RUN IT IF that group is flat. Flat periphery under 7.7% more field says the medial margin was not being missed, and a resolution-matched version cannot rescue a coverage effect that is not there.
  DO NOT RUN IT IF the group goes NEGATIVE with the mean. That is resolution dominating, and the arm that follows is finer pixels at the SAME extent, which res392 already measured at +0.0002 -- i.e. the axis closes.

WHY THE PERIPHERY GROUP IS THE RIGHT READ, and it is not this arm's own reasoning: the label-contest pilot (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_label_contest_pilot.md) read 1,200 cells against the incumbent labeler's verbatim rulebook and found MCL contested ZERO times out of 100 while scoring 0.788-0.793, the WORST label in the corpus. Its labels are clean and its score is bad, so whatever bounds MCL is not supervision. MCL is a thin ligament at the MEDIAL MARGIN of the field read coronally -- the structure a 130 mm centre crop is most likely to clip. That is a fourth independent line arriving where resolution.sh's occlusion evidence already pointed, and it is what makes the periphery group the deciding clause rather than a post-hoc slice.

title: No layer-wise LR decay exists — the depth axis has been measured without the mechanism that makes it readable
description:
StudyModel.parameter_groups builds exactly TWO param groups: head at head_lr, and every opened backbone block at ONE flat backbone_lr. There is no layer-wise decay anywhere in the repo - grep over kneemri/, experiments/README.md and research/ for layer-wise / llrd / layer_decay / lr_decay returns zero hits. It has never been built, tried, or written about.

WHY THIS MATTERS RIGHT NOW. Adaptation's own docstring says depth and rate are ENTANGLED and that a null depth result at 8e-6 cannot distinguish 'more blocks do not help' from 'no block was going to move anyway'. The fix it reached for was raising the rate. But with a FLAT rate, raising it to make the top blocks move necessarily applies the same rate to the earliest blocks, which are the most general and the most damaging to disturb. So the axis has only ever been measurable along a diagonal: every point trades top-block motion against bottom-block destruction. LLRD is precisely the mechanism that decouples them, and it is the standard one for pretrained-trunk transfer (ULMFiT, BERT fine-tuning, ViT/BEiT/MAE transfer all ship it).

THE EVIDENCE THE LEDGER ALREADY HAS, read under this lens:
- unfreezing every block was worth +0.0008 at 8e-6 (nothing moved)
- encoder_adapt_thawed, running now: 12 blocks open at 4e-5 on a one-cycle peak, holdout FALLING monotonically 0.6651 -> 0.6533 -> 0.6456 while its matched 6-block control rose 0.6548 -> 0.6608 -> 0.6890 at the same schedule position. Training loss above the control at every epoch. That is the shape of a trunk being damaged at the bottom, and under a flat rate it is the only shape available.
- the whole encoder_adapt family sits near 0.73 against band_dense 0.8578.

WHAT IT WOULD LOOK LIKE: parameter_groups returns one group per block with lr = backbone_lr * decay^(depth - i), decay ~0.65-0.75, head unchanged. That is a change to one method plus a flag, and it makes --unfreeze-last 12 a DIFFERENT experiment rather than a louder version of the same one.

HONEST PRICING: this is a mechanism that could plausibly deliver the 1.5% bar because it reopens an axis that has produced four null-to-negative results, rather than sharpening a subscore. But it is a PREDICTION, not a measurement. The cheap proxy is a short arm at 12 blocks with decay against the 12-block flat arm now on the card - same recipe, one variable, and the flat arm is already paid for.

DEPENDS ON: encoder_adapt_thawed finishing, which gives the flat-rate control at the exact depth.
notes:
SHIPPED b1829bb 2026-08-21, gates green, pushed. Arm band_dense_llrd is written, arm_check-clean, smoke-clean, and NOT YET RUN — the queue watcher gating it on encoder_adapt_thawed's checkpoint was killed when that arm was killed, so it needs re-arming by hand.

PRICED HONESTLY (the new wall-clock/gain rule applied to our own build): ~2.5 h of card for a run whose OWN pre-registration predicts a null, P(clears the 1.5% bar) under 5%. It is an INSTRUMENT, not a score bet — it either licenses re-running the whole depth axis (every depth arm to date was measured at a flat rate) or closes it. It must be scheduled as that, behind the 140 mm cache build, which is the prerequisite for the highest-expected-gain arm we have left.
PRICING RE-EXAMINED 2026-08-21 and it comes back to the SAME number by a better argument, which is why it is written down.

I re-opened this arm because the ledger's own conclusion -- 'the limit is upstream, in what one slice's feature vector contains' -- points straight at the trunk, and only 6 of 12 blocks adapt. The tempting evidence is the slope: unfreeze_4 scored 0.8320 against wsfold0_e6's 0.8457, so TWO blocks were worth 0.0137, 2.2x the floor, single-variable and flag-verified. Extrapolated to twelve that is +0.04 and this becomes the best bet on the board.

THAT EXTRAPOLATION IS WRONG AND I NEARLY MADE IT. 4 -> 6 adds blocks 7 and 8, i.e. it moves along the LATE end of the encoder. It says the late blocks carry the adaptation. It says nothing whatever about blocks 1-6, which are the early, generic, most-transferable layers -- the part of a ViT that a downstream task least needs to move and is most easily damaged by moving. The slope is steep exactly where the prior already expected it to be steep, and flat-to-harmful exactly where this arm proposes to go. So the two measured points do NOT raise the prior; they locate it.

PRICE UNCHANGED: ~2.5 h of card, P(clears the 1.5% bar) under 5%, INSTRUMENT not score bet. What it buys is the retirement of the depth axis: every depth arm to date was measured at a flat 4e-5 across whatever was open, and lr20x collapsed at depth 12 (0.7524), which is consistent with early blocks being wrecked at a uniform rate. Layer decay 0.7 is the mechanism that makes the axis readable at all, and the training loss is the second instrument -- if early blocks are being wrecked at a flat rate, a flat 12-block arm floors its loss high while this one should track band_dense's 1.2162 -> 0.5780.

The batch-2 substitution is not a free variable: small_accum measured 0.8579 against band_dense's 0.8578, so the accumulation path is priced at 0.0001.

QUEUED third, behind band140 (running, epoch 2) and depth_true. The bead's own scheduling condition -- behind the 140 mm cache build -- is satisfied by band140 being on the card now. Arm carries the '# bead: knee-a2q7' header for the price rule.
PRICE: ~2.5 h wall-clock (12 epochs, batch 2 / accumulate 6, 20 slices, ~750 s/epoch at this depth). P(clears 1.5%) < 5%.

This is an INSTRUMENT, not an improvement, and it is queued as one. The depth bracket it re-reads --
unfreeze 12 worth +0.0008 over unfreeze 6 -- was measured with ONE flat rate on every opened block, so
'more blocks do not help' and 'the extra blocks were wrecked at the top's rate' are indistinguishable in
it. Decay separates them for 2.5 h. What it buys is a keep/kill on a whole axis, not a delta.

NEAR-MISS RECORDED DELIBERATELY: I was about to re-price this UP from unfreeze_4's slope (4->6 blocks
worth 0.0137, extrapolate to +0.04 at 12). That is wrong. 4->6 moves the LATE end of the encoder; it says
nothing about blocks 0-5, the early generic layers a downstream task least needs to move and most easily
damages. The slope is steep exactly where the prior already expected steep, and flat-to-harmful exactly
where this arm proposes to go. Price held.
CLOSED 2026-08-21 on a REFUSED pre-registration. band_dense_llrd ran 12 epochs, best 0.8483 at e10 against band_dense's 0.8578 — -0.0095, past the 0.0062 floor and the wrong way. The seat test agrees: adding it to the shipped five reads 0.8682 (-0.0008) and its best seat swap is 0.8683 (-0.0007), zero of one clearing +0.0015.

The arm's READ-IT-ON ladder said a BELOW result 'closes the depth axis for good'. That reading is REFUSED, and the arm's own second instrument is why. The docstring pre-registered the training loss as that instrument and said this arm's loss should track band_dense's 1.2162 -> 0.5780 curve. It does not: 1.2527 -> 0.7013 at e11, still descending, against the control's 0.5898 at e10. Underfit, not damaged.

THE CAUSE IS A SECOND VARIABLE THE ARM DID NOT PRICE. StudyModel.parameter_groups (kneemri/models/model.py:580) anchors the ladder at the TOP opened block: backbone_lr * layer_decay ** (len(opened) - 1 - depth). Under --unfreeze-last 12 that puts blocks 6-11 — the exact six the control trains at a flat 4e-5 — at 4e-5, 2.8e-5, 2.0e-5, 1.37e-5, 9.6e-6, 6.7e-6, a geometric mean of 0.7^2.5 = 0.41 of the control's rate. The arm did not add six whisper blocks to the control; it added six whisper blocks AND cut the control's own six by 2.4x.

Link by link: PLUMBING green and mechanically so (encoder_rate_decay is a Landed-compared field read off the optimiser's top two backbone groups rather than off the flag, measured ratio 0.7, so the run could not have passed without the decay landing). DATA green (identical cache/band/slices/schedule). TEST green. BATCH green and priced in advance (small_accum 0.8579 vs 0.8578). TRAINING is the red link, and no gate could have caught it: both variables are legitimate values of flags that landed correctly.

WHAT IS NOT RULED OUT: layer-wise decay as a mechanism, and the depth axis. Adaptation's docstring should keep calling depth and rate ENTANGLED — this arm did not disentangle them, it entangled them a second way. The one-variable version anchors the ladder at block 6 so blocks 6-11 keep the flat 4e-5 and only 0-5 decay.

THAT CLEAN ARM IS PRICED AND DECLINED: an anchor argument in parameter_groups, a smoke, and 12 x 580s = 1.93h of card, ~2.2h all in. The flat 12-block bracket measured depth at +0.0008; even granting that this is correction-minus-damage, a generous ceiling is ~+0.005 — under the 1.5% bar — at roughly one-in-five odds of clearing 0.0062. That loses to through_dense's 40 min. Re-testable, not dead.

title: A CNN trunk is the only member axis left: ConvNeXtV2 behind an Encoder.load() seam
description:
v3base_dense settled it: a second ViT family is worth -0.0007 as a sixth seat and -0.0005 as a swap, both inside the ruler's resolution. Encoder diversity paid once (base_dense, 0.930->0.931) and does not pay twice within the transformer inductive bias. The greedy ceiling over all 18 mounted members is 0.8692 against the champion's 0.8690, so new members are the only lever and a genuinely different bias is the only kind of new member worth fitting.

ConvNeXtV2-base is the candidate: 87.7M parameters against DINOv2-base's 86M, 1024-wide, stride 32, FCMAE self-supervised pretraining. Probed 2026-08-21: AutoModel returns last_hidden_state of shape (B, 1024, H/32, W/32) -- a feature MAP, not tokens -- and its config carries hidden_sizes rather than hidden_size and no num_register_tokens.

The head already takes any module callable as backbone(pixel_values=x) returning .last_hidden_state, so the work is an adapter that presents the ViT contract (flatten the map to tokens, prepend the global mean as a pseudo-CLS so prefix_tokens=1 stays correct, expose hidden_size) plus the registry entry. Do it behind a new Encoder.load() so the eight sites that currently call AutoModel.from_pretrained(encoder.repository) themselves keep having exactly one branch between them -- adding a family must not add eight ifs.

352 px is the read size (11x11 grid); 336 does not tile at stride 32. No Kaggle mount yet, so mount=None: trainable here, not submittable until the weights are published as a dataset the way dinov3-hf was.

title: Encoder-family diversity is the axis that paid: find a third family
description:
basedense scored 0.931 (new champion) on the back of base_dense, a member that LOST its own matched control by 0.0066 (outside the 0.0062 floor) at 2.5x the epoch cost. It is the only DINOv2-base in a pool seven DINOv2-small members deep. 0.932-or-above did NOT fire, so encoder CAPACITY is not the lever; encoder DIVERSITY is. Confirmed clean: batch_teardown arm 1 measured batch 6 at +0.0020 vs control, inside the floor, so base_dense's solo loss is an encoder reading and not a VRAM artefact.

The recombination line is exhausted: greedy ceiling over all 18 mounted members is 0.8692 against the champion's 0.8690. New MEMBERS, not new subsets.

Wanted: a member from an encoder family this pool does not contain, trained on the settled band recipe, judged on SEAT value and never retired on its own control. dinov3_base_lora is already mounted and is weak (0.8268, taken 16th by greedy) - a LoRA adapter over a frozen trunk is not the same experiment as a fully-adapted different family. Candidates to price: a ConvNeXt/ResNet CNN trunk (a genuinely different inductive bias, not another ViT), SigLIP/CLIP-family ViT, or a medical-pretrained trunk.
notes: ANSWERED NEGATIVELY 2026-08-21 by cnx_dense. This bead asked for 'a member from an encoder family this pool does not contain' and named ConvNeXt/CNN first among the candidates to price. ConvNeXtV2-base was registered and run on the settled band recipe at 352 px (the stride-32 grid): solo 0.7927 against base_dense 0.8512, seat value -0.0042 as a sixth and -0.0042 as a base_dense swap, 0 of 1 clearing +0.0015. Eleven of twelve labels negative with ten clearing their paired half-widths -- the widest significant sweep in the ledger. The bead's own framing ('encoder CAPACITY is not the lever; encoder DIVERSITY is') is what the arm refutes: a genuinely different inductive bias bought a MORE negative seat than a second ViT family did. Close on the strength of the ledger row experiments/README.md:1549, not on this note.

title: The holdout ranks entries correctly and understates a weak member's cost by ~3x
description:
crossenc (0.926) and maxdiv (0.925) against longseat (0.930) give three entries whose offline
order is 0.8691 / 0.8678 / 0.8668 and whose board order is 0.930 / 0.926 / 0.925 — monotone. The
909-study fold-0 holdout therefore RANKS correctly; what it gets wrong is magnitude, and only in the
direction of understating what a weak member COSTS: -0.0013 offline became -0.004 on the board and
-0.0023 became -0.005.

This inverts the 2.4x diversity under-pricing (knee-nas5, knee-7d1) as a decision rule. That
measurement was taken on the DECODE axis by collapsing three members into one pixel group, and it was
being used to justify firing members whose offline add was negative-but-inside-the-floor on the theory
that the ruler could not see their diversity. Two entries fired on that theory, two refuted. The rule
that replaces it: an offline delta inside the noise floor is not free, it is a board cost of roughly
three times its size, and 'inside the floor' is an argument for NOT spending a slot.

Also retires the reading that 0.927-0.930 is the price band of recombination. Eight entries sat in it;
these two broke below it. It is the range spanned by recombining members that are individually strong.

Consequence to apply: any future entry adding a member must clear the offline delta the board actually
resolves (+0.0015), not merely sit inside the floor.
close_reason:
Mechanised in code rather than left as a habit. MemberCurve.board_cost is now a public method printed by swap(), and it states which of three bands a best-seat delta falls in: above BOARD_RESOLVABLE the ruler orders correctly but saturates; between zero and it the ruler cannot separate candidate from incumbent; below zero the board charges about BOARD_COST_MULTIPLE (3x) what is shown, so -0.0010 offline reads as roughly -0.003 on the board.

The stale docs that talked a reader INTO spending a slot on a negative are gone: member_curve.swap's docstring and seat_value's module docstring both carried the refuted 2.4x diversity under-pricing from knee-7d1 as a licence. That 2.4x came off the DECODE axis (collapsing three members into one pixel group) and does not carry to a member swap; two entries were fired on it and both were refuted. Three paired entries measure the opposite - the holdout RANKS correctly (0.8691/0.8678/0.8668 offline vs 0.930/0.926/0.925 board) and errs only in MAGNITUDE, understating a weak member's cost.

Commits ad04cbd, 5d03e4b. BOARD_RESOLVABLE is documented as a SPENDING GUARD, not a target - the project bar is 1.5% absolute and the noise floor 0.0062, both an order of magnitude above it.

title: GPU lock lives under the knee data root, so it cannot serialise across projects
description: AGREED PATH: D:/personal_projects/.gpu.lock (biohub proposed the project root; our D:/data/gpu.lock counter-proposal was dropped to avoid a round trip). The mutex in experiments/lib.sh is currently $LOGS/gpu.lock inside the knee data root, so it only serialises OUR chains and is invisible to biohub_kaggle's celltrack arms on the same RTX 5090. Two arms on one card is not a crash: Windows pages GPU memory over PCIe and the run crawls at 32-37 img/s against ~520 while nvidia-smi reads 99% util (measured 2026-08-12). MOVE LOCK_DIR, then write to ../biohub_kaggle/inbox/ that it is live — biohub gates on it only from that message on. DO NOT edit lib.sh while base_dense holds the card: the arm sources it.
notes:
2026-08-21: a second failure mode on the same lock, found live. hold_card clears a lock whose HOLDER PID is dead (kill -0), but the holder it records is the snapshot SHELL, not the trainer. Killing encoder_adapt_thawed's wrapper left the snapshot bash alive in its own sleep with its python already gone — a shell holding the card against nothing, and kill -0 says it is healthy. The queue looked correctly parked. Recovery took a manual kill of the shell; the poll then cleared the lock in under a minute, so the loop is self-healing once the shell actually dies. The gap is that liveness is asserted of the wrong process: record the TRAINER's pid beside the shell's, or have the parked arm check that the holder still owns GPU memory. queue_check covers dead watchers; this is the mirror case, a live shell over a dead trainer.
DONE 2026-08-21. Lock moved from $LOGS/gpu.lock (inside this project's data root, invisible to any other project) to $HOME/.gpu.lock, GPU_LOCK_DIR overridable. $HOME rather than a data root because it is the one path both projects resolve identically without reading each other's config, and it is outside both repos.

The non-obvious half: arms execute from a SNAPSHOT of lib.sh taken at launch, so moving the lock does not move it for anything in flight. band140 was mid-epoch under the old path when this landed; depth_true snapshots the new lib and would have taken a lock band140 has never heard of -- two arms on one card, the exact 31.9-GB PCIe-paging overflow the lock exists to prevent, produced by the fix on its first use. wait_out_legacy_lock takes the new lock first (so it cannot deadlock -- nothing old looks at the new path) then blocks on the old path while a live holder is recorded there. Smoked over four classes: absent / dead holder / pidless dir / live holder, the last measured waiting 60s and releasing.

hold_card gained an explicit return 0; its status was whatever wait_for_free_card's last branch test left, under set -e.

Commit 3b73dcc. Removable once no arm snapshotted before 2026-08-21 can still be running. Biohub owes the path -- letter next.

title: No gradient accumulation, so a bigger encoder cannot hold the control's effective batch
description: MEASURED 2026-08-20: base_dense at the settled recipe (batch 12, 336px, 20 slices, whole-stack, recompute-activations) is refused by the VRAM cap - 'this run wants 56.3 GB, 30.3 free' - and the arm parked for the full 1800 s wait without starting. The only lever available is --batch, and lowering it changes the OPTIMISATION as well as the encoder, so a base arm cannot be a one-variable test against band_dense. Gradient accumulation (--accumulate N, step the optimiser every N micro-batches) restores the control's effective batch at a fraction of the activation memory and is what makes the whole larger-backbone axis measurable, not just base.

title: queue_check silently passed: ps is not on the Windows PATH the checker runs on
description: MEASURED 2026-08-20: shutil.which('ps') returns None from the Python interpreter queue_check runs in (MSYS ps lives in git-bash /usr/bin, off the Windows PATH), while 'ps -ef' works in the launching shell. The check therefore reported 'no process listing: liveness cannot be crossed' and RETURNED SUCCESS - the exact silent pass it exists to prevent, on the only machine it runs on. Fixed with an ordered Probe list (ps -ef, then Get-CimInstance Win32_Process which carries the FULL command line where tasklist carries only an image name).

title: base_dense: dinov2-base at the settled operating point, never measured
description: Eleven arms re-read 2026-08-20 are 11/11 negative on the mean, and the oracle over seven members prices per-label recombination at +0.0002 (2026-08-17). Both say the member POPULATION is exhausted, not the tuning - and every member is dinov2-small. The only base arm in the ledger, compose_base, died at epoch 7/24 and predates the whole current operating point (no --whole-stack, 12 slices, no band), so base at the settled recipe is ABSENT, not weak. Arm written at experiments/arms/base_dense.sh with three pre-registered outcomes. Blocked on encoder_adapt_lower freeing the card; smoke at --studies 60 --epochs 1 before queueing.
notes: STALE - this ran and read on 2026-08-20. Ledger experiments/README.md:1521 '### base_dense - a bigger encoder loses on its own ruler and comes back level on the other one', peak holdout 0.8512 at e8 against small's 0.8578 (-0.0066). The batch alibi was then removed by batch_teardown arm 1 (small_batch6): batch is not a lever here, so the -0.0066 is an ENCODER reading. base_dense went on to carry the 0.931 board entry, which is the standing case that a member's SOLO number and its SEAT value are different quantities. Closing against the ledger, not against fresh work.

title: the adaptation file does not record which cache it was adapted on
description:
kneemri.training.pretrain selects its corpus through CacheFlags defaults: 12 slices, band 0.20-0.80 (confirmed in logs/pretrain_lr1e5.log line 4, '12 slices per slot'). Every arm that imports the result trains on 20 slices, band 0.10-0.90. So the adaptation is on-domain for a DIFFERENT slice population than the one it is imported into -- it never saw the outer band (0.10-0.20, 0.80-0.90) at all, and saw the centre at coarser spacing.

Cleared by audit and NOT the mismatch: normalisation is byte-identical between the two paths (/255 then ImageNet mean/std, kneemri/models/model.py:324,330 vs kneemri/training/pretrain.py:141 + spectral_mae.py:163), and both read the cache at its native 336 px with no resampling, so neither input distribution nor spatial scale differs.

Size honestly: a band subset cannot plausibly account for the 0.17 collapse the encoder_adapt arms posted, so this is NOT the explanation for that result. It is a defect that makes the axis harder to read, and it is cheap to fix -- the pretrain already parses CacheFlags, so the arm's --slices/--band-low/--band-high just have to be passed. Fix before any further pretraining run, so the next adaptation is on-domain for the recipe that consumes it.
notes:
CORRECTION to this issue's original framing, which was wrong. I filed it as 'pretrain reads the DEFAULT cache' as though the CLI could not be told otherwise. It can: main() calls CacheFlags.add_to(parser), so --slices/--band-low/--band-high have always been accepted and CacheFlags.cache() honours them. The two adaptations on disk read the default cache because the LAUNCH did not pass the flags, not because the code ignored them. That is an invocation defect and it is already spent.

The real code defect is next door and is the failure class this repo keeps paying for. Pretrainer.save recorded the objective's knobs and the variant, and its own docstring says the recipe travels with the weights so a write-up can ask whether the flag landed -- but it did NOT record the slice population. An adaptation is on-domain for the pixels it SAW, and the only surviving record of which cache each one read was a line in a launch log.

FIXED: save() now stamps cache.key (the name that, per StudyCache.key, states everything deciding the cache's contents) into config, PretrainedEncoder.cache() reads it back, and the loader's log line at import time names it -- so every future arm's full log states the cache its encoder was adapted on. Files written before the stamp report 'unrecorded' rather than reading as a match.

title: Through-plane masked prediction: the SSL objective currently sees zero 3D structure
description:
MRI is volumetric and a study is THREE orthogonal samplings of the knee (SAG/COR/AX x contrast, 6 slots, 12-20 slices each) - strictly richer than the isotropic cube an SL-MAE reads. Our encoder is 2D by choice, because DINOv2's pretrained weights are the asset and a 3D encoder means training from scratch on 4,407 studies. Volume is recovered at the HEAD (--whole-stack pooling, slice_attention +0.0016, seated).

THE GAP: kneemri/training/pretrain.py:127 draws slices INDEPENDENTLY at random, deliberately, so a batch cannot contain near-duplicate neighbours the decoder copies. Correct for batch statistics and it means the self-supervised objective sees no through-plane structure at all - every slice is an island, and masking recovers in-plane texture only. Continuity across slices is how a tear is distinguished from a partial-volume artefact, and menisci/cruciates are exactly the labels the 58-study vision partition says we fail on (Lateral Meniscus -0.193, ACL -0.123, MCL -0.096, Medial Meniscus -0.094).

THE ARM: mask WHOLE SLICES and reconstruct them from their neighbours - sample an adjacent triplet, hide the middle, predict from the outer two. Same backbone, same decoder, same cache; only the sampler and the mask change. Second version hides a whole SLOT and predicts it from another plane, which is the cross-plane consistency no head-level pooling can supervise.

Blocked on encoder_adapt reading out - that arm is the clean one-variable test of the in-plane objective and this must not be folded into it.
notes:
THE VEHICLE IS CLOSED 2026-08-21, and it is closed by a measurement this bead's blocker produced rather than by an argument about 3D.

This bead proposes changing WHAT the self-supervised objective masks -- hide a whole slice, predict it from its neighbours -- while holding the backbone, decoder and cache. The blocker it names ("blocked on encoder_adapt reading out") has now read out twice and the pair is decisive: lr 1e-4 gave 0.6902, lr 1e-5 gave 0.6875, 0.0027 apart and well inside the 0.0062 floor, from two adaptations whose blocks 0-5 differ FOURFOLD in drift (0.034-0.083 against 0.0046-0.0179). If the quality of the adaptation were the variable those two numbers could not agree. What the two share is block 11 moved 0.5510 and 0.2144 of its own norm, against a supervised maximum anywhere of 0.0080 -- the head reads block 11, both arms handed it a representation reshaped for RECONSTRUCTION, and twelve epochs at 4e-5 cannot walk back 21-55%. Against band_dense 0.8578 that is -0.17.

WHY THAT LANDS ON THIS BEAD. The cost is incurred by masked reconstruction reshaping the read block, and it is indifferent to what gets masked. Masking a whole slice instead of a patch grid changes the semantics of the pretext task and changes nothing about the failure mode. This arm would spend a pretrain run plus a fitting arm to re-measure a -0.17 with different flavouring.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, so the asset stays re-testable. (1) The 3D MECHANISM itself is untouched and is now carried by knee-tqn (DepthAttention), the only operator in the tree that can read slice ORDER -- supervised by the actual labels, so no reconstruction objective touches the trunk. (2) A reconstruction objective on a SEPARATE trunk that never has to serve the classifier -- distillation rather than initialisation -- is a different experiment and this result says nothing about it. (3) The spectral term specifically has never been isolated.

DEMOTE, do not close: reopen only if some future arm gives a reconstruction objective a path to the head that does not run through block 11.

title: Arms die at exit 127 when a push re-syncs the shared .venv underneath them
description: A trainer that is mid-run holds an interpreter open against .venv. Every pre-commit/pre-push entry is 'uv run --extra dev' or '--extra devtools', and alternating extras makes uv rewrite .venv IN PLACE. The running interpreter's files vanish and it dies with exit 127 and no traceback -- no error line, no CUDA message, nothing in the trainer log. lib.sh:324-328 already records the first occurrence (2026-08-13, mid epoch 4, traced to a push at 14:03 rewriting uv.lock at 14:05) and added --no-sync to run_train. That fix is one-sided: --no-sync stops the ARM from syncing, and cannot stop another uv process from syncing beneath it. It recurred 2026-08-20 10:32, killing severity_weight at step 182/291 of epoch 1 -- the push that did it was my own. FIX: arms run against a dedicated environment (.venv-arm, built with UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, gitignored) so the shared .venv is no longer shared with a live run. lib.sh must set UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT in run_train -- BLOCKED until the current arm lands, because lib.sh is the file that arm's shell is executing and editing it mid-run is the depth_regions_span failure recorded at lib.sh:219-221. Until then: DO NOT PUSH WHILE AN ARM RUNS.
design:
ONE EDIT POINT, because all four uv sites in lib.sh (46, 329, 388, 464) already pass --no-sync and differ only in what they run. Export the environment once near the top of lib.sh, beside REPO/PROCESSED, and every uv call in every arm inherits it:

    # ARMS DO NOT SHARE AN ENVIRONMENT WITH THE GATES. uv syncs .venv to EXACTLY the extras it is
    # given, so 'uv run --extra dev' and 'uv run --extra devtools' rewrite it in opposite directions
    # -- in place, with no lock. A pre-commit or pre-push hook doing that under a live trainer
    # deletes the files its interpreter is running from: exit 127, no traceback, no error line.
    # Measured twice (2026-08-13 mid epoch 4, 2026-08-20 mid step 182). --no-sync below stops THIS
    # process from syncing and cannot stop another one, which is why the fix is a separate directory
    # rather than another flag.
    export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="$REPO/.venv-arm"
    [ -d "$UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT" ] || uv sync --extra dev --extra devtools

WHY NOT --no-sync ON THE HOOKS INSTEAD: .pre-commit-config.yaml is template-owned (sdlc-scaffold), and
--no-sync there would make a gate silently run against a stale environment, trading a loud failure for
a quiet one.

WHY NOT A LOCK: hold_card already serialises the CARD, and a second lock over the ENVIRONMENT would
make every gate wait out a forty-minute arm. Two directories cost ~2 GB and no waiting.

VERIFICATION, and it must be a positive check rather than 'no crash': with an arm running, run
'uvx nox -s gates' (which alternates extras, the exact trigger) and confirm the arm reaches its next
epoch line. Second check: '.venv-arm/Scripts/python.exe -c "import torch"' still imports after the
gates finish -- the environment the arm holds was not touched.

BLOCKED ON: the current severity_weight run. lib.sh is sourced by that arm's shell and is re-entered
after the trainer returns (to write LIB/_mark, seat value, the best-holdout check). Editing it mid-run
is the depth_regions_span failure at lib.sh:219-221.

ALREADY DONE: .venv-arm built (uv sync with UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, 2026-08-20) and gitignored with the
reasoning. Proven usable in both directions today -- the full AST gate batch and supervision_gap both
ran green against it while the arm held .venv.
notes: knee-z99y is the same race seen from the other side: it recorded gate flakiness, this bead records arm death. One .venv, no lock, two writers.

title: Severity should set the loss WEIGHT, not just the target value: mild YES is right 37.8% of the time and trained at the same 0.95 as severe
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-20, zero GPU, from report_labels_v2.csv and targets.MEASURED_AGREEMENT.

THE DEFECT, in one table. The reader emits five levels. The value carries severity. The weight does not:

  value  meaning    weight(__conf)   cells    radiologist says POSITIVE
  0.08   NO             0.85         22,298      4.1%
  0.28   UNK            0.05         14,445     13.6%
  0.68   mild YES       0.95          6,461     37.8%
  0.82   moderate YES   0.95          6,427     68.8%
  0.94   severe YES     0.95          3,241     95.8%

The three YES levels are severity grades 1/2/3 (the verdict/severity bijection, audited 2026-08-20) and
they all carry conf 0.95, verified over all 52,872 populated cells (min == max == 0.95 at each level).
A mild-grade YES is correct 37.8% of the time and is trained at the SAME confidence as a severe YES that
is correct 95.8%. A 2.5x reliability gap that the loss cannot see.

SIZE OF THE DEFECT, with its denominator stated. 6,461 mild cells x (1 - 0.378) = ~4,020 cells that are
confidently wrong-signed at weight 0.95. Over the 52,872 populated cells that is 7.6% of the corpus —
about twice the 100-report contest pilot's 4.0% contested rate, and unlike the pilot's it is spread
across ALL TWELVE labels rather than concentrated in Fracture and Contusion.

WHY THIS IS NOT calib_span, WHICH LOST 0.0020, and this is the load-bearing distinction.
calib_span (--calibrated-targets, Supervision.applied) rewrites the VALUE to the measured rate:
0.68 -> 0.378. That is BELOW 0.5, so 6,461 mild cells FLIP SIGN — a mild tear becomes a negative target
under BCE. That is a destructive change and is the most likely reason it inverted every clause.
This arm rewrites the WEIGHT and leaves the value alone. The mild tear stays a positive target; it is
merely trusted less. The ordinal ladder 0.68 < 0.82 < 0.94 is preserved intact, so the pairwise ranking
term — the only loss change positive in 3 of 3 matched arms — keeps every pair it currently forms.
So the ledger's one refutation on this axis does NOT transfer: it refuted a value edit, not a weight edit.

THE DESIGN, derived rather than picked (no magic numbers). Weight = P(label is correct | level), which
MEASURED_AGREEMENT already holds:
  NO   0.08 -> correct 95.9%   (weight up slightly from 0.85)
  UNK  0.28 -> 13.6% positive, ambiguous by construction — leave at 0.05
  mild 0.68 -> 0.378
  mod  0.82 -> 0.688
  sev  0.94 -> 0.958
Every number comes from the 58 image reads, fitted there and scored on the fold-0 report holdout, which
is how Supervision already keeps the ruler independent. Gate on WEIGHT_FLOOR interaction: --weight-floor
is in the shipped RECIPE and clamps low weights, so the arm must state what floor it runs under or the
0.378 it is testing never reaches the loss. VERIFY THE FLAG LANDED IN THE CHECKPOINT CONFIG.

DENOMINATOR CAVEAT, stated because it bounds the whole design. MEASURED_AGREEMENT is computed over 684
annotated cells, 311 of them positive calls, so the three YES levels carry roughly 124 / 124 / 62 cells.
The severe rate 95.8% sits on ~62 cells. The per-level ordering is solid (monotone across a 0.58 span,
and the corpus-weighted mean 61.8% reconciles with the independently reported 65% positive agreement),
but no single rate should be treated as precise to better than a few points.

CONTROL: band_dense = 0.8578 at epoch 8, the settled operating point (4e-5 backbone, 20 slices, band
0.10-0.90, whole-stack, 336 px, batch 12, 12 epochs one-cycle). Single variable: the weight column only.

PRE-REGISTERED, written before the run:
  PREDICTION — peak clears 0.8578 by more than 0.0062, and the gain is NOT concentrated in the six
    label-bottlenecked findings (knee-dtk), because a weight change touches all twelve.
  REFUTATION — peak at or below 0.8578. Then reliability weighting is not what the head is missing, the
    flat 0.95 was not costing anything, and the severity axis is closed on the LOSS side as well as the
    value side (calib_span). Say so and stop reaching for supervision.
  THIRD OUTCOME — mean flat but the mild-heavy labels move. Medial Meniscus is 53.3% YES and Effusion
    60.5%; if their per-label numbers move while the mean does not, the mechanism is real and something
    else is absorbing it.

RISK TO THE SHIPPED RESULT: NONE. This is a fold-0 matched arm. It writes a new checkpoint, touches no
member in comp/champion.json, and champion_check still guards that the 0.925 entry rebuilds. The only
cost is GPU time, and the card is currently held for biohub.

NOT QUEUED. Needs the card and an explicit go-ahead.
notes:
2026-08-20 10:32Z — BUILT, SMOKED AND RUNNING. The card freed and the user said so; launched directly
(no sentinel — nothing was running). Commit 2fcfdcf. Log: logs/severity_weight.log.

DENOMINATOR CORRECTION — the "~124 / 124 / 62 cells" above was MY PROPORTIONAL ESTIMATE, not a
measurement, and it was wrong. The real per-level n and CIs are in the Calibration docstring
(kneemri/labels/targets.py:62-67) and were there the whole time:

    level   measured   95% CI            n
     0.68    0.378     [0.282, 0.474]    98
     0.82    0.688     [0.611, 0.764]   141
     0.94    0.958     [0.912, 1.004]    72

This makes the design STRONGER, not weaker: the three intervals DO NOT OVERLAP. 0.474 < 0.611 and
0.764 < 0.912. The ordering is not "solid but imprecise" as the caveat above hedges — it is resolved.
The severe rate sits on 72 cells rather than the 62 I guessed, and moderate on 141 rather than 124.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BUILT, and it differs from the design above in one place:
  Supervision.severity (a bool) + Supervision.trusted() + Supervision.reliability(), consumed at
  targets.py:224 BEFORE applied(), because a calibration rewrites 0.68 to 0.378 in place and a grade
  looked up afterwards would match nothing and fall back to __conf silently. The two switches compose
  only in that order.
  Supervision.moves_the_ruler() now gates the second read in Targets.pair — it was `if calibrated`,
  which would have graded the HOLDOUT under this arm and moved the AUC by construction.
  --severity-weight on TrainingOptions, stamped through Request.wanted() into the checkpoint config,
  so "verify the flag landed" is a config read rather than an inference.

MEASURED ON THE REAL TABLE (52,872 populated cells, post-annotation-override so counts differ slightly
from the raw-table counts in the description above):
  scores byte-identical between arm and control — this is not a calibration
  0.08 NO       n=22,102   0.8875 -> 0.9693
  0.28 UNK      n=14,268   0.2875 -> 0.2875 (untouched, it asserts nothing)
  0.68 mild     n= 6,363   0.9625 -> 0.5335
  0.82 moderate n= 6,286   0.9625 -> 0.7660
  0.94 severe   n= 3,169   0.9625 -> 0.9685

TWO THINGS MOVE, WHICH THE DESIGN ABOVE DID NOT SAY. The NO bucket is the largest at 22,102 cells and
it rises +0.082, uniformly across all twelve labels. So the arm grades the positives AND strengthens
the denials, and a bare mean cannot say which paid. The pre-registered clause was rewritten in the arm
to separate them: the denial uplift can only produce a UNIFORM lift, so a uniform lift now REFUTES.
The grade effect can only appear on labels a report actually grades — meniscus, cartilage/OA, ligament
sprain-to-tear. A lift concentrated in MCL also refutes (the pilot found 0 rulebook errors there and
resolution.sh argues it is bounded by what we can SEE).

Gates: uvx nox -s gates successful; 879 unit tests pass. Four total-partition gates fired on the new
switch and each was answered rather than suppressed — switch_coverage (needs the arm script to exist),
Request/test_not_a_switch, member_record.NOT_IN_CONFIG, run_comparison.SUPERVISION_AXES.
CLOSED 2026-08-21 on the pre-registered REFUTATION clause. The arm ran to completion on 2026-08-20
and its full reading is in experiments/README.md:1238. Peak 0.8530 at epoch 8 against control
band_dense 0.8578 at the same epoch: -0.0048, inside the 0.0062 floor and the wrong sign.

The clause that fired, quoted from the description above: 'REFUTATION -- peak at or below 0.8578.'
It was. The finer pre-registered ruler agrees and is the part that carries the read: the arm predicted a
gain CONCENTRATED in the five graded rows, and four of those five went NEGATIVE (Medial Meniscus -0.0010,
Medial OA -0.0033, PF OA -0.0058, Lateral OA -0.0072; only Lateral Meniscus +0.0064). By structure scale,
focal +0.0001 against regional -0.0118 -- the graded regional findings a severity scale was built to
serve are exactly the ones that lost. The switch fired (the pattern is not uniform, so this is not a
no-op wearing an arm's name); it fired against its own prediction.

THIS BEAD IS BEING CLOSED NOW RATHER THAN ON THE DAY IT RAN because it sat in_progress with the verdict
already written in the ledger -- the same bead/ledger drift ledger_check exists to catch, found here by
reading the ledger rather than the bead.

THE HATCH IT LEFT OPEN IS NOW SHUT, and this is the reason the whole family can be summarised. The
ledger entry ended: 'an ordinal target or a graded head consumes that information without reweighting
the batch, and neither has been tried.' grade_ladder IS that ordinal target and was run 2026-08-21
(knee-t607, ledger 2026-08-21): mean -0.0013, and on the OA triple -- the only labels whose target shape
it changed -- three for three negative. So the severity information has now been spent three independent
ways against the same control:

  calib_span       rewrote the target VALUE   -0.0020   (and flipped sign on 6,363 mild cells)
  severity_weight  rewrote the loss WEIGHT    -0.0048   (regional -0.0118)
  grade_ladder     rewrote the target SHAPE   -0.0013   (OA triple 3/3 negative)

Three parameterisations, three negatives, none clearing the floor in the right direction. The reports do
carry a grade the binary targets discard -- that observation is still true and is not what these arms
refuted. What they refute is that the grade is RECOVERABLE BY SUPERVISION EDITS at this corpus size.

THE AXIS STAYS OPEN AS A BELIEF BY THE OWNER'S STANDING CALL (2026-08-20): 'severity weighting is the
right approach even if it doesnt win out on significant result.' That call is respected here -- nothing
about severity is being deleted, the switches all remain in the trainer and re-testable, and each arm's
mechanism is recorded so a later use is re-tested rather than assumed dead. What closes is the QUEUE
CLAIM: no further severity arm should take a card until something OTHER than a supervision edit is
proposed for it -- a graded HEAD (an output structure, not a target rewrite), or a corpus where the
grades are not already collapsed to binary before we see them.

title: The board frontier is FLAT at 0.952 over 37h; the pack is thickening and recombination is measured at 0.001
description:
RECORDED FRONTIER: 0.942, measured 2026-08-13. USER-REPORTED 2026-08-20: ~0.957, unverified.

If both are right the frontier moves +0.015/wk against our +0.005/wk and the gap has gone 0.014 -> 0.027 and is WIDENING. That changes what is worth queueing: a knob family returning -0.002 a run cannot close 0.027, and four consecutive decode/head knobs have now returned nothing.

WHY IT IS UNVERIFIED — four independent paths tried 2026-08-20, all dead:
  kaggle competitions leaderboard        EXIT 127, not on PATH
  uv run kaggle                          'program not found'
  uv run python -m kaggle                'No module named kaggle'; where.exe kaggle finds nothing
  direct REST, basic auth from ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json   HTTP 401 Unauthorized
KAGGLE_TOKEN is unset; the KGAT_* token survey.py wants expired 2026-07-23 and ~/.kaggle/access_token is stamped that date. WebFetch on /leaderboard and /discussion returns only the page title — Kaggle renders both client-side, so competition discussion has NEVER been readable from here.

WHAT THIS BLOCKS: every 'is our offline edge worth a submission slot' judgement is being made against a number a week old, and the discussion tab — where the frontier's method would be visible — has never been read at all.

FIX: refresh the Kaggle credential (manual, user-side) and re-run the frontier read; then decide whether the recorded 0.942 line in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md gets replaced or annotated.
notes:
2026-08-20 19:58Z FETCHED, and the CLI reads the board fine from here — `kaggle competitions leaderboard
rsna-knee-abnormality-detection -s --csv` returns the public board as CSV with no browser and no token
beyond ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json. Whatever made this unreadable earlier was the transport, not access.

TOP OF THE PUBLIC BOARD, 2026-08-20 19:58Z:
  0.952 Brandon Low          0.947 MKhlystun        0.946 qkrtkddnjs / CloseAI
  0.945 Lukas Nissen Molvaer 0.944 Matteo Vitali / Marcin Jarosz
  0.943 x4    0.942 x2    0.940 x4    0.939 x3
Our best is 0.930 (greedy4_v1 / longseat, tied).

THE GAP IS 0.022, NOT 0.054. knee-jk3 is priced on a frontier reading that is a week stale and its
headline number overstates the distance by 2.5x. That does not refute jk3's mechanism — it re-prices the
prize. Twenty-second place at 0.939 is 0.009 away; the top is 0.022.

WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT TODAY: 0.930 -> 0.939 is 0.009, which is INSIDE the range a single real design
change can move and OUTSIDE anything recombining the mounted pool has ever produced (every board entry
this project has fired sits in 0.927-0.930, a 0.003 band across wildly different member sets). The
recombination lane is priced by this table as worth at most a third of one place.

2026-08-22 08:52Z RE-READ, 37 h after the 08-20 fetch. THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT.

This bead was filed on the fear that "the frontier moves +0.015/wk against our +0.005/wk and the gap is
WIDENING". Verified across 37 hours:

  top      0.952 -> 0.952   SAME TEAM, SAME SCORE, +0.000
  2nd      0.947 -> 0.947
  0.946    x2    -> x2
  0.945    x1    -> x3
  0.943    x2    -> x5

The frontier is FLAT and the pack is THICKENING. That is a saturating leader with the field converging up
into it, not a receding target. The +0.015/wk figure came from differencing a 08-13 reading against an
unverified user report of ~0.957; the verified 08-20 read already corrected it to 0.952 and this read
confirms 0.952 holds.

CONSEQUENCE FOR RANK, and it inverts the usual reading: with five teams tied at 0.943 and three at 0.945,
places are now cheaper to LOSE than to GAIN. A 0.003 move buys nothing where the board is that dense.

OUR SIDE, fetched the same minute (kaggle competitions submissions):
  sixstrong 0.930 | sixfresh 0.931 | sevengrade 0.931 | sixfresh v2 0.931 | sevenplane 0.932

FIVE ENTRIES, WILDLY DIFFERENT MEMBER SETS, A 0.002 BAND. The recombination lane is not merely priced at
"a third of a place" as this bead estimated on two points -- it is now measured on five, and the spread is
0.002 against a 0.011 gap to the 0.943 cluster. Recombination cannot close it by a factor of five.

SLOT DECISION FOR 2026-08-22, and it deliberately does NOT spend the remaining three. The standing
instruction is to pace submissions and complete the day's slots; firing three more recombination entries
priced by six data points at ~0.001 each is flooding, not pacing. The slots are HELD for the one thing
that could move 0.011 -- a member from a family the roster does not contain (knee-jucq, the volume-first
trunk), which is vjepa_warm, on the card now and reading ~09:23Z. If it clears its band the slots have a
use; if it ties, the honest move is to leave them unspent rather than buy a sixth point on a saturated
lane. An unspent slot costs nothing; a spent one costs the arbitration it could have carried tomorrow.

title: DeviceBudget cap was encoder-blind and killed v3base_band
description: GB_PER_SLICE=1.335 was fitted on variant small (dim 384, patch 14) and needed() scaled only by slice count and pixel size. v3base_band (20 slices, --train-size 224, --variant v3base = dim 768 patch 16) derived exactly 1.335*21*(224/336)^2+0.22 = 12.68 GB and died in seconds with 'Tried to allocate 848.00 MiB ... 12.68 GiB allowed' while 17.51 GiB of the card was free. Same class as knee-ylp0 (train_size vs image_size), one axis further along. Fix: FITTED_PATCH/FITTED_DIM constants, patch+dim fields on DeviceBudget, needed() scales by token count (size/patch)^2 and feature width dim/FITTED_DIM; both construction sites (train.py, arm_check.overstated) resolve ENCODERS[variant]. Verified every DINOv2 arm is numerically unchanged; only v3 arms move (v3base 224x20: 12.68 -> 19.3). Re-queue v3base_band so the new cap gets a real test.
close_reason: Fixed in 9c33422: FITTED_PATCH/FITTED_DIM constants, patch+dim fields on DeviceBudget, needed() scales by token count and feature width, both construction sites resolve ENCODERS[variant]. test_needed_reads_the_encoder pins that every DINOv2 arm is byte-identical and that the v3base 224x20 cap clears the 12.68 that OOMed (19.30). v3base_band re-queued behind headlr_dense, watcher pid 108689 - that run is the real test.

title: A queue watcher dies with the session that launched it, and nothing notices until the card is idle
description: Measured 2026-08-20 06:22Z. aug_long finished and wrote its ARM DONE marker, and the card then sat at 5 percent for about five minutes because the after.sh watcher gating on that marker no longer existed. ps showed exactly one after.sh alive (the headlr one launched this session, PPID 1); the three older watchers for v3base_band, aprior_dense and rank0_dense - launched in a session that has since ended - were gone. Their log files still say 'waiting for ARM DONE ...' forever, which is the trap: the queue LOOKS armed. nohup gives PPID 1 but does not survive whatever ends the harness shell here. Recovered by relaunching one chained after.sh over all three arms; the marker was already present so v3base_band started immediately. WHAT IS MISSING is a check that answers 'is every queued arm still gated by a live process', in the family of arm_check/ledger_check. Cheapest form: read the after_*.log headers for the arm each claims to be waiting on, cross them against ps for a live after.sh with that marker in its argv, and report any arm whose watcher is dead. Second, progress.py already knows when nothing is producing - an idle card with arms still queued is exactly the state it could name in one line instead of leaving it to a manual nvidia-smi.
close_reason: Built as kneemri/experiments/queue_check.py in 84993e3. Crosses the after_*.log headers against ps -ef: an arm is stranded when its watcher log says it has not started and no live after.sh carries that marker in its argv. Reports stranded ARMS, not watches, because recovery relaunches a chain over the arms; an arm anyone has announced counts as covered, which the first live run earned when aprior_dense was training and a dead log still claimed it. Ten unit tests, listing injected so the crossing is pure. Added to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as the eighth check.

title: final_fit.sh, the deliverable, is written against the pre-settlement operating point and its central geometry argument is now INVERTED
description:
Found by knee-aixw's enumeration on 2026-08-20. This is that bead's failure mode in the highest-stakes place it can occur: final_fit.sh runs with --fold -1, so NO STUDY IS HELD OUT, there is no score, and train.py keeps the last epoch by construction. A regression here ships unseen. The script's own header says 'EVERY CHOICE HERE IS NOW THE ONE THAT SURVIVED', and that sentence was true when written.

RESOLVED THE SCRIPT'S EFFECTIVE CONFIG BY PARSING ITS ACTUAL ARGV rather than reading its comments. final_fit.sh names neither --slices nor --band-low/--band-high, so it takes the parser defaults:

    slices     12     settled recipe: 20
    band       0.2-0.8    settled recipe: 0.10-0.90
    image_size 448 / train_size 392
    ema        True

The band widening paid +0.0039 and the ledger describes it as 'already in the recipe every arm inherits'. final_fit.sh does NOT inherit it: band and slices are per-arm flags, not part of RECIPE, and this script names neither.

THE GEOMETRY ARGUMENT IS INVERTED, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. The header builds the whole 448/392 choice on res392 = 0.8523, 'our best single member' and 'the one coverage lever that whole-stack does not already contain', concluding that 'fitting the deliverable at 336 would ship a model measurably worse than a member we already have'. Read against the champion as it stands today:

    band_dense_s2026            img=336 slices=20 band=0.1-0.9   0.8578
    calib_span_s2026            img=336 slices=12 band=0.1-0.9
    band_span_s2026             img=336 slices=12 band=0.1-0.9
    depth_regions_narrow_s2026  img=336 slices=12 band=0.2-0.8

ALL FOUR MEMBERS OF THE 0.930 CHAMPION ARE 336 px. res392 is in none of them and no longer has a metrics file on disk. The best single member this project has is band_dense at 336 px and 0.8578, which BEATS the 392 px member the deliverable is built around by +0.0055. The sentence the geometry rests on is now false in its own terms.

SECONDARY, both real and both smaller:
  - --ema is justified by exactly one measurement, weight_average at +0.0003 against wsfold0_e6 - flat, and taken at the pre-settlement operating point. It is the only one of knee-aixw's six stale rows with a live consumer, and this script is that consumer. The argument FOR it (no holdout, so no best-epoch selection to fall back on) is sound independently of the number, so this is 'the number is stale', not 'the flag is wrong'.
  - The script hardcodes '--one-cycle --weight-floor --rank-weight 1.0' instead of sourcing RECIPE. That is precisely the copy-paste drift recipe.sh was created to remove, and its own header cites knee-7tq needing FOUR corrections for it. This is the arm that would ship, and it is the one still doing it.

DO NOT JUST ADD THE FLAGS. 392 px with 20 slices at band 0.10-0.90 is a configuration NOBODY HAS RUN, and the script's own header forbids exactly that: 'a deliverable is the wrong place to run an experiment: with --fold -1 there is no score, so a regression would ship unseen.' VRAM is a second reason to be careful - the measured 1.335 GB/slice + 0.22 rule puts 20 slices near 27 GB at 336 px, and 392 px is more.

THE OPTIONS, and choosing between them is a design call:
  (a) Re-base onto band_dense exactly: 336 px, slices 20, band 0.10-0.90, 4e-5. Ships the configuration that actually scored best, changes nothing unmeasured, and drops the 392 px argument that no longer holds. Cheapest and most defensible.
  (b) Keep 392 px and measure the missing pair first (392 with slices 20 / band 0.10-0.90 on fold 0), then ship whichever wins. Costs a card slot but is the only path that keeps the coverage lever without shipping an unrun config.
  (c) Ship 392 px as written. Requires believing res392's +0.0066 survives an operating point that has since moved twice, which is the exact belief knee-aixw exists to distrust.

Recommend (a) unless a slot is spent on (b) first. NOT EDITED UNILATERALLY: the deliverable's geometry is a decision, not a typo.
notes:
2026-08-20: the SAFE half is done in 7f1b9c1 -- final_fit.sh now sources $RECIPE instead of holding a private copy of --one-cycle --weight-floor --rank-weight 1.0 (verified config-identical by parsing both argv forms), and its header carries the audit plus a DO NOT RUN marker. The GEOMETRY half stays open and needs a decision: (a) re-base onto band_dense exactly (336 px, 20 slices, band 0.10-0.90), (b) measure 392 px at the settled band on fold 0 first, then ship what scores, or (c) ship as written. Recommend (a). Not edited here on purpose: naming the missing flags at the current 392/448 would ship 392 px x 20 slices x 0.10-0.90, which nobody has run, and with --fold -1 there is no holdout to catch a regression.
2026-08-22, half_data PRICES this bead. Halving the training studies costs ~0.019 net of the schedule confound, a slope of ~0.020 per doubling. final_fit.sh's --fold -1 is the only path that collects the ~80% -> 100% step, worth ~+0.0064 by that slope (0.32 of a doubling). So the misconfiguration recorded here is not tidiness: it spends the single free data gain this project has on the parser defaults (12 slices at 0.20-0.80) instead of the settled recipe (20 at 0.10-0.90), on the one run with no holdout to notice. Fixing it is now worth a known number rather than an argument.
REPRICED by knee-krnd. The 80->100% step is 0.32 of a doubling on a CONCAVE curve, so ~+0.0029 rather than the ~+0.0064 half_data's log-linear fit gave it. Still worth fixing — final_fit.sh naming neither --slices nor the band means the DELIVERABLE runs 12 slices at 0.20-0.80 instead of the settled 20 at 0.10-0.90, which is a bug in the shipped path rather than an experiment — but the data gain it collects is knob-sized and must be reported as directional.
DECIDED 2026-08-22: option (a). final_fit.sh is re-based onto band_dense exactly — 336 px, --slices 20, --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9, --backbone-lr 4e-5 — and the 448/392 argument is removed from its header. Option (b) (measure 392 at the settled band on fold 0 first) was priced and refused: 448 px exists on disk at TWELVE slices only (images_448px_12sl.npy), so 392 x 20 slices x 0.10-0.90 needs a fresh ~106 GB cache built before its first step, turning a 40-minute measurement into over an hour, to decide a question the resolution axis has already measured flat twice at 336 — for a member gain that would sit under the bar even if res392's +0.0066 transferred whole. The coverage lever is NOT discarded, it is left re-testable and becomes worth a slot again if a 448 cache gets cheap or resolution looks live at 336. Smoked at --studies 60 --epochs 1 --fold -1: parses, 27.01 GB peak inside the 28.3 GB cap, 18 s. The DO NOT RUN marker is lifted; both defects the audit named are fixed. Data gain collected by --fold -1 is ~+0.0029 (knee-krnd's concave slope), directional.

title: The offline seat ruler saturates above ~0.868 — six board points now say so
description:
MEASURED across six entries pairing an offline joint-holdout score with a board score: 0.8648/0.928, 0.8653/0.928, 0.8661/0.927, 0.8670/0.929, 0.8679/0.930, 0.8691/0.930. The chain rises over the first 0.003 of offline spread and then stops responding over the next 0.0012. Combined with seat_value's sweep of all 56 same-split checkpoints — exactly three positive seats against greedy4_v1, largest +0.0012 (just spent, tie), second +0.0002 — the working conclusion is that the ruler tracks the board while offline gaps are LARGE relative to the board's one-tick resolution and saturates once they are not.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN JUST WRITTEN UP: it changes what an arm has to clear to be worth a slot. A candidate that prices at +0.0002 in the seat is not a submission even though the ruler says it is the best remaining move, because the ruler has been shown not to resolve at that scale. The bar for spending a slot is now a member from an axis the pool does not contain, not the pool's argmax.

WHAT WOULD REFUTE IT: a future entry whose offline gain is under 0.0015 and which moves the board a tick. That would say the plateau is two points of noise rather than saturation. Two points is a thin basis for a claim this load-bearing and the issue should stay open until a third lands on either side.
notes:
2026-08-24: the missing anchor is BUILT and needs no GPU. record_mix over the 28 packaged members, seven weakest solos (0.8215-0.8462) => joint 0.8562, which is 0.0086 below the chain floor 0.8648: 2x the chain's total range, 3x its span, and the furthest a point can sit with every member still rebuildable from comp/members.roster. Count (7) and vote (RankAverage) held fixed so only quality moves - a 1-2 member entry reaches 0.8512-0.8636 but changes vote WIDTH, which confounds the reading. Kernel comp/kernels/kneemri-weakseven carries the pre-registration: 4.67 slope predicts 0.885-0.890, slope ~1-2 predicts 0.905-0.920, indifference predicts >0.925. mount/kit/champion checks all green. Awaiting a slot.
2026-08-24 REFRAMING — this is no longer a housekeeping bead, it GATES the remaining plan. Audit of the ledger for the 0.016 gap to 0.950 found every offline family already closed: slice aggregation saturated from three directions (more slices -0.0001, more slots +0.0002, four combining rules span 0.0019); decode/head four consecutive knobs returning nothing (-0.0009, -0.0044, +0.0014, -0.0021); SSL-as-init five collapses; backbone size inverted (v3base_dense 0.8455 and dinov3_base_lora 0.8268 BELOW small-based band_dense 0.8578); resolution flat (res392 0.8459-0.8523); slice order slightly costly; and ensemble WIDTH saturated too (greedy peaks 0.8719 at 9-11 members against the champion seven's 0.8716, +0.0003). Offline sits at ~0.872 whichever direction it is pushed, and the board sits at 0.934 against a 0.950 goal. So the decisive question is not which lever to pull next but WHAT AN OFFLINE POINT IS WORTH: at the recorded slope 4.67, board 0.950 needs offline ~0.875, which nothing in this saturated space reaches, and the whole member-search axis is dead by arithmetic. At slope ~1 the offline holdout is simply a poor guide above 0.868 and board gains must be sought where the holdout cannot see them. Those two readings imply OPPOSITE plans, and they are separated by one unfired submission that costs no GPU. kneemri-weakseven (offline 0.8562, v1 pushed and running) is that submission.
2026-08-24 07:14Z RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT. weakseven (submission 55734428) read 0.908, inside the pre-registered 0.905-0.920 band. board_transfer refits to +2.14 board points per holdout point over 12 entries; hand arithmetic on the two anchor pairs gives 1.97 and 2.21. The recorded 4.67 was a slope through noise (six pairs spanning 0.0043 offline against a 0.0062 floor) and is retired.

THE BEAD'S OWN FRAMING NEEDS ONE CORRECTION. It was filed as 'the ruler SATURATES above ~0.868'. That is not what happened.
