  base_dense_ff    -> base_dense_s2026     ok 0.00908 of 0.0312, 5 of 12 labels
  lr4e-5_ws_ff     -> lr4e-5_ws_s2026      ok 0.00219 of 0.0312, 5 of 12 labels
  through_dense_ff -> through_dense_s2026  ok 0.01    of 0.0312, 6 of 12 labels
  final_ws_e12     -> grade_ladder_s2026   (same row; differs only in ema)

All five residuals spread across 4-8 of 12 labels, which is the arithmetic shape rather than the concentrated shape every real reading defect produced.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT BUY. A witness pass on config C proves the SERVING PATH reads config C the way training did, and every defect this check has ever caught was a consumer-side default disagreeing with a recorded value — which is a property of the config and the code, not of the weights. So the transfer covers exactly that defect class, and it is what licenses reading the pending allfit score as a fact about the all-data axis rather than about plumbing. It does NOT prove anything about the _ff weights themselves.

The real backfill (replay trainer.predict over 8 studies through a RunSetup rebuilt from the checkpoint recipe, compare against the serving path) is still worth building if a future entry seats an unwitnessed member whose config has NO witnessed twin. It was not built here because reconstructing the training path by hand risks a FALSE refusal, and the twin argument closed the question for these six at a fraction of the cost.

title: Slot availability is signal, not noise: per-stratum normalisation refuted 12/12
description: Hypothesis: SlotHead renormalisation + decoded_at zero-mask make prediction LEVEL depend on which of six primary slots a study presents; if that level shift were orthogonal to the label it would inject spurious population-wide ordering, recoverable by within-stratum rank normalisation. Measured on the 909-study fold-0 holdout over the six champion seats that keep a holdout.npz, rank-averaged. Result: normalising within slot-COUNT costs -0.0091 mean AUC, within presence-PATTERN -0.0209, negative on all twelve labels under both stratifications. Inverted reading: which sequences a study was scanned with records what the ordering clinician suspected, so the level shift is NOT orthogonal to the label and the ensemble already exploits it. Full account in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_slot_availability_is_signal.md, including the harness bug (continuous truth summed as a count, AUCs out of [0,1]) and the reconstruction check that licensed the numbers (0.8693 vs the champion's recorded 0.8694). Live descendant: whether the ensemble captures ALL the protocol signal or only part — fit a per-pattern per-label prior and ask whether blending moves the holdout. Card-free.

title: Serving reads all geometry from the member's own config, not a kernel literal — audited, and the residual hazard is an EDIT to a default
description:
Ported from a peer project's defect: their kernel pins the decode grid as a literal, so a checkpoint trained at another grid mounts clean and decodes wrong with no raise. Audited whether the same shape exists here. It does not, and the audit is recorded so nobody pays for it twice.

FINDING 1 — NO KERNEL-SIDE GEOMETRY LITERAL. A kernel script passes member names and 'overlap' and nothing else; KernelRun.__init__ (kernel_run.py:37-57) has no size/slices/band/pool parameter. Every geometry value is read from the member's own checkpoint config, which is copied wholesale into the manifest (package_members.py:69) and back out (members.py:505). So roster heterogeneity — 20 slices beside 12, band 0.10-0.90 beside 0.20-0.80 — is correct by construction rather than a hazard.

FINDING 2 — THE SHIPPED SEVEN ARE CLEAN. Checked every checkpoint on disk for key presence. The shipped seven carry every geometry key; the only absences are 'through_plane' and 'slice_regions', whose defaults (off, 1) are what the code did before those keys existed. So no shipped member is served off-grid.

FINDING 3 — greedy7 IS NOT PLUMBING. Its +0.0018 offline -> +0.000 board was the one inversion in an otherwise zero-inversion transfer, and this defect class was a candidate explanation for it. It is refuted: nothing in the serve path could have served a greedy7 member off-grid. Selection overfit (+0.0033 measured over subsets) stands as the read.

FINDING 4 — WHAT I GOT WRONG, AND THE REAL RESIDUAL. I first wrote a packaging gate refusing any member whose config omits a geometry key. Run against the committed roster it refused SEVEN members (res392_ws, calibrated_targets, sliceattn, intensity392_ws, extended_ws, lora_r8_v3small_224 on centre+tie; deep24 also on whole_stack) — all false positives, zero true positives, so it was reverted rather than shipped. The reason it has no true positive is worth stating: every default was chosen to reproduce the behaviour that existed before its key did, so an absent key means the member WAS trained at the default. deep24's config confirms it directly (12 slices, band 0.2-0.8, channels pooling — pre-settlement geometry throughout).

That guarantee holds only while nobody EDITS a default. Move SLICE_BAND and every keyless member is retro-served on a band it never saw; move LEGACY_SLICES and their stacks change depth. Nothing raises, and the fingerprint is taken over read_size and group alone (members.py:658) so it is blind to slices, band, crop and pooling by construction. That is the real instance of the peer's mechanism here, and it fires on edit rather than on any checkpoint now on disk.

DONE: a pin test in tests/unit/kneemri/inference/members.py asserts the eight default values with the argument attached, so changing one fails a test that explains what it retro-breaks. Zero false positives, catches the actual mechanism.

title: Serve-path routing asymmetry: training never routes, serving always does
description: TRAIN reads a memmap cache routed ONCE offline over train_series.csv (fitting.py, options.py, pretrain.py, trainer.py all consume CachedCorpus/StudyCache; no training module imports Study or SlotScheme). The Kaggle kernel routes EVERY hidden-test study live through core/data/corpus/slots.py predicates (submission.py:144-166). Five hazards sit on that seam. THREE ARE NOW EMPIRICALLY CLOSED: (1) plane vocabulary is closed and clean -- exactly {Sagittal,Coronal,Axial}, zero NaN, exact match to the slot predicates, on train_series.csv (24,371 rows) and test_series.csv (15 rows), so the silent-unroute hazard does not fire on any data we can see; (2) the duplicated plane lookups (study_cache.py:420-424 vs submission.py:328-331) are IDENTICAL -- 24,371 rows each, 0 mismatches, so drift is latent not live; (3) hidden-test fill is unmeasurable by construction -- test_series.csv is 2,213 bytes, the public sample. The FOURTH -- the serve path measured nothing -- is closed by SlotFill (commit 2db2389): per-slot fill and empty-study count now logged on every served split, with a legislated 5% zero-slot ceiling that refuses above FILL_WITNESS_FLOOR=100 studies. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: the two lookups should share one home rather than stay two identical copies, and there is no assertion tying the serve-time scheme to the scheme its members were CACHED under.

title: Lateral OA, PF OA, Baker's and Fracture have NO published comparator - our 0.7099 on Lateral OA is unpriceable
description:
A frontier sweep on 2026-08-23 found no published AUC for: compartment-specific (medial/lateral/patellofemoral) OA detection on MRI (located OAI/MOST work reports Dice/IoU or PF-OA incidence, not detection AUC); Baker's/popliteal cyst detection (nearest: SE-YOLOv5 cyst mAP 0.942); knee fracture on MRI (all located AUC figures are radiograph-based).

Consequence: Lateral OA at 0.7099 is our second-lowest annotation-ruler number and we cannot tell whether that is a large deficit or near the ceiling of a genuinely hard task. Same for PF OA at 0.8005. Together these two labels are 1/6 of the metric and are currently unpriceable, which means knee-9707's +0.025 ceiling is a LOWER bound on available headroom, not an upper one.

Cheapest way to price them: an internal oracle rather than a literature number - e.g. what does a model trained on Lateral OA alone reach, or what is the inter-annotator agreement on compartment OA in our own 58 annotated studies. Do not spend card time on this before knee-9707.

Source: research/2026-08-23_published-per-label-auc-vs-ours.md

title: Two live jobs on one card: queue_check guards watchers, nothing guards the card
description:
On 2026-08-23 two identical member_curve scans ran concurrently on the same GPU for 25 minutes (pids 40228/51260 at 13:22:33 and 52524/43408 at 13:23:26, same 15 checkpoints, same cache dir). A nohup relaunch landed on top of a job that had NOT failed; the launcher's own exit told me nothing, which is the documented nohup hole.

The cost was not only the wasted card. The contention made base_dense take 11 minutes instead of ~3, and I was one step from recording 'the DINOv2-base member is slow' as a fact about the member. A harness fault wearing a measurement's clothes -- exactly the class CLAUDE.md says to suspect first.

queue_check already blocks the symmetric holes for WATCHERS (zero watchers owing an arm, two watchers owing one arm). The card has no equivalent: nothing asks 'is a training or scoring job already holding the GPU?' before a launch.

Proposed: a card_check (or a flag on queue_check) that reads the process table for python.exe under this repo's venv running a card-taking module, and refuses/warns on a second. Cheap: one Win32_Process query. Should be in the eight-checks list in CLAUDE.md, which is where every other already-happened failure is written down.
notes:
BUILT 2026-08-23 as kneemri/experiments/card_check.py, and NOT the way this bead proposed. The bead
said "read the process table for python.exe under this repo's venv running a card-taking module" --
that needs a maintained list of which modules take the card, which is wrong the first time an arm is
renamed and wrong the other way for `member_curve --device cpu` (reads like a card job, takes no card).
It asks the DEVICE instead. nvidia-smi reports the pids actually computing; the process table is used
only to NAME them. Blocks on two of OURS; a biohub job is reported as shared, not as a fault.

THREE DRIVER DEFECTS FOUND ON FIRST LIVE RUN, each already coded around wrongly:
1. `--query-compute-apps` is not the compute apps. On this Windows display driver it answered with 31
   processes including explorer.exe and two Firefoxes. Only the plain table's `Type` column separates
   `C` from `C+G`, and that field exists in no CSV query -- so the human table is what gets parsed.
2. Per-process memory is `[N/A]` for every process, in both the CSV query and the plain table. Not a
   permission problem; the display driver does not account per client. The check reports the DEVICE
   total and never a per-process figure -- a column of zeroes would have read as an idle card.
3. nvidia-smi's own `process_name` is WRONG. It named our training pid 55356
   `...User\miniconda3\python.exe` while Win32_Process had the same pid as `...\.venv-arm\Scripts\
   python.exe`. Deciding ours/theirs on the driver's name would have filed our own job under biohub's.
Plus a fourth, mine: `Type.startswith("C")` is true of `C+G`, which is 24 false holders.

Shared vocabulary extracted to kneemri/process_table.py (Probe/PROBES/listing/parentage/command), since
queue_check and card_check both cross something against the process table. Note the two pid namespaces:
nvidia-smi gives Windows pids, MSYS `ps -ef` gives MSYS ones, so crossing against the wrong probe yields
a confident empty answer. Resolved without an OS branch -- each probe is scored by how many of the
driver's pids it names, best wins.

title: Residual distance: bake it into seat_value only if twinswap confirms it
description:
MemberDistance's nearest-neighbour column correlates with solo score at pearson 0.890 over 23 same-split checkpoints, so ~79% of its variance is quality, not distance. Its docstring's argument that it cannot restate a quality reading (it never opens the label table) covers the truth vector and not the predictions -- a weaker member's ordering is noisier and decorrelates from everything.

The correction is nearest = 2.270 * solo - 1.038, residual sd 0.0133, and it reorders the pool sharply: lr4e-5_ws goes from mid-pack to the most redundant SEATED member (+0.0173), aug_long to second most distant unseated for its strength (-0.0134).

DO NOT BAKE IT IN YET, for a stated reason: the residual INVERTS the single paired board observation MemberDistance was built to reproduce (lr4e-5_ws 0.931 over band_span 0.930 -- raw says lr4e-5_ws is more distant, residual says it is more redundant). Correcting the confound costs the ruler its only supporting case. Neither form orders the three tested sevenths.

WHERE IT GOES IF IT SURVIVES: seat_value, not member_distance. The residual needs a solo score and MemberDistance's label-free invariant is load-bearing; seat_value already holds both rulers and is where they are printed together.

GATED ON: kneemri-twinswap (built, comp/kernels/kneemri-twinswap, NOT fired). Above 0.932 supports the residual; below 0.932 refutes the subtraction side of the twin claim and says the raw column was the better ruler.

title: DeviceBudget over-reserves 1.84x for a tubelet trunk (22219 MiB gated, 12.10 GB peak)
description:
MEASURED on vjepa_member, 2026-08-22. The gate line reads 'this recipe reserves 22219 MiB' (21.7 GB, the derivation knee-2nxh corrected). The run's own report two epochs in: 'peak memory 12.10 GB reserved, 10.47 GB allocated'. The derivation is 1.84x the truth on this trunk.

WHY IT LIKELY OVERSHOOTS. knee-kwdh made the cap read the encoder rather than the recipe, and knee-2nxh fixed the tubelet DIRECTION (a token spanning two slices HALVES the per-slice unit count). Both landed. What is left is that the tubelet halving is applied to token COUNT but the activation estimate behind it was fitted on a 2D trunk's per-slice residual stream, which a volumetric trunk does not have one of per slice.

WHAT IT COSTS. Not an OOM and not a crash — it is throughput left on the floor. At 12.10 GB actual on a 31.8 GB card this arm could have run roughly double the batch, or more slices, at the same wall-clock risk. vjepa_member takes ~16 min/epoch (1027s then 939s measured); halving that is over an hour on a 12-epoch arm, and every future 3D-trunk arm pays the same tax.

NOT URGENT AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED MID-ARM: changing the budget would change the batch, which is a second variable on the one arm whose whole point is a clean read of pretraining domain. Fix after vjepa_member reads.

DENOMINATOR NOTE: one trunk, one recipe. This says the derivation is wrong FOR A TUBELET TRUNK. It says nothing about the 2D path, where the same derivation has gated every member on the leaderboard without incident.
notes:
2026-08-25: PARTIAL FIX LANDED (7218a24), bead stays open on the residual.

The bead's own hypothesis was REFUTED by reading backbone.py: `Encoder.activation_units` already sums per-stage with each stage's own stride and width, so it does NOT price a downsampling trunk at its widest point. The real defect was the COMPOSITION in `DeviceBudget.needed()` — a whole-trunk activation sum multiplied by a scalar in the block COUNT, which prices the open suffix at the trunk's AVERAGE block. Exact on a 12-deep ViT, wrong on the two trunks that are not ViTs.

Fixed by splitting the activation term in two (forward-all + retain-open) with NO new constant: RETAINED_WEIGHT = TRAINABLE_PER_BLOCK * FITTED_DEPTH is the same affine fit expressed per unit.

Measured (budget_residuals, 74 priceable of 104):
  cnx_dense_s2026       -49.1% -> -35.9%  (derived 20.59 -> 16.36)
  cnx_own_recipe_s2026  -49.9% -> -37.2%  (derived 16.92 -> 13.49)
  vjepa_member_s2026    -42.1% -> -35.5%  (derived 20.91 -> 18.76)
No ViT row moved; refusals still the same two (knee-dmp4's encoder_layer_9, v3base_dense).

HONEST SCOPE: ConvNeXt needs x0.51 and V-JEPA x0.58 to reach measured peak; this delivers x0.79 and x0.90 — ~22% and ~14% of the gaps. The residual (~1.56x over on ConvNeXt, ~1.55x on V-JEPA) is STILL UNEXPLAINED and is what this bead now owns. Both remaining over-derivers are non-ViT and both land near the same 1.55x, which is a lead: a factor common to convolution/tubelet trunks rather than two separate errors. Candidates not yet tested: channels-last/conv workspace vs attention, activation checkpointing on the timm trunk, or the per-slice unit simply not being the right currency for a conv feature map.

Two separate bugs found and fixed in the same change:
- cnxbase.depth = 12 (dataclass default, meaningless once stages given) against 36 real blocks. run_setup clamped unfreeze_last against it, so a fully-open ConvNeXt retained 12 of 36. Clamp moved into Encoder.retained_units.
- arm_check hand-built its DeviceBudget without the trainable term, silently pricing every arm at six blocks open. Now routes through RunSetup(options).budget().

title: poll_scores.sh reports ALL RESOLVED while a submission is still PENDING
description: comp/poll_scores.sh exited at poll 1 with 'ALL RESOLVED' at 2026-08-22 02:45 while submission 55681546 (sevenplane) was listed in its own output as SubmissionStatus.PENDING with an empty publicScore. The exit condition is therefore not 'no PENDING rows' -- it is matching something else (most likely it only inspects rows it recognises, or it treats an empty score column as resolved). The cost is silent: the poller is the tool that frees the session from watching the board, so a false ALL RESOLVED means a slot's answer is never read and the next slot gets fired without it. Fix the predicate to be 'no row has status PENDING', and make the success line name which submissions it resolved so a false positive is visible in the log rather than inferred.
close_reason: Fixed in 441b3cf. Root cause: the exit test read grep -q "pending" against a CLI that prints SubmissionStatus.PENDING, so it matched nothing and every launch announced ALL RESOLVED at poll 1. Proven on the exact failing board (sevenplane 55681546 PENDING): the poller now reaches POLL CAP instead of claiming resolution. Also collapsed two API queries per poll into one — they could disagree, and the printed one was not the one the exit decision used — and the success line now names which submissions resolved.

title: Price the data slope with a 25% point -- one point cannot locate the knee
description:
half_data measured 50% of the training studies at 0.8344 against band_dense's 0.8578 (100%), a raw -0.0234 and ~0.019 net of the registered schedule confound. That is ONE point, and the arm said in advance that one point separates 'flat' from 'steep' and cannot say where the knee is. Every downstream price -- MRNet at ~+0.0095, a full doubling at ~+0.020, the final_fit 80->100% step at ~+0.0064 -- is a LOG-LINEAR EXTRAPOLATION from a single interval, and each of those numbers is currently deciding what gets built.

MEASUREMENT: band_dense's recipe at --train-fraction 0.25, everything else identical, read against the same holdout. Three points (25/50/100) fit a slope instead of assuming one.

PRICE: ~18 min of card (half_data ran 204 s an epoch on 50%; 25% is ~110 s, 12 epochs).

P(clears 1.5%) = 0, DECLARED. It is an INSTRUMENT and must be justified as one. What it buys: whether the curve is still steep at our operating point (in which case external data is priced correctly and knee-ombx's schedule stands) or already flattening (in which case ~0.020 per doubling is an OVERESTIMATE at 3,526 studies, MRNet's ~+0.0095 falls further, and the data axis is worth less than the one point suggests). Both branches change what the next expensive hour buys.

READ IT ON: if the 25 -> 50 interval is materially STEEPER than 50 -> 100, the curve is flattening and every extrapolation above is optimistic. If the two intervals are comparable, log-linear holds over 2 doublings and the external-data price stands as written. If 25% scores WITHIN the floor of 50%, the corpus saturates far below where we sit and the whole axis re-reads.
notes:
PRICE: ~22 minutes of card. half_data ran 204 s an epoch on 50% of the studies, so 25% is ~110 s and twelve epochs is ~22 min.

P(clears 1.5%) = 0, DECLARED. The arm is handicapped by construction and cannot produce a member. It is an INSTRUMENT and is justified as one: it decides whether the only axis measured above the bar is priced right before any expensive hour is spent on it.

Arm written: experiments/arms/quarter_data.sh. The schedule confound is charged per point -- schedule_length prices step compression at 0.0028 for 0.67x the steps, so 0.25x scales to ~0.0056-0.0096, and the three-point fit must be read on confound-corrected points rather than raw ones.
ANSWERED. 0.7907 @ e9 (25%), against 0.8344 (50%) and 0.8578 (100%). Raw intervals +0.0437 and +0.0234; confound-corrected per point (0.0097 at 25%, 0.0048 at 50%, both downward) +0.0388 and +0.0186. Ratio 2.09x — the FIRST pre-registered branch: the curve is CONCAVE, log-linear is refuted, and we sit past the steep part. Each doubling buys ~0.48 of the last, so the next doubling (the whole external-data programme) prices at ~+0.009 and ALL remaining doublings sum to ~+0.017. The correction is if anything under-priced: the arm ends at train loss 0.7113 against the control's 0.5780 on the same twelve epochs, so it UNDERFITS, and any residual under-pricing flattens the curve further. Write-up in experiments/README.md. No seat (-0.0035), as declared.

title: member_distance is unvalidated as a predictor — one paired observation constrains it
description:
MemberDistance (kneemri/evaluation/member_distance.py, printed by seat_value) reproduces the one board split it was designed from: lr4e-5_ws reads nearest 0.9143 / mean 0.8816 and took 0.931, band_span reads 0.9188 / 0.8925 and cost a tick, which is the ordering seat_value and solo score both inverted. Reproducing the designing case is not evidence.

The out-of-sample test is already registered in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md and costs nothing to collect: grade_ladder reads the LEAST distant of four candidates (0.9248), and sevengrade (55678597) was PENDING when the prediction was written. If distance is what buys a seat, sevengrade should not exceed 0.931.

The confound is recorded with it: sevengrade is a SEVENTH seat AND the first entry carrying the severity objective, so a null has two explanations and only a BEAT cleanly refutes the ruler.

WHAT IS STILL MISSING after that reads: a price. The ruler ranks and does not say how many board ticks a unit of distance buys, so no slot may be spent on this number alone. Pricing it needs paired entries that vary distance while holding count, which is expensive in slots — do not plan one until at least two more paired readings land for free.

It also reports the pool is exhausted for distance: every candidate but through_dense sits closer to a seated member (0.9143-0.9248) than the roster's own worst neighbour pair (0.8911). That is the label-free argument for the V-JEPA 2 probe (knee-jucq), independent of the board split.

title: Two prediction stores that never share: the seat test recomputes arrays training already wrote
description:
FOUND 2026-08-21 by paying for it. A band140 seat read on six members was launched as card-free gap
work on the assumption it would read the .holdout.npz files on disk. It did not: it logged
'band_dense_s2026.pt: cache MISS, computing on cpu' and began a full CPU inference pass over the 909-study
holdout. It was killed after ~33 minutes, still on the FIRST of six members, and while it ran it stole
CPU from the live band_dense_llrd arm -- epoch time went 581s -> 672s. Wall-time cost: ~35 min of my own
gap work plus ~100 s/epoch of someone else's arm, to compute numbers that already existed.

THE MECHANISM IS NOT A BUG, IT IS TWO STORES, and holdout_predictions.py:123-128 already documents it in a
comment written after an earlier instance of the same loss (two CPU subset searches killed as hung on
2026-08-19):

  * TRAINING writes <member>_s2026.holdout.npz at the best epoch. run_comparison reads these. That is why
    the grade_ladder per-label read this morning cost zero GPU and returned instantly.
  * PredictionCache is a SECOND store, keyed (file, window, precision), filled only on its own misses.
    member_curve / the seat test read this one. record_mix reads training's arrays and never fills it.

Same probabilities, two filenames, no bridge. So the choice of which analysis tool you reach for silently
decides whether the read is free or costs a GPU-hour, and nothing in either tool's interface says so.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A CACHE MISS: the seat test is the ruler that DECIDES MEMBERSHIP -- solo AUC
decides nothing here, and +0.0015 is the resolution limit. Making the deciding ruler the expensive one
and the non-deciding one free is exactly backwards, and it biases which question gets asked in a gap.

WHAT NEEDS CHECKING BEFORE ANY FIX -- do not assume the arrays correspond. Training writes its holdout at
ONE window/TTA/precision setting (its own). PredictionCache keys on (file, window, precision) precisely
because member_curve can be asked for a different window, --overlap or --tta. The two stores hold the same
numbers ONLY when member_curve's requested window and precision match what training used. So the fix is
not 'point one at the other'; it is: derive the key training's array corresponds to, and let PredictionCache
.read() satisfy a request from the training array when and only when that key matches. A wrong bridge here
would serve a differently-windowed array under a seat test and move the deciding number by construction --
worse than the recompute it saves.

INTERIM RULE, worth following even before the fix: a seat read is NOT card-free gap work. Run it on cuda
when the card is free, or not at all. Never launch one on cpu beside a live arm.

RELATED: knee-t607 (the per-label read that WAS free, via run_comparison) shows the contrast directly.

title: Read grade_ladder per-label on the OA triple — the mean AUC may be averaging the ladder's effect away
description:
grade_ladder measured -0.0013 solo and +0.0001 at its best roster seat (ledger, experiments/README.md, 2026-08-21), and was read on the TWELVE-LABEL MEAN only. A ladder over grades should bite where the labels are actually graded — the OA triple (Medial OA, Lateral OA, PF OA) — and a mean over twelve labels is exactly the denominator that would hide a real per-label move behind nine labels it cannot touch. This project has read a mean where a subset was the right denominator before.

COST: an evaluation, no training. The checkpoint is on disk at grade_ladder_s2026.pt and the control band_dense's is beside it. Minutes on the card, or CPU.

WHAT IT DECIDES: nothing about shipping — a per-label win on three labels that does not move the roster seat is still not a member. It decides whether the ORDINAL MECHANISM works at all, which is what licenses or retires the severity-target axis as a family. If the OA triple moves and the mean does not, the ladder is real and mis-aggregated; if the OA triple is flat too, the ladder is genuinely inert here and the whole target-shape axis can close, leaving only the loss-WEIGHT axis (knee-t1ho) alive.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-21, and the hypothesis is REFUTED rather than confirmed.

run_comparison, control band_dense_s2026 (0.8578 @ e8) vs grade_ladder_s2026, no card needed -- both
.holdout.npz were already on disk, so the read cost a model load of zero and a GPU-second of zero.

  Synovitis -0.0231*  ACL +0.0212*  Lateral OA -0.0115  Lateral Meniscus +0.0093  Medial OA -0.0092
  Fracture +0.0089  PF OA -0.0065  Medial Meniscus -0.0036  Contusion +0.0029  Effusion -0.0024
  Baker's -0.0019  MEAN -0.0013  MCL +0.0003
  half-widths up to +/-0.0367 on this pair's own paired floor
  by structure scale: focal +0.0000  regional -0.0031

THE OA TRIPLE IS THE WHOLE TEST and all three members of it move NEGATIVE: Medial -0.0092,
Lateral -0.0115, PF -0.0065. The bead was filed on the suspicion that a twelve-label mean was
averaging away a win on the three labels a KL-graded ladder can actually bite on. There is no win
under the mean to find. The mean was not hiding anything; it was reporting it.

Nothing here is individually resolvable -- every delta sits inside +/-0.0367 -- so the honest claim is
not 'the ladder hurt the OA labels' but 'the ladder produced no positive signal on the only labels
whose targets it changed the shape of'. A mechanism that works should at minimum point the right way
on three labels at once; three-for-three wrong-way is what an inert switch looks like.

WHICH LINK: the idea, in this use. Not plumbing (GRADE_LADDER is a Landed-compared switch and the run
passed the check), not data (same split, same cache), not the test (the ruler is the one the five
held members were selected under, and the per-label read is the finer ruler the bead asked for --
it was run and it says the same thing the coarse one did).

CLOSING ON THE PRE-REGISTERED CLAUSE: 'if the OA triple is flat too, the ladder is genuinely inert
here and the whole target-shape axis can close, leaving only the loss-WEIGHT axis (knee-t1ho) alive.'
The triple is flat-to-negative. The target-SHAPE axis is closed.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT: the severity WEIGHT axis (knee-t1ho) -- reweighting which STUDIES the
loss listens to is a different mechanism from reshaping what the target IS, and the owner has called
that axis alive by decision. It also does not rule out an ordinal target on a corpus with more graded
labels than three, or with grades that are not already collapsed to binary before we see them.

title: Volume-pretrained trunk: our encoder has never seen a 3D medical volume
description:
CoPAS child (B) of knee-pq8u. CoPAS uses ResNet3D-18 pretrained on Med3D (Chen/Ma/Zheng, arXiv:1904.00625) - a trunk whose pretraining task was 3D medical volumes, not 2D natural images. Our whole roster runs 2D-pretrained encoders over slices, with the depth axis handled downstream by the aggregator.

THE MECHANISM. A 2D encoder cannot represent a feature that only exists across slices; whatever through-plane structure matters has to be reconstructed by the aggregator from per-slice features. A volume-pretrained trunk carries it in the features themselves. That is an ARCHITECTURE-class lever, not a knob - the class the doctrine says to spend machine-time on.

WHAT IT IS NOT. This is not the same claim as knee-40wh (--through-plane) or knee-vigl (registered reformats). Those give the EXISTING 2D trunk a through-plane input; this changes what the trunk was trained to see. If through_dense moves the number, the axis is live and this is its expensive version. If through_dense is flat, that is evidence the axis is not carried by input reshaping - which does NOT refute this bead, because a 2D-pretrained trunk fed a reformatted slice is still a 2D trunk.

GATE. Do not start until through_dense (knee-40wh) is read. Not because a null there kills this, but because the reading changes the price: a live axis makes this the follow-on, a dead one makes it a from-scratch bet on pretraining alone.

PRICE. Med3D weights are small and openly released; wiring a 3D trunk into the slot pipeline is real work because our reader hands out per-slice stacks and a 3D trunk wants the volume - call it ~6h dev plus one ~1h arm. Plausible gain: this is the component CoPAS does not ablate, so we have no borrowed number for it; from the architecture-class prior, 1-2%. Odds it clears 1.5%: ~1 in 4.

RISK NAMED UP FRONT. Med3D pretraining is on CT-heavy segmentation corpora at coarse resolution; the domain gap to knee MRI may exceed the gap ImageNet has to knee MRI. A 3D trunk also costs VRAM per study in a way the 2D one does not, and knee-kwdh has just been closed on the VRAM cap - check the cap reads the encoder before arming.
notes:
2026-08-21: promoted by elimination rather than by evidence, and the warrant is labelled as such in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-21_what_survives_the_closures.md. Every other axis on the board closed (see the table there). The non-elimination part of the argument: this is the only surviving axis whose mechanism is REPRESENTATIONAL rather than routing — every closed axis changes what the model is shown or how per-slice features are combined, none changes what a feature can ENCODE. So an aggregation-stage null is exactly what a live depth signal would produce under an encoder that discarded it, which is knee-tqn's harness-suspect reading surviving its own closure. Gate through_dense (knee-40wh) reads out ~21:50 UTC and prices the SIZE, not the direction — both its branches point here, which is stated in the interpretation as the gate's weakness.
AUDIT 2026-08-21 of the actual seam, done card-free while through_dense runs, because '~6h dev plus one ~1h arm' was an estimate made without reading the code. Five findings, and two of them change the price.

1. THE PIPELINE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS AND A 3D TRUNK FITS THE EXISTING CONTRACT. model.py:351-352: 'if not per_slice: return pooled.reshape(batch, slots, 1, -1)'. The tensor contract at the aggregator is Float[b s g w], and an encoder with no per-slice axis already returns g=1, which slot_features collapses at line 290. Channel stacking ALREADY uses this path. So a volume trunk returns (b, s, 1, w) and the head, slot attention, the mask, the prior, fingerprint() and the kernel's inference contract are all untouched. This is NOT a plumbing project; that was the part I had priced highest and it is nearly free.

2. THE LOADER IS THE REAL GAP, AND IT SELECTS THE CANDIDATE. backbone.py:227 builds every trunk with AutoModel.from_pretrained(repository). Med3D's ResNet3D-18 is a raw torch state_dict, not a transformers model, so it needs a SECOND construction strategy in Encoder. A VIDEO TRANSFORMER (VideoMAE, V-JEPA) loads through the existing path UNCHANGED and takes (n, frames, c, h, w) natively. knee-tqn already gathered that prior art: V-JEPA over VideoMAE on ultrasound video, frozen-encoder gains up to 3.4% at full data and 8.35% at 10%.

3. THE CHEAP GATE IS ALREADY BUILT, AND IT IS CHEAPER THAN THIS BEAD ASSUMED. knee-tqn specified 'gate it behind a frozen-encoder probe before any fine-tuning', and kneemri/training/head_trial.py exists and is unit-tested. So the first test is an EMBEDDING PASS PLUS A HEAD FIT, not a ~1h fine-tuning arm. That is the cost-tiered proxy the doctrine asks for and it was already on disk.

4. THE VRAM CAP ALREADY GENERALISES. Encoder carries stages, depth and params_m explicitly, stated per encoder rather than counted off loaded weights precisely so the cap is derived BEFORE anything is fetched (the knee-bj90 lesson, where RESIDENT_GB fitted on a 22M trunk refused a ViT-B with nine gigabytes free). A 3D trunk states its own numbers and the cap reads them. The risk named in this bead's original text - 'check the cap reads the encoder before arming' - is already discharged by knee-kwdh.

5. NORMALISATION IS A REAL SMALL GAP. model.py:348 applies a 3-channel ImageNet mean/std. A volume trunk wants its own, and a medical one wants a different one again.

RE-PRICE. Dev is NOT ~6h. The seam is free, the cap is free, the gate is built; the work is a second trunk-construction strategy, normalisation, the flag plus its Landed witness, and the jaxtyping boundaries. Call it 2-3h to a FROZEN PROBE, which is a genuinely cheaper first read than the arm this bead priced.

THE CANDIDATE CHOICE IS A REAL TENSION AND NEITHER OPTION IS FREE. A video transformer loads for nothing but is pretrained on NATURAL video - natural-domain pretraining again, and our cautionary instance is on our own ledger: DINOv3, a STRONGER natural-image SSL encoder, scored ~0.04 WORSE than DINOv2 with the deficit in focal findings. Med3D is medical but CT-heavy, coarse, and needs the new loader. knee-tqn's own caveat is the sharpest statement of the problem: ultrasound video is genuinely TEMPORAL and MRI depth is not, so a trunk pretrained on motion may or may not transfer to a spatial axis, and nothing measured anywhere here says which. The frozen probe is cheap enough to read BOTH rather than argue about it, and that is the recommendation.
CANDIDATE SELECTED BY LICENCE AND LOADER, 2026-08-21 21:05 UTC — card-free work while through_dense runs. The 'video transformer vs Med3D' tension recorded in the audit above is DECIDED, and not by intuition.

LICENCE PICKS THE TRUNK. Queried the HF API for the four obvious video candidates:
  MCG-NJU/videomae-base                      cc-by-nc-4.0
  facebook/timesformer-base-finetuned-k400   cc-by-nc-4.0
  facebook/vjepa2-vitl-fpc64-256             mit
  microsoft/xclip-base-patch32               mit
VideoMAE and TimeSformer carry the SAME non-commercial clause that has knee-ombx blocked on an owner
decision. Choosing either would import that block into an axis that does not currently have one. V-JEPA 2
is MIT and does not. That is the selection.

THE LOADER GAP IS NOT A GAP FOR THIS CANDIDATE. transformers 5.15.0 (the pinned one, checked in .venv)
exports VJEPA2Model / VJEPA2Config, so backbone.py:227's existing AutoModel.from_pretrained path loads it
UNCHANGED. Med3D remains the one needing a second construction strategy (raw torch state_dict), on top of
its CT-domain-gap risk and an unclear licence. Med3D is not refuted — it is deselected on cost, and stays
re-testable if V-JEPA2's read is bad for a reason specific to natural video.

SUBMITTABILITY IS NOT THE GATE EITHER, which I had flagged as a possible hard block. DINOv3's mount is
'dimiturnt/dinov3-hf/vitb16' — our own dataset upload, not a vendor mirror. backbone.py's CONVNEXT_BASE
comment states the general rule already: 'that is a dataset upload, not a code change'. An MIT trunk
mirrors the same way. So the mount question is deferred work, not a block.

THE MECHANISM MATCHES THE RESIDUE EXACTLY, which is the part that raises this above 'last axis standing'.
V-JEPA2's config gives tubelet_size 2, patch_size 16, hidden 1024, 24 layers. Tubelet 2 means the trunk
emits SEVERAL depth positions (frames/2) rather than collapsing the depth window to one linear projection.
That is verbatim the residue named in the through_dense correction on knee-40wh as the thing no 2D-stem
reshaping can do at any window. The cheap arm and the expensive one are not two sizes of the same claim;
the expensive one reaches something the cheap one provably cannot.

PRICE, recomputed rather than guessed. Per slot at 12 slices: (12/2) x (256/16)^2 = 1536 tokens, against
DINOv2-small's 12 x 576 = 6912 for the same slot. 4.5x FEWER tokens offsets most of ViT-L's 13.6x
parameter count over ViT-S, and the attention term is lower too (1536^2 = 2.36M pairs vs 12 x 576^2 =
3.98M). So the embedding pass is on the order of 3x the 5.6 min DINOv2 pass quoted in head_trial.py's
docstring — call it 15-25 min, not hours. Head fit after that is seconds.

THE GATE IS ASYMMETRIC AND I AM NOT GOING TO PRETEND OTHERWISE. head_trial.py's own docstring says the
frozen proxy 'has not yet been shown to rank anything' — experiments/head_axes.jsonl holds exactly one
resolved pair. And our ledger has the counter-instance: DINOv3 is a stronger encoder that scored ~0.04
WORSE fine-tuned. So a good frozen read licenses nothing. A BAD frozen read - V-JEPA2 features far below
DINOv2's on the same head - is still worth having, because it kills a multi-hour fine-tune for 25 minutes.
Use it as a kill gate only, and do not let a green read stand in for a result.

OPEN PLUMBING RISK, to check before the pass and not after: V-JEPA2 is pretrained at 64 frames / 256 px,
and we would feed 12 frames. Whether its position handling extrapolates to a shorter clip is unverified.
If it does not, the fix is to feed 64 frames or to pad, and both change the price above.
PLUMBING RISK CHECKED AND CLOSED, 21:06 UTC, by reading transformers' modeling_vjepa2.py rather than downloading 1.2 GB to find out.

V-JEPA2 HAS NO LEARNED POSITION EMBEDDINGS. Attention applies 3D RoPE (apply_rotary_embeddings at
modeling_vjepa2.py:279), with position ids derived from the ACTUAL token count at run time
(get_position_ids reads x.size(1)) and decomposed into frame / height / width by integer division
against grid_size = crop_size // patch_size.

CONSEQUENCE 1, depth is free. frame_pos = ids // (grid_size^2), so a 12-frame clip simply produces
fewer distinct frame positions. RoPE has no parameters to interpolate, so a shorter clip than the
pretrained 64 is not an extrapolation hazard the way a learned pos_embed table would be. The 12-frame
read is legitimate. modeling_vjepa2.py:135-144 also handles num_frames < tubelet_size explicitly.

CONSEQUENCE 2, spatial is NOT free in the same way. grid_size comes from config.crop_size, so the
spatial read must be 256 px (or config.crop_size overridden to match whatever we feed, which is safe
precisely because RoPE is parameter-free). It cannot silently be our current 336 - that would decode
frame/height/width from the wrong divisor and scramble every position. This is a plumbing assert to
write, not a hope: check grid_size^2 * (frames/tubelet) == token count before trusting a pass.

THE line-531 CAVEAT IN THAT FILE IS NOT OURS. 'problematic if the config isn't initialized with the
right frames_per_clip value' sits in VJEPA2Predictor, the JEPA prediction head. We want VJEPA2Model's
encoder embeddings; the predictor is not on our path.

Net: the 15-25 min price stands, and the resolution-freedom is a real advantage over DINOv2, whose
pos_embed has to be interpolated for every non-native read.

WIRED 2026-08-21/22, card-free, CPU only. V-JEPA 2 (facebook/vjepa2-vitl-fpc64-256, MIT — VideoMAE and
TimeSformer are both cc-by-nc-4.0, so licence picked the candidate) is registered as vjepa2l and the
volume path is live end to end on CPU: (1, 2, 1, 1024) out of slice_features, the exact (b, s, 1, w)
contract finding (1) of the audit predicted. Finding (5)'s normalisation gap is discharged by reading
transformers' source rather than assuming: video_processing_vjepa2.py:23-24 uses IMAGENET_DEFAULT_MEAN/STD,
byte-identical to model.py's buffers, so no new buffer.

THE GUARD I WROTE FIRST WAS WORTHLESS AND A NEGATIVE TEST IS WHAT FOUND IT. It predicted the token count
from the input tensor's own shape and compared it to what the trunk returned — but the trunk derives its
grid from that same tensor, so the two agreed at 224 and at 240 exactly as they agreed at 256. It could
not fail. Measured: 256 -> 512 tokens, 240 -> 450, 224 -> 392, NO ERROR at any of them. So V-JEPA 2's
spatial grid is adaptive (3D RoPE, position ids from the run-time token count, no learned position table)
and the hazard is not a crash but a silent one — pretrained weights handed a grid they were never fitted
on, returning a plausible number. The guard now asserts against the CONFIG's native crop, which the input
cannot move. Consequence for the probe: READ SIZE MUST BE 256, not merely a multiple of 16.

Depth, by the same mechanism, is genuinely free: a 12-frame read of a 64-frame-pretrained trunk is an
ordinary read, not an extrapolation.

model.py crossed the 750-line god-file threshold, so the concern was split into two modules rather than
suppressed: kneemri/models/token_pooling.py (the third sibling of slice_pooling and slot_head — across
PATCH TOKENS, holding the vocabulary and the reduction, with POOL_PARTS now DERIVED from the table so the
head's built width and the forward pass's produced width cannot drift) and kneemri/models/volume_read.py
(VolumeRead: the tubelet, the two refusals, the frame fold and the guard — one fact about the trunk).
1044 tests pass.

NEXT: build_embeddings --variant vjepa2l --pool mean --read-size 256, then head_trial against a DINOv2
control. GPU work, so not before ~01:50 UTC when biohub's HOCT block ends.
2026-08-21 23:30 UTC - PLUMBING IS DONE AND THE PROBE AS SPECIFIED IS CONFOUNDED. Fix the second before spending the card.

PLUMBING (done, cde66ee): EmbeddingSpec now carries slice_read, so a volumetric cache cannot overwrite the per-slice one; build() probes the DEPTH from the model instead of taking it from corpus.slices, which is a fact about the pixels rather than the encoder. Verified end to end on CPU: vjepa2l at 256 px with pool=mean, slice_read=channels constructs and returns slice_features of shape (1, 6, 1, 1024). The flag lands, the refusal fires, the shape is depth 1. No card time was spent finding that out.

THE CONFOUND: the only embedding cache on disk is dinov2-SMALL (384-dim) and vjepa2l is a ViT-LARGE (1024-dim). Ranking one against the other measures encoder SIZE and volumetric pretraining at once, and size is the explanation that needs no new idea - so a win reads as 'large beats small', which this project already knows, and a loss reads as nothing at all. Neither outcome is about the 3D axis.

THE CONTROL THIS ARM NEEDS: a matched-capacity 2D cache at the SAME read size (256) before or beside the V-JEPA one - dinov2-base is the cheap version, dinov2-large the honest one. Encode both, rank both against the same head. The comparison is then volumetric-vs-2D at held capacity, which is the question. Budget it as two encode passes, not one.
2026-08-22 00:05 UTC: arm WRITTEN and committed (45d58b0, experiments/arms/vjepa_probe.sh), card-free. Confound removed by encoding a MATCHED-CAPACITY control rather than reusing the dinov2-small cache: dinov2-large (1024 wide, 304M) at read 252 vs vjepa2l at 256, each on the size its own patch grid tiles. Flags validated against both parsers. Volumetric path verified in model.py: slice_read=channels + a vjepa encoder takes the self.volume branch, which folds the 12-slice group in as FRAMES (volume.frames), so 12 slices become 6 tubelets rather than 3 channels. NOT controlled, on purpose: the READING is bundled with the pretraining and cannot be separated. Cost ~35 min of card (control ~21, tubelet ~5, both head fits minutes). BLOCKED only on the card, which is biohub's until ~01:50 UTC.
RESULT 2026-08-22: TIE, the pre-registered middle branch. DINOv2-large control 0.7669, V-JEPA2-large 0.7620, delta -0.0049 against a 0.0062 floor. Card 15 min against 35 priced.

Plumbing verified BEFORE the numbers were read: control cache (4407, 6, 12, 1024), V-JEPA cache (4407, 6, 1, 1024). Depth 1 is the proof the tubelet path fired -- the slice group was consumed inside the encoder as frames, not folded into channels. A depth-12 array would have made the whole arm a capacity comparison wearing a pretraining-domain label.

The tie is asymmetric. V-JEPA's latent-prediction objective has no reason to yield linearly separable features and the frozen probe is the ruler that most favours DINOv2, yet it ties -- while handing the head ONE vector per slot where the control hands it twelve to max over. Depth reduction inside the trunk with learned weights loses nothing against a max over twelve.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT: fine-tuned V-JEPA (untested; the frozen probe is a known-weak instrument for this objective, so this is evidence about the probe as much as the trunk); tubelet sizes other than 2; slice windows other than 12; V-JEPA as a seat (still licensed by the tie, just not worth the card).

WHY THE SEAT FRAMING IS RETIRED, and this is the night's real finding: the split this arm appealed to is 0.931 vs 0.930, and the whole champion progression across many seats is 0.925 -> 0.931. A seat played perfectly is worth ~one board tick against a 1.5% bar. The 119-checkpoint distance sweep agrees independently -- every working member orders the studies 0.87-0.92 alike, so there is little disagreement left to buy. Frozen probes read 0.76 and fitted members 0.85+, so fine-tuning carries ~+0.09. That is where the mass is, and it makes V-JEPA a BACKBONE question, not a seat question.

NEXT: fine-tuned V-JEPA member against a matched fine-tuned DINOv2-large, read as member quality. knee-2nxh becomes BLOCKING for it.

Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-22_vjepa_frozen_probe.md
MEASURED, and the ledger was silent about it until 2026-08-22. vjepa_probe ran a frozen-feature head trial: DINOv2-large control 0.7669, vjepa2l 0.7620, delta -0.0049 — INSIDE the 0.0062 holdout floor. The arm's own pre-registration calls that branch a TIE, explicitly not a kill.

WHY IT IS NOT A KILL, in two independent ways. (1) V-JEPA's objective is prediction in LATENT space, not linear separability, so a flat frozen probe is a known property of that objective and says nothing about the trunk with its blocks opened. (2) The probe read it through a THREE-slice window — one and a half tubelets — because Trainer.whole_stack was unarmable for a volumetric read until StudyModel.check_whole_stack landed the same day. So the trunk's only advantage over a 2D ViT-L was spent on a window too narrow to carry it.

CAPACITY IS NOT THE CONFOUND: the control is DINOv2-LARGE (1024 wide, 24 blocks, 304M) against vjepa2l's 326M, chosen so the surviving difference is pretraining DOMAIN. 252 vs 256 px because patch 14 cannot tile 256 and patch 16 was fitted at it; forcing either onto the other's grid means interpolated position embeddings.

Note this bead is about Med3D/ResNet3D specifically; V-JEPA2 is the same axis reached with a trunk already in the registry, at zero wiring cost. The fitted re-test is knee-rpkw (experiments/arms/vjepa_member.sh, priced there). Read that before spending 6h wiring Med3D — if volume pretraining is flat at this data scale with a free trunk, it will be flat with an expensive one.

title: Our crop is IMAGE-centred, never ANATOMY-centred — the +0.056 component of CoPAS, and 107 runs have never tried it
description:
Child of knee-pq8u, and on the ablation numbers the highest-ratio item on the whole board. P0 because it
is the largest externally-measured lever we have, it needs no external data, no licence decision, and its
cheapest version needs no model at all.

THE EXTERNAL NUMBER. CoPAS Table 10: removing the ROI crop takes their mean AUC from 0.781 to 0.725.
+0.056 - the largest single component in that paper, larger than the cross-plane attention it is famous
for, and 3.7x our 1.5% bar. Their explanation, quoted: "cropping along ROI can align the spatial position
across sequences". They find the ROI with a U-Net meniscus segmentation, crop 448x448 around it, then
resize to 224x224.

WHAT WE ACTUALLY DO, from the audit (not a grep - anatomy.py, model.py, slot_reader.py, crop_coverage.py
and the crop80_span / aprior_dense ledger rows):
1. Our crop is a FIXED 130 mm box CENTRED ON THE IMAGE, via SlotReader.window. Nothing about it is
   content-adaptive. If the knee sits off-centre in the frame - and across five vendors, five field
   strengths and twelve countries it will - we crop the wrong tissue, and we crop DIFFERENTLY WRONG in
   every slot, which is precisely the cross-sequence misalignment CoPAS's ROI removes.
2. `--anatomical-prior` IS NOT A CROP. It warm-starts SlotHead.prior from a 12x6 plane-by-finding table
   at PRIOR_STRENGTH 2.0. That is 72 numbers on an nn.Parameter, it measured -0.0021, and the ledger's
   own mechanism read is that the warm start WASHED OUT (train loss tracked the control to four decimals
   at every epoch). It has nothing to do with where the pixels come from. The name has been hiding the
   gap: the repo has an "anatomical" switch and has never once cropped to anatomy.
3. So in 107 recorded runs the crop CENTRE has never been a variable. crop80_span moved the crop WIDTH
   in (130 -> 80, costing MCL -0.0265* and ACL -0.0263*); knee-7zw7 tried to move it OUT and its own
   proxy refuted the premise (only 19.6% of series even reach 170 mm). Both arms moved the SIZE of an
   image-centred box. Neither moved the box.

WHY THE crop80 AND knee-7zw7 EVIDENCE ARGUES *FOR* THIS RATHER THAN AGAINST IT. crop80's losses were
"exactly the structures at the field's margins" - MCL medial, ACL central-but-oblique, Baker's
posterior. A margin structure is lost when the box is off-centre for exactly the same reason it is lost
when the box is too small, and knee-7zw7's proxy measured the damage without naming the cause: median
retention 0.8495 but p10 0.7299 and worst 0.4537. A fixed box that is correctly placed does not have a
tenth of its corpus at 0.73 retention. That spread IS the centring error, measured, already in the repo.

CHEAP FIRST VERSION - NO MODEL, NO SEGMENTATION, NO EXTERNAL DATA. Do not start with a U-Net. Centre the
130 mm window on the TISSUE CENTROID of the slot (intensity-weighted centroid, or the centroid of an
Otsu/percentile foreground mask) instead of on the image centre. That is a few lines in SlotReader.window
plus a cache rebuild, it buys the entire "align the spatial position across sequences" mechanism the
authors credit, and it can be validated with ZERO GPU by re-running crop_coverage: if centroid-centring
lifts p10 retention from 0.7299 toward the median, the box was misplaced and the arm is justified; if
p10 barely moves, our boxes were already well placed and this bead dies for the price of a proxy - the
same gate knee-7zw7 used, which worked.

PRICE. Proxy: ~30 min, zero GPU, and it is a real keep/kill. Arm if the proxy passes: cache rebuild
(~1h wall, CPU, can overlap a training arm) + one 45-min arm. Total ~2.5h for a lever an external
ablation prices at +0.056. Odds of clearing 1.5%: call it 1 in 3 - their +0.056 is against a baseline
with NO crop at all, whereas ours is a mediocre crop rather than no crop, so we can only recover the
MISPLACEMENT part, not the whole. But even a third of it clears the bar, and the proxy tells us the size
of the misplacement before any GPU is spent. Best wall-clock-per-expected-gain on the board.

REFUTATION CLAUSE, pre-registered. If the proxy shows p10 retention is already high once centring is
fixed only slightly (i.e. our boxes are near-centred), then the +0.056 does NOT transfer, the mechanism
is about their no-crop baseline rather than about centring, and this bead closes without an arm. If the
proxy shows large misplacement AND the arm still lands flat, then spatial alignment is not our binding
constraint and knee-vigl's +0.049 should be discounted by the same argument, since the paper says the
two are the same mechanism.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-21, SAME DAY AS FILING, and it is my error not the idea's. I filed this after auditing
model.py/anatomy.py but BEFORE reading crop_coverage.py, knee-yrf and
interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-15_crop_centre_coverage.md. All three already exist and they answer the
gate this bead set itself. Dropped P0 -> P2.

WHAT WAS ALREADY BUILT AND ALREADY MEASURED:
- `TissueCentre` EXISTS, is plumbed through six call sites, and is opt-in via CENTRES in
  kneemri/corpus/crop_centre.py. My "cheap first version - a few lines in SlotReader.window" is a
  proposal to write code the repo already has.
- The proxy EXISTS: `python -m kneemri.corpus.crop_coverage` scores both centres at both extents, paired,
  with a bootstrap interval. It was run 2026-08-15 on 1822-1848 series from 400 studies:
      tissue - image at 130 mm  +0.0294 [+0.0276, +0.0312]*
      tissue - image at  80 mm  +0.0233 [+0.0215, +0.0251]*
      tissue@130 median 0.8860 / p10 0.7576 / worst 0.4524  (image@130: 0.8566 / 0.7299 / 0.4537)
- knee-yrf (P0 BUG, CLOSED 2026-08-15) is exactly this bead. Its close reason: real, knob-sized, and NOT
  promoted, because 2-3 pp of retained tissue does not pay for a 99 GB cache rebuild plus a refit of
  every seated member. It also recorded a failure mode I did not: an Otsu mass centroid gets DRAGGED by
  coil, fat and the far limb, so tissue-centring's WORST series is worse than image-centring's at 80 mm
  (0.0929 vs 0.1423).

SO THE +0.056 DOES NOT TRANSFER THE WAY I WROTE IT. CoPAS's 0.725 -> 0.781 is NO CROP versus an
ROI crop. Ours is a decent crop versus a slightly better crop, and the measured size of "slightly" is
+2.9 pp of retained tissue - not a 5.6-point-of-AUC kind of gap. The refutation clause I pre-registered
("if the proxy shows our boxes are near-centred, the +0.056 does not transfer and this bead closes
without an arm") has already fired, on evidence recorded six days before I filed it.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is a genuinely different measurement rather than a rescue of the same one.
knee-yrf and crop_coverage both score RETAINED TISSUE PER SERIES. CoPAS's stated mechanism is not
retention, it is quoted as "cropping along ROI can align the spatial position across sequences" - a
BETWEEN-SLOT quantity. Nothing in this repo has ever measured the DISAGREEMENT between the crop centres
of different slots of the SAME study. If a study's sagittal and axial slots are centred 15 mm apart, every
slot presents the knee at a different offset, and the slot-aggregation axis - which landed inside the
noise floor across every arm we ran - has been fusing views that do not correspond. That is the same
argument knee-vigl makes for reformats, and image-centring is a cheaper place for it to be true.

THE NEXT STEP IS THEREFORE A NEW STATISTIC ON THE EXISTING TOOL, NOT AN ARM: add a per-study spread of
crop-centre offsets across routed slots, under each centre strategy. Zero GPU, reuses the decode that is
already written. Read it as: if image-centring's between-slot spread is large and tissue-centring's is
small, the alignment mechanism is live here and knee-yrf was closed on the wrong statistic. If both
spreads are small, slots are already mutually aligned, CoPAS's ROI gain is about their no-crop baseline,
and this bead closes for good along with a chunk of knee-vigl's price.

The 99 GB rebuild cost still stands and still gates any arm, whatever the spread says.
MEASURED 2026-08-21. New tool `kneemri/corpus/crop_alignment.py` (the statistic the correction called for - between-slot, not within-series). 400 studies sampled every k-th of 4407, ALL 400 decoded, 1848 routed slots.

Per-slot |offset| from image centre to Otsu tissue centroid, in mm:
  AX_FLUID_FS     p50  9.9  p90 18.3   down p50 +8.2  across p50 -0.6   396 slots
  COR_FLUID_FS    p50 10.2  p90 22.5   down p50 -8.1  across p50 -0.8   386
  COR_T1          p50  9.1  p90 19.6   down p50 -6.0  across p50 -0.6   263
  SAG_FLUID_FS    p50 13.9  p90 26.1   down p50 -4.7  across p50 +10.7  380
  SAG_FLUID_NOFS  p50 11.1  p90 22.3   down p50 -8.1  across p50 +2.9   246
  SAG_T1          p50 12.9  p90 23.4   down p50 -8.5  across p50 +3.4   177
Within-study spread of |offset| across slots: p50 5.7 mm, p90 10.7 mm, max 18.8 mm.

THE READING - THE ALIGNMENT MECHANISM IS NOT AVAILABLE HERE. The 130 mm box is read to 336 px, so 0.387 mm/px; the encoder pools at stride 32, so one feature cell is 12.4 mm. The median between-slot disagreement of 5.7 mm is 0.46 of ONE feature cell, and the p90 of 10.7 mm is 0.86 of one. Our slots already agree on where the knee is to finer than the granularity any attention over pooled features could act on - and our aggregator collapses H and W entirely before the slots ever meet, so in-plane position is not even present at the point of fusion. CoPAS's +0.056 is measured against a full-FOV 576-matrix baseline where the disagreement would be tens of mm; the number does not transfer to a corpus that already crops.

SECOND READING, AND IT IS THE MORE USEFUL ONE. The signed medians are PLANE-SYSTEMATIC, not per-study jitter: every sagittal slot sits ~8 mm up and a few mm anterior, every coronal ~8 mm up, axial ~8 mm DOWN. That is a framing convention per acquisition type, constant across studies - which is exactly the kind of offset a per-slot encoder absorbs into its own weights for free. It is not a defect to correct.

CLOSING knee-f6u4. The bead's own pre-registered clause fires: 'if both spreads are small, slots are already mutually aligned, CoPAS's ROI gain is about their no-crop baseline, and this bead closes for good'. Both are small. Combined with knee-yrf (tissue-centring buys +0.029 retained tissue, not worth a 99 GB cache rebuild), the crop-centre axis is now closed from BOTH sides: it keeps enough tissue, and the slots agree where that tissue is.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT - stated so a later use is re-tested rather than assumed dead. This is an IN-PLANE statistic only. It says nothing about THROUGH-PLANE correspondence: whether two acquisitions sample the same anatomy at the same slice positions and orientations. That is knee-vigl's actual claim, and it is still unmeasured. knee-vigl loses the in-plane half of its price and keeps the through-plane half; its gate on through_dense stands.

title: Inflate the trunk stem to 3D: the one exclusion depth_true wrote into its own close
description:
depth_true closed slice ORDER at the feature level and stated its exclusion verbatim: 'a 3D encoder that sees the volume before any per-slice feature exists is a different mechanism and untouched.' All 107 runs are per-slice-features-then-pool.

The aggregation stage is now saturated from three directions at once: more slices -0.0001 (knee-ezz, 20 vs 12), more slots +0.0002 (extended_slots, 83297 previously unseen slices), and every combining rule within 0.0019 (max 0.8457, order-aware gate 0.8461, mean 0.8473, permutation-blind gate 0.8476). Both attend_true and depth_true conclude the limit is UPSTREAM, in what one slice's feature vector contains. A trunk that never produces a per-slice feature is the only thing that changes that.

CHEAP VERSION FIRST - do not build a full video transformer. Inflate the existing 2D trunk's stem to 3D over a short depth window, keep everything else identical: a single-variable arm against band_dense 0.8578. One 45-min arm.

WHAT IT BUYS EITHER WAY. This is an INSTRUMENT, not an expected improvement. A null retires the whole 3D axis for about an hour. A positive licenses the expensive version.

RISK, stated up front: this is a different inductive bias, and the last different inductive bias (cnx_dense) lost by 0.0585 at MATCHED TRAIN LOSS on the same 3498 studies. A 3D trunk has more parameters per unit of data, so the same generalisation gap should be expected worse, not better - UNLESS it is pretrained, which points at knee-ombx (external data / MRNet supervised pretraining). Sequence them: if knee-ombx unblocks, run this on top of the pretrained trunk rather than from a natural-image one.

Distinct from knee-ec0p, which changes the SSL OBJECTIVE to see through-plane structure; this changes the TRUNK.

Full argument: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-21_three-failures-one-mechanism.md
notes:
2026-08-21: implemented, not as filed. The audit changed the design. `slice_features` already replicates one slice across the encoder's three channels, and the OLD default `channels` pooling already stacks three consecutive slices into them - but INSTEAD of per-slice pooling (one forward per slot, no slice axis), which couples group thickness to slice count and is why 12->32 inference slices cost -0.018 there. So pixel-level through-plane mixing was only ever measured bundled with the loss of the slice axis, and the bundle is what lost. The clean single-variable instrument keeps per-slice pooling and changes ONLY what the three channels hold: (i-1, i, i+1) clamped at the slot's depth ends, gathered strictly within a slot. Same slice axis, same tokens, same parameters, same FLOPs; differs from the control on slices-2 of slices slices. Shipped as `--through-plane` -> StudyDesign.through_plane -> kneemri/models/depth_window.py (DepthWindow.channels), stamped in the manifest and listed in landed.py. Arm: experiments/arms/through_dense.sh, control band_dense 0.8578 @ e8, ~40 min.
PRICE: ~40 min of card (12 epochs at 20 slices, band_dense's own ~200 s/epoch; the window is a gather, so the FLOP count and the step time are the control's). P(clears the 1.5% bar) under 10% — the regime has looked data-limited from nine directions and this adds information, not capacity. It is an INSTRUMENT: a null discharges the exclusion clause depth_true wrote into its own close ("a 3D encoder that sees the volume before any per-slice feature exists is a different mechanism and untouched") and lets the aggregation chapter be closed without an asterisk, for the cheapest arm on the board. A BELOW-control result is the informative one: it says the pretrained colour-channel stem cannot be asked to mean depth, so a 3D trunk must be PRETRAINED on volumes rather than adapted at its first convolution — which prices knee-ec0p and the 3D-encoder axis generally.
PRE-REGISTERED MID-RUN 2026-08-21 20:50 UTC, at epoch 3 of 12, written BEFORE the result so it cannot be a story told afterwards. Matched-epoch against band_dense: e0 0.7403 v 0.7430, e1 0.7812 v 0.7783, e2 0.8141 v 0.8197. Deltas oscillate in SIGN inside the 0.0062 floor. Training loss 1.2205/1.0830/0.9899 against the control's 1.2162/1.0743/0.9851 - within 0.009 at every epoch.

THE SECOND INSTRUMENT IS THE INTERESTING ONE, and this is the lesson from knee-a2q7 applied forward. On band_dense_llrd the loss DIVERGED from the control and that is what exposed underfitting and refuted the arm's own pre-registration. Here the loss curves are near-identical, which is a different and more specific statement: the input change is almost INVISIBLE TO THE OPTIMISATION. The model fits the training set at the same rate with neighbours in the channels as with three copies of one slice.

THE MECHANISM I EXPECT, stated in advance so it is falsifiable. A ViT patch embedding is a single strided conv whose channel dimension is SUMMED at the first layer. Three copies of slice i sum to 3*i; slices i-1, i, i+1 sum to a three-tap blur along depth. The stem cannot separate the three channels because it never represents them separately - so 'putting depth in the channels' delivers a depth-BLURRED single image, not three readable views. That predicts exactly this signature: near-identical loss, oscillating sub-floor AUC deltas.

IF THAT IS RIGHT the reading is NOT 'the depth axis is dead'. It is that the CHANNEL is the wrong place to put depth in a trunk whose first op sums channels, which is a statement about the vehicle. It strengthens rather than weakens knee-jucq: a trunk that represents depth needs an operator that does not collapse it at layer one.

FALSIFIER: if the arm lands ABOVE the floor, this account is wrong - the stem does carry channel-separable information and the cheap vehicle worked, which prices knee-jucq as the expensive version of a live axis instead.
CORRECTION 2026-08-21 20:52 UTC, to the pre-registration I wrote two minutes ago and to this bead's own 'implemented, not as filed' note. Both were wrong on the same point and it changes what a null means.

THE ARITHMETIC. Conv2d(3, D, k=14, s=14) applied to channels (i-1, i, i+1) is MATHEMATICALLY IDENTICAL to Conv3d(1, D, k=(3,14,14), s=(1,14,14)) applied to that 3-slice volume. Same parameters, same output, exactly. So --through-plane IS stem inflation at a depth window of 3. It is not a cheaper proxy for the filed design; for window 3 it IS the filed design, and this bead's note describing the shipped arm as a departure from 'inflate the stem' is wrong.

WHAT I GOT WRONG IN THE PRE-REGISTRATION. I wrote that the stem 'cannot separate the three channels because it never represents them separately', calling the result a depth-BLURRED image. That overstates it. The three channel filters W_r, W_g, W_b are DISTINCT learned kernels, so the stem computes a learned linear combination across depth, not an equal-weight blur - it can in principle express a depth derivative, not just a smear. The correct and narrower statement is: the stem collapses the depth window to ONE linear projection per output dimension, and those weights were pretrained to mean COLOUR rather than depth. It has no capacity to carry 'the slice at i' and 'how it changes with depth' as separate quantities, because there is only one output token per patch.

CONSEQUENCES, and they cut both ways.
- A null is MORE informative than I said, not less. It genuinely does test stem inflation, so it discharges the exclusion clause AT A DEPTH WINDOW OF 3 rather than merely gesturing at it. The bead's original claim to discharge the clause is largely restored.
- What a null does NOT retire is now sharp and small: (a) a depth window LARGER than 3, which needs a real Conv3d because the channel trick is capped at 3 by the pretrained stem's channel count, and (b) a stem that outputs SEVERAL depth positions instead of collapsing to one, which is the thing no reshaping of a 2D stem can do at any window size. Those two are what knee-jucq's volume trunk actually buys, and they are the honest residue.

FALSIFIER UNCHANGED: above the floor and this whole account is wrong.
CLOSED 2026-08-21 21:46 UTC. RESULT: best 0.8558 at epoch 6 against control band_dense 0.8578. -0.0020, a third of the 0.0062 floor. FLAT. The pre-registered BELOW-or-FLAT branch fired; the FALSIFIER (landing above the floor) did not.

MECHANISM NAMED, and it is the one written in advance rather than fitted afterwards. Matched-epoch training loss tracked the control within 0.009 at EVERY epoch (1.2205/1.0830/0.9899/0.9141/0.8475 vs 1.2162/1.0743/0.9851/0.9115/0.8466). The input change was nearly invisible to the optimisation, which is a sharper claim than the flat AUC: the depth information did not hurt, the trunk had no way to use it. The stem collapses the depth window to ONE linear projection per output dimension and those weights were pretrained to mean colour; there is one output token per patch, so it cannot carry "the slice at i" and "how it changes with depth" as separate quantities.

HARNESS SUSPECTED FIRST, per the standing rule, and cleared on each link. DATA: the window is a gather inside the slot, and the arm differs from control on slices-2 of slices slices, so the change is present in every batch. TRAINING: identical recipe, identical step count, identical img/s (~1215), loss curves within 0.009 - not an under-trained arm. TEST: same 909-study fold-0 holdout, same metric, and the delta is read against a control measured on the same split. PLUMBING: the flag landed - --through-plane -> StudyDesign.through_plane -> DepthWindow.channels, stamped in the manifest and listed in landed.py, and the two arms are NOT byte-identical in output. IDEA: what remains, and it is the vehicle rather than the axis.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT, narrow and explicit. Per the mid-run correction, Conv2d(3, D, k=14, s=14) over (i-1, i, i+1) IS Conv3d(1, D, k=(3,14,14), s=(1,14,14)) over the 3-slice volume - identical parameters, identical output. So this genuinely discharges depth_true's exclusion clause AT A DEPTH WINDOW OF 3. It does NOT retire (a) a window larger than 3, capped here by the pretrained stem's channel count, or (b) a stem emitting SEVERAL depth positions rather than collapsing to one - which no reshaping of a 2D stem can do at any window size. Those two are exactly what knee-jucq's volume-pretrained trunk buys, so this result STRENGTHENS knee-jucq rather than weakening it, as the pre-registration said it would.

THE CHECKPOINT OUTLIVED THE ANSWER, by the largest margin any refuted arm has yet produced. Priced against the 0.931 champion five: +0.0008 as an add, +0.0010 taking base_dense's seat - the best of all TWENTY-FOUR candidates scored on 2026-08-21 (mounted and unmounted), where the next value is +0.0005 and the best mounted move is +0.0002. Under +0.0015 BOARD_RESOLVABLE and not claimed as an edge. The reason to weight it is mechanical: every other member reads the SAME pixels and differs only downstream of an identical input tensor; this is the only one that changes what the encoder is shown at the first op, and knee-nas5 measured that axis under-priced by this holdout by 2.4x. Mounted in comp/members.roster and pushed in the 23-member package. Third consecutive arm whose premise was refuted and whose checkpoint the roster wanted (calib_span carried 0.929, band_dense_long carried 0.930).

Ledger: experiments/README.md, "through_dense - stem inflation at a depth window of 3".

title: A push during a training arm reports 9 false test failures: Windows STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED, not a defect
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 11:41 UTC, while band140 held 26.92 GB of the card and the box was saturated. `git push` ran the pre-push suite and reported 9 failed, 946 passed:

  tests/unit/kneemri/experiments/arm_check.py::test_invocations, ::test_queued
  tests/unit/kneemri/kaggle/kit_check.py:: test_asked, test_stamped, test_drift, test_recorded, test_behind, test_drift_refuses_a_kit_built_from_a_dirty_tree, test_a_path_inside_the_repo_answers_the_same_as_its_root

THE CAUSE IS NOT IN THE TESTS. kit_check's fixture calls `git -C <tmp> init -q` and it returned exit status 3221225794 = 0xC0000142 = STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED -- Windows declining to START a child process, not git failing at anything. arm_check's two are the same fault wearing a different mask: it SOURCES each arm through bash, the bash never started, and the empty capture asserts as {} == {'real': ...}. Every one of the nine shells out; none of the 946 that passed do.

Confirmed by rerunning: both files pass clean on a second run minutes later with nothing changed, and the push then succeeded.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG. The failure mode is a harness fault dressed as a result, which is the thing this project's own instructions say to suspect first -- and it fires precisely when the machine is BUSY, i.e. every time an arm is running, which is when pushes actually happen. The cost is not the retry; it is the pull to 'fix' seven tests that were never broken. A push during an arm has already cost one investigation.

WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT, in preference order:
1. Make the subprocess-spawning tests retry once on 0xC0000142 specifically, and only that code -- a targeted retry on a documented OS resource failure is not flakiness tolerance.
2. Or mark them and have the pre-push hook run a spawn-free subset, leaving the full suite to `uvx nox -s gates`.
Do NOT widen it to a blanket retry: every other failure in this suite is real.

title: Integration layer exercises only one slice_pooling name
description: Found 2026-08-21 while fixing knee-7gyw. Every test in tests/integration/ passed slice_pooling='max' or the default -- grep over the whole dir returns max, max, max. So the pair contract 'a name options.py accepts is a name model.py builds AND trains' had no test at ANY layer, which is exactly the hole knee-7gyw fell through: attend parsed, stamped, built, and trained none of its weights. Closed for slice_pooling by test_every_slice_pooling_a_run_can_ask_for_reaches_the_optimiser in tests/integration/options_to_policies.py, which walks the vocabulary rather than naming today's members. THE GENERAL CASE IS STILL OPEN: pool, slot_pooling, scheme, tie, centre each have their own vocabulary and the integration suite pins one value of each the same way. A second silent mis-build is available on any of those axes.
notes:
RANKED the general case, 2026-08-21, by whether the axis can hide a knee-7gyw-class defect (a module BUILT and then never given gradient) rather than merely a wrong-pixels one.

Registries and what the integration suite pins:
  SLOT_POOLINGS  {attended: SlotHead, averaged: MeanSlotHead}  pinned to AVERAGED         -- HAS WEIGHTS
  POOLS          (pool= in StudyDesign)                        pinned to CLS_MEAN_FOCAL   -- loss/readout
  SCHEMES        kneemri/corpus/slots.py:137                   pinned to MULTISCALE       -- no weights
  CENTRES        kneemri/corpus/crop_centre.py:124             pinned to TISSUE           -- no weights
  ties           Routing(tie=...)                              pinned to LAST_MAXIMAL     -- no weights

Only SLOT_POOLINGS carries trainable parameters, so it is the only one where the silent failure mode is 'the module exists and the optimiser never moves it'. The other three decide WHICH PIXELS are read, and argv_to_checkpoint's design ratchet already asserts their stamp survives argv -> manifest -> member, so a mis-build there shows up as a changed reading rather than as a frozen tensor.

Consequence: extend test_every_slice_pooling_a_run_can_ask_for_reaches_the_optimiser to walk SLOT_POOLINGS too and the weighted half of this bead is closed. The pixel axes are a separate, lower-priority sweep.
close_reason: Both halves closed. The WEIGHTED half (SLOT_POOLINGS) was already done by 41e48ef on 2026-08-21 in the same commit that opened this bead — tests/integration/options_to_policies.py:156 READOUT_VOCABULARIES walks SLICE_POOLINGS and SLOT_POOLINGS, and the bead was never updated to say so. The PIXEL half is commit 88ea7df: test_every_reading_a_run_can_name_reaches_the_key in tests/integration/argv_to_cache_key.py walks scheme, centre and tie, asserting each name either IS the historic reading and keeps its cache name or is named for itself. The tie was not enumerable — its argparse choices were a literal (FIRST_MAXIMAL, LAST_MAXIMAL) rather than a registry — so core/data/corpus/slots.py now holds TIES beside them and cache_flags reads choices from it. Mutation-checked: dropping the tie from Routing.suffix fails the walk. 18 tests green, uvx nox -s gates successful.

title: build_cache.sh dies AFTER the build with a line-55 syntax error, so ARM DONE is never printed
description:
logs/cache_crop80_span.log (2026-08-19 19:54) ends:

  CACHE BUILD COMPLETE
  experiments/arms/build_cache.sh: line 55: syntax error near unexpected token `('
  experiments/arms/build_cache.sh: line 55: `[ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "ARM FAILED build_cache_${KEY} (exit $status)"; exit "$status"; }'

The DECODE succeeded — the failure is in the wrapper's own epilogue, after the expensive part. Consequences, in order of cost:
  1. 'ARM DONE build_cache_<key>' is NEVER echoed, so an after.sh watcher gated on that marker waits forever behind a cache that is already on disk. That is the exact five-minute-idle failure queue_check exists to catch, except here the producer is dead rather than the watcher.
  2. the mask-written check on line 56 never runs, so a truncated build reads the same as a complete one.
  3. the arm exits non-zero, so any caller chaining on it aborts a step that actually worked.

SUSPECT: line endings. `file` reports experiments/arms/build_cache.sh as 'with CRLF line terminators' (lib.sh too), and a stray CR inside a brace group is a classic 'syntax error near unexpected token' in Git Bash. Line 55 is valid bash otherwise. Fix is a .gitattributes eol=lf for experiments/**/*.sh plus a renormalise, not an edit to the line.

BLOCKS: the 140 mm FOV cache (knee-n3yx), which is the next machine-alone job and would be queued behind exactly this marker.
notes:
DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED, and the corrected one is worse (2026-08-21). The .gitattributes theory was wrong: this repo ALREADY carries '* text=auto eol=lf', git ls-files --eol reports i/lf for every affected script, and after stripping the CRs 'git diff --numstat' is EMPTY. The index was never wrong.

The CRLF lived in the WORKING COPY ONLY. That is the whole problem: git normalises on add, so a CRLF worktree file shows NO diff, NO status change and NO warning at review time — while bash reads the file as it is on disk and chokes on the constructs that CR breaks (brace groups, subshells). The repo looks clean at every layer that anyone checks, and the breakage is invisible until a wrapper's epilogue runs.
