12 of the tree's shell scripts were CRLF in the worktree: experiments/{lib,recipe,stub_lib}.sh and experiments/arms/{attribution,build_cache,compose_base,compose_small,diversity_curve,rate_isolate,report_supervision,severity_flat,slice_count_maxpool}.sh. Stripped with tr -d '\r'; build_cache.sh now passes 'bash -n' and its --dry-run reaches the key (336px_20sl_140mm_0.1-0.9band).

RECURRENCE IS THE OPEN PART. Something on this machine writes CRLF into the worktree (the commit of b1829bb printed 'CRLF will be replaced by LF' for twelve files, so it is whatever edits them, not the checkout). A .gitattributes change cannot fix that — it already says the right thing. What would: a gate that asserts no tracked .sh has a CR on disk, run in the same place arm_check runs, so an edited wrapper is caught before it is queued rather than after it has eaten a decode's completion marker.

title: An arm log carries no positive witness that its flags landed
description:
Reading encoder_adapt_thawed's log to decide whether --unfreeze-last 12 actually took effect, there is nothing in the log that says so. landed.py builds a Request and refuses on a mismatch, so a silent pass IS the assertion - but that makes the check legible only when it BLOCKS, which is the exact defect just fixed one layer out in experiments/lib.sh (a free-VRAM gate that printed nothing when it passed, and so hid a constant that was wrong in both directions for weeks).

The only positive witness available in the thawed log was indirect: the derived VRAM cap printed 9.6 GB, which is the twelve-block figure rather than the six-block one. That is a coincidence of the cap fix, not a designed witness, and it will not exist for flags that do not move the cap.

FIX: have the pre-flight check log the Request it verified - one line, unconditional, on the passing path. Then reading an arm's verdict does not require reasoning backwards from a memory figure.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the loop mandate requires naming which link broke (data/training/test/plumbing/idea) BEFORE writing a verdict, and PLUMBING is the link that cannot currently be cleared from the artefact an arm leaves behind.

title: In-plane FOV was closed only in the cropping-IN direction
description:
crop80_span measured a significant per-label gradient on in-plane extent: tightening 130mm -> 80mm cost MCL -0.0265* and ACL -0.0263*, both clearing the pair's own paired half-widths, plus Baker's -0.0164*. The ledger read this as antagonism between in-plane and through-plane coverage and CLOSED the crop axis. But every arm on this axis has moved the crop INWARD (130 default, 80 tight). Nobody has widened it.

The mechanism the crop80 row itself names is that the losses are 'exactly the structures at the field's margins' - the collaterals and the cruciate. MCL is the corpus's worst label (0.788-0.793 holdout) and the label-contest pilot found it has 0 contested cells and the LOWEST UNK share (9.8%), i.e. its supervision is clean and its ceiling is a VISION ceiling. MCL runs along the medial margin; Baker's is posterior. Both live in the ring a 130mm box discards.

crop_coverage.py's own docstring records that at 130mm the margin is about 15mm, so native imaged extent is roughly 160mm and widening to ~160 costs no padding.

DENOMINATOR, stated honestly: +0.0265 on 2 of 12 labels is +0.0044 on the mean, under the 0.0062 floor. This is only worth an arm if the gain is broader than MCL+ACL - which crop80's group reading suggests it might be (regional -0.0104, focal -0.0095 when cropping in, so the loss was broad).

CHEAP PROXY FIRST (running): crop_coverage --tight-mm 170 measures retained tissue share at 130 vs 170 and, via the series that reader.window refuses, how many studies image beyond each extent. If most studies image well past 130, the crop is discarding real anatomy at the margins and the arm is justified. If not, the axis really is closed and this bead dies without a GPU slot.
notes:
PROXY READ 2026-08-21 (logs/crop_140.log, crop_150.log, crop_wide.log; 1822 series from 400 studies of 4407, zero GPU). The gate this bead set itself is answered, and it answers AGAINST the arm as filed.

WHAT 130 mm DISCARDS, which is the half that survives. The image-centred 130 mm box keeps a median 0.8495 of a series' tissue, p10 0.7299, worst 0.4537. So the standing read throws away about a seventh of the imaged knee at the median and better than a quarter of it for one series in ten. That is real anatomy at the margins and it is the mechanism this bead was filed on.

WHAT IS NOT THERE, which kills the arm as filed. The retention row at each extent is computed ONLY over series whose acquisition is at least that wide -- SlotReader.window returns None for a crop wider than the frame (slot_reader.py:256), and crop_coverage.series drops those rather than scoring them as perfect (crop_coverage.py:96). So the series column IS the availability:
    140 mm  1718/1822 = 94.3% of series, retention 0.9052
    150 mm  1489/1822 = 81.7%,            retention 0.9495
    170 mm  358/1822  = 19.6%,            retention 0.9767
This bead's premise -- 'native imaged extent is roughly 160mm, widening to ~160 costs no padding' -- is REFUTED by its own proxy. Four series in five never reach 160-170. The 0.9767 at 170 is a number about the widest fifth of the corpus, not about the corpus.

THE PLUMBING CONSEQUENCE nobody had priced. A series narrower than the requested crop is not padded; window returns None and the read takes the whole frame, which is then resampled to the same pixel grid. That means a different mm/pixel for those series -- the one property slot_reader's docstring says the crop exists to hold constant. At 140 that breaks for 5.7% of series; at 150 for 18.3%. So the widest defensible arm is 140 mm, not 150 and not 170.

PRICED, and it does not clear. crop80_span measured the inward gradient: 130 -> 80 mm, -50 mm, cost -0.0044 on the mean (MCL -0.0265*, ACL -0.0263*). 130 -> 140 is +10 mm, a fifth of that step, so a linear read predicts +0.0009 and even a generous margin-weighted read gives +0.002-0.005 -- at or under the 0.0062 floor. The cost is not one slot: a new crop is a new cache key, and build_cache.sh must have the machine ALONE (no resume; it once killed a trainer and itself), so it is ~2 h of exclusive machine for a predicted sub-floor mean.

VERDICT. Dead as a mean-gain arm, on its own pre-registered gate. NOT dead as a SEAT arm: every mounted member crops at 130 or 80, so a 140 mm member is decode-diverse in a direction the pool has never held, and decode-side diversity is what cnx_dense's consequence clause commits the next member to (band_dense's decode change bought +0.0053 of seat). Demoted to P2 and queued only into a gap where no member arm is waiting -- never ahead of one.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT. The 15% of tissue that 130 mm discards is still discarded, and MCL/ACL/Baker's are still the labels at the margin. What is refuted is that WIDENING THE BOX can recover it: the acquisitions do not extend far enough. A mechanism that reaches margin tissue without a wider physical box -- more pixels over the same extent, or a second slot read off-centre -- is untouched by this measurement.

SIDE READ, recorded because it is a free mechanism check. Tissue-centring's advantage over image-centring shrinks as the box widens: +0.0294* at 130 mm, +0.0249* at 140, +0.0189* at 150, +0.0137* at 170. Centring and extent are substitutes, exactly as they should be if the wide box captures what the centred one had to aim at.
CORRECTION to the paragraph above, same sitting. 'A mechanism that reaches margin tissue without a wider physical box -- more pixels over the same extent' is wrong and I am striking the first half: resolution cannot recover tissue that the box excludes, and 392 px buys detail inside the 130 mm, not extent beyond it. What survives is the second half only -- a read taken off the tissue centre, i.e. a member whose crop is deliberately offset toward the margin the default discards. That is untested and is not the same axis as centre_tissue, which moves the box to keep MORE of the knee rather than to keep a DIFFERENT part of it.

title: VRAM cap was trainable-depth-blind — needed() priced six open blocks for a run that opened twelve
description: encoder_adapt_thawed (--unfreeze-last 12) derived 9.56 GB at batch 4 and died with 'Tried to allocate 204.00 MiB ... 9.56 GiB allowed' while 9.55 GiB of the card sat free. DeviceBudget.needed() scaled its step term by units and batch but by nothing that describes what supervision OPENED. A frozen block's activations are freed once the next block consumes them; a trainable block's must survive to its backward, so the retained stack goes with unfreeze_last and not with the trunk's depth (cnx_dense runs 36 blocks with 6 open). Fixed by a FITTED_TRAINABLE=6 term and a trainable_blocks field, wired in train.py from min(unfreeze_last, encoder.depth) — or encoder.depth under LoRA, where every block carries an adapter. Fitted point reproduces exactly (band_dense still 28.255). This is the FIFTH incident of a term fitted on one configuration handed to another; the previous four are named in the module docstrings.
notes:
Closed in effect by 0505bd8, which took the fix one layer out: DeviceBudget gained the trainable_blocks term (943ac58) and the SHELL gate that had the same defect now derives from the same model. ARM_NEEDS_MIB=18432 was a 12-slice arm's peak handed to every arm — overstating this batch-2 recipe (9795) by 8 GB and understating the shipped 20-slice one (28934) by 10 GB. RunSetup.budget is the one home; kneemri.experiments.vram_need prints MiB for wait_for_free_card; a failed derivation falls back to the constant, never to zero.
CLOSED 2026-08-21. Verified before queueing band_dense_llrd, which is the exact recipe that exposed the bug: --unfreeze-last 12 at batch 2. The derivation now prices it at 9795 MiB against the shipped 20-slice arm's 28934, a 3x spread the old flat ARM_NEEDS_MIB=18432 got wrong in both directions. Nothing left to do; the bead was open only because the fix landed under knee-kwdh's number.

title: The label axis is BLOCKED by its ruler (57 studies), not un-priced
description:
knee-jk3 leaves 'a weight derived from something the reader did NOT see' as the one axis it never priced. Audited 2026-08-21 against a live reader_agreement run (logs/reader_agreement.log). The conclusion is not that the axis is open - it is that NO weight can be established on this ground truth, and the reason is the denominator.

THE DEFECT IS REAL AND LARGE. 140 wrong of 684 cells over 57 annotated studies. It is ASYMMETRIC: 108 false positives, all at confident YES, against 32 misses. And it is SYSTEMATIC, which the earlier note did not say - 11 of the 12 findings are net over-callers (Contusion +18, Effusion +16, ACL +9, MCL +9), with Synovitis the sole inversion (-11). So the positive class is roughly a third contaminated while the negative class is nearly clean.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS ALREADY SPENT. Asymmetric contamination of the positive class asks for the target to be pulled off 1.0 toward the measured agreement rate. That IS calibrated_targets: MEASURED_AGREEMENT already maps each level to its radiologist agreement (0.68->0.378, 0.82->0.688, 0.94->0.958). It ran as calib_span and lost 0.0020 with its per-label prediction INVERTED.

AND THE CENSUS EXPLAINS THE INVERSION, which is the new part. calibrated_targets remaps along GRADE LEVEL, and grade level does not track the error: the over-call sits at YES across 11 of 12 findings, and the graded split runs the other way (graded reports agree 63.2% against 77.8% plain). It is remapping an axis orthogonal to the defect, so an inverted per-label signature is what it should have produced.

WHY THE REMAINING CANDIDATE CANNOT BE MEASURED. That -0.146 [-0.277, +0.005] over 266 positive calls is the largest split any report-level property produces, and it is report-grades-at-all, which is orthogonal to severity_weight's grade-within-report. But it is confounded with level composition (graded reports may simply skew mild), and separating those means conditioning 266 calls on three levels. The unconditioned interval already spans zero; the conditioned one measures nothing. Language is flat (+0.025 [-0.076, +0.126]) and hedged is flat (+0.052 [-0.163, +0.202]) for the same reason.

CONSEQUENCE: the label axis is not an arm we are declining to run, it is an arm the harness cannot score. Unblocking it needs more radiologist-truth studies, which the competition does not give us. Do not spend card time here; do not report a weight fitted on 57 studies as a finding. See also the confident_labels refutation filed the same day.

title: confident_labels (strike UNK) is refuted pre-run by the reader's own error census
description:
kneemri/labels/confident_labels.py is written, tested and NEVER RUN as an arm. Its premise is that removing the reader's UNK verdicts trades less supervision for cleaner supervision. The error census refutes it before it costs a card slot, and the numbers are the tool's own (logs/reader_agreement.log, 2026-08-21, 684 cells over 57 annotated studies):

  false positive: 108   (the reader said YES 108)
  missed:          32   (the reader said UNK 24, NO 8)

Striking UNK therefore removes cells that are DOMINANTLY THE READER'S MISSES - 24 of the 32 under-calls, i.e. cells where the radiologist is positive and the reader hedged - and leaves ALL 108 confident false positives in place. It deletes recoverable signal on the smaller error direction and cannot touch the larger one. Its docstring's own framing ('strictly less, but cleaner') is wrong about which cells it strikes.

DO NOT ARM IT. If the label axis is retried it has to target the YES verdicts, which is where the whole defect is.

The tool itself stays: struck() is still the right primitive if a future reader marks unsure cells that ARE the wrong ones. What is refuted is arming it against THIS reader.

title: ConvNeXtV2 inherits a learning rate settled on DINOv2, and the rate is untested here
description:
OBSERVED MID-RUN 2026-08-21, cnx_dense at epoch 6 of 12. Its training loss is 0.9419 against base_dense's 0.8038 at the same epoch on the same data, and its holdout is still climbing +0.010 an epoch where the control had flattened to +0.0026. Both readings say the same thing: the trunk has not finished fitting inside the twelve-epoch one-cycle schedule, where the ViT had.

WHY THAT IS A RECIPE SUSPECT AND NOT A TRUNK VERDICT. Every constant in $RECIPE — 4e-5 backbone LR, 12 epochs, one-cycle — was settled on DINOv2-small and carried to DINOv2-base unchanged because the family did not change. ConvNeXtV2-base is a different optimisation object: FCMAE pretraining then IN-22k supervised finetuning (every incumbent is SSL-only), stagewise depths rather than a uniform block stack, LayerNorm placement and GRN where the ViTs have none. A rate that is right for one is not evidence about the other, and the project rule is explicit that a well-argued idea failing implicates the harness — here specifically 'faulty TRAINING: a recipe tuned for the old method'.

WHAT THIS BLOCKS. cnx_dense's own pre-registered clauses read a sub-0.80 solo as a RESOLUTION finding and prescribe 448 px (cnx_dense_448, written and arm_checked). That arm holds the schedule fixed on purpose so it separates grid from pixels — it separates neither from the rate. So a flat 448 result exonerates resolution and still does NOT judge ConvNeXtV2 as a family. This bead is the arm that would.

WHAT IT WOULD BE. One variable off cnx_dense: either the rate (1e-4, the direction underfitting points) or the schedule length, not both. Cheapest signal first per the stage-gate rule — a short arm against the trajectory already banked (epoch-by-epoch holdout for cnx_dense is in logs/cnx_dense.log and for the control in logs/base_dense.log), not a fresh matched control.

DO NOT QUEUE THIS BEFORE cnx_dense LANDS. Its solo peak is what decides whether the family is worth a second forty minutes at all.
notes: TRAJECTORY UPDATE 2026-08-21, taken before cnx_dense finished. This bead was raised at cnx_dense epoch 6 on an UNDERFIT reading: holdout climbing +0.0098/epoch where the control had flattened to +0.0026. Two epochs later that reading does not hold. Holdout 0.7858 -> 0.7908 -> 0.7921 (+0.0050, +0.0013) while train loss fell 0.9419 -> 0.9088 -> 0.8833. Loss still dropping fast with holdout already flat is a GENERALISATION gap, not a trunk short of steps, so a larger rate or more epochs buys more of the same fit. This bead is NOT retired by that - a rate settled on DINOv2 is still an untested inheritance, and a rate change alters WHAT is fit, not only how far. But it drops behind cnx_dense_448 in the ordering: geometry is now the live suspect and this is the follow-up, not the first question.

title: DeviceBudget.needed() prices attention linearly, and it is 12% low for a ViT-B
description:
knee-kwdh taught the SLICE term to read the encoder width. The INTERCEPT did not learn. RESIDENT_GB = 0.22 stands for weights + gradients + Adam state, quantities that scale with PARAMETER COUNT, and it was fitted on DINOv2-small (22M). A ViT-B is 86M, so at fp32 params + grads + two Adam moments that intercept should be ~1.4 GB, not 0.22.

COST, 2026-08-20 22:55Z: v3base_dense was refused outright. 'Tried to allocate 946.00 MiB ... 9.17 GiB is free; 21.68 GiB allowed' - nine gigabytes of the card sat unused while the run died, and the card then sat IDLE for an hour because the arm was queued behind a watcher that had already fired. Derived cap was 1.335 x 20 slices x (441/576 tokens at patch 16) x (768/384 width) x (6/12 batch) + 0.22 = 21.7. Every factor is right except the intercept. The arm ran fine at --vram-gb 27 and peaked around 25.9 GB.

This is the SAME SHAPE as knee-kwdh and knee-ylp0, one term further along, and it is the third time: a cap fitted on one configuration handed to another, refusing a run that fits. The pattern is that each fix taught ONE term to read the config and left the others constant.

FIX: make the intercept read parameter count from the encoder rather than being a constant - RESIDENT_GB becomes RESIDENT_GB_PER_MPARAM x the encoder's parameter count, or a per-encoder measured intercept in the ENCODERS registry beside the width it already carries (a supplementary value lives beside its producer).

SECOND DEFECT, same incident: arm_check's OVERSTATED warning is computed from the same needed(), so it advised dropping the --vram-gb 27 that was the fix. A ruler that is broken should not also be the thing that grades the workaround. Once needed() reads the intercept, re-check whether that warning still fires on v3base_dense; if it does, the warning needs its own tolerance.
notes: 2026-08-25 08:57Z — id correction: the two spawned beads are knee-pf8b (trainable-blocks, +35.7%) and knee-dmp4 (intermediate-layer read, +23.0%). The note above names ids that were guessed before creation.

title: Gate an SSL adaptation on its drift profile before it spends a training slot
description: encoder_adapt lost 0.168 uniformly because 6 epochs at lr 1e-4 moved encoder blocks 0-5 by 3.4-8.3% of their own norm, where supervision moves them by exactly 0.0000 and never moves any block more than 2.1%. encoder_drift now reads an adaptation checkpoint (2026-08-20), so the check is a one-minute CPU read guarding a 75-minute arm. Pre-registered: early-block drift <= ~0.02 or the checkpoint does not get armed. First candidate under the gate: adapt_small_e6_lr1e5.pt (same objective/data/schedule, rate 1e-5).
close_reason: The gate ran and adapt_small_e6_lr1e5.pt PASSED it: encoder blocks 0-5 drifted 0.0046-0.0179 of their own norm, inside the pre-registered <=0.02 clause, with the top-4 block share at 0.821 (drift concentrated late, which is what supervision itself does). So the check exists, is a one-minute CPU read, and has now been exercised end to end against a real candidate. The remaining question is not the gate but the arm behind it, which is encoder_adapt_thawed's business.

title: Ordinal severity target: the three YES levels as ordered classes
description: severity_weight (2026-08-20) refuted the MULTIPLIER use of the report grade: matched control band_dense 0.8578 vs arm 0.8530, and four of the five pre-registered graded labels came back negative (focal +0.0001, regional -0.0118). The owner's call is that the axis stays open - the grade is real per-study information the loss still discards. The successor consumes it WITHOUT reweighting any example: the three YES levels (0.68/0.82/0.94) become ordered classes behind a cumulative-threshold head, so it cannot reproduce the batch-starvation mechanism that sank the multiplier. Pre-register the falsifiable clause before queueing. See experiments/README.md, section severity_weight.
notes:
PRICE + PRE-REGISTERED CLAUSE (2026-08-21) — and the justification is RE-FRAMED, because the old one was for a lever this is not.

PRICE: ~55 min of card (12 epochs at ~365 s, band_dense geometry unchanged) + ~10 min to read the seat.
P(clears 1.5% solo) < 3%. severity_flat's own -0.0044 is the size of the information the gradation
carries, so as a SOLO arm this prices at ~0.005 and would be a knob. Do not queue it as one.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH THE SLOT — it is a DIVERSITY arm, not an accuracy arm. The axis ledger on knee-jk3
closes encoder family on three arms; the champion's whole +0.011 over its best member came from
ensembling. Every member in the roster today optimises the SAME binary target and differs only in slice
GEOMETRY, so their errors correlate through the objective. An ordinal cumulative-threshold head is the
first member that would optimise a DIFFERENT TARGET on identical inputs — a different error structure by
construction, which is what a seat pays for.

PRE-REGISTERED CLAUSE, and it is a SEAT clause so it cannot be read off solo AUC:
  - PASS: seat value >= +0.0015 into the roster of five (the bar v3base_dense and cnx_dense both missed,
    at -0.0007 and -0.0035), REGARDLESS of solo AUC. A member 0.005 below band_dense that still buys a
    seat is the finding; that is exactly the trade a diversity member is supposed to make.
  - FAIL: seat < +0.0015. Then the target axis buys no more diversity than the encoder axis did, and the
    conclusion is the STRONG one this arm exists to reach — that member diversity in this roster is
    saturated on every axis we can reach, and the 0.054 frontier gap is not an ensembling gap.
  - The solo number decides NOTHING here. Recorded, not judged.

MECHANISM GUARD (why this is not severity_weight again): the cumulative head consumes the grade through
the TARGET, so no example's weight in the batch changes. severity_weight's refutation was batch
starvation of the rare high grades; that mechanism cannot fire when the batch composition is untouched.
Assert it landed: the checkpoint's options block must record the ordinal head, and the head must emit
K-1 thresholds rather than 1 logit, before the number is read.
2026-08-21 BUILT. The ladder lives in its own module, kneemri/training/grades.py (Predicted moved with it — the class-roles gate refuses two primary classes in objective.py). GRADE_LADDER flag, --grade-ladder, Request/landed vocabulary, member_record write-off, 8 method-level tests. Thresholds derived from MEASURED_AGREEMENT logit midpoints: [-2.501, -1.173, 0.146, 1.959], monotone by construction; boundaries [0.18, 0.48, 0.75, 0.88]. Staircase verified 0.08->[0,0,0,0] .. 0.94->[1,1,1,1]. Gradient scale 1.26x plain under a realistic level mix, so no learning-rate confound. Arm: experiments/arms/grade_ladder.sh, band_dense geometry, ~55 min, queued ahead of band_dense_llrd. PASS = >= +0.0015 into the roster of five; solo AUC decides nothing.
THE BRANCH AFTER THIS ARM IS PRE-REGISTERED, so the read decides the next arm rather than the next arm being chosen after seeing the number.

PASS (>= +0.0015 into the roster of five): a member optimising a DIFFERENT TARGET on identical inputs buys seat value, so target diversity is a live axis and knee-ewi7 (a third encoder FAMILY) is the follow-through — the two are the same claim, that the roster's errors correlate through something shared, tested on two different shared things.

FAIL: diversity is then saturated on every axis reachable from this roster, and the 0.054 frontier gap is not an ensembling gap. The lever is then SUPERVISION, not capacity and not the objective: knee-c5n, adapting the encoder without labels on the ~2.5x more slices supervision never sees. Capacity is already answered and must not be re-reached-for — knee-f0a measured DINOv2-large at +0.0021 for 3.7x the wall-clock, and the two biggest gains this project has ever measured (whole-stack +0.0147, 392 px +0.0066) both add zero parameters.
CORRECTION 2026-08-21, same day, before the arm ran. The PASS branch above named knee-ewi7 (a third encoder FAMILY) and that bead is answered NEGATIVELY and now closed: cnx_dense put ConvNeXtV2-base on the settled band recipe and read solo 0.7927 against base_dense 0.8512, seat value -0.0042 both as a sixth and as a swap, eleven of twelve labels negative with ten clearing their paired half-widths — the widest significant sweep in the ledger (experiments/README.md:1549). A genuinely different inductive bias bought a MORE negative seat than a second ViT family did.

So diversity-by-ENCODER is closed on both rungs it had left, and the ladder is now the only live test of diversity at all — which sharpens what it reads rather than weakening it. The two branches, restated:

PASS: diversity lives on the TARGET, not on the trunk. The follow-through is more of the same axis and nothing to do with encoders — a rank-only member (RankedObjective at weight 1 with cross-entropy off is not currently a member), a per-label-normalised member, a member trained on a label subset. Cheap, all on the settled geometry, all differing only in what the loss asks for.

FAIL: diversity is saturated everywhere reachable — trunk AND target — and the 0.054 frontier gap is a SUPERVISION gap. knee-c5n, unlabelled adaptation on the ~2.5x more slices supervision never sees. Capacity stays closed either way (knee-f0a: DINOv2-large +0.0021 at 3.7x wall-clock).
SECOND CORRECTION, same day: the FAIL branch above says 'knee-c5n' as if it were unstarted. It is not — the SSL axis has three arms on the board, all collapses (encoder_adapt 0.6902, encoder_adapt_gentle 0.6875, and the pair is 0.0027 apart from initialisations whose early-block drift differs FOURFOLD, so initialisation quality was NOT the mechanism). The instrument is the TRAINING LOSS, not the AUC: all three floor near the control's epoch-ZERO loss and are still falling at epoch 11 — not fitting worse, barely fitting at all, because the head sits on frozen blocks 0-5 that were rewritten for spectral reconstruction and the six blocks supervision CAN write cannot re-encode what the frozen half no longer represents.

So on FAIL the arm is not 'run SSL'. It is the two cheap removals the ledger already names (experiments/README.md:1441): converge the MAE, on the ARM'S OWN 20-slice 0.10-0.90 cache rather than the default 12-slice one it was actually trained on, and either do not freeze the adapted blocks or unfreeze deeper. Both are stated there as cheap and both point the same way. Priced before it is queued, not after.

title: rank0_dense is written and un-queued, with no bead of its own
description:
experiments/arms/rank0_dense.sh exists on disk and was owed by after_rank0.log, a watcher that had died with its launching session. bd search finds no issue for it, so the arm's hypothesis, control and pre-registered clause live only in the file header — which means nothing surfaces it in bd ready and it would be re-derived or forgotten.

UN-QUEUED 2026-08-20 rather than lost: the card is going to biohub, and the dead watcher chain has been retired to logs/retired/ so queue_check reports the true state.

TODO on this bead: read the arm header, lift its hypothesis / control / pre-registered clause into this description so the bead is self-contained, then decide whether it is still worth a slot. The context it has to argue against is four consecutive decode/head knobs returning nothing (attend_dense -0.0009, focal_dense -0.0044, band_density +0.0014, aprior_dense -0.0021) — the subsystem, not the levers, is what that pattern is evidence about.

title: [bug] nohup watchers do not survive a harness restart, so a queue can look armed with nothing behind it
description:
ROOT CAUSE, unfixed. aug_long wrote its completion marker on 2026-08-20 and the card then sat at 5% for about five minutes, because the three after.sh watchers meant to start the next arms no longer existed. nohup gives them PPID 1 but does not survive whatever ends the harness shell on Windows.

THE TRAP: a dead watcher's log still reads "waiting for 'ARM DONE ...'" forever, because that line was printed before it died. The one artefact a queue leaves behind says the same thing whether it is waiting or gone.

MITIGATED, NOT FIXED: kneemri/experiments/queue_check.py crosses the watcher logs against the process table and reports STRANDED arms. That DETECTS the hole after the fact; it does not stop it opening, and it only helps if someone runs it.

REAL FIX: a detached Windows launcher — schtasks /create with a one-shot trigger, or a service — so the watcher's lifetime is not tied to the shell that spawned it. Then queue_check becomes a belt-and-braces check rather than the only defence.

title: --patience 3 is below the derived floor and would truncate the run the floor was measured from
description: stale_gap derives the safe patience from every curve on disk: the longest NON-improving streak a run later recovered from is 3 epochs (lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026, 16 epochs, best at 12, survived 3), so patience must EXCEED it and the safe value is 4. Seven arms pass --patience 3 (calibrated_targets, dinov3_base_lora, encoder_layer, focal_pool, peak_rate, resolution, v3base_band) - exactly the value that stops at the third stale epoch, which is the epoch before that run's later best. resolution.sh's own comment claims patience 3 cannot change a recorded best; that replay predates the run that set the floor. Fix: raise the seven to 4, and give recipe.sh a single derived PATIENCE constant so a new knob arm inherits it instead of copy-pasting a number. Corpus at 4 recovers 52 epochs, 29 percent of 177 wasted across 56 runs. NOT for schedule-shape arms (band_dense_long, aug_long) - a stopper deletes the measurement those are launched to take - and not for final_fit, which has no holdout under --fold -1.
close_reason: Landed in 1d95c8e. PATIENCE=--patience 4 lives once in recipe.sh with the derivation beside it; the seven arms inherit it. Verified the flag resolves under stub_lib.sh (ARM_LIB=experiments/stub_lib.sh bash experiments/arms/focal_pool.sh prints --patience 4), which is the lib arm_check sources, and all 60 arms still check clean. resolution.sh's stale comment replaced with why the old replay aged. Excluded by design: schedule-shape arms and final_fit.

title: headlr_dense: the head:backbone rate ratio is the last unmeasured constant of the adaptation triple
description: Adaptation carries head_lr 1e-3, backbone_lr 8e-6, unfreeze_last 6, and trainer.py's own docstring says the 125:1 ratio 'was inherited from the reference rather than measured'. Two of the three have since been opened (backbone rate to 4e-5, depth bracketed by deep24/shallow24); head_lr never was. Moving the backbone rate five-fold silently changed the ratio to 25:1 -- not the inherited one and not a measured one, just leftover arithmetic from changing one number of a pair only ever justified as a pair. headlr_dense restores 125:1 with --head-lr 5e-3 at the settled operating point. Control band_dense 0.8578, seat greedy4_v1 0.8679, cost ~1.2h. Queued behind rank0_dense (watcher pid 105660). Three outcomes pre-registered in the arm header, including a divergence signature (epoch-0 AUC near 0.5, flat loss) written down in advance so a hot-head failure cannot be misread as a refutation of the ratio.
notes:
UN-QUEUED 2026-08-20. The arm is written and was owed by after_headlr.log, whose watcher had died with the session that launched it (see the nohup-watcher bug bead). The card is being handed to biohub, so it is deliberately NOT relaunched rather than lost. Eight dead watcher logs moved to logs/retired/ so queue_check reads the true state ('OK: nothing is queued') instead of reporting a permanent false strand.

Re-queue by relaunching after.sh over experiments/arms/headlr_dense.sh when the card comes back. Read it against the four-knob run of nothing first (attend_dense -0.0009, focal_dense -0.0044, band_density +0.0014, aprior_dense -0.0021): another constant on the same subsystem is the shape that has stopped paying.

title: Anatomical prior: does the head still need to rediscover which plane shows which finding?
description: The second of the five never-run switches (--anatomical-prior). SlotHead initialises self.prior at ZEROS, so the plane-by-finding mapping is learned from 4,407 study-level label vectors that contain no localisation. The flag initialises that same nn.Parameter from the 12x6 table in kneemri/corpus/anatomy.py (two facts per finding, PRIOR_STRENGTH 2.0, all entries non-negative so it is a preference and never a mask). Parameter count, shapes, compute, VRAM and wall-clock are unchanged. Arm: experiments/arms/aprior_dense.sh, 12 epochs against band_dense 0.8578, single variable, about 1.2 h. Sits on the supervision axis that four independent lines converged on (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_what_is_left_after_decode_and_data.md) and is the only one of the three that needs neither a new label nor a user go-ahead. Three outcomes pre-registered in the arm header; the third one — flat mean, per-label pattern moving along the peaked-row split — makes it a diversity generator priced by seat value rather than a mean lever.
notes:
RAN 2026-08-20 as aprior_dense. REFUTED, and the refutation clause was pre-registered.

0.8557 best (epoch 8) vs matched control band_dense 0.8578 (also epoch 8) = -0.0021, a third of the 0.0062 floor, on the wrong side.

Flag verified in the CHECKPOINT config: anatomical_prior false->true, slices 20 / slice_pooling max / whole_stack true / pool cls_mean / backbone_lr 4e-05 identical. Only other config diff is slice_regions absent-vs-1, the StudyDesign default arriving in the manifest, not a variable.

Per-label at matched epoch 8: peaked rows (MCL, Medial OA, Lateral OA, PF OA, Synovitis) -0.0008, flat rows -0.0033. The split is the predicted direction and 0.0025 wide, under half the floor, so the arm's THIRD OUTCOME does not fire either; and the single largest mover in the table is Synovitis -0.010, a PEAKED axial-weighted row going the wrong way.

MECHANISM: the warm start WASHED OUT rather than failed to land, and the training loss separates those. Losses track the control to the fourth decimal at every epoch (1.2117/1.2162 at e0, 0.6508/0.6529 at e8 - the arm slightly LOWER). Not a plumbing failure: landed.py asserts the parameter constructed and switch_coverage smokes it.

Cost was as predicted and is the one clause that held: 26.92 GB reserved / 24.93 GB allocated, 368 s an epoch, identical to band_dense. Free, and bought nothing.

Seat: +0.0009 as a fifth member, +0.0004 as best swap (displacing band_dense, the member it is a variant of). 0 of 1 clears +0.0015. No seat on either ruler.

CONSEQUENCE (pre-registered, so owed): the head had ALREADY recovered the plane-by-finding mapping from study-level supervision alone. 'Supervision never says where' is wrong about THIS head. The localisation argument must buy a REAL localisation signal (knee-mxj), not a warm start on an existing parameter.

Second of the five never-run switches spent (after --pool cls_mean_focal). Fourth consecutive decode/head knob returning nothing: attend_dense -0.0009, focal_dense -0.0044, band_density +0.0014, aprior_dense -0.0021.

Written up in experiments/README.md (row + long entry).

title: v3base_band: the settled data recipe on a different encoder family
description:
RE-PRICED 2026-08-21 as an INSTRUMENT. The seat half of this bead is answered and gone; what is left is a scope question about the ledger's own decode chapter.

THE QUESTION. Every decode number this project holds -- span +0.0039, density +0.0014, band_dense's +0.0053, whole-stack +0.0147, 392 px +0.0066 -- was measured on DINOv2. Nothing yet says whether those are facts about knee MRI geometry or facts about DINOv2's feature geometry. That got MORE load-bearing, not less, when the encoder axis closed: cnx_dense's consequence clause commits the next member to the DATA side, so the decode chapter is now the thing being built on, and its scope is unmeasured.

THE ARM. Single variable against dinov3_base_lora 0.8268: --slices 20 --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9 substituted, encoder / LoRA / rate / pixels all held at 224. Every v3 number we hold was taken at the OLD operating point (band 0.20-0.80, 12 slices) and got none of the decode work.

READ IT AS AN INSTRUMENT, NOT A GAIN. Solo clearly above 0.8268 = the decode recipe transfers across encoder families, and the chapter is a fact about the data; the whole decode axis stays licensed for the next member. Solo at or below 0.8268 = it does not transfer, and every decode number in this ledger gets 'on DINOv2' written on its scope -- which is a real finding and changes what the next data-side member is allowed to assume. There is no outcome in which this arm produces a member: v3base_dense already measured -0.0005 of seat value inside the transformer family and cnx_dense -0.0042 outside it, so the seat clause this bead was filed with is closed and must not be re-read off this run.

PRICE. One slot, ~40 min, expected direct gain zero by construction. Justified only against gain arms that are themselves cheap or blocked -- it buys scope for the axis the project is committed to, and it retires a suspicion rather than moving a number. Queue it in a gap, never ahead of a member arm.

VRAM sized, not assumed: base_lora peaked at 16.1 GB with 12 slices, so 20 slices lands near 27 GB against band_dense's measured 26.9 on the same card. Train size stays 224 for exactly that reason -- one variable.
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN ITS PREMISE 2026-08-21 by cnx_dense, which ran after this was filed. This bead's WHY THIS AND NOT A DECODE ARM paragraph argues that encoder family is "the right thing to spend the card on rather than another occupant of the band seat". That argument is now measured and it lost: three encoders have been read on seat value and the axis closed -- v3base_dense -0.0005 inside the transformer family, cnx_dense -0.0042 outside it entirely (a stride-32 CNN, a different inductive bias, solo 0.7927 against base_dense 0.8512), against base_dense's one paying seat. A different inductive bias is not a different error structure. cnx_dense's own consequence clause states the replacement: the next member has to come from the DATA side rather than the encoder side.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is not the seat half. This arm's INSTRUMENT half is untouched and is now the whole of its value: every decode number this ledger holds (span +0.0039, density +0.0014, band_dense's +0.0053) was taken on DINOv2, and nothing says whether that is a fact about knee MRI or a fact about DINOv2's feature geometry. That question got MORE important, not less, when the encoder axis closed -- a decode-side member is what the project is now committed to, so the scope of the decode chapter is the thing worth an instrument. Re-price it as an instrument and drop the seat clause, which is answered.

title: Lateral Meniscus moves on both rulers in both pooling arms, and it was pre-registered
description:
focal_dense and attend_dense both closed their cell of the decode family on the mean (-0.0044, -0.0009) and both are flat-to-negative on the ordinal ruler too (-0.0047, -0.0002), so neither bought severity ordering the binary ruler was missing.

Lateral Meniscus is the only one of twelve labels positive on all four readings: binary +0.010/+0.009, ordinal +0.017/+0.018, tightly clustered. It survives the best-of-twelve objection because focal_dense.sh PRE-REGISTERED it by mechanism before the run (finest-scale finding, largest model-side gap, knee-dtk -0.1932) and because attend_dense, which never named it, replicates the effect. The pre-registration's second named label, Fracture, went the other way.

Does NOT license another pooling arm (both lost on the mean, both seat at +0.0015 = an ADD not a seat, and inside the 0.0062 floor per knee-yu3e) and does NOT license tuning toward the label. Records that pooling can shift budget toward the finest-scale finding but cannot create it, so whatever limits that label is upstream - supervision or encoder, the same direction both closed arms send the bottleneck.

Written up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_pooling-is-closed-on-the-mean-but-not-on-lateral-meniscus.md

title: Seat reads go through record_mix, not member_curve
description: A seat value (does member X earn a place in the four?) is arithmetic over per-study probabilities that every run already wrote beside its checkpoint as <name>.holdout.npz. kneemri.evaluation.record_mix reads those and returns the subset curve in seconds with no card. kneemri.evaluation.member_curve answers the same question by REBUILDING each member's reading from the pixel cache, which is a full inference pass for anything not in processed/holdout_predictions - and that store is missing the pool's three best members (band_dense, band_span, depth_regions_narrow) even though the 12-member search scored them, because that search was record_mix and never touched the cache. On CPU a miss is hours, so two curve runs on 2026-08-19 looked like a hang and were killed; they were computing. record_mix's own docstring says all of this. Cost: about an hour, plus a queue swap that would have spent card time re-deriving arrays that were already on disk. Follow-up worth doing: either backfill the prediction cache for the pool's top members during an idle card window, or make member_curve say MISS - computing N members loudly when it is about to do inference.

title: The beads daemon rewrites issues.jsonl during the pre-push hooks, so every push needs two attempts
description:
SYMPTOM: git push aborts with a hook reporting 'Failed / - files were modified by this hook', and the hook named is whichever one was running at the time. It has been unit-tests twice, because at 96s that hook holds the widest window.

IT IS NOT A GATE FINDING, and it has been misread as one twice in one session. Verified 2026-08-19: running the unit-tests hook's exact entry (uv run --extra dev pytest tests/unit -q) by hand leaves git status byte-identical and uv.lock + .beads/issues.jsonl md5-identical, exit 0, 845 passed. ruff format --check reports 153 files already formatted, so the format gate is not it either. What actually changes under the hooks is .beads/issues.jsonl, and the writer is the bd daemon's auto-export, which fires on its own schedule rather than on anything the push does.

COST: every push is a two-step — the first aborts, the file is committed as a 'beads: sync issue ledger' commit, the second succeeds. That is one wasted full gate run (~3 min) per push, and worse, it trains the reader to treat a red gate as noise.

FIX DIRECTION: the export should not race the hooks. Either pause the daemon for the duration of a push, or make the pre-push sequence commit a pending issues.jsonl export before it starts rather than discovering it half-way through. Do not paper over it by adding issues.jsonl to an exclude list — the file is git-tracked on purpose and a push that silently drops a pending export is worse than a retry.
notes: 2026-08-25 ROOT CAUSE, and it is not what this bead guessed. core.hooksPath points at .beads/hooks, and both pre-commit and pre-push there hold pre-commit.com's generated body - which execs the runner at line 15 - followed by the beads block bd appends to the END of the file. Nothing below an exec runs, so bd hooks run had NEVER fired in this repo. With the integration inert nothing flushes or stages a pending issues.jsonl export before a push, so the export lands during the gates and whichever hook holds the widest window (unit-tests, 96s) reports 'files were modified by this hook'. Fixed in c02a06a by moving both blocks above the exec. Verified: the next commit printed 'Exported 486 issues and 22 memories', which it had never done before, and the following push went through on the first attempt with a clean tree. The verdict rests on the mechanism rather than on that one clean push. HAZARD RECORDED IN THE HOOK: bd hooks install or pre-commit install re-appends the block below the exec and kills it silently again.

title: queue.sh silently drops an arm's arguments, so a parameterised arm queues as its default
description:
queue.sh:40 runs `timeout "$ARM_TIMEOUT" bash "$script"` where script=experiments/arms/$arm.sh — it takes arm NAMES and forwards nothing after them. after.sh takes entries-with-args and calls run_snapshot $entry, so the two runners disagree on what a queue entry IS.

THE FAILURE. Several arms are parameterised: resolution.sh takes <train_size> <cache_size> [rate], and its defaults are 392/448. Naming 'resolution' in a queue does not fail, warn, or refuse — it runs the 392 default, spends the slot re-running a member we already have, and overwrites res392_ws_s2026.pt with a fresh copy of itself. The loss is silent in both directions: the queue file looks like it asked for a rung, and the output looks like a completed arm.

WHY IT HAS NOT BITTEN YET. Every parameterised arm so far went through after.sh (which forwards) or a hand-launch. The moment someone queues one by name, it costs a slot to discover.

THE FIX. queue.sh should split each entry on whitespace the way after.sh does and forward the tail, and route through run_snapshot rather than bare `bash` — which is also what lib.sh's new guard (51dfc98) now catches at runtime, but catching it after the card is taken is worse than expressing it in the queue. Small test: a queue entry with args reaches the arm's $1.

title: A killed run strands its checkpoint as .partial and leaves a stale .pt beside it
description: depth_regions_span_s2026 run 2 was killed mid-epoch-9. Its epoch-8 checkpoint sits on disk as depth_regions_span_s2026.partial (89 MB, 21:25:53) while depth_regions_span_s2026.pt carries an mtime of 20:49:38 -- older than the run1.pt the rotation wrote at 20:55:57. So the live .pt name does not hold the run that last wrote under it, and 89 MB of orphaned .partial is left for nobody to clean. Establish whether the pending-rename commit can be interrupted between write and rename, and whether a .partial with no .pt beside it should be adopted or deleted at the next begin().
notes:
CORRECTED after reading the code. .partial is NOT a strand: trainer.save_partial writes destination.with_suffix('.partial') at every improving epoch as the crash-safety net (tmp -> replace, atomic), and .pt is written only when a run completes. A killed run leaving 89 MB of .partial holding its best weights is the design working. What is NOT explained, and is the whole bead now: depth_regions_span_s2026.pt exists with mtime 20:49:38 while run1.pt carries 20:55:57. RunMetrics.begin moved .pt aside to run1.pt when run 2 started, and run 2 never completed, so the live .pt name should be ABSENT. Path.replace preserves mtime, so run1.pt's newer stamp cannot come from that move either. Either a third run exists under this name or something writes .pt outside the completion path. Priority stays P2 -- the ledger quotes run 1 from run1.metrics.jsonl and is not wrong -- but a .pt whose provenance nobody can name is the file every roster loads by.
RESOLVED, no defect. Sizes+mtimes settle it: .pt (20:49:38) is run 1's completed epoch-9 payload and was NEVER moved; _run1.pt (20:55:57), _run1.holdout.npz (20:57:07), _run1.metrics.jsonl (20:57:16) are byte-size-identical to run 1's originals but carry LATER mtimes, and Path.replace preserves mtime while a copy does not - so the _run1.* set was COPIED by hand, before RunMetrics grew artefact rotation. .metrics.1.jsonl (20:49:38, mtime preserved) is the one real replace: run 2's begin under the OLD epochs-only code. .partial/.metrics.jsonl/.holdout.npz (21:25:53) are run 2's epoch-8 best (0.8486847394797142). Both .pt and _run1.pt therefore hold the same run-1 payload (epoch 9, holdout 0.8504566982315008) because one is a hand copy of the other, not because the rotation duplicated. The hazard the ec3727c rotation closes is real and unchanged: had run 2 COMPLETED it would have overwritten .pt and run 1 would be gone.

title: kit_check answered about the wrong repository under a git hook: -C is overruled by an inherited GIT_DIR
description:
Git exports GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_WORK_TREE into every hook it runs, and a git child inherits them. An inherited GIT_DIR OUTRANKS -C, so KitCheck.asked() - which is 'git -C <repo> ...' - answered about the repository that invoked the hook rather than the one it was handed. kit_check runs from pre-commit and pre-push, which is exactly where those variables are set.

In this repo the two are the same tree, so the wrong answer happened to be the right one and nothing said otherwise. It surfaced sideways: the unit tests build their own repository in a temp directory, and two of them failed inside a pre-push run while passing on their own. Reproduced deterministically with GIT_DIR=.git pytest tests/unit/kneemri/kaggle/kit_check.py.

FIXED: kneemri/kaggle/kit_check.py gains unhooked(), the environment minus GIT_*, passed to the subprocess; the tests' own raw git calls take it too; test_unhooked covers it. 8 pass under an inherited GIT_DIR where 1 failed before.

REMAINING (why this is open rather than closed): kit_check is not the only thing in the tree that shells git from a place a hook can reach. experiments/lib.sh runs 'git -C $REPO hash-object' for the lib blob stamp, and comp/ has its own git reads. Audit those for the same inheritance and decide whether unhooked() should move to the package root as shared vocabulary rather than living beside its first consumer.
notes:
AUDIT DONE, and it found a second site that matters more than the first.

comp/build_kit.py:93 shelled the same 'git -C $_REPO' to stamp the kit's commit AND its dirty flag. An inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE would have had 'status --porcelain' read a borrowed index, so the stamp - the ground truth every later kit_check compares against - could have been written from a different tree. Same fix applied: env=unhooked(), imported from kit_check.

experiments/lib.sh:39 is CLEAN and stays as it is: 'git hash-object <file>' hashes the file's bytes, so no repository variable can change its answer.

That is every git-shelling site in kneemri/, core/, comp/, experiments/ and tests/. unhooked() stays beside kit_check, its first consumer, rather than moving to the package root - two consumers in the same subsystem is not yet shared vocabulary.
2026-08-19: named the second half of this. A push started right after a bd mutation fails at pre-push with 'shape-contracts ... files were modified by this hook' while that hook's own output reads '0 bare-array boundaries'. The hook is read-only (--assert, pass_filenames: false); what actually changed the tree was bd's ASYNC export of .beads/issues.jsonl landing mid-hook-run, and pre-commit blames whichever hook was running. Cost one failed push tonight, and the failure names an innocent gate — so the reader goes looking in devtools for a defect that is not there. Operating rule until fixed: after any bd mutation, git add .beads/issues.jsonl and commit BEFORE pushing. Verified: the identical push passed on the retry once the export was committed.
2026-08-19: the candidate mechanical fix this bead proposed is REFUTED, measured rather than assumed. 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl' is synchronous, but it is not byte-equivalent to what bd's async writer produces: exported to a probe file it gave the SAME SET of 318 lines (298 issues + 20 memories) in a DIFFERENT ORDER - sorted, the two files are identical; unsorted they differ on 36 lines. So wiring it in as a pre-push flush would rewrite the tracked file with an equivalent-but-reordered payload on every push, fight the async writer for the ordering, and put a large meaningless diff in every commit. That is worse than the race. Do not reach for bd export here again. What remains viable is a LEGIBILITY guard rather than a flush: the defect that costs time is not the dirty file, it is that pre-commit blames whichever hook was running, so the reader goes hunting in devtools for a fault that is not there. A pre-push check that refuses early and names bd as the writer would convert a twenty-hook misattribution into one line. Blocked on where it can live: .pre-commit-config.yaml is template-owned and carries ZERO '# >>> LOCAL-SLOT' regions (grep -c = 0), so the honest home for it is upstream in sdlc-scaffold, not a hand-edit here. Operating rule stands unchanged in the meantime: after any bd mutation, git add .beads/issues.jsonl and commit BEFORE pushing, and run no bd mutation while a push is in flight.
2026-08-25: the second half is CLOSED, and by a mechanism neither this bead nor knee-dsbi had found. It was never a race that needed a flush - core.hooksPath points at .beads/hooks, and both pre-commit and pre-push there hold pre-commit.com's generated body, which execs the runner at line 15, followed by the beads block bd APPENDS to the end of the file. Nothing below an exec runs, so bd hooks run had never fired in this repo once. With the integration inert, nothing flushed or staged a pending export before a push and it landed mid-gate. Fixed in c02a06a by moving both blocks above the exec; the next commit printed 'Exported 486 issues and 22 memories' for the first time and the push went through first attempt. This also retires the LEGIBILITY-guard plan recorded above, which was blocked on .pre-commit-config.yaml having no LOCAL-SLOT region: no guard is needed for a race that no longer happens, and no template-owned file was touched. The bd export refutation recorded above still stands and is still worth not re-trying. First half (unhooked(), build_kit.py, the audit of every git-shelling site) was already done.

title: witness_check's cuda tolerance assumes fp16 arithmetic and is 4x too tight for bf16
description:
comp/witness_check.py applies CROSS_PRECISION_FACTOR = 4.0 (line 46) only on the CPU branch. The cuda branch's premise is that arithmetic MATCHES between arms, so any residual difference is kernel nondeterminism and a near-zero tolerance is right. Measured on the card (knee-djk8 leg b): that premise holds for fp16 - three members pass at EXACTLY 0 - and is false for bf16, whose refusals sit at 0.63-2.47x bf16 eps (2^-7 = 7.8e-3), the same 1.6-2.4x band the CPU calibration already measured. So the gate refuses bf16 members for being bf16, not for drifting. The bead knee-djk8 stated this as 'every bf16 member fails', which is both too strong (three pass) and too weak (they pass at exactly 0, not merely inside tolerance).

NOT fixed on discovery on purpose: this is the pre-submission safety gate, and widening a tolerance is exactly the edit that must arrive with its own test rather than beside an unrelated commit. The fix is to derive the cuda tolerance from the arm's DTYPE eps the way the CPU branch does, and the test is the equivalence class that let it survive - a bf16 pair whose difference is one eps.
close_reason: Fixed: tolerance() now derives from dtype eps on both devices (EPS_FACTOR * finfo(precision).eps); the cuda branch is gone because both regimes measured into the same 1.6-2.5x eps band. Three tests: the bf16-one-eps equivalence class, the discrimination check (bound stays 6x under the 0.05 smallest real reading defect), and the mantissa-scaling identity. Commit 7dc6f87.

title: Split the remaining measure/render classes (ServeBench, OutOfFoldOracle, ReaderAgreement)
notes: 2026-08-19 14:49 UTC, c7dc613: ServeBench and OutOfFoldOracle done, along with TieDivergence and CropLaterality in f2f32f0. Only ReaderAgreement remains, and it is the one that needs a decision rather than a move - its report shares _resample with by_label and gap, so splitting it means deciding whether the resampling is part of the measurement or part of the reading. Gates green and 99% coverage on both passes; archmap regenerated in the same commit each time, which is what stopped the pre-push hook rejecting it the way it did twice yesterday.
close_reason:
Four of the five split (f2f32f0 TieDivergence + CropLaterality, c7dc613 ServeBench + OutOfFoldOracle), and the fifth is REFUSED on the mechanism rather than deferred.

The pattern earns its keep only where the render is trapped behind an apparatus: Attribution needs a GPU, StackCoverage the published predictions, SlotTies and TieDivergence and CropLaterality a corpus of DICOMs to walk, ServeBench a loaded member on a card, OutOfFoldOracle both. In every one of those the table could not be exercised without constructing the thing that measures.

ReaderAgreement has no such apparatus. Its whole input is one DataFrame of annotated cells, and tests/unit/kneemri/labels/reader_agreement.py:83 already builds that by hand - every report test there runs today without a corpus, a card or a checkpoint. Its LCOM4 3 is not a measure/render seam at all: the islands are {_resample,by_label,gap,report}, {error_report,errors} and {cells}, which are THREE QUESTIONS (agreement rate, error census, cell construction) that happen to share a table. Splitting a Report off it would buy no testability and would copy a pattern past the reason the pattern exists.

Recorded so the next lcom scan does not re-raise it: ReaderAgreement's LCOM4 3 is accepted, on the same grounds TrainingOptions' LCOM4 5 is.

title: A check that measures nothing reports a clean pass
description:
THE CLASS, not one bug: every check ends with a count and an exit code, and the two are independent, so a collapsed denominator prints the sentence a passing check prints and exits 0. Four occurrences in a week from three unrelated causes: arm_check twice (WSL bash / PowerShell PATH without coreutils - every arm timed out, '0 arms checked, 0 refused'), kit_check for 53 shipped-package commits (pathspec anchored one level down matched no file, so git log named no commit and every stale kit read as current), and the encoder drift gate (a compiled checkpoint whose keys all carry _orig_mod. matched no stock tensor and reported drift 0.000).

AUDIT 2026-08-19: arm_check was the only one of the five guarded. ledger_check ('0 finished runs, 0 unrecorded' when paths.yaml points at an unmounted or wrong root), kit_check (an empty import closure), champion_check ('0 members named and packaged' when the kernel tuple does not parse) and mount_check ('0 ok, 0 skipped, 0 refused' when no kernel is checkable) all passed over an empty set.

FIX: kneemri/denominator.refuse_empty is the one home for the refusal, wired into all five; each caller names its own empty set and its likeliest cause. Live denominators after the fix: 83 runs / 25 closure files / 4 champion members / 17 checkable kernels.

title: Run the pre-registered CUDA legs for witness batch geometry
description: Queued behind centre_tissue's chain (pid 52853): two CUDA runs of 'witness_check.py --batch 12' into logs/witness_cuda_batch12_run{1,2}.log. Run 1 answers whether feeding the recorded shape collapses the 0.0135-0.0156 the five bf16 members read; run 1 vs run 2 answers leg (a), whether the CUDA diff is stable or kernel-nondeterministic. If the diffs collapse under the 2e-3 bound, knee-djk8 closes without the constant being touched. If they do not, geometry is refuted and MATCHED_TOLERANCE's premise is wrong for a reason still unfound. Leg (c) -- why crop80 read exactly 0 on CUDA while reading 0.0152 on CPU -- is untouched by either outcome and stays open on knee-djk8.

title: [bug] A running chain freezes lib.sh at source time, so a mechanism added mid-session silently skips queued arms
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-19. run_train gained _seat_value in 96d7b80 (12:36 local). focal_pool and unfreeze_4 both finished AFTER that commit and neither printed a SEAT VALUE line; centre_tissue, whose chain shell sourced lib.sh at 13:12, is expected to print one.

MECHANISM: bash parses a sourced file ONCE into function definitions held in that shell's memory. A chain is one long-lived shell that sources experiments/lib.sh at launch and then runs arm after arm, so every arm in a chain runs the lib.sh that existed when the CHAIN started, not when the ARM started. run_snapshot deliberately snapshots the arm and the package but points ARM_LIB at the LIVE repo lib.sh - which is safe for editability but does nothing for a chain, because the chain already holds its copy.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the failure is SILENT and it looks exactly like a broken mechanism. Reading unfreeze_4's log, the honest conclusion from the evidence is 'seat value does not fire', and the fix one would reach for is in _seat_value. The seat value had to be recomputed by hand for both arms.

OPTIONS: (a) have run_train re-source lib.sh per arm - cheap, but re-sourcing mid-run is the class of thing run_snapshot exists to avoid; (b) stamp the lib.sh commit into each arm's log at run_train entry, so a missing mechanism is attributable in one grep instead of an hour; (c) have a chain re-exec itself per arm. (b) is the cheapest and turns a silent skip into a readable fact; it does not fix the staleness, it makes it legible.

Recorded in experiments/README.md alongside the unfreeze_4 row.
notes: Option (a) landed 2026-08-19 in 24f4ff8: run_train compares the parsed blob to the working tree and re-sources + re-dispatches when they differ, so the CURRENT arm gets the current mechanisms. _LIB_REFRESHING bounds it to one attempt. queue.sh was never affected (fresh shell per arm). experiments/lib_staleness_check.sh proves the decision; the re-source path is not proved end to end because it holds the card.

title: attribution's depth section draws a conclusion from a single window
description:
On band_dense_s2026 the reading was '1 window(s) of 20', so the depth sweep had one window: 'best single window starts at slice 0 (0.8558)', 'range 0.8558 to 0.8558 over 1 windows', 'per-label best window: 1 distinct depths over 12 labels'. It then prints the interpretation line 'one shared depth means a re-weighting of the sampled windows helps every label; several means the only correct answer is to read more of the stack'.

That sentence cannot be true from n=1. With one window every label trivially shares it, so the report states a conclusion the data cannot support, in the same wording it would use for a real result. Same family as the failures arm_check and ledger_check exist for: a vacuous result that reads identically to a measured one.

FIX: refuse the depth section when the window count is 1, the way RecordMix.shared refuses a too-small intersection rather than reporting over the survivors. Print what was asked and why it could not be answered.

Note the slice-cost section below it IS informative on the same run (6 distinct depths over 12 labels, slice 9 carrying 17%) — so only the window sweep degenerates, not the whole axis.

title: Report every arm's SEAT value beside its control delta
description:
BUILT 2026-08-19. record_mix --roster and kneemri.kaggle.seat_value now price a candidate against the members comp/champion.json pins, card-free.

WHY: arms were read against a MATCHED control only, which answers 'did this knob do anything' and not 'does this earn a seat'. depth_regions_narrow read +0.0097 against the fixed control wsfold0_e6, +0.0005 against its own predecessor depth_regions, and +0.0006 as a seat. Only the first was going to be reported. res392_ws is the case that forces it: 0.8523 solo, a member of the 0.925 four, and the greedy over 22 members takes it ninth - the first pick that does not raise the mix.

MEASURED against the shipped four (0.8648): every one of 18 same-split candidates is inside +0.0010, and 14 of 18 are negative. The roster is saturated. depth_regions +0.0010 and band_wide +0.0007 are the only two clearly above zero, which is the band axis topping the list a THIRD time by a method that shares nothing with solo AUC or the greedy.

CAVEAT ON THE RULER: the holdout under-prices diversity 2.4x against the board (knee-7d1), so a small negative here sits in the region where this ruler is known to be wrong. dinov3_base_lora - a genuinely different encoder - reads -0.0013.

REMAINING: arm headers still quote only their matched control. The convention should be that a finished arm reports both numbers.
close_reason: run_train prints it after ARM DONE; checkpoint parsed from the trainer's own best line, failures reported not propagated. Verified on encoder_layer_9 and on a missing-checkpoint log. 96d7b80

title: [bug] The card gate sat in run_snapshot, so the documented smoke procedure spent GPU ungated
description:
FOUND 2026-08-19 by walking into it. Smoking the new focal_pool recipe the way CLAUDE.md documents it — source experiments/lib.sh, call run_train with --studies 60 --epochs 1 — launched onto a card already running depth_regions_narrow and died with 'CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 366.00 MiB ... 4.84 GiB is free'.

THE HOLE: hold_card was called by run_snapshot, which only a QUEUED arm passes through. run_train is what actually starts the trainer, and it is reachable three other ways — the documented smoke, an ad-hoc one-off, and any script that sources the lib. All three spent GPU with no gate, by construction rather than by accident.

WHY THE NEAR-MISS IS NOT REASSURING: the incumbent survived at 1255 img/s with no STALLED line, but only because the NEWCOMER lost the allocation race. That is luck. The same collision at a smaller footprint is two arms sharing one card, which is exactly the 31.9-GB PCIe-paging collapse the lock exists to prevent — the serialiser would again have been the thing producing the overflow it guards against, the same shape as knee-n7ql.

FIX: hold_card moved from run_snapshot into run_train, which is the ONE point every GPU-spending path crosses, with release_card on every exit path including the failures (a crashed trainer holding the lock would idle the queue behind it). Per call rather than per arm, so a sweep arm calling run_train several times lets another chain interleave between its runs instead of holding across all of them. run_snapshot copies the package and the arm, which spends no GPU, so nothing needed protecting before the trainer starts.

VERIFIED: the identical command that OOM'd now prints 'waiting for another process to release the card: 12369 MiB free, want 18432' and queues.

title: TARGETS moved to kneemri/findings.py (13 CLIs no longer import torch to read it)
description: models.model was the graph's top bottleneck (fan-in 25, bottleneck 125, chokepoint 0.014). 13 of its 25 importers wanted only TARGETS, a 12-string tuple, and paid a 637-line torch module for it. TARGETS now lives at the package root as vocabulary; the order is the submission-column contract, pinned by tests/unit/kneemri/findings.py::test_targets.
notes: Direct importers of models.model: 27 -> 14. The fitness 'fan-in 25' is a transitive measure and did not move; what moved is the import COST — kneemri.labels.targets now imports in 0.3s with torch absent from sys.modules.

title: RunSetup split out of TrainingOptions (LCOM4=5)
description: train.py was 706 lines at a 750 ceiling and TrainingOptions was the worst-cohesion class in the repo (LCOM4=5, five disjoint method clusters). Split into options.py (what the command line SAYS), run_setup.py (what it BUILDS) and train.py (the run). Done.

title: champion_check guards the 0.925 reproduction path; run it when the roster or a champion kernel changes
description: comp/champion.json pins solotop_v1 (board 0.925, kit e4cffcf, four members, overlap=False/RankAverage/no views) plus the six principles it is evidence for. python -m kneemri.kaggle.champion_check asserts the kernel's chosen tuple still names those four and members.roster still packages them. It is not wired into nox/pre-commit (neither are the other six checks) so it needs running by hand after a roster edit or a kernel rewrite. If a later entry beats 0.925, repin champion.json to it in the same commit that records the board score.

title: res392_ws has no cached holdout logits, so the 0.925 champion has NO offline number
description: board.jsonl records solotop_v1 (0.925, our best) and ratepair_v1 (0.921) with offline=null, because the joint holdout of any subset containing res392_ws_s2026 has never been computed: that member alone has no .holdout.npz under the processed root, while calibrated_targets, intensity392, lr1e-4 and lr4e-5 all do. CONSEQUENCE: the two most recent entries cannot enter board_transfer's pair analysis, so the compression estimate (+4.95 board points per holdout point over 17 pairs) is fitted without the champion. Filling it in must NOT be done by arithmetic - the pre-swap subset plus the member's solo delta is exactly what pre-registered 0.927 against an actual 0.925. It needs one GPU pass to write res392_ws_s2026.holdout.npz over the 909-study fold-0 holdout, then member_curve over the named four. title: [bug] noxfile.py:14 is 274 chars and fails our own E501 gate, so nox -s gates is red at HEAD
description: uvx nox -s gates fails on 'ruff check . --statistics' with exactly one error: E501 Line too long (274 > 120) at noxfile.py:14, the SELECT string. Verified pre-existing, not introduced by working-tree changes — git stash --include-untracked and re-run reproduces it at HEAD. Two consequences: the merge gate is red for a reason unrelated to any change being gated, which trains the operator to read past a failure; and 'ruff check .' scans noxfile while the first ruff invocation (core kneemri tests comp) does not, so the two ruff passes disagree about which files are in scope. noxfile.py is TEMPLATE-OWNED by sdlc-scaffold, so per CLAUDE.md the fix is upstream (wrap SELECT across lines, or add noxfile.py to the ruff extend-exclude the way pyproject already excludes it from deptry) and then copier update — not a hand-edit here, and not a noqa.
close_reason: duplicate of knee-cjuw, same noxfile.py:14 E501

title: comp/members is a second local dir stamping dimiturnt/kneemri-members, and it is mount_check's default root
description: Two local directories carry a dataset-metadata.json with id dimiturnt/kneemri-members: comp/members (a stale mirror, 7 members) and D:/data/.../all_ours (what package_members writes and push.sh uploads, now 9). mount_check defaults --root to comp/members, so on 2026-08-18 the DEFAULT invocation REFUSED a valid kernel: 'comp\members holds [...] and was asked for [lr4e-5_ws_s2026]' - the member was in the package that is actually mounted on Kaggle, and absent only from the mirror. A check whose default answer is wrong is worse than no check: it teaches the operator to pass --root and stop reading the refusal. comp/SUBMISSIONS.md already documents the two-local-dirs hazard, which means this is the hazard firing, not a surprise. FIX (low backwards-compat, per project directive): one home. Delete comp/members and make mount_check resolve its root from paths.yaml + the package name, so there is exactly one directory that can carry that dataset id and the default is the one that ships.

title: arm_check --switches reports smoke-only recipes as UNCACHED forever
description: arm_check --switches merges SwitchCoverage recipes into the same dict uncached() judges, and uncached() asks about the FULL cache. A switch recipe is smoke-only by construction (decode_smoke_caches builds its sixty-study truncation), so switch_tie reports "UNCACHED switch_tie: nothing decoded at 336px_12sl_last" on every run and always will. Unactionable noise, against arm_smoke.learned own standard: a check that cries about a recipe working as specified is one nobody reads by the third sweep. It also makes --require-caches unable to pass together with --switches. Fix: exclude the switch half from the uncached report.

title: The six-axis cache construction is spelled by hand three times on the BUILD/TRAIN side
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-18. StudyCache(directory, slices, image_size, routing, reading, first) is written out at kneemri/training/train.py:614, kneemri/experiments/arm_check.py:234 and kneemri/corpus/cache_flags.py:102. All three agree TODAY - checked field by field.

This is the duplication Member.cache() was created to remove on the SERVE side, where three call sites (the oracle, the witness check, the curve) each named a cache by size, depth and router while the member also recorded a crop and a band - so any member that read anything else resolved to the DEFAULT arrays, which exist, load, and are the wrong pixels. members.py:193 states the rule: 'the set of fields that names a cache is not knowledge a consumer should hold'. The build/train side still holds it in three places.

WHAT IT COSTS WHEN IT DRIFTS: a seventh cache axis added to StudyCache.key() and forgotten at one of the three means arm_check reports 'cached' for a cache the run will not open (a queue slot spent discovering it), or build_cache writes under a name the trainer does not ask for.

FIX: TrainingOptions.cache(directory) - train.py and arm_check both hold a TrainingOptions and would call it; cache_flags builds from an argparse Namespace for the build CLI and would keep its own or take the same shape. NOTE it adds a seventh factory method to TrainingOptions (see knee-d2z6, which says the setup-on-the-config residue is deliberate but growing), and it edits the training entrypoint - so gates plus a 60-study smoke, and not between an arm being queued and run.
close_reason: TrainingOptions.cache(directory) is the one home for the dataclass half; main and arm_check both call it. CacheFlags.cache stays the namespace half (build_cache, build_embeddings, head_trial parse into a bare Namespace). A Protocol collapsing the two was tried and REJECTED BY THE GATES, correctly: fitness reads a second class in cache_flags.py as a second subject, envy reads a method touching 9 foreign fields and 0 of its own as belonging elsewhere. The two halves are pinned equal by tests/unit/kneemri/training/train.py::test_cache instead. Verified: gates green (99% cov), and arm_check over the real queue reports 37 arms, 0 refused, 0 uncached - every arm's reading still names a cache that is on disk. Commit 0acd323.

title: Serve-side read of a recorded config had no mechanical guard - the nine-defect class, from the reader's end
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-18, for the silent train/serve mismatch class (a value recorded in the config, a consumer reading a module default - nine instances counted in MemberRecord's own docstrings, each found AFTER a run by a witness, a refused fingerprint or a lost submission).

The WRITER was already guarded: tests/unit/kneemri/runs/member_record.py::test_payload_takes_each_config_field_from_the_option_of_its_own_name moves one option and demands exactly one stamped field follow (21 shared fields). Nothing guarded the READER, so a key could be stamped correctly and consumed by nobody - which is what happened all nine times.

LANDED: tests/unit/kneemri/inference/members.py::test_every_recorded_field_is_either_consumed_or_declared_unread. Builds the config the WRITER actually stamps (imports its helper rather than copying it), and asserts recorded == CONSUMED | PROVENANCE_ONLY - 27 keys = 20 with a declared serve-side reader + 7 declared unread (ema, rank_weight, pair_memory, report_weight, unfreeze_last, head_lr, backbone_lr: training rules that leave no trace in a forward pass). Then probes each consumed key with a second legal value and demands its reader follow. A NEW recorded field can no longer arrive with no consumer and no stated reason for having none.

TWO OTHER AUDIT RESULTS, written down so they are not re-derived:

  - READING/ROUTING NEED NO LANDED CHECK. StudyCache.key() puts crop, band, router and truncation in the cache FILENAME, so a mis-wired reading is a FileNotFoundError on a memory map, not a silent swap. That is a stronger guard than a comparison and it already exists. Do not add one.
  - Ensemble.slices/decoded_scheme took 'members or self.package.members', so an EMPTY subset silently meant the whole package - a default in two methods whose own docstrings say 'derived, never defaulted'. Unreachable today (reads() groups are non-empty and members[0] would raise first), fixed anyway to 'is None' via Ensemble._asked so an empty subset surfaces as max() refusing an empty sequence / agreed() refusing zero distinct values.

title: Landed guard does not reach the DATA switches: --weight-floor, --calibrated-targets, crop/band/centre/scheme
description: kneemri.training.landed now checks 14 switches across the model, trainer, objective and augmentation. The switches that map to a DATA argument rather than to a policy object are still outside it: Supervision (--weight-floor, --calibrated-targets) is consumed by Targets.load, and the routing/crop/band/centre trio shapes the cache read. Each changes what the model is fitted on while every recorded config agrees with itself -- the same shape as the nine defects already paid for. Needs a reporter on the loaded Targets and on the corpus reader, then four more Request fields.
notes:
RESOLVED IN PART, AND THE OTHER PART IS VOID BY CONSTRUCTION.

DONE: the two label switches. Targets now carries the Supervision it was loaded under and answers for it via supervised(); Landed takes the targets as a third authority and Request gained weight_floor/calibrated_targets. wanted() re-derives the floor from the FLAG rather than reading arguments.supervision.floor, so a broken bool-to-value rule in TrainingOptions.supervision is visible at the guard instead of only in the loss.

VOID: crop/band/centre/scheme cannot silently fail to land. Every one of them is in StudyCache.key -- reading.suffix() carries crop+band, routing.suffix() carries scheme+tie -- so the cache path IS the geometry. A flag that never reached StudyCache opens a different filename and np.load raises FileNotFoundError before the card is taken. There is nothing for a landed check to add: the failure is already loud. A guard here would have been a redundant check that reads as coverage.

Recorded because the same reasoning applies to any future data axis: put it in the cache key and it guards itself.

title: A run asserts its switches LANDED on the model, not just that it asked for them
description: train.py now builds Landed(model, trainer) and refuses to start when a requested switch shows no effect: adapters counted in the module tree, HF's is_gradient_checkpointing, the compiled call impl, the trainer's autocast dtype, window and read size. Motivated by three paid-for failures — low_rank matching projections BY NAME and wrapping nothing on an unknown encoder, a str.replace that matched nothing, and a trainable-parameter count that validated the first by counting non-adapters. Landed + Request live in kneemri/training/landed.py; smoked on lora_r8_small_336 (lora + whole-stack + train-size all land).
